Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-100-FITAP Age Document No./Name B-110-FITAP Age Limits Effective Date May 1, 2022

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

A child must be:

● under 18 years of age, or

● 18 years of age and a full-time student in a secondary school (or in the equivalent level of vocational or technical training). Full-time status is defined by the institution.

II. PROCEDURES

Refer to B-120-FITAP for verification of age.

* LITE will send an automated Case Action Task: 18th Birthday Approaching two months (on the 15th) prior to the child’s birth month. This allows the case owner sufficient time to call the family and request verification of school enrollment, if the child is enrolled full-time.

For example: A child is approaching their 18th birthday and the date of birth is 8/25, the 18th Birthday Approaching Task will appear on the dashboard on 6/15 with a due date of 7/10.

Call the qualified relative and inquire if the child is enrolled full-time in school.

If the child is not enrolled full-time, no further action is required.

If the child is enrolled full-time, send a semi-automated FFCCL - Client Contact Letter (18C FF) in LITE requesting the school enrollment/attendance verification.

To request verification of school enrollment on the LITE Education – Details screen:

 Input the Enrollment Status for the member.

 Enrollment Verification should be updated to Pending Verification

 Is this person working towards a High School Diploma or GED/HiSET? Yes

 Type of Educational Institution/Training Program should be updated to reflect the educational institute the 18 year old is attending (i.e. High School, GED Program/HiSET, etc.)

Upon running EDBC, LITE will request the verification of school enrollment and allow the client 10 days to provide the requested verification. ** Verification of full-time enrollment in a secondary school or its equivalent must be current.

2 of 2

* The LITE Education – Details screen must be updated once school enrollment verification is received. Acceptable sources for verification include school records, such as progress or report cards, or a verbal statement from a school official, which must be documented in Case Notes. Authorize the case. **

Remove the 18 year old child when *** * they are no longer enrolled in school full-time or have completed their course of study.

Send advance notice of adverse action to remove the child in the month of their ** 19th birthday to be effective the following month.

***

* LITE eligibility batches automatically update the case when a child is turning a specific age.

For Example:

 FITAP: Child is turning 18 years of age in the next month. On the 1st day of the month prior to the birthday month, the child who was receiving FITAP will be excluded if they are not a verified full-time student in a secondary school, and will stop receiving FITAP. If that child was the only eligible individual in the AU, the case will close.

 FITAP: Child is turning 19 years of age in the next month. On the 1st day of the month prior to the birthday month, the child who was receiving FITAP will be excluded, and will stop receiving FITAP. If that child was the only eligible individual in the AU, the case will close.

Note: LITE currently sends advance notice of adverse action to be effective for the birthday month. This is a known defect that is scheduled for correction. The child must be excluded effective the month after their birth month.

Workers must use the LITE Override feature to allow eligibility and benefit issuance for the birth month when they are processing applications, redeterminations, and changes. **

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms associated with this policy.

IV. REFERENCES

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B − Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-100-FITAP Age Document No./Name B-120-FITAP Verification of Age Effective Date July 3, 2024

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Verify the age of each child at certification or when adding a child. Do not delay certification of a child obviously under age 16 pending receipt of verification.

II. PROCEDURES

B-121-FITAP- PR HOW TO VERIFY AGE

View an official birth record, or baptismal certificate from a church with valid records.

If these proofs do not exist, use: Passports, naturalization papers, United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) documentation and/or identifying information provided in correspondence from a Voluntary Agency, insurance policies over 3 years old, church records, medical records, licensed midwife records, U. S. Census records, family Bible, immunization or other Health Unit records, school records or other reliable documents. The document must include the child's name and birthdate.

* Paternity Establishment and Support Enforcement (PESE) interface must be checked prior to requesting verification of age from the person being interviewed. If age is verified through PESE, document the case with a case note and enter the birth certificate number in the Document Type/Number column on the family tree in LITE. **

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms associated with this policy.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1000-FITAP-SNAP Resources Document No./Name B-1010-SNAP Definitions Effective Date January 1, 2010

1 of 1 Resources are assets or possessions which a household can convert to cash to meet needs.

The value of liquid resources is considered when determining eligibility. Examples of liquid resources include cash, bank accounts, and stocks. Refer to B-1040-SNAP for additional information.

The value of non-liquid resources is not considered when determining eligibility. Examples of non- liquid resources include buildings, land, and mineral rights.

B-1021-SNAP PO – PERSONS LIQUID RESOURCES TO CONSIDER

Consider the liquid resources of the following persons:

 Household members

 Disqualified members

 Ineligible aliens

 Alien Sponsors

B-1022 – SNAP PO - BROAD-BASED CATEGORICAL ELIGIBILITY (BBCE)

If the household is determined to be BBCE as defined in E-280-SNAP, the household’s resources reported must not be counted.

II. PROCEDURES

B-1021-SNAP – PERSONS LIQUID RESOURCES TO CONSIDER

The client’s statement is accepted as verification for non-Broad Based Categorically Eligible (BBCE) households if the household’s cash on hand and liquid resources are $2000 or less.

Count the resources of an alien's sponsor and the sponsor's spouse if living with the sponsor until the alien becomes a citizen or has worked 40 qualifying quarters of Social Security coverage. (Refer to E- 110-SNAP.) Beginning January 1, 1997, a quarter in which the alien received federal means-tested assistance is not counted as a qualifying quarter. The resources of the sponsor and sponsor's spouse must be reviewed at application and each redetermination.

B-1022 – SNAP PR - BROAD-BASED CATEGORICAL ELIGIBILITY (BBCE)

*** * Resources for all members included in the Broad-Based Categorically Eligible households are excluded from eligibility determination. Resource questions do not need to be cleared when processing applications, Simplified Reports, or redeterminations. Verification of resources for BBCE households do not need to be requested.

LITE will determine if the household is BBCE based on criteria in E-282-SNAP-PO and will automatically make a case note indicating that the household is eligible for BBCE. **

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1000-FITAP-SNAP Resources Document No./Name B-1030-SNAP Resource Limits Effective Date October 1, 2024

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The maximum allowable resources of all members of the household shall not exceed.

• * $4,500 for households which include at least one member age 60 or over or a member who is disabled.

• $3,000 for all other households.

The resource test is not applied to SNAP households that are traditional or Broad-Based categorically eligible. (Refer to policy at E-280-SNAP.)

Count only the equity value of countable resources. The equity value is the fair market value less encumbrances (liens or claims).

Countable resources are the resources that are available:

• At the time of the application interview, or

• When the household submits the redetermination.

II. PROCEDURES

Allow the following maximum resources:

• $4,500 for households which include at least one member age 60 or over or a member who is disabled.

• $3,000 ** for all other households.

Do not apply the resource test to SNAP households which are traditional or Broad-Based categorically eligible. (Refer to policy at E-280-SNAP.)

Count only the equity value of countable resources.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms and instructions associated with this policy.

IV. REFERENCES

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1000-FITAP-SNAP Resources Document No./Name B-1040-SNAP Types Of Resources Effective Date October 1, 2024

1 of 7 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The following are countable resources:

• Cash,

• Checking accounts,

• Saving accounts, including money market accounts,

• Certificates of deposit (CDs),

• Stocks, including mutual funds,

• Bonds, and

• Credit card company gift cards, prepaid debit cards, and payroll deposit debit card accounts.

Note: Any exempt resource that is kept in a separate account remains exempt. If an exempt resource is combined with money which is countable, exempt the excluded funds for six months from the date the funds are combined. After six months, count the total amount of combined funds as an available resource.

Exception: Resources for individuals who are not traditional Categorically Eligible (Refer to policy at E-280-SNAP), must meet required resource limits (Refer to policy at B-1030-SNAP).

B-1040-1-SNAP - PO AGENT ORANGE SETTLEMENT PAYMENTS AS A RESOURCE

Exempt payments made from the Agent Orange Settlement Fund. This includes both disability payments made to veterans each year they are disabled and non-recurring lump-sum payments made to survivors of deceased veterans. This exclusion is retroactive to January 1, 1989.

B-1040-1-A SNAP – PO ACHIEVING A BETTER LIFE EXPERIENCE (ABLE)

Exempt the value of ABLE accounts. An ABLE account is a tax-favored savings account established to provide secure funding for disability-related expenses on behalf of designated beneficiaries deemed disabled before the age of 26 years old.

B-1040-2-SNAP - PO CERTIFICATES OF DEPOSIT

Count the value of Certificates of Deposit (CDs) as an available resource. If there is a penalty for early withdrawal, count the amount the client would receive if the CD is cashed in. If the CD is collateral for a loan, count the amount the client would receive after payoff of the loan.

2 of 7 B-1040-3-SNAP - PO DISASTER PAYMENTS AS A RESOURCE

Exempt Disaster Payments provided as a result of a Presidentially-Declared emergency or major disaster. This includes federal assistance provided to persons directly affected and to comparable disaster assistance provided by states, local governments, and disaster assistance organizations. This includes Individual and Family Grant (IFG) payments, Small Business Administration (SBA) loans, and Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) payments.

B-1040-4-SNAP - PO Earned Income Tax Credit as a Resource

Exempt federal Earned Income Tax Credits (EITC) received either as a lump sum or as payments under Section 3507 of the Internal Revenue Code.

Exempt any federal, state, or local EITC (including EITC exemption under Section 3507), as resources for 12 months from the date of receipt. Therefore, if a refund is received on March 15, it will be excluded through March 14 of the following year.

B-1040-5-SNAP - PO Educational Assistance

Exempt all educational assistance, including, but not limited to:

• Funds received from educational grants, loans, and scholarships, • Qualified tuition programs established under Section 529 of the Internal Revenue Code, and • Funds in a Coverdell education savings account under Section 530 of the Internal Revenue Code.

B-1040-6-SNAP - PO Student Tuition Assistance and Revenue Trust (START) Saving Program

Exempt the cash value of an Education Savings Account (ESA) established through the Student Tuition Assistance and Revenue Trust (START) Saving Program. The START Saving Program is administered by the Louisiana Office of Student Financial Assistance. An ESA may be opened on behalf of a named beneficiary by any Louisiana resident.

B-1040-7-SNAP - PO Energy Assistance Payments as a Resource

Exempt payments or allowances made for the purpose of providing energy assistance under any federal law other than Title IV-A of the Social Security Act (TANF).

B-1040-7A-SNAP - PO Gift Cards

Establishment-specific gift cards are not counted as a resource. The value of credit card company gift cards and prepaid debit cards are counted as a resource.

3 of 7 B-1040-8-SNAP - PO Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Benefits as a Resource

Exempt only HUD retroactive tax and utility cost subsidies issued because of the settlement of Underwood vs. Harris against HUD for the month in which the payment was received and for the following month.

B-1040-9-SNAP - PO Income as a Resource

Do not count income from any source as a resource in the month of receipt.

Do not count as a resource money which has been prorated as income. If this money is combined with countable funds, such as a bank account, exempt the prorated amounts for the time it is prorated. An example is self-employment income.

B-1040-10-SNAP - PO Indian and Native Claims and Lands Payments as a Resource

Exempt payments received under the following acts:

• Public Law 92-203, Section 21(a) (Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act),

• Public Law 94-189 (Sac and Fox Indian Claims Agreement),

• Public Law 94-540 (Grand River Band of Ottawa Indians),

• Public Law 96-420 Section 5 (Passamaquoddy Tribe and the Penobscot Nation received according to the Maine Indian Claims Settlement Act of 1980),

• Public Law 95-433, Section 2, Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakima Nation and the Apache Tribe of the Mescalero Reservation received from the Claims Commission, and

• Public Law 93-531 (Navajo and Hope Tribes).

Exempt payments received by certain Indian tribal members under Public Law 94-114, Sect. 6, regarding submarginal lands held in trust by the United States.

Exempt payments from Indian lands held jointly with the tribe or land that can be sold only with approval of the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

B-1040-11-SNAP - PO Individual Development Accounts (IDA)

Exempt Individual Development Accounts.

4 of 7 B-1040-12-SNAP - PO Individual Retirement Accounts (IRAs) as a Resource

Exempt the value of IRAs.

B-1040-13-SNAP - PO Insurance Settlements

Insurance settlements are considered a lump-sum payment.

B-1040-14-SNAP - PO Joint Accounts

Consider resources as inaccessible to a victim of domestic violence if the resources are jointly owned with a member of the former household and the individual is unable to access the resource because of fear for her safety or because the joint owner will not allow it, etc. The individual must verify the status as a victim of domestic violence and verify that she cannot access the resource for her personal use.

Count the entire value as available to each of the joint owners. Exceptions:

• If the client's name is on another individual’s account for convenience purposes only, the account may be disregarded provided all of the following circumstances exist:

o The client's name was placed on the account to enable the client to transact business for the other individual such as an elderly or disabled parent;

o The client does not contribute to the account, and does not use money from the account for personal needs;

o The client is accountable to the other individual for actions on the bank account; and

o The other individual is contacted and verifies that the money does not belong to the client and may not be used to meet the client's needs.

• If an SSI recipient and a non-SSI recipient, who are members of the same SNAP household, jointly own an account, the account shall be treated as if it were solely owned by the SSI recipient.

B-1040-15-SNAP - PO Keogh Plans as a Resource

Exempt the value of Keogh Plans.

B-1040-16-SNAP - PO Loans as a Resource

All loans, both business and personal, other than deferred repayment educational loans, are counted as resources in the month received even if the household anticipates spending some or all of it in the

5 of 7 same month. Any amount remaining after month of receipt continues to be counted a resource until the money is spent.

B-1040-17-SNAP - PO Lump-Sum Payments as a Resource

Count non-recurring lump-sum payments as resources in the month received.

Non-recurring payments are payments which are received one time only and are not anticipated to be received again. Consider payments which are recurring as income.

Countable lump-sum payments include, but are not limited to, income tax refunds, retroactive lump- sum initial social security or UCB, worker's compensation, insurance settlements, and refunds of security deposits on rental property or utilities. Count the gross amount before attorneys' fees are deducted.

When a lump-sum payment is earmarked for a specific purpose, allow the client six months to use the money for the purpose for which it was received.

Exempt Federal tax refunds as a resource for 12 months from the date of receipt. The Federal tax refund must be excluded from the household’s resources by subtracting the amount of federal tax refund received by the household in the last 12 months from the household’s resources. If the difference between the resources and the amount of the Federal tax refund is less than the resource limit, the household meets the resource limit.

Example: Ms. Smith reported that she has a balance of * $4500 in her checking account at application for SNAP on 02/01/11. She stated that she received an $1850 refund from her Federal taxes on 07/2/10. The worker requested verification of the tax refund and received a copy of the client’s 08/10 checking account statement showing the $1850 was directly deposited into the account on 07/2/10. Ms. Smith is below the household’s $3000 resource limit after subtracting the amount of the federal tax refund from the checking account balance ($4500 - $1850 = $2650). **

B-1040-18-SNAP - PO Payments to Victims of Nazi Persecution

Payments made to individuals because of their status as victims of Nazi persecution are exempt.

B-1040-19-SNAP - PO Relocation Assistance as a Resource

Exempt reimbursements from the Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Properties Acquisition Policy Act of 1970.

B-1040-20-SNAP - PO Retirement Plans as a Resource

Exempt the value of pension plans.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1000-FITAP-SNAP Resources Document No./Name B-1040-SNAP Types Of Resources Effective Date October 1, 2024

6 of 7 B-1040-21-SNAP - PO Trust Funds as a Resource

Exempt trust funds if all of the following conditions are met: • The trust arrangement is unlikely to end during the certification period and no household member can revoke the trust agreement or change the name of the beneficiary during the certification period.

• The trustee of the fund is either:

o A court, institution, corporation, or organization not under the direction or ownership of a household member, or o A court-appointed individual who has court-imposed limitations placed on the use of the funds.

• The trust investments do not directly involve or help any business or corporation under the control, direction, or influence of a household member. Exempt trusts established from the household's own funds if the trustee uses the funds only to make investments on behalf of the trust or to pay the education or medical expense of the beneficiary.

B-1040-22-SNAP - PO Tutorship Funds as a Resource

Funds awarded to a minor to be managed by a tutor or tutrix in accordance with the law of tutorship are not accessible for the maintenance and support of the household and are therefore excluded.

The client must provide documentation to verify the funds are covered under the law of tutorship.

B-1040-23-SNAP - PO Wartime Relocation of Civilians Payments

Exempt the following payments made through the Wartime Relocation of Civilians Law:

• Payments of $20,000 made to eligible persons of Japanese ancestry who were interned during World War II, or such payments made to the spouse, children or parents if the eligible individual is deceased.

• Payments of $12,000 made to eligible Aleuts who were relocated from their home on the Pribolof or Aleutian Islands to an internment camp during World War II, or such payments made to an individual who was born while his mother was relocated.

B-1040-24-SNAP - PO Winnings from Gambling

Winnings from gambling (lottery, etc.) that are non-recurring and are not anticipated to be received again are considered as a resource in the month received.

Refer to B-620-55A-FITAP/SNAP for winnings from gambling that are recurring.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B − Eligibility Factors (SNAP) Section No./Name B-1000-SNAP Resources (SNAP) Document No./Name B-1050-SNAP Transferring Resources Effective Dates October 1, 2021

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

B-1051-SNAP - PO PENALTIES FOR TRANSFERRING RESOURCES

The household unit is ineligible if within three months before application or any time after certification a member or disqualified member transfers a countable resource for less than its fair market value to qualify for benefits. This penalty applies only if the total of the transferred resource added to other countable resources would have affected eligibility.

The transfer of resources between members of the same SNAP household does not affect eligibility.

The transfer of resources for reasons other than qualifying for benefits, such as funds placed in an educational trust fund, does not affect eligibility.

B-1052-SNAP - PO HOW TO DETERMINE INTENT

Determine if the transfer of resources was an intentional act for the purpose of qualifying for benefits by:

● Evaluating the client's circumstances before and after the transfer and

● The reason for the transfer. An example of a transfer made for an acceptable purpose would be a transfer to cancel a legitimate debt.

B-1053-SNAP - PO LENGTH OF DISQUALIFICATION PERIOD

The length of disqualification is based on the amount by which the transferred resource exceeds the resource maximum when added to other countable resources.

Amount in Excess of Resource Limit Period of Denial

$.01 to $249.99 1 month $250 to $999.99 3 months $1000 to $2999.99 6 months $3000 to $4999.99 9 months $5000 and more 12 months

Example: A one-person household has $1750 in a bank account and transfers ownership of a certificate of deposit worth $2000. When the countable value of the transferred resource is added to other resources, it exceeds the * $2500 resource limit by $1250. The $1250 ** is used to determine the period of disqualification of six months.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – ELIGIBILITY FACTORS Section No./Name B-1200-FITAP SUPPORT ENFORCEMENT SERVICES Document No./Name B-1220-FITAP Notification To Client of Support Enforcement Requirement Effective Date August 15, 2019

1 of 5 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Each applicant for, or recipient of, FITAP is required to assign to the Louisiana Department of Children and Family Services, any accrued rights to support for any other person that such applicant or recipient may have, including such rights in his own behalf or in behalf of any other family member for whom the applicant or recipient is applying for or receiving.

B-1221-FITAP - PO THE AUTOMATIC ASSIGNMENT OF SUPPORT

By accepting FITAP, the client automatically assigns to the State past, present, and future rights to support for the assistance unit.

B-1222-FITAP - PO REQUIREMENTS TO COOPERATE WITH CSE

The client is required to cooperate with Child Support Enforcement (CSE) in:

● identifying and locating the absent parent,

● establishing paternity, and

● obtaining support payments, other payments or property.

Cooperation includes:

● appearing at an office of CSE or contract District Attorney to provide information he has or can secure,

● appearing as a witness, providing information, or attesting to lack of information under penalty of perjury, and

● repaying to CSE all child support payments received and retained after certification. (See B-1252- FITAP.)

B-1223-FITAP - PO GOOD CAUSE CLAIM

A client has the right to refuse to comply with support requirements if it can be proven that compliance is against the caretaker relative's or child's best interest.

2 of 5 B-1224-FITAP - PO PENALTIES FOR NOT COOPERATING WITH CSE PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS

*** Failure to sign the OFS Flyer 6 will result in ineligibility for the applicant. * Unless Good Cause is verified, ** failure to cooperate with ongoing support requirements will result in a penalty (Refer to B- 1224-FITAP-PR).

II. PROCEDURES

Explain to the client:

● the automatic assignment of support,

● the requirement to cooperate with CSE,

● that he may claim good cause for not cooperating with CSE, and

● the penalties for not cooperating with program requirements.

B-1221-FITAP - PR THE AUTOMATIC ASSIGNMENT OF SUPPORT

The client acknowledges the automatic assignment by signing (manually or electronically) the OFS Flyer 6. Refer to B-620-8-FITAP and B-1270-FITAP for two-parent households.

B-1222-FITAP - PR REQUIREMENTS TO COOPERATE WITH CSE

Cooperation includes:

● appearing at an office of CSE or contract District Attorney to provide information he has or can secure,

● appearing as a witness, providing information, or attesting to lack of information under penalty of perjury, and

● repaying to CSE all child support payments received and retained after certification. (See B-1252- FITAP.)

B-1223-FITAP - PR GOOD CAUSE CLAIM

The good cause provision is not meant to be a blanket waiver of the child support requirements. It serves to protect families at risk of physical or emotional harm because of these requirements.

3 of 5 Explain and complete OFS Flyer 6, Notice of Cooperation Requirements and Good Cause provisions under Title IV-D.

Use OFS Flyer 6 at application and at any other time the worker feels it is necessary to assist the client with claiming good cause.

If the application is received online, the Child Support Agreement to Relinquish Child Support Payments (electronic OFS Flyer 6) will display and the applicant may select “Yes” or “No” to the question, “I have read this notice concerning my agreement to relinquish child support payments, to cooperate with CSE, and my right to claim good cause for not cooperating.” and will provide an electronic signature.

● Review the CAFÉ Application Summary PDF to determine whether the applicant selected “Yes” or “No” and explain the content of the OFS Flyer 6 to ensure the applicant understands the requirements.

● If the applicant selected “No”, a manual OFS Flyer 6 is not required if the worker documents in the Wizard that the requirements were discussed and the client expressed understanding of the agreement and intentions to comply.

A manual OFS Flyer 6 must be completed with applicants/recipients if the applicant/recipient submits a paper application, or submits an online application and adds the cash program during the interview. Enter all identifying information. The application must be rejected if the applicant fails to sign and return the manual form.

For all applications:

● acknowledge that the applicant has been provided notice of the requirement by indicating “Yes” to the question, “Is the member informed on this notice of cooperation with Child Support Enforcement and Agreement to Relinquish Child Support Payments?” in the ‘Notice of Cooperation with Child Support Enforcement and Agreement to Relinquish Child Support Payments’ section of the Interview Wizard, and

● make a *** *Case Note ** indicating whether the client expressed understanding of the agreement and intentions to comply.

Note: If the applicant/recipient understands the requirements but is unwilling to cooperate, good cause must be explored and documented before the application can be rejected. The applicant should be asked if there is any particular reason they do not want to comply and their statement must be documented.

4 of 5 Explain and complete OFS Flyer 6A, Notice of Good Cause provisions under Title IV-D, if the client wants to claim good cause or requests more information.

If the application is received online, review the CAFÉ Application Summary PDF to determine whether the applicant is claiming good cause:

● The applicant may select “Yes” or “No” to the question, “Would you like to claim good cause?” in the ‘Cooperation with Child Support Enforcement’ section of the online application.

● If the applicant selects “Yes”, then:

o the applicant will be required to select one of the Good Cause Reasons listed below:

 Your help may cause serious physical harm to you,  Your help may cause serious emotional harm to you,  Your help may cause serious physical harm to your child,  Your help may cause serious emotional harm to your child,  The child was born as a result of rape or incest, or  Adoption of the child is pending, and

o the Notice of Good Cause Provisions under Title IV-D Program (electronic OFS Flyer 6A) will appear near the end of the application and the applicant will be required to check the box, “I have read this notice concerning my right to claim good cause for non-cooperation.” and will provide an electronic signature.

If the applicant/recipient claims good cause through an online application or re-application, explain the good cause provisions contained in the Notice of Good Cause Provisions under Title IV-D Program and accept the electronic signature of the applicant/recipient.

A manual OFS Flyer 6A must be completed with applicants/recipients who wish to claim good cause if the applicant/recipient:

● submits a paper application, ● submits an online application and adds the cash program during the interview, ● submits an online application indicating he/she did not wish to claim good cause and subsequently decides during the interview to claim good cause, ● requests good cause after certification, or ● requests more information regarding good cause.

For all applications, acknowledge receipt of the applicant’s/recipient’s wish to claim good cause by indicating “Yes” or “No” to the question, “Is the applicant claiming good cause?” in the ‘Cooperation with Child Support Enforcement’ section of the Interview Wizard.

body:
Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 04 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1200-FITAP Support Enforcement Services Document No./Name B-1230-FITAP Reporting to Child Support Enforcement Effective Date July 1, 2019

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Each applicant or recipient of FITAP is required to cooperate in identifying and locating the parent(s) of a child (ren) who is absent from the home.

B-1231-FITAP - PO INITIAL REFERRAL

* Initial referrals to CSE are made at certification ** on all parents of FITAP children who are absent from the home, with the Referral Exceptions noted in B-1231-1-FITAP. These parents include:

● the child's mother,

● a man named as the child's father by the mother,

● the child's legal father. A legally responsible father is defined as a man married to the mother at the time the child is born, unless another man is presumed to be the father. (A common law union which has been formed in another state and recognized there as legally valid is considered a legal marriage in Louisiana.)

This includes a husband:

o who was legally separated or divorced from the mother less than 300 days before the birth of the child, and who has not obtained a court judgment declaring that he is not the child's father.

o who is informally separated from the mother, regardless of duration of the separation, and who has not obtained court judgment declaring he is not the child's father.

o who is aware of his wife's pregnancy at the time of the marriage, regardless of how soon the child is born after the marriage.

● the adoptive parent who has been legally granted a final decree of adoption,

● the child's natural father determined by the agency on the basis of reliable information such as:

o A man whose name appears on the child's birth certificate as father, or

o A man who has acknowledged paternity of the child in a written document executed before a notary public in the presence of two witnesses, or

o A man who has been declared to be the child's father by a court judgment, or

o A man who verbally acknowledges that he is the father, or

o A man who is shown as the father in school records.

2 of 4

Note: A biological parent of a child who has been legally adopted is no longer a parent.

* Completion of the form OFS 4NCP is required at application for households in which a legal or non- legal parent is absent unless:

● the absent parent meets a referral exception per B-1231-1-FITAP, or

● a form OFS 4NCP on the noncustodial parent has previously been submitted to CSE for this particular payee and child.

When the form OFS 4NCP is required, completion of the form OFS 4NCP Supplement is also required if the natural mother is residing in the household to establish paternity for children born out of wedlock with a non-legal noncustodial absent parent.

The application must be rejected when an applicant fails to sign and return a required OFS 4NCP or OFS 4NCP Supplement.

Referrals to CSE are made on-line by completion of the noncustodial Absent ** Parent screen when the FITAP certification is processed. ***

* Note: Absent parents of an unborn child are not referred until after the birth of the child. **

B-1231-1-FITAP - PO Referral Exceptions

All absent parents are referred to CSE except the following:

● Parents of SSI children.

● Parents whose death has been verified.

* Note: The client’s statement must be verified prior to certification. Acceptable sources of verification include, but are not limited to, death certificate, medical records, mortuary records, obituary, state or government agencies, etc.

● Biological parents of a child who has been legally adopted.

● Parents excluded by genetic test as verified by CSE or other reputable sources such as an American Association of Blood Banks (AABB) accredited laboratory that administered a legal DNA paternity test which included specimen collection by a third party trained laboratory technician after all persons being tested presented legally valid forms of identification. **

***

3 of 4 B-1232-FITAP - PO REPORTING AFTER INITIAL REFERRAL/* SUBSEQUENT REFERRALS **

To report information, which cannot be entered on LAMI (corrections, changes or other additional information, transmitting documents relating to the establishment of paternity and child support, report the payee received child support payments, etc.) send an e-mail, fax, or other written correspondence to CSE.

* Subsequent Referrals

Subsequent referrals to CSE are made after certification for all parents who are absent from the home in support of FITAP children who are new household members, with the Referral Exceptions noted in B-1231-1-FITAP.

Completion of the form OFS 4NCP is required after certification for households who report a new household member (i.e. birth of a child, a child moving into the home, etc.) in which a legal or non- legal parent is absent unless:

● the absent parent meets a referral exception per B-1231-1-FITAP, or

● a form OFS 4NCP on the noncustodial parent has previously been submitted to CSE for this particular payee and child, or

● the new household member is the child of an existing noncustodial parent who has already been referred for the case.

When the form OFS 4NCP is required, completion of the form OFS 4NCP Supplement is also required if the natural mother is residing in the household to establish paternity for children born out of wedlock with a non-legal noncustodial absent parent.

Process the addition of a new household member according to C-840-FITAP. Send a manual or semi-automated advance Notice of Adverse Action proposing closure if the new member is a required household member and the client fails to sign and return a required OFS 4NCP or OFS 4NCP Supplement by the due date given on the OFS 18C request for signature.

Referrals to CSE are made on-line by completion of the noncustodial Absent Parent screen when a child is added to an existing certification and the change is dispositioned.

Example 1: A household includes a natural mother payee, Susie, and her son, Jack. At certification, the absent parent, John, was referred on-line for the child, Jack. At change report, Susie reports that she gave birth to Jane who is also the non-legal child of John. The OFS 4NCP and OFS 4NCP Supplement are not required because John is an existing NCP for the case. The child, Jane, is added to the existing Absent Parent record on LAMI for John and the case is dispositioned.

At redetermination, Rose reports that a new grandchild, Chloe, is now living in the home. Chloe is the half-sibling of Holly and Dane. Chloe’s absent parents are Bill and Martina. The OFS 4NCP is not required for Martina because she is an existing NCP for the case. The OFS 4NCP is required for Bill because he does not meet any of the exceptions listed at B-1231-1-FITAP, a form OFS 4NCP has not been previously submitted to CSE for Rose and Chloe, and Bill is not an existing NCP for the case. Upon receipt of a completed and signed OFS 4NCP form for Bill, Chloe is added to the existing Absent Parent record on LAMI for Martina, a new Absent Parent record is created for Bill, and the case is dispositioned.

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

* Each applicant for or recipient of cash assistance benefits must cooperate in obtaining child support for the child (ren) for whom they are applying or receiving cash assistance benefits unless good cause is established. **

B-1241-FITAP - * PO ** GOOD CAUSE SITUATIONS AND ACCEPTABLE DOCUMENTATION

Good cause exists when:

1. The client's cooperation with Child Support Enforcement (CSE) is reasonably anticipated to result in:

● Physical harm to the child or caretaker relative which reduces his capacity to care for the child adequately, or

● Emotional harm to the child or caretaker relative which reduces his capacity to care for the child adequately.

Physical or emotional harm is considered domestic violence. Refer to E-330-FITAP for procedures and documentation used to establish good cause based on domestic violence.

2. One of the following situations exists and proceeding would be detrimental to the child:

● The child was conceived as a result of incest or rape.

Documentation - birth certificates or medical or law enforcement records which indicate the circumstances surrounding the child's conception.

● Legal proceedings for the adoption of the child are pending before a court.

Documentation - court documents or other records.

● The client is being assisted by a licensed or private social agency to resolve the issue of whether to keep the child or relinquish him for adoption. The issue must not have been under discussion more than three months.

Documentation - a written statement of facts from a public or licensed private social agency.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 04 – Family Assistance Manual (FAM) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1200-FITAP Support Enforcement Services Document No./Name B-1250-FITAP Noncooperation With Child Support Enforcement Effective Date February 1, 2018

1 of 4 I.

STATEMENT OF POLICY

If an applicant or recipient does not cooperate and does not have good cause, the client or the child (ren) will not be eligible for cash assistance.

B-1251-FITAP - PO NONCOOPERATION

CSE will notify IV-A daily through the LAMI/LASES interface via Infopac Report LAIN21P if the client fails to cooperate with CSE by:

● failure to keep two scheduled office appointments (Code S1),

● failure to appear for a blood test (Code S2),

● failure to appear in court (Code S3),

● failure to provide information during an interview (Code S4), or

● refusal to name the noncustodial parent (Code S5).

The report is coded as shown above to show the reason for the client's noncooperation.

B-1252-FITAP - PO FAILURE TO SUBMIT CHILD SUPPORT PAYMENTS TO CSE

When CSE determines that a client failed to submit child support payments to CSE, the case will be referred to the Fraud and Recovery Section. The Fraud and Recovery Section will contact the client and request repayment. If the client refuses to sign a repayment agreement or fails to submit agreed- upon payments, the Fraud and Recovery Section will notify the worker by form FR 64.

Note: Any child support received for FITAP two-parent households must be budgeted. If the two- parent household is placed in Simplified Reporting, refer to S-310-FITAP for reporting requirements. Refer to F-110-FITAP for overpayment/overissuances.

B-1253-FITAP - PO REAPPLICATION FOLLOWING CASE CLOSURE ***

Once a case has been closed for failure to cooperate with CSE:

● If the family is not work-eligible, the family may not be recertified until the client misses at least one month of benefits and goes to the CSE office and agrees to cooperate.

● If the family is work-eligible, the family must not receive benefits for the number of months required by the terms of the applicable STEP sanction and the client goes to the CSE office and agrees to cooperate.

2 of 4 * If a case was closed for a reason other than CSE non-compliance and the client failed to comply during a month of receipt of cash assistance, the family may not be recertified until the client goes to the CSE office and agrees to cooperate.

Example: Client’s case closes on November 16th for failure to timely reapply. LAIN21P is received on November 29thadvising that the client did not cooperate on November 21th. Even though the date of noncompliance was after the case closed, the client received benefits for the month of November and may not be recertified unless the client goes to the CSE office and agrees to cooperate. **

II. PROCEDURES

B-1251-FITAP - PR NONCOOPERATION

Take the following action upon receipt of the LAIN21P advising of noncooperation:

● * Document the case with a Case Note including the date of the LAIN21P, name of the Absent Parent, date of noncooperation, and the reason provided by CSE. **

● * If the case is active, send ** Advance Notice of Adverse Action (automated or manual) to the client within 10 days of receipt of the LAIN2IP to notify the client that the cash assistance case will be closed for failure to cooperate with CSE and to advise the client of the mandatory period of ineligibility. The case record must be documented with the type of notification (automated or manual) sent to the client.

○ If the family is not work-eligible, the case must remain closed for at least one month and the client complies with this requirement, whichever is later.

○ If the family is work-eligible, impose a STEP sanction with the appropriate occurrence and reason. The case must remain closed for the duration of the sanction period and until the client complies with this requirement, whichever is later.

o Close the case upon expiration of the 13-day notice unless the client ends his failure to

comply prior to that time.

● If the case is closed or pending closure (Active Closure) for another reason upon receipt of

the LAIN21P, send Advance Notice of Adverse Action (manual) to the client within 10 days to

notify the client of the CSE non-compliance, including the period of ineligibility based on the

STEP sanction occurrence for the work-eligible family or one month period for the not work-

eligible family, and the requirement to comply with Child Support Enforcement to regain

eligibility for benefits.

o If the reason for pending closure is resolved and the case is returned to an active status,

the appropriate STEP sanction for the work-eligible family or the one month case closure

for the not work-eligible family is imposed on LAMI and is effective the month following

Take the following action upon receipt of the LAIN21P advising of cooperation:

● If the client ends his failure to comply prior to expiration of the 13-day adverse action, remove the CSE sanction, disposition the case and send a concurrent notice.

● If the LAIN21P is received after case closure indicating the client *** cooperated * prior to case closure, ** reopen the case, remove the CSE sanction, disposition the case and send a concurrent notice. Corrective payments must be made to the client, if appropriate.

● * Document the case with a Case Note including the date of the LAIN21P, name of the Absent Parent, and date of cooperation. **

B-1252-FITAP - PR FAILURE TO SUBMIT CHILD SUPPORT PAYMENTS TO CSE

The Fraud and Recovery Section will notify the worker via FR 64 if the client fails to:

● Sign a repayment agreement (S6), or

● Comply with a repayment agreement (S7).

Upon receipt of form FR 64, send the OFS 19S and close the case as soon as possible after expiration of the notice of adverse action, unless the client ends his failure to comply prior to that time.

● If the family is not work-eligible, the case must remain closed for at least one month and the client complies with this requirement, whichever is later.

● If the family is work-eligible, impose a STEP sanction with the appropriate occurrence and reason. The case must remain closed for the duration of the sanction period and until the client complies with this requirement, whichever is later.

B-1253-FITAP - PR REAPPLICATION FOLLOWING CASE CLOSURE ***

Advise the client of this requirement at the time of the application interview and give the client form OFS 53, * Requirement ** to Cooperate with CSE. When the client appears at the CSE office, the client will meet with a CSE Specialist who will complete the bottom section of the form indicating whether the client has agreed to cooperate. The completed form will be given to the client at the conclusion of the CSE meeting. The client will be required to return the form to the local DCFS office.

Allow the client 10 days to go to the CSE office and return the form to the local DCFS office.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B-ELIGIBILITY FACTORS Section No./Name B-1200-FITAP SUPPORT ENFORCEMENT SERVICES Document No./Name B-1270-FITAP Grant Review Effective Date March 1, 2017

1 of 3 I.

STATEMENT OF POLICY

For a FITAP case to become subject to the grant review process, both the court-ordered amount of child support and the amount collected must be equal to or greater than the FITAP grant amount.

* Documentation of child support received is captured on INFOPAC report, LAIN23P. ** LAIN23P is a two-part report which is generated monthly. The first part of the report, LAIN23P4, identifies cases in which it appears that both child support collected in the prior month by Child Support Enforcement (CSE) and the amount of the court order are equal to or exceed the grant amount. The second part of the report, LAIN23P7, identifies payees with multiple grants for whom child support was collected and who may meet grant review criteria. These listings are available on INFOPAC for use by the * worker ** for the grant review process.

The listings contain the following information:

● LAMI case ID number(s)

● LAMI Case Name(s)

● LASES Case ID number(s)

● Grant Amount - This is the amount of the FITAP grant for the month of collection and is the amount which was reimbursed. For two-parent households, this field will be blank. Refer to B-620-FITAP, section B-620-8 to determine child support to be budgeted.

● Collect Amount - All LASES cases associated with the FITAP case will be listed with the amount collected shown for each case. The amounts are totaled and show the monthly collection amount.

● Court Order - The court-ordered amount for each associated LASES case is listed. These amounts are totaled and show the monthly court-ordered amounts.

● Disposition

B-1271-FITAP - * PO ** FAILURE TO RECEIVE BUDGETED CHILD SUPPORT DURING GRANT REVIEW PERIOD

* Continued eligibility must be determined if the client reports during the month following the first month cash benefits are stopped that no child support was received or that the amount of child support received was less than the amount budgeted. **

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B-ELIGIBILITY FACTORS Section No./Name B-1200-FITAP SUPPORT ENFORCEMENT SERVICES Document No./Name B-1270-FITAP Grant Review Effective Date March 1, 2017

2 of 3 II. PROCEDURES

When the grant review listing is received, take the following action:

● Budget any child support payment collected on all FITAP two-parent households. CSE will not retain the money collected and will send the amount collected to the household. Refer to B-620-FITAP, section B-620-8 for budgeting procedures.

● Compare the current month’s FITAP grant amount to the grant amount shown on the grant review listing. If there has been a grant increase, and if the increased grant amount is more than both the collect amount and court order amount, clear the listing by indicating it is not a valid grant review. If there has been no grant change or if the increased grant amount remains less than or equal to both the collect amount and court order amount, follow steps 1 through 5 below.

● Review the LASES case(s) listed * by completing a ‘Cross Program Case Search’ ** to determine * whether ** the child(ren) for whom the support was paid is in the assistance and/or income unit of the LAMI case indicated. If the child(ren) is not active in the LAMI case, clear the listing by indicating it is not a valid grant review. If the child(ren) is active in the LAMI case, take the following action as soon as possible but no later than 10 days from the run date of the LAIN23P:

1. Complete a manual budget to determine whether both the court-ordered amount and the child support collected equal or exceed the FITAP grant amount for the current month.

2. If the court-ordered amount and the child support collected do not equal or exceed the grant amount, post the listing and take no further action.

3. If both the court ordered amount and the child support collected equal or exceed the grant amount, enter a disposition reason code 06, a closure code 15, and a notice/adverse action suppression code of 2. DO NOT enter unearned income type IV-D. Send a manual notice of closure using form OFS 18.

4. If the member is receiving SNAP benefits, the child support should be entered with unearned income type CSA prior to dispositioning the FITAP case. After the FITAP case is dispositioned, disposition the SNAP case with disposition reason code 02. Notice of Adverse Action will be sent for the SNAP case.

5. Indicate action on the LAIN23P no later than the last day of the month the report was produced and sign the sheet. * Redact or mask data for other clients if present. The signed/documented report must be scanned into OnBase.

Note: A ‘Cross Program Case Search' is completed by following these steps: ● once in CAFÉ, click on the ‘Cases’ tab, ● click on the case number listed in ‘Cases’ tab and select the appropriate case to view,

This will enable the cross program pop up box, ● from the ‘Cross Program Case Search’ box drop-down menu, choose the program Child Support, and ● if the data available is not clear or seems questionable, email the details to the Regional FITAP Consultant for clearance.

B-1271-FITAP - PR FAILURE TO RECEIVE BUDGETED CHILD SUPPORT DURING GRANT REVIEW PERIOD **

If the client reports during the first month cash benefits are stopped that the amount of support budgeted was not received, advise the client to contact the office at the beginning of the following month if the money is not received or is less than the amount budgeted.

Take the following action if the client reports in the * month ** following *** the first month cash benefits were stopped * that the amount of child support received ** was less than the amount budgeted:

1. Verify on LASES the amount of any child support payments received during the month of discontinuance * by completing a ‘Cross Program Case Search’ through CAFE. **

2. Determine eligibility for that first month using the verified amount of support payments received.

3. If eligible, re-certify the case effective the first day of the month the case was previously closed. Completion of the application form is not required and proration of benefits does not apply.

This procedure is applicable only for the first month cash benefits are stopped. After this the client must reapply if child support payments are not received or are less than the amount budgeted.

* OFS 018 Form/Instructions Notice of Decision

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1400-FITAP-SNAP-STEP SNAP Work Requirements Document No./Name B-1410-FITAP Work Requirements Effective Date February 1, 2021

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

All work-eligible FITAP recipients are required to participate in STEP, unless good cause is granted. Referral * is automated and will occur at certification, redetermination and case change. Failure to participate will result in a STEP sanction unless good cause is determined.

Exception:

● If an applicant claims incapacity, a disability, or the need to provide care for a family member living in the home who is incapacitated or disabled, the applicant must provide verification of the incapacity, disability, or need to provide care. If the applicant is unable to provide verification or if the reason for the non-work eligible status no longer exists, the applicant/recipient must participate in STEP.

● Work-eligible recipients shall be granted a temporary exception from participation in work activities until engaged by the STEP Case Manager, also known as the STEP Coach, in the completion of a Family Assessment and Family Success Agreement.

Note: A sanctioned FITAP applicant must be manually referred to STEP in LITE in order to cure their STEP sanction while the application is pending. **

II. PROCEDURES

STEP recipients must participate in a STEP work activity as assigned by their *** * STEP ** Case Manager. ***

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

***

* There are no forms associated with this policy. **

IV. REFERENCES

LAC 67:III.1243

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1400-FITAP-SNAP-STEP SNAP Work Requirements Document No./Name B-1410-SNAP Work Registration Requirements Effective Date February 1, 2021

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

All SNAP applicants/recipients who are not exempt from work registration requirements are considered Mandatory Work Registrants (MWRs) and are required to:

● Register for work with the Louisiana Workforce Commission (LWC) by having an active Helping Individuals Reach Employment (HiRE) account before the SNAP case is certified at application and registration must be verified at redetermination. Refer to B-1430-SNAP.

***

● Comply with all other work registration requirements, which includes:

o Accepting an Offer of Employment,

o Providing Sufficient Information to Determine Employment Status or Job Availability,

o Not Voluntarily Quitting a Job, and

o Not Voluntarily Reducing Work Effort.

MWRs are ineligible if they fail or refuse to comply with the work registration requirements identified above.

***

II. PROCEDURES

There are no procedures associated with this policy.

***

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms associated with this policy.

IV. REFERENCES

7CFR 273.7(f)

LAC 67:III Subpart 3, Chapter 19, Subchapter G

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1400-FITAP-SNAP-STEP SNAP Work Requirements Document No./Name B-1420-SNAP Exemptions from Work Registration Requirements Effective Date April 1, 2025

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The following persons are exempt from work registration requirements:

1. Persons under age 16 or age 60 or older. An individual is subject to the work registration requirement beginning the month after his 16th birthday. An individual becomes exempt from the work registration requirement effective the month of his 60th birthday.

2. Persons age 16 or 17 who are not the head of the household or person 16 or 17 attending school, or enrolled in an employment-training program on at least a half-time basis.

3. Persons age 18 through 59 enrolled at least half-time in any recognized school (including high school), training program, or institution of higher education. Students enrolled at least half-time in an institution of higher education must meet the student eligibility requirements in E-260 to meet this exemption. A student will remain exempt during normal periods of class attendance, vacation, and recess if he intends to return.

Note: Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) is an accepted training program and participants who are enrolled in these programs at least half time are exempt from work requirements.

4. Parents or other household members personally providing the care of a dependent child under age 6 or an incapacitated person of any age. Verify that the person is needed to care for the incapacitated person.

Note: Verification from a medical provider must be obtained to verify the need for care for the incapacitated person.

5. Regular participants in drug or alcohol treatment and rehabilitation programs. Individuals participating in either an inpatient or outpatient drug or alcohol treatment and rehabilitation program are considered temporarily unfit for work.

6. Persons who are temporarily or permanently disabled (physically or mentally). Form SNAP 90 may be used to verify the disability.

A pregnant woman must register unless a doctor's statement verifies incapacity.

7. Persons working an average of 30 hours per week or receiving average weekly gross earnings equivalent to 30 multiplied by the federal minimum wage. Migrant and seasonal farm workers under contract or similar agreement with an employer or crew chief to begin work within 30 days are exempt.

8. Persons subject to and complying with STEP.

2 of 4 9. Persons receiving unemployment compensation benefits (UCB). A person who has applied for but is not yet receiving UCB is also exempt if that person is complying with the work requirements of the Louisiana Workforce Commission.

B-1421-SNAP - PO VERIFICATION AND DOCUMENTATION OF EXEMPTION FROM WORK REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS

LITE automatically assigns work registration status. Verify that the person is needed to provide care for an incapacitated person. Incapacity due to pregnancy complications must be verified. Verify all other exemptions only when they are questionable.

II. PROCEDURES

B-1421-SNAP - PR VERIFICATION AND DOCUMENTATION OF EXEMPTION FROM WORK REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS

LITE automatically assigns work registration status.

Listed below are the work registration statuses to be used for the appropriate exemptions from work registration requirements.

Work Registration Status Description WORKING 30 OR MORE HOURS PER WEEK AGE EXEMPTION, UNDER 18(UNDER 16 IF NOT IN SCHOOL) DISABLED (MEM DOES NOT MEET ELDERLY/DISABLED DEF) DEPENDENT CARE FOR CHILD UNDER 6 YEARS OLD REHABILITATION PROGRAM (DRUG OR ALCOHOL ADDICTION) UNEMPLOYMENT COMPENSATION STEP STUDENT/ELIGIBLE DISABLED AND NOT SSI OR VA SSI 60 YEARS OR OVER AND NOT SSI RESPONSIBLE FOR THE CARE OF AN INCAPACITATED PERSON ABAWD MEETING SNAP WORK REQUIREMENT MIGRANT FARM WORKER IN THE JOB STREAM 100% DISABLED VETERAN, DISABLED SPOUSE/CHILD OF VET

***

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1400-FITAP-SNAP-STEP SNAP Work Requirements Document No./Name B-1420-SNAP Exemptions from Work Registration Requirements Effective Date April 1, 2025

3 of 4 If an individual received UCB in the last 12 months and complied with the work requirements for UCB, that individual is exempt from work registration requirements. Work registration status ‘Unemployment Compensation’ should be used.

An individual who is enrolled at least half-time in a school (including high school) or training program that is not considered an institution of higher education is considered a student. The student is exempt from work registration requirements and must have a work registration status of ‘Student/Eligible’.

Verify that the person is needed to provide care for an incapacitated person. Verification from a medical provider must be obtained to verify the need for the incapacitated person. The Request for Verification of the Need for Full-Time Care (OFS 90L) may be used to verify if there is an incapacitated person who requires full-time care. Incapacity due to pregnancy complications must be verified. The worker's observation of an obvious disability is adequate justification for granting an exemption. If questionable, verify disability by a doctor's statement or other third party documentary evidence which supports the person's claim. The SNAP Disability Verification Form (SNAP 90) may be used.

Examples of questionable exemptions:

Example: A client reports she is disabled. She says her doctor does not want her to work. When asked what is her disability or what is the reason the doctor does not want her to work she says she is not really sure. She just knows he told her he does not want her to work. This is questionable. Verification would be needed to exempt the client.

Example: A client reports she is disabled. She says she is not able to work because of migraine headaches that she has been having for the last three years. The client stated she has never applied for disability because of her condition. Verification would be needed to exempt the client.

Example: A client reports at application that she is unable to work because she recently broke her right leg. Client is exempt due to temporary disability. At redetermination, the client reports she is unable to work because she recently broke her right leg. When questioned about previous report of breaking right leg she changes to say that it is now her left leg that is broken. The information is now questionable. Verification would be needed to exempt the client at redetermination.

Individuals participating in an approved inpatient drug or alcohol treatment program must documented on the Living Arrangement- Details screen in LITE.

Individuals regularly participating in an outpatient drug or alcohol treatment program are considered temporarily unfit for work and must be documented on the Disability screen in LITE. Outpatient drug or alcohol treatment participants must be coded as temporarily disabled with the criteria of ‘No Federal Disability’. Select the applicable verification type from the “If no criteria from above:” drop down.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1400-FITAP-SNAP-STEP SNAP Work Requirements Document No./Name B-1430-SNAP Work Registration Procedures Effective Date January 1, 2024

1 of 7 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

A * determination must be made if a household includes a Mandatory Work Registrant (MWR) at application and at redetermination. The household must be contacted to provide an oral explanation of the MWRs SNAP work registration requirements. A MWR is required to register for work before the SNAP case is certified at application and at redetermination.

Registering for work means the MWR must register for work with the Louisiana Workforce Commission (LWC) by having an active Helping Individuals Reach Employment (HiRE) account.

When a member of the household is a MWR, inform the head of household of the member's rights, responsibilities, and the consequences of failure to comply.

The following actions must be taken at every application and redetermination when the household contains a MWR:

 Advise the applicant/recipient during the interview of the SNAP work registration requirements and the consequences of a MWR failing to comply with the work registration requirements.

o The SNAP Interviewing Guide, SNAP 8, must be used to ensure all work registration requirements and consequences are explained to the household.

o Clicking on the ‘MWR Work Requirements’ link on the ‘Non-Financial – Questions’ screen navigates the worker to the DCFS intranet and the oral explanation that must be provided to the household regarding the SNAP work registration requirements. **

 Advise the applicant/recipient during the interview that registering for work with LWC must be completed to be eligible for SNAP. The work registration may be completed online at www.louisianaworks.net or at the local LWC Business and Career Solutions Center. Addresses can be found at www.laworks.net/ServiceLocator.asp. The LWC link is also available on the kiosk in each ES office. When registering for work with LWC, the MWR must click on the ‘Register for your HiRE account’ link and complete the registration process.

 Advise the applicant that if the household is eligible for expedited service and the applicant is a MWR, he must register for work with LWC by creating a HiRE account by 3:00 pm on the 7th day. Work registration for MWRs other than the applicant may be postponed. A household that is screened for expedited service and the applicant is a MWR who failed to register for work by 3:00 pm on the 7th day is not eligible for expedited service.

 Provide a Client Contact Letter (OFS 18C) and a Work Registration Requirement with Louisiana Workforce Commission (LWC) SNAP 4RW flyer to households, which contain a MWR who does not have an active HiRE account, including households that are eligible for expedited service,

2 of 7 advising of the requirement to register for work with LWC. At redetermination, a SNAP 4RW must be provided to each MWR.

The SNAP 4RW provides the MWR with information about registering for work. The deadline to register for work must be entered on the flyer.

The deadline to register for work is: o 3:00 pm on the 30th day from the application date for applications, o 3:00 pm on the last workday of the redetermination month.

A MWR must always be allowed at least 10 days to register for work with LWC from the date the household is notified of the requirement.

 Ensure that the MWR receives a * SNAP Work Requirements (SNAP 4WR) to inform the household of the MWR’s rights and responsibilities. This is an automated notice that will be mailed upon authorization of a certification/recertification in LITE.

B-1431-SNAP - PO CHANGES IN STATUS

When an individual reports a change which affects work registration status, the worker will enter the change in LITE and run eligibility on the case. LITE will update the work registration status when the case is authorized. Document changes as a case note.

B-1432-SNAP - PO LOUISIANA WORKFORCE COMMISSION – HELPING INDIVIDUALS REACH EMPLOYMENT (HIRE) ACCOUNT

Each MWR must have an active work registration in HiRE before the SNAP case is certified at application and at redetermination.

B-1433-SNAP - PO WORKER RESPONSIBILITY

The worker is responsible for contacting the household and providing an oral explanation of the SNAP work registration requirements at application and at redetermination. ** The worker’s responsibilities are outlined in B-1433-SNAP-PR.

B-1434-SNAP - PO FAILURE TO REGISTER FOR WORK WITH LWC

Failure to register for work with LWC at application, will result in the exclusion of the household member who failed to register for work.

Failure to register for work with LWC at redetermination, without good cause, will result in a SNAP work registration “Non-Compliance Violation Type’ - SNAP E&T (E&T)” sanction.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1400-FITAP-SNAP-STEP SNAP Work Requirements Document No./Name B-1430-SNAP Work Registration Procedures Effective Date January 1, 2024

3 of 7 II. PROCEDURES

B-1431-SNAP - PR CHANGES IN STATUS

If an individual reports a change which affects work registration status and all verification is provided, take action within 10 days by entering the change in LITE and running eligibility on the case. LITE will update the work registration code when the case is authorized.

If an individual becomes a MWR * or a new member is identified as a MWR, the worker must contact the household to provide an oral explanation of the MWR’s SNAP work registration requirements and the consequences of a MWR failing to comply with the work registration requirements. The oral explanation can be accessed by clicking on the ‘MWR Work Requirements’ link on the Non-Financial – Questions screen in LITE. The worker will be navigated to the DCFS intranet.

 Complete the MWR discussion by reading the oral explanation and answering ‘Yes’ to the question, “Did you discuss the MWR requirements with the household?”.

o If the MWR discussion is not completed, select ‘No’. If ‘No’ is selected to the question, a missing information warning will display on the ‘Missing Information’ page. The missing information warning is generated by LITE when eligibility is run and will not allow the case to be authorized until the missing information is cleared.

 Document successful and unsuccessful attempts to provide an oral explanation of the SNAP work registration requirements. Only one successful attempt to contact the household is required.

 Provide a Work Registration Requirement with Louisiana Workforce Commission (LWC), SNAP 4RW.

A SNAP Work Requirements (SNAP 4WR) must be sent if a household member becomes a MWR. If the work registration status ** is updated and the case is authorized, an automated *** SNAP 4WR will be sent in LITE.

B-1432-SNAP - PR LOUISIANA WORKFORCE COMMISSION – HELPING INDIVIDUALS REACH EMPLOYMENT (HIRE) ACCOUNT

In LITE, an automated interface is run to check the work registration of all MWRs in HiRE. The results are displayed in the Clearance Summary.

Staff must review the Clearance Summary to determine if the MWR is registered for work with LWC. If the HiRE account information is not displayed in the Clearance Summary, staff must use the On Demand LWC button to run the query.

4 of 7 B-1433-SNAP - PR WORKER RESPONSIBILITY * AT APPLICATION AND REDETERMINATION

The worker must determine if the household includes a MWR at application and at redetermination. The worker must run eligibility before ending the interview and review the ‘Filing Unit Summary Chart’ on the LITE ‘SNAP-Filing Unit Summary’ screen to identity which household member is a MWR so that the worker can discuss the SNAP work registration requirements.

If the household includes a MWR, the worker must:

 Discuss the SNAP work registration requirements, which includes how to register for a Helping Individuals Reach Employment (HiRE) account.  Determine if the MWR is an ABAWD.  Determine if the ABAWD is subject to the SNAP time limit.

If there is an MWR in the household, contact with the household must be made to provide an oral explanation of the MWR’s SNAP work registration requirements.

 Navigate to the ‘Non-Financial – Questions’ screen and answer ‘Yes’ to the question, “Did you discuss the MWR requirements with the household?”

 Complete the MWR discussion by reading the oral explanation and answering ‘Yes’ to the question, “Did you discuss the MWR requirements with the household?”.

o If ‘No’ is selected to the question, a missing information warning will display on the ‘Missing Information’ page. The missing information warning is generated by LITE when eligibility is run and will not allow the case to be authorized until the missing information is cleared. o To clear the missing information, click the ‘MWR Discussion Required’ link. LITE will redirect to the ‘Non-Financial Questions’ to update the answer. Staff must complete the MWR discussion, select ‘Yes’ to the question, run eligibility, and authorize the case.

 Document the case record. **

B-1433-1-SNAP - PR At Application

If all other mandatory verifications (i.e. identity verification, wage verification) are received (regular and expedited applications), except for registering for work with LWC, check Clearance Summary for compliance to determine if each MWR registered for work by having an active HiRE account. If all MWRs have registered for work, process the application.

If the household is eligible for expedited service and the applicant is a MWR and failed to register for work with LWC by 3:00 pm on the 7th day, the household loses entitlement to expedited service.

5 of 7 If the household reports an exemption for not registering for work with LWC, which is questionable, send an OFS 18C to request verification of the questionable information and allow 10 days for the household to provide the requested verification. The reason the information is questionable must be thoroughly documented.

A HiRE Task will be created in LITE for the MWR allowing 10 days to register for work with LWC. Check the Clearance Summary by completing an on-demand search on the 7th day for expedited service and on the 10th day but no later than the 30th day following the application date for other applications to determine if the MWR has registered. If the 7th or 30th day falls on a weekend or holiday, treat the next workday as the 7th or 30th day. If the applicant is a MWR and did not register for work by 3:00 pm on the 7th day for an expedited case, change the expedited SNAP case to a regular SNAP case. If the MWR did not register for work by 3:00 pm on the 30th day, exclude the household member from the SNAP case and follow procedures listed in B-1434-SNAP-PR. Certify the SNAP case with the remaining household members if all other eligibility requirements are met.

B-1433-2-SNAP - PR - At Redetermination

Prior to the redetermination interview, all cases for households that timely reapplied must be reviewed to determine if there is a MWR included in the household. If the household did not timely reapply, no further action is taken.

If the MWR has not registered for work with LWC, discuss if good cause exists during the interview. Ensure that a SNAP 4RW was previously issued.

If the household reports an exemption or good cause for not complying with LWC, which is questionable, send an OFS 18C to request verification of the questionable information and allow 10 days for the household to provide the requested verification. The reason the information is questionable must be thoroughly documented.

If the household misses the redetermination interview, contact the household to determine if good cause exists. If the household is reached, conduct the interview at that time. Refer to B-1440-SNAP for good cause determination.

If good cause does not exist for failure to register for work, the sanction must be imposed at the same time action on the redetermination is completed. A concurrent Notice of Adverse Action must be sent the same day the redetermination is processed. Follow procedures listed in B-1434 SNAP-PR.

Example: The household was interviewed for an October redetermination. Good cause did not exist for failure to register for work with LWC. The redetermination, sanction, and concurrent Notice of Adverse Action are completed on October 30th. The sanction is effective November with the new certification period.

If the redetermination is not extended due to a procedural reason and the case contains a MWR who failed to register for work with LWC and good cause does not exist, close the case the last workday of

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1400-FITAP-SNAP-STEP SNAP Work Requirements Document No./Name B-1430-SNAP Work Registration Procedures Effective Date January 1, 2024

6 of 7 the redetermination month. Send Concurrent Notice of Adverse Action to impose a sanction on all MWRs who failed to register with HiRE effective the month following the redetermination month. Follow procedures listed in B-1434 SNAP-PR.

Example: The household was interviewed for an October redetermination but failed to provide verification. The case was closed on October 31st for that reason. Good cause did not exist for failure to register for work with LWC. Concurrent Notice of Adverse Action must be sent listing the effective month of the sanction as November. The notice must indicate that the case was closed for failure to provide the required verification (listing the verification) and include the sanction for failure to register for work – HiRE.

B-1434-SNAP-PR FAILURE TO REGISTER FOR WORK WITH LWC

A sanction may only be imposed for a MWR, who failed to register for work with LWC without good cause, if the MWR is certified for SNAP when the non-compliance occurred.

If the redetermination is being extended and the case contains a MWR who failed to register for work with LWC and good cause does not exist, enter the work registration sanction using the steps below:

 Navigate to the Non-Compliance/Sanction- Questions screen. If the member has any Non- Compliance/Sanction History in LITE, this question is pre-populated to “Yes”. After clicking the ‘Next’ button on the screen, the user is navigated to the ‘Non-Compliance/Sanction Summary’ Screen and the steps are correctly stated in the policy. If the member does not have Sanction History in LITE, the user must answer “Yes” to the question. After clicking ‘Next’, the user is navigated directly to the ‘Non-Compliance-Details’ screen.

 On the ‘Non-Compliance – Details’ screen, Enter the ‘Start/Change’ Date, ‘Reported On’ Date, ‘Non-Compliance Violation Type’ - SNAP E&T, and Non-Compliance Reason - Failed to Register for Work – HiRE, and the Decision Date. Since the Violation Type is ‘SNAP E&T’, a Good Cause Status/Reason must be entered.

 Enter the ‘Good Cause Status/Reason’ as ‘No Good Cause’ and click the NEXT button.

 The ‘Non-Compliance/Sanction Summary’ screen will display the new sanction in the ‘Non- Compliance Summary’ section of the screen. The sanction will not display in the Sanction Summary section of the Non-Compliance Summary screen until Eligibility Determination is completed on the case action.
