1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Good cause must be determined by the DCFS worker.

B-1441-SNAP RESERVED

B-1442-SNAP - PO WORKER DETERMINED GOOD CAUSE

The worker determines good cause for failure to comply with work registration requirements.

Failure to comply with work registration requirements may include:

● Refusal to Accept an Offer of Employment,

● Refusal to Provide Sufficient Information to Determine Employment Status or Job Availability,

● Voluntarily Quitting a Job,

● Voluntarily Reducing Work Effort,* and **

● Failure to Register for Work with Louisiana Workforce Commission (LWC) by having an active HiRE Account,

***

Good cause exists when circumstances beyond the client's control prevent compliance with work registration requirements.

Good cause may include but is not limited to:

● Personal illness,

● Illness of another household member requiring the presence of the member,

● A household emergency, ●

● The unavailability of public or private transportation,

● The lack of adequate child care for children who have reached age 6 but are under age 12,

***

● The lack of a valid SSN, because it is required for registering for work with LWC,

2 of 4 ● Problems caused by inability of the client to speak or write English,

● Remoteness – see A-100-SNAP,

● Work demands or conditions that render continued employment unreasonable, such as working without being paid on schedule,

● Resignations which are recognized by the employer as retirement,

● Leaving one job to take another that later, because of circumstances beyond the control of the individual, does not materialize or results in employment of less than 30 hours a week or weekly earnings of less than the federal minimum multiplied by 30 hours,

● Leaving a job in which workers frequently move from one employer to another such as migrant farm labor or construction work. Circumstances exist when households apply for benefits between jobs, particularly in cases where work may not yet be available at the new job site. Even though employment at the new site has not actually begun, the quitting of the previous employment shall be considered to be with good cause if it is part of the pattern of that type of employment,

● Acceptance by the individual of other employment or enrollment of at least half-time in any recognized school, training program, or institution of higher education that requires the individual to leave present employment,

o Wages are on a piece-rate basis and the average hourly yield the employee expects to earn is less than the applicable hourly wage specified in the bullet listed above.

o As a condition of employment or continuing employment, the individual must join, resign from, or agree not to join a legitimate labor organization.

o The work offered is at a place subject to a strike or lockout at the time of the offer, unless:

o The working hours or nature of the employment interferes with the individual's religious beliefs.

The worker must determine whether good cause exists within 10 days of determining non-compliance or being notified of non-compliance.

The worker must:

● Contact the client by telephone. If the client cannot be reached by telephone, send a Client Contact Letter (OFS 18C) in CAFÉ requesting that the client contact the worker regarding the reason for non-compliance allowing the client 10 days to respond. Enter your direct telephone number on the OFS 18C. The DCFS Customer Service Center’s contact number 1-888- LAHELPU (1-888-524-3578) should not be listed. ●

● Send an OFS 18C if the client cannot be reached by telephone to discuss the reason for non- compliance.

o Check the “To request client to call” box on the OFS 18C advising the client to call the worker, and

o Indicate on the OFS 18C that DCFS is providing the client with an opportunity to explain their reason for non-compliance in order to avoid a potential sanction.

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Non-compliance and subsequent compliance are determined *** by *** the worker.

B-1451-SNAP – PO * RESERVED **

B-1452-SNAP - PO WORKER DETERMINED NON-COMPLIANCE

The worker determines non-compliance for failure to comply with *** registration requirements which include:

● Refusal to Accept an Offer of Employment,

● Refusal to Provide Sufficient Information to Determine Employment Status or Job Availability,

● Voluntarily Quitting a Job,

● Voluntarily Reducing Work Effort, and

● Failure to Register for Work with Louisiana Workforce Commission (LWC) by having an active HiRE Account at application/redetermination.

If the answer to all the questions in the applicable sections below is yes and good cause does not exist, the disqualification applies.

B-1452-1-SNAP - PO Refusal to Accept an Offer of Employment

● Is the individual subject to work registration requirements?

● Has the individual refused an offer of employment within 60 days before the application date or anytime thereafter?

● Was the offer of employment at a site or plant not subject to a strike or lockout at the time of the refusal?

● Were the wages offered at least the higher of the federal minimum wage or, if federal minimum wage is not applicable, 80% of the minimum hourly rate under the Fair Labor Standards Act?

● Did the individual refuse the offer without good cause? Refer to B-1440-SNAP.

2 of 4

B-1452-2-SNAP - PO Refusal to Provide Sufficient Information to Determine Employment Status or Job Availability

● Is the individual subject to work registration requirements?

● Has the individual refused to provide sufficient information to determine his employment status or job availability? (Failure to provide requested information does not constitute refusal).

● Was the refusal without good cause? Refer to B-1440-SNAP.

B-1452-3-SNAP - PO Voluntary Quit

● Is the individual subject to work registration requirements?

● Has the individual quit his most recent job within 60 days before the application date or anytime thereafter?

● Did the job involve 30 or more hours per week or earnings equivalent to 30 hours per week times the federal minimum wage?

● Did the individual quit the job without good cause? Refer to B-1440-SNAP.

A person is not considered to have voluntarily quit his job when:

● A self-employment enterprise ends,

● He resigns a job at the demand of an employer,

● He is currently on strike, or

● He quits a job but obtains new employment at 30 hours per week, or has earnings equivalent to 30 hours per week times the federal minimum wage.

o If the person is laid off or loses the new job through no fault of his own, disqualification for the earlier quit does not apply.

Any local, state or federal government employee who loses his job because he participates in a strike is considered to have voluntarily quit without good cause. Refer to B-1440-SNAP.

B-1452-4-SNAP - PO Voluntary Reduction in Work Effort

● Is the individual subject to work registration requirements?

● Has the individual's work effort been reduced within 60 days before the application date or anytime after?

● Did the job involve 30 or more hours per week?

● Is the individual now working less than 30 hours per week?

● Did the individual reduce his work effort without good cause? Refer to B-1440-SNAP.

A person is not considered to have voluntarily reduced his work effort if after the reduction in hours the person still has earnings equal to 30 hours per week times the federal minimum wage.

B-1452-5-SNAP - PO Failure to Register for Work with Louisiana Workforce Commission (LWC)

● Is the individual subject to work registration requirements?

● Did the individual fail to register for work with LWC without good cause at redetermination? Refer to B-1440-SNAP.

***

B-1453-SNAP - PO Compliance

***

If the non-compliance was refusal to accept an offer of employment, the individual must agree to accept a comparable offer of employment when, and if, such an offer is received.

If the non-compliance was refusal to provide sufficient information to determine employment status or job availability, the individual must provide sufficient information.

If the non-compliance was voluntary quit, the individual must agree to search for and accept a job comparable in salary or hours to the job that was quit.

If the non-compliance was voluntary reduction in work effort, the individual must agree to increase work hours to at least 30 hours per week when, and if, given the opportunity.

If the non-compliance was failure to register for work with LWC, the individual must register for work with LWC.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1400-FITAP-SNAP-STEP SNAP Work Requirements Document No./Name B-1460-SNAP Work Registration Penalties Effective Date February 1, 2021

1 of 8 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Mandatory Work Registrants (MWR’s) are ineligible if they fail to meet work registration requirements set forth in B-1410-SNAP. This includes ABAWDs and non-ABAWDs.

Length of disqualification:

● First violation - the individual will be ineligible for 1 *** month or until he complies, whichever is later.

● Second *** violation - the individual will be ineligible for 3 *** months or until he complies, whichever is later.

● * Third and subsequent violation – the individual will be ineligible for 6 months or until he complies, whichever is longer. **

Exception: Failure to register for work with LWC by creating a HiRE account at application will result in the *** exclusion of a household member instead of a disqualification. * If the MWR is the only household member, the application will be denied since there is no eligible person in the household.

At application, exclude the household member, who is a MWR, that failed to register for work with LWC by creating a HiRE account. At redetermination, disqualify the household member who is a MWR, that failed to register for work with LWC by creating a HiRE account.

Note: If the MWR becomes exempt anytime after non-compliance, the disqualification ends.

If the individual who does not comply is the head of the household, only the head of household is ineligible for the duration of the individual's disqualification. The other members of the household remain eligible. **

***

If the disqualified individual joins another household, * the disqualified individual remains ineligible for the remainder of the individual’s disqualification period. **

***

B-1461-SNAP - PO ACTION ON NON-COMPLIANCE WITH SNAP WORK REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS

*** * When the worker determines that non-compliance with work registration requirements was without good cause, review the record to determine whether the household member continues to be a MWR and whether a disqualification is appropriate.

2 of 8 ● If the household member is a MWR and good cause does not exist, enter the appropriate sanction within ten days from the date that it was determined that good cause does not exist. LITE will automatically send a Notice of Decision to the household advising of the disqualification. ● If the household member is a MWR, but met an exemption from work registration requirements after the act of non-compliance, the member should not be disqualified. ● If the household member is no longer a MWR, LITE will update the work registration code to the appropriate code.

● If an application or redetermination is not processed timely and the MWR registers for work with LWC prior to processing the application or redetermination, the member must not be excluded/disqualified.

● If the redetermination is not extended due to a procedural reason and the worker determines non-compliance and good cause does not exist, close the case the last workday of the redetermination month. Send a Concurrent Notice of Adverse Action to impose a sanction on all MWRs who failed to comply effective the month following the redetermination month.

● If a case closed (advance notice period has expired) due to a procedural reason, and good cause does not exist, another Notice of Adverse Action must be sent to impose the disqualification, however, this notice is a concurrent notice.

o If the non-compliance is failure to register for work and the household failed to timely reapply, no action is taken since the household is not requesting benefits.

● If a case is within the 13-day Advance Notice of Adverse Action period, anytime other than at redetermination due to a procedural reason, such as failure to provide verification, failure to be interviewed, failure to timely reapply, or failure to provide a complete Simplified Report, etc., and good cause does not exist, another Advance Notice of Adverse Action must be issued to impose the appropriate sanction. The disqualification period begins the month following the expiration of the new Advance Notice of Adverse Action.

● A sanction is not appropriate if the case closed or is within the 13-day advance notice period due to the household’s SNAP ineligibility. This includes but is not limited to reasons such as gross income over the limit, resources over the limit, IPV, work registration with LWC at application, disqualified due to receipt of lottery or gambling winnings equal to or greater than the elderly or disabled resource limit, etc. **

B-1462-SNAP - PO APPLYING THE DISQUALIFICATION

At application, the disqualification begins with the date of the voluntary quit, reduction in work effort or refusal of an offer of employment.

3 of 8 Prior to certification, if the agency learns that a member of the applicant’s household voluntarily quit, reduced their work effort, or refused an offer of employment after the application date, and good cause did not exist, then the individual who quit is not eligible for inclusion in the household * and must be disqualified. **

Impose a disqualification the earliest possible month for ongoing cases and cases closed due to procedural reasons. ***

EXCEPTION:

If non-compliance was not reported, not discovered timely, or the worker did not take timely action, determine when the disqualification would have been effective had it been imposed timely and good cause does not exist:

● If the disqualification period would still be in effect, impose the disqualification the first month following expiration of the Advance Notice of Adverse Action and complete a claim for the months of disqualification that were not imposed timely, or

● If the disqualification period would be over, complete a claim for the months of disqualification that were not imposed.

B-1463-SNAP - PO ENDING DISQUALIFICATION

The disqualification ends when:

● The mandatory one-* month, three-month, ** or six-month disqualification expires and the non- compliant member complies (See section B-1453-SNAP of B-1450-SNAP).

or

● The recipient becomes exempt at any point after non-compliance from work registration requirements according to B-1420-SNAP.

***

An individual can be added to the on-going certification effective the month after the disqualification ends. Follow procedures in B-1463-2 SNAP-PR.

II. PROCEDURES

B-1461-SNAP - PR ACTION ON NON-COMPLIANCE WITH SNAP WORK REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS

* If a MWR must be disqualified, follow procedures in B-1462-SNAP-PR. ** ***

4 of 8 B-1462-SNAP - PR Applying The Disqualification

B-1462-1-SNAP ** PR - At Application or Ongoing Cases

At application or an ongoing case, apply the disqualification by entering the appropriate disqualification using the steps below:

 Navigate to the Non-Compliance/Sanction- Questions screen. If the member has any Non- Compliance/Sanction History in LITE, this question is pre-populated to “Yes”. After clicking the ‘Next’ button on the screen, the user is navigated to the ‘Non-Compliance/Sanction Summary’ Screen and the steps are correctly stated in the policy. If the member does not have Sanction History in LITE, the user must answer “Yes” to the question. After clicking ‘Next’, the user is navigated directly to the ‘Non-Compliance-Details’ screen.

 On the ‘Non-Compliance – Details’ screen, Enter the ‘Start/Change’ Date, ‘Reported On’ Date, ‘Non-Compliance Violation Type’ - SNAP E&T, and Non-Compliance Reason - Failed to Register for Work – HiRE, and the Decision Date. Since the Violation Type is ‘SNAP E&T’, a Good Cause Status/Reason must be entered.

 Enter the ‘Good Cause Status/Reason’ as ‘No Good Cause’ and click the NEXT button.

 The ‘Non-Compliance/Sanction Summary’ screen will display the new sanction in the ‘Non- Compliance Summary’ section of the screen. The sanction will not display in the Sanction Summary section of the Non-Compliance Summary screen until Eligibility Determination is completed on the case action. After Eligibility Determination is run, LITE will automatically populate the Occurrence, Sanction Begin Date, and Program fields on the ‘Non- Compliance/Sanction-Summary’ screen. The sanction will be effective the month following the Expiration Date on the Notice of Decision.

LITE will automatically send a Notice of Decision to impose the sanction. If multiple household members failed to register for work, only one notice is sent.

If the client takes the required action before the Advance Notice of Adverse Action expires, disposition the change, and select ‘Y’ (Yes) to override the closure. **

***

Prior to certification, if a member of the applicant’s household voluntarily quit, reduced their work effort, or refused an offer of employment after the application date, and good cause did not exist, the individual who quit is not eligible for inclusion in the household. * Follow the steps above to apply the disqualification. **

***

B-1463-SNAP - PR ENDING DISQUALIFICATION

If the MWR complies with the work registration requirements that caused the proposed sanction by the Notice Expiration Date on the * Notice of Decision , the sanction must be removed and eligibility run on the ** case ***. If the compliance was not reported or discovered prior to the sanction becoming effective, the sanction must be removed and the case reopened, if the case was closed. 1 of 22 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

A SNAP recipient classified as an Able-Bodied Adult Without Dependents (ABAWD) can receive benefits for only three months in a 36-month period unless they meet the ABAWD work requirement or qualify for an exemption. This is the SNAP time limit.

An ABAWD is an individual who is:

• Age 18 (beginning the month after their eighteen birthday) through 64, (ending the month prior to their 65th birthday).

• Physically or mentally fit for employment,

• Not pregnant,

• Not living in a SNAP household with a child who is under age 14, even if the child is not eligible to receive SNAP benefits, and

***

In LITE, if there is an ABAWD included on the case, they will be listed on the ABAWD Summary screen. The ABAWD indicator can also be seen on the Person Summary pop up screen if you search for an individual.

Exception for Unfit for Employment

An individual who is physically or mentally unfit for employment is exempt from the SNAP time limit. Unfitness for work can include anything that affects the ability to work or maintain employment. An individual does not need to be disabled to be unfit for work. Unfitness for work may be temporary or permanent. Unfit for work means the individual may be able to work some hours but is not able to work at least 20 hours per week because of their own physical or mental condition.

An individual who is temporarily unfit for work is exempt until their next redetermination.

An individual is unfit for work if the individual:

• is receiving temporary or permanent disability benefits issued by governmental or private sources. This includes persons receiving Social Security Disability (SSA), Supplemental Security Income (SSI) due to disability, and any percentage of disability through the Veterans Administration (VA). A pending application for one of these programs qualifies an individual for this exemption.

2 of 22 The SNAP time limit does not apply to an individual receiving temporary or permanent disability issued by the government or private source. Veterans who receive VA disability compensation are considered unfit for work regardless of the veteran’s disability percentage rating.

• provides a written or verbal statement from a physician, physician’s assistant, nurse, nurse practitioner, designated representative of the physician’s office, a licensed or certified psychologist, a social worker, or other medical personnel declaring that the individual is physically or mentally unfit for employment.

• is obviously mentally or physically unfit for employment as determined by the worker.

Examples of obvious unfitness for work include but are not limited to:

▪ developmental disabilities

▪ mental illness

▪ treatment for drug addiction

▪ physical or psychological trauma experienced from domestic violence

▪ a broken bone

▪ recovering from surgery

An obvious determination of unfit for work may be made during the face-to-face or telephone interview. Documentation of obvious unfitness for work must include at least the following:

▪ The conversation the worker held with the household. Include the details of the household’s statement and the reason the statement was accepted.

▪ What observations were made by the worker e.g. cast, sling, wheelchair, behavior health issues.

▪ Why further verification was not requested.

The worker must screen to determine if any household member has something that prevents them from working 20 hours per week. This may be temporary or permanent.

If it is not obvious to the worker that someone is unfit for work, the SNAP 90, SNAP Disability Verification Form, may be used to verify this.

Refer to B-1421-SNAP-PR for how to document this in LITE.

3 of 22 Exception for Pregnant Woman

For a pregnant woman, the expected delivery/due date must be entered on the system so that the system will determine that the woman is a non-ABAWD. If the pregnancy is not obvious by worker observation, request verification of pregnancy, including the expected delivery/due date as verified by a healthcare provider.

Exception for Child Included in SNAP Household

A child who is under age 14 living in the home must be included in the SNAP filing unit to be considered included in the SNAP household. Possible reasons the child may be included in the filing unit but might not be included in the assistance unit are because of failure to provide a valid Social Security Number or verification of alien status, being an ineligible alien, etc. The child must be living in the home and purchasing and preparing meals with the SNAP household for other members of the SNAP household to be considered non-ABAWDs.

If the child lives in more than one home, the case where the child is part of the SNAP filing unit will determine if the adults in the household are considered non-ABAWDs. For example, if John and Jane share joint custody of Bob, but Jane gets SNAP for Bob, Jane will be a non-ABAWD. Even though John might get SNAP and Bob lives with John part of the time, Bob would not make John a non- ABAWD.

Exception for “Indians”, “Urban Indians” and “California Indians”

The SNAP Time Limit does not apply to Indians, Urban Indians, and California Indians as defined below.

An individual is an “Indian” if they:

• Are a member of an Indian tribe. • Indian tribe is defined as any Indian tribe, band, nation, or other organized group or community, including any Alaska Native village or group or regional or village corporation as defined in or established pursuant to the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act, which is recognized as eligible for the special programs and services provided by the United States to Indians because of their status as Indians.

An individual is an “Urban Indian”, if they:

• Reside in an urban center and meet at least one of the following four criteria: o Regardless of if they live on or near a reservation, are a member of a tribe, band, or other organized group of Indians, including those tribes, bands, or groups terminated since 1940 and those recognized now or in the future by the State in which they reside, or who is a descendant, in the first or second degree of any such member;

An individual is a “California Indian”, if they:

• Are a member of a federally recognized Indian tribe; • Are a descendant of an Indian who was residing in California on June 1, 1852, if such descendant— o Is a member of the Indian community served by a local program of the Indian Health Service; and o Is regarded as an Indian by the community in which such descendant lives; o Are an Indian who holds trust interests in public domain, national forest, or reservation allotments in California; or o Are an Indian of California who is listed on the plans for distribution of the assets of rancherias and reservations located within the State of California under the Act of August 18, 1958, and any descendant of such an Indian.

Document the individual’s statement of Indian, Urban Indian or California Indian and any details provided about a specific tribe affiliation. Discuss what documentary evidence is available to verify the affiliation and request verification.

Verification options are: • Tribal Membership or Enrollment Card • Certificate of Degree of Indian Blood (CDIB) • Documentation or letter of Tribal Affiliation • Membership in a local Urban Indian Organization (UIO) or other community group • Calindian Documentation • Native American Tribal Document • Documentation from the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) • Tribal census roll / tribal enrollment records • Indian Health Service (IHS) or tribal health services documents/records • Signed Statement or Self-attestation of tribal affiliation

5 of 22 B-1471-SNAP - PO SNAP TIME CLOCK PERIOD

LDH uses a universal fixed time clock for SNAP time-limited benefits. The 36-month SNAP time clock period begins and ends on the same date for all individuals. The SNAP time clock period begins April 1, 2023 and ends March 31, 2026. The next SNAP time clock period will begin April 1, 2026 and end March 31, 2029.

Months from other states that have implemented the SNAP time limit for ABAWDs are countable when they occur during the applicable fixed SNAP time clock period.

B-1472-SNAP - PO WHEN THE SNAP TIME LIMIT DOES NOT APPLY

The SNAP time limit does not apply in any month in which the ABAWD:

• Received prorated benefits.

• Is exempt from SNAP work registration requirements for a reason other than age in accordance with section B-1420-SNAP.

• Meets the ABAWD work requirement. Refer to B-1472-1-SNAP.

• Resided in a parish that was waived from the SNAP time limit. Refer to section B-1490-SNAP.

• Was granted a discretionary exemption prior to October 1, 2024. Refer to B-1472-2-SNAP-PO.

B-1472-1-SNAP - PO Meeting the ABAWD Work Requirement

An ABAWD meets the ABAWD work requirement by fulfilling any of the following:

• Working an average of at least 20 hours per week. Work may be paid, unpaid (volunteer), or for in-kind services (work in exchange for goods or services).

• Participating for an average of at least 20 hours per week and complying with the requirements of any training program under the SNAP Employment and Training (E&T) program, the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) (formerly the Workforce Investment Act – WIA), any program under section 236 of the Trade Act of 1974, or any program of employment and training for veterans operated by the Department of Labor of the Department of Veterans Affairs that serves veterans.

• Any combination of working and participating in a training program described above for an average of at least 20 hours per week.

6 of 22 NOTE: For the purpose of the ABAWD work requirement, an average of at least 20 hours per week means a minimum of 80 hours per month.

Work registration of ‘ABAWD meeting SNAP Work Requirement’ in LITE must be used for any month that the ABAWD meets the ABAWD work requirement to ensure that the month will not count in the SNAP time limit.

An ABAWD subject to the SNAP time limit must report when the ABAWD is no longer working or participating in a training program for an average of less than 20 hours per week or 80 hours monthly. This change must be reported by the 10th of the month following the month in which the change occurred.

B-1472-1-1 SNAP - PO Unpaid Work (Volunteers)

Unpaid work must be at a recognized business or at a private, public, or non-profit organization in order for volunteer hours to count towards meeting the ABAWD work requirement.

The following are not allowable as unpaid work for volunteers:

• Volunteering in a private home, unless a bona fide business is operated from the home.

• Volunteering which would benefit a LDH employee or his immediate family.

• Volunteering which would result in an ABAWD receiving direct supervision from a relative.

The volunteer work must be verified with the business or organization prior to determining if the volunteer hours will count toward the ABAWD work requirement. The Verification of ABAWD Volunteer Hours (ABAWD 6) may be used to verify the number of volunteer hours expected to work and to verify past volunteer hours worked. Verification of volunteer hours is required at application, Simplified Report, redetermination, when a change is reported in volunteer work, and when questionable.

B-1472-1-2-SNAP - PO Good Cause

An ABAWD who has been meeting the ABAWD work requirement by participating an average of 20 hours per week (80 hours per month) may be granted good cause if the ABAWD is not meeting the ABAWD work requirement in certain instances. Good cause includes circumstances beyond the individual’s control, such as, but not limited to, illness, illness of another household member requiring the presence of the member, a household emergency, the unavailability of transportation, or natural disaster.

If an ABAWD, who was meeting the ABAWD work requirement would have participated an average of 20 hours per week (80 hours per month) but missed some of the activity because of good cause, the

7 of 22 individual shall be considered to have met the ABAWD work requirement if the absence from the activity is temporary and the individual retains his or her job/enrollment in the activity. The key to determining good cause is to establish that it is only a temporary situation and the ABAWD retains the job or enrollment in the activity.

EXAMPLE: Lisa is an ABAWD who is working the required 20 hours per week. For the month of June, she worked 60 hours. However, Lisa’s car is being repaired and she is unable to work any hours for the month of July. Lisa would be allowed good cause for June and July since she is still employed, but due to her car being repaired she is temporarily unable to work.

EXAMPLE: Jesse is an ABAWD who is working the required 20 hours per week. In the month of June, Jesse worked 60 hours because his car was repossessed and he lost his job. Jesse reported this July 1. Jesse is unable to work since he has no transportation to work. Jesse would not be allowed good cause since he has lost his job. Since Jesse met the work requirement for part of June, that month is not considered a countable month because it would not be a full month of benefits without meeting the work requirement. July will be a countable month.

B-1472-2-SNAP - PO Discretionary Exemptions

The agency was allotted a certain number of discretionary exemptions each year that were used so that a month did not count towards the SNAP time limit. These exemptions were automatically tracked using work registration ‘Discretionary Exemption’ to ensure that the State does not exceed the allowable number of exemptions available.

Effective October 1, 2024, discretionary exemptions are no longer allowed due to Act 308 of 2024 Louisiana Legislative Session.

B-1472-3-SNAP- PO Temporary Exemptions due to the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023

The Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 provided three temporary exemptions to the SNAP time limit, beginning September 1, 2023. The three temporary exemptions were being a veteran, homeless, and 24 years old and aged out of foster care.

Effective November 1, 2025, the three exemptions are no longer allowed due to passage of the Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025.

B-1473-SNAP - PO SUBSEQUENT ELIGIBILITY

B-1473-1-SNAP - PO Regaining Eligibility

If an ABAWD was denied eligibility because he received three countable months and was subject to the SNAP time limit, the ABAWD may regain eligibility if he meets one of the requirements listed below. There is no limit to the number of times an ABAWD may regain eligibility.

8 of 22

An ABAWD who is subject to the SNAP time limit may regain eligibility if, during any consecutive 30-day period after the ABAWD became ineligible due to the SNAP time limit, the ABAWD:

• Worked 80 or more hours, or

• Participated for 80 hours or more and complied with any program under SNAP Employment and Training, WIOA, any program under section 236 of the Trade Act of 1974, or a program of employment and training for veterans operated by the Department of Labor or the Department of Veterans Affairs that serves veterans, or

• Did any combination of working and participating in a training program described above for 80 hours or more.

For applications, if the ABAWD regains eligibility through one of the above actions, eligibility begins on the application date. The ABAWD is not required to regain eligibility prior to the application date but must regain eligibility prior to being certified. As long as the ABAWD regains eligibility within 30 days from the application date, the case may be certified if otherwise eligible upon receiving proof that the ABAWD regained eligibility. If verification of regaining eligibility is not received by the due date on the request, the application may be rejected the day following the due date. If verification is provided, the application must be reopened following policy at C-638-SNAP.

For on-going cases, the ABAWD must be added back to the household effective the month after the household reported that the ABAWD regained eligibility and the verification was received by the due date given on the request for verification. Allow the household 10 days to provide the required verification. If the 10th day falls on a weekend or holiday, the due date becomes the following workday. If verification is not received by the due date, the ABAWD must be added to the household effective the month following the month that the verification was received.

If an ABAWD regains and maintains eligibility, refer to B-1473-2-SNAP-PO.

If an ABAWD regains eligibility but is not maintaining eligibility and has not already received the one- time three-month extension during the SNAP time clock period, refer to B-1473-3-SNAP-PO.

If an ABAWD regains eligibility but is not maintaining eligibility and has already used the one-time three-month extension during the SNAP time clock period, the ABAWD is not eligible.

B-1473-1-1-SNAP - PO Expedited Applications

If an application eligible for expedited service includes an ABAWD, verification that the ABAWD has already met the ABAWD work requirement to regain eligibility may be postponed.

B-1473-2-SNAP - PO Maintaining Eligibility

An ABAWD who regains eligibility under section B-1473-1-SNAP will remain eligible as long as the SNAP time limit does not apply as described in B-1472-SNAP.

When an ABAWD regains and maintains eligibility, the ABAWD must be allowed 30 days to provide verification of working/participating in training at least 80 hours within a 30-day period. The case must be allowed to pend for verification for 30 days from the application date. The work registration status must be ‘ABAWD meeting SNAP Work Requirement’ once verification is received.

EXAMPLE: Julie is an ABAWD who received three countable months of SNAP benefits and her case closed effective January due to no longer meeting the ABAWD work requirement. Julie reapplied for SNAP benefits on March 2. She reported that she started a new job on February 15, works 25 hours per week and has already worked 50 hours. By March 16, Julie worked an additional 50 hours. Julie must be allowed 30 days to provide verification of working 80 hours within a 30-day period. On March 20, Julie provided verification that she has worked 80 hours during a 30-day period. Julie has regained eligibility by working 80 hours and is maintaining eligibility by continuing to work at least an average of 20 hours per week. Julie’s work registration status must be updated ‘ABAWD meeting SNAP Work Requirement’.

B-1473-3-SNAP - PO One-Time Three-Month Extension During a 36-Month Period

An ABAWD who regained eligibility under section B-1473-1-SNAP but is no longer maintaining eligibility becomes ineligible because of the SNAP time limit. However, the ABAWD will be eligible for a one-time three-month extension and will remain eligible for a period of three consecutive months. The three consecutive months of eligibility begins the month following the month that the ABAWD stopped meeting the ABAWD work requirement. Work registration status ‘Regained eligibility – (ABAWD) eligible for Three Consecutive Months Only’ must be used to identify that the ABAWD used the three-month extension.

Example: Amanda received three countable months of benefits and her case was closed. In August, Amanda reapplied for benefits and was meeting the ABAWD work requirement. Amanda worked 30

B-1474-SNAP - PO FAILURE TO MEET THE ABAWD WORK REQUIREMENT

An ABAWD who is subject to the SNAP time limit and does not meet the ABAWD work requirement must have the work registration status ‘ABAWD (No waiver)’ or ‘Striker/ABAWD (No waiver)’. B-1475-SNAP – PO TRACKING ABAWD PARTICIPATION

Changes in household circumstances that occur after the household is certified can affect a household member’s ABAWD eligibility. A household member who was not subject to the time limit when the household was certified may later become subject to the SNAP time limit during the certification period or vice-versa. When it is discovered, after the fact that a month for a member was coded incorrectly, the individual’s SNAP time clock may be required to be updated to reflect the correct circumstances. A non-countable month may only be updated to a countable month if the ABAWD was notified about the ABAWD work requirement and SNAP time limit during the current certification period by issuance of the SNAP 4WR that includes the ABAWD work requirement page. If the ABAWD was not notified by being issued a SNAP 4WR, non-countable months must not be changed to countable. A case note must be made when changes are made to the tracking of ABAWD participation. As long as the ABAWD was properly notified of the ABAWD work requirement, the following apply:

• If the ABAWD failed to timely report he was no longer working or participating in training an average of 20 hours per week (80 hours per month), the month following the month the ABAWD no longer met the ABAWD work requirement must updated to reflect as not meeting the ABAWD work requirement. Any ineligible benefits must be recovered.

• If a non-reportable change occurred that resulted in a household member becoming an ABAWD or the ABAWD is now subject to the SNAP time limit, the month following the month that the ABAWD no longer met the ABAWD work requirement must be updated as not meeting the ABAWD work requirement ineligible benefits must not be completed due to a non-reportable change.

• If the worker made a mistake when coding the ABAWD and the ABAWD was not meeting the ABAWD work requirement, the months must be updated as not meeting the ABAWD work requirement. Any ineligible benefits must be recovered.

Follow procedures in B-1476-SNAP-PR CASE PROCESSING AT APPLICATION AND REDETERMINATION.

The 36-month period will be documented automatically in LITE. When a household member becomes an ABAWD or a new household member who is an ABAWD moves into the home, an oral explanation of the ABAWD work requirement and SNAP time limit are required to be provided to the household.

Follow procedures in B-1477-SNAP-PR SIMPLIFIED REPORTING (SR), CHANGES, VERIFICATION, AND DOCUMENTATION.

B-1478-SNAP - PO DISQUALIFICATIONS

The agency disqualifies an ABAWD for failure to meet the ABAWD work requirement when he has received three countable months of SNAP benefits within the SNAP time clock period. This is done automatically in LITE.

If an ABAWD fails to meet the ABAWD work requirement and is subject to the SNAP time limit, has received three countable months of SNAP benefits within the SNAP time clock period, LITE will run an automated mass update on the 10th of the third countable month that will disqualify the ABAWD from the case or close the case if the ABAWD is the only household member. The mass update will send an Advance Notice of Adverse Action to advise the ABAWD that effective the following month, the ABAWD is being disqualified or the case is being closed if the ABAWD is the only household member.

EXAMPLE: Amy is an ABAWD who submits an application on May 13 and is the only household member. Amy has never received SNAP benefits, is subject to the SNAP time limit, and is not meeting the ABAWD work requirement. The case was certified on May 28. Work registration status ‘ABAWD (No Waiver)’ was used when certifying the case. Amy is eligible to receive three full months of SNAP benefits for June, July, and August. May is a partial month, so it is not countable. A task will be sent to the worker to review the case on August 1st. If there are no changes made to the case, on August 10th when the automated mass update is run, the Eligibility Summary will show the case as closed for September. An Advance Notice of Adverse Action is automatically sent to the household advising the case is being closed because Amy received SNAP benefits for three months during the SNAP time clock period without meeting the ABAWD work requirement.

The same appeal rights that apply to all households also apply to an ABAWD who is being disqualified for not meeting the ABAWD work requirement. Refer to Chapter 7, K-210.

If the household reports that an ABAWD is meeting the ABAWD work requirement during the Advance Notice of Adverse Action (NOAA) period and provides the verification, the disqualification must be removed.

If the household reports that an ABAWD is meeting the ABAWD work requirement and provides the verification that the ABAWD is meeting the ABAWD work requirement after the expiration of the NOAA period and the ABAWD is:

• the only household member, the ABAWD must reapply. Policy at C-638-SNAP does not apply in this situation.

• a household member, the disqualified member must be added back to the case the following month.

B-1479- SNAP - PO AUTOMATIC UPDATES

LITE is programmed to make several automated updates. Refer to B-1479-SNAP-PR Automatic Updates.

II. PROCEDURES

LITE will automatically determine a member’s ABAWD status based on information obtained about the household composition, the member’s age, disability, unfitness, pregnancy status, and exemptions to SNAP work registration requirements. If there is an ABAWD in the household, the ABAWD will be listed on the ABAWD Summary screen. The ABAWD Indicator is also displayed on the Person Summary pop-up screen.

The pregnancy question is mandatory for all cases on the Household - Questions screen. If the worker selects ‘Yes’ to Pregnancy on the Household Individuals - Questions page, the Pregnancy – Details screen is queued to enter pregnancy details. If the pregnancy is not obvious by worker observation, request verification of pregnancy, including the expected delivery/due date as verified by a healthcare provider.

B-1471-SNAP - PR SNAP TIME CLOCK PERIOD

LITE automatically tracks the SNAP time clock period for each ABAWD. The ABAWD Clock screen in LITE is used to provide a summary of the ABAWD time clock for each ABAWD. The screen is automatically updated when the Benefit Issuance batch job is run. This screen displays the benefit month, the work registration status, whether a manual override has been applied and the override reason, countable months received in another state, and the verification used. The ABAWD period displayed indicates the SNAP time clock period. The ABAWD Summary displays the countable months used toward the SNAP time limit.

B-1472-SNAP - PR WHEN THE SNAP TIME LIMIT DOES NOT APPLY

LITE tracks month when the SNAP time limit does not apply to ensure that those months are not counted in the SNAP time limit.

B-1472-1-SNAP - PR Meeting the ABAWD Work Requirement

Ensure work registration status ‘ABAWD meeting SNAP Work Requirement’ in LITE is entered timely for each month the ABAWD meets the ABAWD work requirement.

B-1473-SNAP - PR SUBSEQUENT ELIGIBILITY

B-1473-1-SNAP - PR Regaining Eligibility

At application, if the ABAWD regains eligibility through one of the actions outlined in B-1473-1-SNAP- PO, eligibility begins on the application date. The ABAWD is not required to regain eligibility prior to the application date. If the ABAWD regains eligibility within 30 days from the application date, the case may be certified, if otherwise eligible, upon receiving proof that the ABAWD regained eligibility. If verification of regaining eligibility is not received by the due date on the request, the application may be rejected the day following the due date. If verification is provided, the application must be reopened following policy at C-638-SNAP.

EXAMPLE: Kim is an ABAWD who received three countable months of SNAP benefits and her case closed effective May due to no longer meeting the ABAWD work requirement. Kim reapplied for SNAP benefits on October 2. Kim reported that she started a new job on September 15, works 25 hours per week and has already worked 50 hours. By October 16, Kim worked an additional 50 hours. Kim must be allowed 30 days to provide verification of working 80 hours within a 30-day period. On October 20, Kim provided verification that she has worked 80 hours during a 30-day period. Therefore, Kim regained eligibility by working 80 hours.

For on-going cases, add the ABAWD to the household effective the month after the household reported that the ABAWD regained eligibility and the verification was received by the due date given on the request for verification. Allow the household 10 days to provide the required verification. If the 10th day falls on a weekend or holiday, the due date becomes the following workday.

If the ABAWD regained eligibility by working, the worker must complete the Earned Income – Details screen and Earned Income – Payments screen with the ABAWD’s employment details and select ’Pending Verification’ as the verification type. After the worker runs eligibility a Request for Verification (OFS 18C) is automatically generated to request verification that the ABAWD has worked 80 hours in a 30-day period.

B-1476-SNAP - PR CASE PROCESSING AT APPLICATION AND REDETERMINATION

The worker must determine if the household includes an ABAWD at application and redetermination. An automated notice, SNAP 4WR will be automatically sent to the household that contains an ABAWD who is a mandatory work registrant. This form is sent upon certification, SR, change report, and recertification to provide information concerning the SNAP time limit for ABAWDs.

The ABAWD Interviewing Guide (ABAWD 3) may be used during the SNAP interview to assist the worker in determining whether the household includes an ABAWD and if the ABAWD is exempt from the SNAP time limit.

If the household includes an ABAWD, the worker must:

• Discuss the SNAP time limit with the household,

• Discuss the ABAWD work requirement with the household,

• Advise the household that the ABAWD must report a change in the number of hours worked or participating in training if the change results in the ABAWD working or participating in training an average of less than 20 hours per week, and

• Determine if the ABAWD is subject to the SNAP time limit.

• Verify the number of countable months SNAP benefits were received in another state during the SNAP time clock period.

B-1477-SNAP – PR SIMPLIFIED REPORTING (SR), CHANGES, VERIFICATION, AND DOCUMENTATION At SR and CR, when a new member is identified as being an MWR and/or ABAWD, staff must contact the household to provide an oral explanation of the SNAP work registration requirements and/or the ABAWD work requirement and SNAP time limit.

• Verify changes, if required or questionable.

• Document all changes in LITE.

• Document successful and unsuccessful attempts to provide an oral explanation of the SNAP work registration requirements and/or the ABAWD work requirement.

o Only one unsuccessful attempt to contact the household is required.

Staff must also discuss the following with the household:

• The SNAP time limit.

• The ABAWD work requirement.

• The ABAWD reporting requirement.

Staff must determine the ABAWD status for all household members. If there is an ABAWD in the household, determine if the ABAWD is subject to the SNAP time limit or meeting the ABAWD work requirement and request verification.

MWRs and ABAWDs

The questions “Did you discuss the MWR requirements with the household?” on the LITE ‘Non- Financial – Questions’ screen and “Did you discuss the ABAWD work requirements and SNAP time limit with the Household?” on the LITE ‘ABAWD – Details’ screen may be answered ‘No’. Unlike at application and redetermination, ‘No’ may be a valid answer at SR and CR because the worker may be unable to reach the household in order to complete the discussion.

B-1477-1-SNAP – PR ABAWD Reports Now Meeting the ABAWD Work Requirement or Becomes a Non-ABAWD

If a household reports that an ABAWD is not subject to the SNAP time limit or becomes a non- ABAWD, the worker must request verification of the change allowing 10 days to provide the verification. The change must be verified before action may be taken. Due to Simplified Reporting, if verification is not provided, no further action must be taken. The case must not be closed for failure to provide verification.

If the household reports the birth of a baby and there is another household member who is an ABAWD and is currently excluded from the case, the ABAWD becomes a non-ABAWD. Due to Simplified Reporting, no additional questions need to be asked about the member who became a non-ABAWD. Once the newborn is added to the case, eligibility must be run again and the case must be authorized. The household member will be included back in the case and their ABAWD Indicator status will be updated to No.

EXAMPLE: The SNAP household consists of an ABAWD and his pregnant sister. The ABAWD is excluded. The household reports the birth of his sister’s baby. When the baby is added to the SNAP case, the ABAWD becomes a non-ABAWD.

B-1477-2-SNAP – PR HOUSEHOLD MEMBER BECOMES AN ABAWD

If a household reports a change that results in a household member becoming an ABAWD, such as when the only child moved out of the home, the member is no longer disabled, a pregnant woman had a miscarriage or still birth, or when a child turns 18, follow the procedures listed below.

• Discuss the SNAP time limit with the household.

• Discuss the ABAWD work requirement with the household.

• Discuss the ABAWD reporting requirement with the household.

• Determine the ABAWD status for all household members.

If there is an ABAWD in the household, determine if the ABAWD is subject to the SNAP time limit or meeting the ABAWD work requirement and request verification.

B-1478-SNAP - PR DISQUALIFICATIONS

The household has appeal rights for an ABAWD who is included in a SNAP household. If the household appeals the decision and indicates they wish to continue to receive SNAP benefits because the ABAWD has been removed or the case has closed after the ABAWD has received three countable months of SNAP benefits, update the ABAWD – Clock screen for the countable months using work registration status ‘ABAWD Meeting SNAP Work Requirement’ until the hearing is complete. A comment must be entered on any month updated to document the pending Fair Hearing Decision.

If the household reports that an ABAWD is meeting the ABAWD work requirement during the Advance Notice of Adverse Action (NOAA) period and provides the verification, update the ABAWD’s work registration on the ABAWD details screen.

If it is determined that an ABAWD is not meeting the ABAWD work requirement, at application, Simplified Reporting (SR), redetermination, or interim change follow procedures at B-1476-SNAP-PR.

B-1479- SNAP - PR AUTOMATIC UPDATES

A batch update will identify an individual not previously identified as an MWR and/or ABAWD when it is not at application, SR, or redetermination. LITE will automatically mail the SNAP Work Requirements (SNAP 4WR) to the household and create a task. The task is to remind the worker to contact the household to provide the oral explanation of the SNAP work registration requirements, the ABAWD work requirement, and the SNAP time limit.

1 of 5 Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B. – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1400 FITAP-SNAP-STEP SNAP Work Requirements Document No./Name B-1480-SNAP SNAP Employment & Training Effective Date June 1, 2023

I. STATEMENT OF POLICY * All SNAP recipients who are at least 16 years of age and not in school, or are unemployed or underemployed (earning less than 20 hours per week at minimum wage), and are interested and willing to participate in gaining employment and training skills are eligible to participate in the SNAP Employment &Training (E&T) Program.

At application and redetermination each household member must be screened for eligibility to participate in the SNAP E&T Program. Each eligible member must be offered the opportunity to volunteer to participate in the SNAP E&T Program.

The household must be informed of the SNAP E&T rights and responsibilities of volunteer participants:

 The SNAP E&T Program is a free program that helps SNAP recipients gain skills, training, work or experience to get a job or get a better job.

 Participants with the SNAP E&T Program can receive reimbursements such as transportation, childcare, and supportive services such as clothing, uniforms, equipment, books, supplies, and tools.

 SNAP benefits are not affected when volunteer participants stop participating or choose not to participate with the SNAP E&T Program.

 More information on the SNAP E&T Program can be found by visiting the DCFS website at www.dcfs.louisana.gov/page/snap-et.

Each volunteer SNAP recipient must be referred to the SNAP E&T Program model they select. The participant may select more than one model of interest. A participant will only be referred to the second choice model if they are not enrolled in their first choice model because it is not available or the SNAP E&T provider determines they are not a good fit. Referrals are sent when the individual is authorized to receive SNAP benefits.

The SNAP E&T provider will initiate the enrollment process by contacting the participant to schedule an appointment (virtual or in-person), completing an assessment with the participant to determine if the participant meets the E&T provider’s specific program criteria and identify barriers for participant reimbursements, scheduling orientation, completing an employment plan, and completing the E&T component placement.

If an individual contacts a SNAP E&T provider directly for services, the provider will present the participant with an overview of their program and SNAP E&T services, as well as SNAP E&T availability. The SNAP E&T provider will obtain consent to participate and determine if the participant is receiving SNAP benefits. If the participant is currently receiving SNAP benefits, the SNAP E&T provider will assess the participant and notify the eligibility worker to screen for E&T appropriateness.

If a SNAP E&T provider determines that a volunteer is not a good fit for the organization, a notice providing the determination and explaining the next steps to be taken must be sent within 10 days. The notice must inform the participant that SNAP benefits are not affected as a result of the determination and to contact the agency if they have any questions regarding the determination or continued participation in the SNAP E&T Program.

If the volunteer contacts the agency regarding continuing SNAP E&T participation, the household member must be re-screened and appropriate referrals must be completed.

II. PROCEDURES

B-1481-SNAP – PR WORKER RESPONSIBILITY

The SNAP 8 – SNAP Interviewing Guide must be reviewed at each application and redetermination interview to assist in ensuring that all requirements are met.

At each application and redetermination, the worker must:

 Inform the household of the SNAP E&T rights and responsibilities of volunteer participants.

 Screen all household members for eligibility to participate in the SNAP E&T Program.

 Offer each eligible individual the opportunity to volunteer to participate in the SNAP E&T Program.

 Review the program models available with the household to identify the program model(s) of interest to each eligible volunteer.

 Inform the household that someone from the SNAP E&T Program will contact the volunteer.

 Enter all screening and referral information for each individual in LITE.

When appropriate, the worker must:

 Notify the participant of SNAP E&T Provider assignment terminations. **

 Re-screen and make appropriate referrals for volunteers who contact the SNAP E&T provider directly for services or who contact the agency regarding continued participation in the SNAP E&T Program.

All case actions must be documented in LITE.

B-1481-1-SNAP – PR SCREENING AND REFERRAL

SNAP E&T screening and referral are completed in LITE. To document SNAP E&T screening and

If the participant is currently receiving SNAP benefits, a Task will be generated in LITE notifying the eligibility worker of the need to screen the participant for E&T appropriateness. Upon receipt of the Task notification, contact the participant, complete SNAP E&T screening, and make all appropriate referrals through a Change Report or as part of the Simplified Reporting process in LITE.

B-1482-3-SNAP – PR SNAP E&T PROVIDER ASSIGNMENT TERMINATION – INAPROPRIATE REFERRALS

If the SNAP E&T provider determines that a participant is not a good fit for their program, a Task is generated in LITE notifying the SNAP eligibility worker of the determination. Upon receipt of this Task notification, send the participant a semi-automated 18C-FF Client Contact Letter stating:

“This notice is to inform you that the SNAP E&T provider, has completed your assessment and determined that the program offered is not appropriate for you. Your benefits will not stop as a result of this determination. If you have any questions regarding this determination or continued participation in the SNAP E&T Program, please contact me at the number below, or by calling 1-888- LAHELPU (1-888-524-3578).”

If the volunteer contacts the agency regarding continuing SNAP E&T participation, the household member must be re-screened and appropriate referrals must be completed. Re-screen the participant and make any appropriate SNAP E&T referrals though a Change Report or as part of the Simplified Reporting process in LITE.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 - Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B - Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1500 Parenting Skills Document No./Name B-1510-FITAP Parenting Skills Training Effective Date March 1, 2023

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The purpose of the Parenting Skills Training Program is to provide parenting skills education to FITAP applicants and recipients who are pregnant or have a child under age one, unless they satisfactorily participated in the training during the pregnancy for that child.

***

* A parent or pregnant woman may postpone participation in Parenting Skills Training for good cause reasons, such as conflicts with work or training schedules, personal family illness, etc. Once good cause is established, the parent or pregnant woman is not required to participate in Parenting Skills Training unless the good cause reason ceased to exist prior to the child’s first birthday.

Parents participating in Parenting Skills Training when their child turns age one are not required to complete the training. However, the parent(s) should be encouraged to complete the training.

Parents sanctioned for failure to participate in Parenting Skills Training are not required to cure the sanction if the youngest child has turned age one since the sanction was imposed.

II. PROCEDURES

If it is not the client’s first pregnancy or first child, and the client has completed the current Parenting Skills Training, participation may be allowed in other work activities instead of Parenting Skills Training, if deemed appropriate by the STEP Coach.

In work-eligible families, participation in this activity is a primary work activity under the Family Success Agreement. Work-eligible recipients with children under age one are not considered exempt from participation in this work activity. Work-eligible recipients who fail to participate in these activities and do not have good cause shall be subject to a STEP sanction for non-participation and shall be considered to be out of compliance with the Family Success Agreement.

For families that are not work-eligible, failure to participate without good cause will result in case closure for at least one month and until the recipient complies, whichever is later.

Parenting Skills Training requirements will be monitored by the STEP Coach. Participation in Parenting Skills Training must be documented in person notes and activity hours entered in LITE.

If needed, child care and transportation shall be provided to the clients participating in Parenting Skills Training.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms or instructions associated with this policy.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-1700-FITAP Time-Limited Benefits Document No./Name B-1710-FITAP Time Limits Effective Date January 1, 2023

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Each FITAP client who is a parent included in the assistance unit, may receive cash assistance for no more than 24 months in a 60-month period. In addition, each FITAP client, who is a parent or other caretaker relative, or the spouse of the parent or caretaker relative, who is included in the assistance unit, may receive cash assistance for a total of 60 months in a lifetime.

***

B-1711-FITAP - PO APPLICATION OF THE TIME-LIMIT POLICY

The entire family is ineligible to receive cash benefits, unless granted an extension as described in *** B-1740-FITAP, if:

● the parent (including a legal stepparent), or either parent in a two-parent family, has received cash benefits for a total of 24 months of the prior 60 months, or

● the assistance unit, that includes a parent or other caretaker relative (or spouse of the parent or other caretaker relative), has received cash benefits for a total of 60 months.

A minor parent who receives benefits as a child is not considered a parent for purposes of applying either the 24-month or 60-month time-limit policy.

A minor parent who is not a dependent child is subject to both the 24-month and 60-month time-limit policy.

Months of receipt of benefits prior to January 1997 are not counted toward the time-limit.

The months of receipt of benefits need not be consecutive.

B-1712-FITAP - PO VERIFICATION

Exemptions or extensions to this provision must be verified as necessary.

B-1713-FITAP - PO DOCUMENTATION

Document *** extension * determinations ** to the 24-month time-limit and the 60-month lifetime-limit * in the LITE system. ES staff must document the rationale for the extension approval or denial in LITE case notes. WD STEP staff must document the rationale for the extension approval or denial in LITE person notes.

B-1714-FITAP – PO OFFICE RESPONSIBILITIES

There is no statement of policy.

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Each FITAP client who is a parent included in the assistance unit may receive cash assistance for no more than 24 months in a 60-month period, unless granted an extension as described in B-1740- FITAP.

B-1721-FITAP - PO COUNTING THE 24 MONTHS

In determining months which count toward the 24-month time-limit, * LITE will ** count all months of receipt of FITAP benefits in Louisiana in which:

● the parent (including a legal stepparent) is included in the assistance unit, or

● no cash benefits are paid because of the "less than $10 deficit rule".

* LITE will ** not count months in which:

● the disability or incapacity of the parent has been established in accordance with section C-1510- FITAP , or

● the parent has earned income and is eligible to receive the $900 time-limited deduction in accordance with B-650-FITAP, section B-651-3-FITAP. This applies only to months after June 1999 in which the $900 deduction was allowed.

Note: Any month in which an exemption is granted is not considered as a month of receipt of benefits when counting months of benefits for the 24-month time limit.

B-1722-FITAP - PO RESERVED

***

B-1723-FITAP - PO 24-MONTH FAMILY TRANSITION

* For FITAP intake applications and FITAP ineligible alien cases: **

In the twenty-second month, during normal case * maintenance** activities, * an ** assessment should occur by asking questions about the family’s situation to determine if there are extenuating circumstances that might warrant an extension. The * DCFS ** worker must not create the perception that an extension is automatic.

B-1724-FITAP – PO RESERVED

***

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Each FITAP client who is a parent or other caretaker relative (or the spouse of a parent or other caretaker relative) included in the assistance unit may receive cash assistance for a total of 60 months in a lifetime unless the criteria to be granted an extension is met as described in B-1740- FITAP.

B-1731-FITAP - PO COUNTING THE 60 MONTHS

In determining months which count toward the 60-month time-limit, * LITE counts ** all months in which:

● the parent or other caretaker relative, or the spouse of the parent or other caretaker relative, has received TANF cash benefits in any state, including those months when no benefits are paid because of the "less than $10 deficit rule", and

● the parent or other caretaker relative, or the spouse of the parent or other caretaker relative, is included in the assistance unit.

B-1732-FITAP - PO RESERVED

***

B-1733-FITAP - PO 60-MONTH TRANSITION

In the fifty-eighth month, during normal case * maintenance ** activities, assess the client’s family to determine the need for continuation of benefits. The assessment should occur by asking questions about the family’s situation to determine if there are extenuating circumstances that might warrant an extension. The worker must not create the perception that an extension is automatic.

The DCFS worker and supervisor *** will jointly determine if an extension should be granted for * ineligible cases. ** ***

The 24/60 Month Time Limit Tracking report * tracks ** all cases approaching the fifty-eighth month.

II. PROCEDURES

B-1731-FITAP-PR COUNTING THE 60 MONTHS

When a client states they have received TANF benefits from another state, verify with the state the number of months and the dates benefits were received. Notify the * ES Supervisor ** to add these months to the * FITAP Time Clock screen in LITE **.

Upon receipt of the Benefit Clock Extension task, the supervisor will start the work item.  The client has received twenty-two months of FITAP,  An extension period is expiring and additional time is needed, or  When a client has exceeded the 24-month time-limit and reapplies for assistance.

Note: Consideration of an extension is not required for cases in which the 24-month time clock is halted due to the limited earned income deduction, or when the work registration code is * Temporary Incapacity (WRC 03), Permanent Incapacity (WRC 11), or Incapacitated Single Parent (Head of Household) (WRC 24), and a form OFS 90 is approved for the current month, or when the time clock is halted due to a break in FITAP assistance in the prior 60 calendar month time period.

Consideration of a subsequent extension must be made by the 10th day of the last month of an extension period. The determination is based on:

 Factors relating to job availability or job loss, or  A hardship as outlined in section B-1744 FITAP. **

B-1741-2-FITAP - PR 60-Month Time Limit Responsibilities

In the fifty-eighth month, the case should be reviewed to determine if a condition for an extension exists. Discussion *** * should include: **

***  The challenges the client has had in the past and is currently facing, and  Assessment of a hardship situation.

The * ES worker will thoroughly document case notes ** regarding the approaching 60-month time limit and a clear rationale for recommendation of an extension. *** * The extension determination will be input in the LITE FITAP Extended Benefits Referral module on the FITAP Time Limit Decision – Details screen. This screen allows the worker to create an extension request for approval. Once the worker inputs all the required information then clicks, LITE will generate a Benefit Clock Extension task item for the supervisor to review and authorize or deny the extension request. **

* Upon receipt of the Benefit Clock Extension task, the supervisor will start the work item. The system will bring the supervisor to the FITAP Extended Benefits Referral – Summary screen, with the CID already populated. The supervisor will select Search, followed by the Edit Pencil icon next to the pending approval/denial. This will bring the supervisor to the FITAP Time Limit Decision – Details screen where they can approve or deny the decision. If approved, the extension may be granted for no more than six months. ** A decision must be made by the 10th day of the sixtieth month of benefits, or by the 10th day of the last month of an extension period.

7 of 8 B-1744-FITAP - PR EXTENSION REASONS

Among other factors as discussed in B-1720-FITAP, section B-1723-FITAP and B-1730-FITAP, section B-1733-FITAP, a clear rationale must exist for an extension to be recommended. The following circumstances may justify a time-limit extension:

***

Loss of Job/No Fault (T3)

The individual loses his job as a result of factors not related to his job performance. ***

Hardship (T5)

Other hardships have occurred which affect the individual’s ability to obtain employment. These hardship extensions are limited to the period of time the condition or situation is expected to last.

Examples of such hardships include:

a) when a parent/caretaker relative is under treatment for a serious addiction and work force participation is not recommended by the treating organization, or

b) when adequate child care or transportation is not available, or

c) a temporary family crisis such as death of a family member, eviction, serious illness or accident has occurred, or

d) domestic violence situations, or

e) when a parent is required to provide full-time care to an incapacitated or disabled member of the household, or

f) incapacity of the parent or other caretaker relative for purposes of applying the 60-month limit.

Pending Appeal (T6)

The case remains eligible pending a decision by the DCFS Bureau of Appeals.

NOTE: This reason does not require approval as a basis of extension.

***

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B-Eligibility Factors (FITAP) Section No./Name B-1800 Drug Testing (FITAP) Document No./Name B-1810-FITAP Purpose Effective Date February 1, 2013

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The FITAP Drug Testing policy is intended to detect the possible use of or dependence on illegal drugs by FITAP recipients age 18 and over in order that they may be referred to the Office of Behavioral Health (OBH) – Addictive Disorder (AD) for further testing to confirm whether the recipient uses or is dependent on illegal drugs. If use of or dependence on illegal drugs is confirmed by OBH; OBH will provide education, treatment and rehabilitation services. Detection and treatment of drug related problems is an essential step in assisting the recipient to overcome barriers which prevent the recipient from achieving self-sufficiency and promotes the safety and well-being of the recipient and his dependent children.

II. PROCEDURES

* There are no procedures associated with this policy.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms or instructions associated with this policy.

IV. REFERENCES

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B-Eligibility Factors (FITAP) Section No./Name B-1800 Drug Testing (FITAP) Document No./Name B-1820-FITAP ES Screening Effective Date September 1, 2015

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

* Certain adult ** FITAP applicants and recipients age 18 and over will be screened by the ES worker for the possible use of or dependence on illegal drugs at:

● Change report,

● the initial application for FITAP benefits, and

● at each redetermination of continued eligibility.

Applicants and recipients are to be advised that use of or dependence on illegal drugs will not, in itself, negatively impact their eligibility.

For applications, do not complete the screening until eligibility based on other factors has been established. Do not screen if the application is to be denied.

II. PROCEDURES

B-1821-FITAP - PR RESULTS OF ES SCREENING

If the response to any question on the DAST 20 indicates possible use of or dependence on illegal drugs, the recipient shall be referred to Office of Behavioral Health (OBH) for:

● additional screening, ● possible urine testing, ● education, ● treatment, and ● rehabilitation services, where necessary.

Note: If the applicant/recipient indicates they have already completed a treatment program, the applicant/recipient should still be referred to OBH. OBH will determine whether additional treatment is necessary.

B-1822-FITAP - PR SCREENING AT APPLICATION

ES screening is accomplished through the use of the DAST 20 screening form administered by staff. Prior to completion of the DAST 20 , give the client form OFS DT 1 and fully explain the purpose of drug testing policy (see B-1810-FITAP). This explanation must include an explanation of the screening referral to OBH, the cooperation requirements and the sanctions for failure to participate. After providing this information to the client, as appropriate, administer the DAST 20 either by telephone or in a face-to-face interview. If no further referral to OBH is required, enter a case note upon completion of the DAST 20.

2 of 2

B-1822-1-FITAP - PR SCREENING AT REDETERMINATION

At redetermination, send form OFS 18C scheduling a telephone interview for the completion of the DAST 20 prior to the end of the certification period. If no further referral to OBH is required, enter a case note upon completion of the DAST 20.

B-1822-2-FITAP - PR SCREENING AT CHANGE REPORT

When a * required ** household member age 18 or older is added to an active FITAP case, a drug screening questionnaire must be administered. Send form OFS 18C and/or OFS 12 scheduling a telephone interview for the completion of the DAST 20 prior to including the household member. If no further referral to OBH is required, enter a case note upon completion of the DAST 20.

B-1823-FITAP - PR REASONABLE CAUSE

Refer recipients to OBH at any time there is reasonable cause to suspect that a recipient is using or is dependent on illegal drugs. This may be based on direct observation or on reliable information indicating the use of or dependence on illegal drugs received from a reliable source.

Referrals to OBH on the basis of observation or reliable information from a reliable source must be approved by a supervisor.

It is not necessary to complete the DAST 20 prior to referral to OBH when the referral is based on observation or on reliable information from an outside source.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

OFS DT 1 Form/Instructions Drug Testing, Education and Rehabilitation Program

OFS 18C Form/Instructions Client Contact Letter

DAST 20 Form/Instructions Drug Use Questionnaire

Division/Section Family Support (ES) Chapter No./Name Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B-Eligibility Factors (FITAP) Section No./Name B-1800 Drug Testing (FITAP) Document No./Name B-1830-FITAP Consent for Release of Information Effective Date February 1, 2013

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Prior to referral to OBH, have each recipient being referred sign the following Consent for Release of Information forms:

● Consent for release of information by the Department of Children and Family Services to OBH.

● Consent for release of information by OBH to the Department of Children and Family Services.

II. PROCEDURES

Use the * Form DCFS 35 and DCFS 35H ** for these releases. Complete the release forms after the initial ES screening is completed and referral to OBH is indicated or prior to making a referral based on reasonable cause. The client’s failure to sign either of the release forms constitutes a failure to participate (Refer to B-1870-FITAP-Failure to Satisfactorily Participate).

Each release form must contain a specific expiration date agreed to by the client. The release may be revoked by the client before the expiration date. The expiration date should not exceed 12 months from the date the release is completed. If a client remains in a treatment/rehabilitation program at the time the releases expire, OBH will execute two new releases.

Any break in FITAP eligibility of the recipient referred to OBH will result in the automatic termination of both releases. A break in eligibility is defined as the loss of cash eligibility for one or more months, with the exception of those cases which do not receive a cash benefit wholly due to the minimum $10 grant. Subsequent referrals to OBH will require the completion of two new releases.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

* DCFS 35 Form/Instructions - Consent to Release Information (Other than Protected Health Information) Waiver of Confidentiality Form

DCFS 35H Form/Instructions - Authorization to Release Protected Health Information
