17 of 22 Homeless Shelter Deduction

Homeless households may receive the excess shelter deduction, the homeless shelter deduction, or actual shelter costs if the actual costs are higher than the homeless shelter deduction and the actual costs are verified.

B-655-SNAP - PR DEPENDENT CARE DEDUCTION

Budgeting Out-of-Pocket Dependent Care Expenses

Verify dependent care expenses only if the household’s total expense exceeds $500 per month or is questionable:

• at initial certification,

• at redetermination, or

• if the household reports a change in the expense which would result in an increase in benefits.

Document the reason the expense is questionable.

A dependent care expense which is reimbursed or paid by a third party is not a deductible expense. Only the amount of the dependent care expense which exceeds the reimbursement or the amount paid by a third party is allowed as a deduction if the client is expected to pay the excess.

When a dependent care expense is reported which is subject to reimbursement or payment by a third party, the out-of-pocket expense must be anticipated and budgeted as follows:

Determine the average monthly amount of the dependent care expense.

• Determine the average monthly amount of the reimbursement or the third party payment.

• Subtract the average monthly reimbursement or third party payment from the average monthly amount of the dependent care expense.

• If this computation results in a determination that the client will incur an out-of-pocket expense, include this amount as a dependent care expense in the SNAP budget.

When actual transportation expense incurred, allow out-of-pocket expense that SNAP household is required to pay.

Example: Care provider has a van which provides transportation service for their clients. They charge a separate fee of $5 per day to ride the van. Client rides the van 5 days per week; therefore,

18 of 22 the actual transportation cost incurred, $25 per week, would be considered an allowable dependent care transportation expense.

When determining the mileage cost incurred, do not include the normal mileage incurred by the household to go to and from work. Only allow the additional mileage traveled by the household to take the child or incapacitated adult to and from care provider.

Example: Client lives in Opelousas, works in Carencro, and the day care provider is in Lafayette. Client normally travels from Opelousas (home) to Carencro (work) every weekday. Client has to travel additional miles from Carencro (work) to Lafayette (day care) every weekday, therefore the additional miles from work to day care multiplied by the allowable mileage rate would be considered an allowable dependent care transportation expense.

Example: Client lives in Opelousas, works in Lafayette and the day care provider is in Carencro. Client normally travels from Opelousas (home) to Lafayette (work) every weekday. Day care provider is on the same route as client normally travels to work, therefore there are no additional miles traveled and no dependent care transportation expense.

When the dependent care expense is paid through the Child Care Assistance Program (CCAP), the dependent care deduction is equal to the CCAP co-payment.

If the client reports caretaker costs that could qualify under both dependent care and medical deductions, the household must be allowed a deduction of either dependent care or medical expense, but not both. If the household has no medical expenses, the caretaker expense should be allowed as a dependent care deduction. If the expense is allowed as a dependent care deduction and is less than $500, the household will not be required to provide documentation of the expense.

Example: Joan is disabled and has no other medical expenses. Joan’s son lives with her and pays a caretaker $400 per month to take care of her while he works. The expense can be allowed as either a medical or a dependent care deduction. The worker should budget as a dependent care expense instead of a medical expense since the medical deduction would be only the net deduction of $365 ($400 minus the $35 medical threshold).

When the client’s total expense exceeds $500 or is questionable, the client’s out-of-pocket expense may be verified by:

• Using form OFS 85, Child Care Expense Verification,

• A statement from the provider, or

• Receipts or canceled checks.

19 of 22 B-656-SNAP - PR CHILD SUPPORT PAYMENTS

Budgeting Child Support Payment Deduction

To determine the amount of the deduction to allow for child support payments, look at each individual's situation.

When a household has a record of paying legally obligated child support at least three months out of the past six months:

• Look at the past payments made, and

• Discuss with the client what payments are expected to be made in the future.

• Use both sources to determine prospective payments.

• Document to show how the decision was reached.

NOTE: Unless there is a change expected, usually a six-month average is a good indicator of future payments. Usually, at least the last three months of payments are used if averaging. Arrearages may be included in the average.

EXAMPLE:

Mr. A applies on October 4, 2021. It is verified that Mr. A was ordered by the court on May 24, 2021 to pay $500 per month child support. He anticipates no changes. The worker verifies the following payment history:

Month Total Amt Paid -(Includes Arrearages) Arrearages

April 2021 $1000 $ 500 May 2021 $ 500 None June 2021 $1500 $1000 July 2021 $ 200 None August 2021 $ 0 None September 2021 $ 300 None

Arrearages may be allowed when computing the budget. Mr. A did not anticipate any changes; therefore, average the last six months of actual payments (the obligated amount plus arrearages) to arrive at an average monthly payment amount of $583.

At redetermination, obtain updated information on which to base a new average for the new certification period.

20 of 22 Usually, the three-month payment history would continue to be met until the SNAP case closes. For households with no history or a history of less than three months out of the past six months of paying legally obligated child support, base the child support payment amount on anticipated payments using the best available information. Include arrearages in the average if the client expects to continue payments towards arrearages.

Included in the category of households without a payment record would be households with a newly established legal obligation and households that have failed to meet an obligation.

Verification of Child Support Payments

Verify the legal obligation to pay child support, the legally obligated amount, and the actual amount paid. The household is the primary source of verification of the legal obligation to pay child support, the amount of the obligation, and the amount paid.

Verify the child support payment at certification, redetermination, and whenever a change is reported which will increase the household's benefits. Document verification in LITE.

Verification of Legal Obligation and Legally Obligated Amount

Any document that verifies the obligation to pay child support, such as a court order, administrative order, or legally enforceable separation agreement would be sufficient verification of the obligation and obligated amount. CSE records may be used to verify the legal obligation.

Verification of Actual Amount Paid

Acceptable verification of amount paid includes, but is not limited to, canceled checks, wage withholding statements, verification of withholding from UCB and statements from the custodial parent regarding direct payments or third party payments the noncustodial parent pays or expects to pay on behalf of the custodial parent. Use CSE records to verify payments made to CSE. Clearance Summary may be used to verify payments made to CSE.

NOTE: Separate sources must be used to verify legal obligation and actual payments unless source is CSE records.

Failure or Refusal to Submit Required Verification of Child Support

If the household fails or refuses to submit required verification, determine the household's eligibility and benefit amount without consideration of the child support deduction.

• Do not deduct expenses paid by a reimbursement.

21 of 22 • Do not deduct expenses paid by vendor payment except for vendor payments made as part of legally obligated child support. (See B-656-SNAP.) o Example 1: The absent parent pays the client’s $500 mortgage directly to the mortgage company instead of paying the agreed upon $500 voluntary child support to the client. Since there is no court order for the child support and the client’s mortgage is being paid through the absent parent’s vendor payments, the mortgage expense is not an allowable shelter deduction. o Example 2: The absent parent is court-ordered to pay $500 child support to the client. Instead of giving the money to the client, he pays her $500 mortgage directly to the mortgage company. Since the absent parent is court-ordered to pay child support of $500 to the client, the mortgage payment is diverted income and must be counted as income to the client. The mortgage expense is an allowable shelter deduction.

• Deduct expenses only in the month the expense is billed or becomes due, regardless of when the household intends to pay it. Do not deduct past-due balances and late charges. Arrearages in child support payments are allowable for certain households eligible for a child support deduction. (See B-656-SNAP).

EXCEPTION: When a household pays an expense in advance, the deductible amount is the amount that would otherwise be due. Typically, this would be the monthly obligation. The entire pre-payment must not be deducted at one time.

• Expenses will not be deductible if the service is provided by a member of the same SNAP household.

• Do not allow deductions for work-related expenses for individuals who are not self-employed.

• Refer to E-220-SNAP for deductions of disqualified members.

1 of 8 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

B-661-FITAP - PO DETERMINING ELIGIBILITY AND BENEFITS

TO DETERMINE THE AMOUNT OF INCOME TO BUDGET:

● EVALUATE THE HOUSEHOLD'S CIRCUMSTANCES AND INCOME WITH THE CLIENT.

● CONSIDER THE INCOME THE HOUSEHOLD HAS ALREADY RECEIVED AND/OR EXPECTS TO RECEIVE IN DETERMINING THE AMOUNT OF INCOME TO BE BUDGETED. IF THE HOUSEHOLD IS UNSURE OF THE AMOUNT OF INCOME EXPECTED, USE THE BEST ESTIMATE OF THE AMOUNT TO BE RECEIVED. DO NOT COUNT INCOME FROM A NEW SOURCE WHICH THE CLIENT IS NOT CERTAIN TO RECEIVE.

● Decide if any factors are likely to change in the current or future months.

● If changes are unlikely, CERTIFY THE HOUSEHOLD BASED ON ANTICIPATED INCOME AND CIRCUMSTANCES.

● IF CHANGES ARE LIKELY, DETERMINE HOW THE CHANGE WILL AFFECT ELIGIBILITY AND BENEFITS.

B-661-1-FITAP - PO Determining Earned Income

NOTE: THIS SECTION DOES NOT APPLY TO SELF-EMPLOYMENT OR CONTRACTUAL EMPLOYMENT. REFER TO B-620-44-SNAP/FITAP FOR SELF-EMPLOYMENT AND B-620-10- SNAP/FITAP FOR CONTRACTUAL EMPLOYMENT.

INCOME FROM EARNINGS MUST BE THE MOST CURRENT OR RECENT INFORMATION AVAILABLE. INCOME FROM THE CURRENT CALENDAR MONTH AND THE PRIOR CALENDAR MONTH ARE USED WHEN DETERMINING EARNED INCOME. USE AT LEAST TWO PAY PERIODS THAT ARE REPRESENTATIVE DURING THIS TIME PERIOD. IF MORE THAN TWO PAY PERIODS ARE PROVIDED, AND THEY ARE REPRESENTATIVE OF EARNINGS, WAGES FROM EACH PAY PERIOD PROVIDED THAT ARE WITHIN THE CURRENT CALENDAR MONTH AND THE PRIOR CALENDAR MONTH MUST BE USED IN DETERMINING INCOME.

IF EARNINGS FROM AT LEAST TWO PAY PERIODS WITHIN THE CURRENT CALENDAR MONTH AND THE PRIOR CALENDAR MONTH HAVE NOT BEEN PROVIDED WITH THE APPLICATION, SIMPLIFIED REPORT, REDETERMINATION, OR CHANGE REPORT, REQUEST VERIFICATION OF WAGES FOR THE CURRENT AND PRIOR CALENDAR MONTH.

EXCEPTION: ONLY ONE PAY PERIOD IS REQUIRED FOR INCOME WHICH IS PAID ON A MONTHLY BASIS.

ENTER COUNTABLE INCOME ON LAMI.

EXAMPLE: DURING THE INTERVIEW, THE CLIENT STATES THAT SHE MAKES AN AVERAGE OF $250 A WEEK. THE CLIENT PROVIDES TWO CHECK STUBS, ONE THAT IS FOR $150 AND ONE FOR $200. THE CLIENT MUST BE CONTACTED TO DISCUSS THIS DISCREPANCY TO MAKE A DETERMINATION IF THE CHECK STUBS PROVIDED ARE REPRESENTATIVE OF HER EARNINGS. IF THE CHECK STUBS ARE NOT REPRESENTATIVE OF HER EARNINGS, ADDITIONAL VERIFICATION MUST BE OBTAINED. THE INTERVIEW WIZARD MUST BE DOCUMENTED TO INDICATE WHICH CHECKS ARE REPRESENTATIVE OF EARNINGS. IF THE WIZARD IS UNAVAILABLE, DOCUMENT ON THE OFS 3.

EXAMPLE: DURING THE INTERVIEW, THE CLIENT STATES THAT SHE MAKES AN AVERAGE OF $250 A WEEK. THE CLIENT PROVIDES TWO CHECK STUBS, ONE THAT IS FOR $250 AND ONE FOR $230. 1 of 8 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

B-661-SNAP - PO DETERMINING ELIGIBILITY AND BENEFITS

TO DETERMINE THE AMOUNT OF INCOME TO BUDGET:

● EVALUATE THE HOUSEHOLD'S CIRCUMSTANCES AND INCOME WITH THE CLIENT.

● CONSIDER THE INCOME THE HOUSEHOLD HAS ALREADY RECEIVED AND/OR EXPECTS TO RECEIVE IN DETERMINING THE AMOUNT OF INCOME TO BE BUDGETED. IF THE HOUSEHOLD IS UNSURE OF THE AMOUNT OF INCOME EXPECTED, USE THE BEST ESTIMATE OF THE AMOUNT TO BE RECEIVED. DO NOT COUNT INCOME FROM A NEW SOURCE WHICH THE CLIENT IS NOT CERTAIN TO RECEIVE. ● CERTIFY THE HOUSEHOLD BASED ON ANTICIPATED INCOME AND CIRCUMSTANCES.

● IF CHANGES ARE LIKELY, DETERMINE HOW THE CHANGE WILL AFFECT ELIGIBILITY AND BENEFITS.

B-661-1-SNAP - PO Determining Earned Income

NOTE: THIS SECTION DOES NOT APPLY TO SELF-EMPLOYMENT OR CONTRACTUAL EMPLOYMENT. REFER TO B-620-44-SNAP/FITAP FOR SELF-EMPLOYMENT AND B-620-10- SNAP/FITAP FOR CONTRACTUAL EMPLOYMENT.

INCOME FROM EARNINGS MUST BE THE MOST CURRENT OR RECENT INFORMATION AVAILABLE. INCOME FROM THE CURRENT CALENDAR MONTH AND THE PRIOR CALENDAR MONTH ARE USED WHEN DETERMINING EARNED INCOME. USE AT LEAST TWO PAY PERIODS THAT ARE REPRESENTATIVE DURING THIS TIME PERIOD. IF MORE THAN TWO PAY PERIODS ARE PROVIDED, AND THEY ARE REPRESENTATIVE OF EARNINGS, WAGES FROM EACH PAY PERIOD PROVIDED THAT ARE WITHIN THE CURRENT CALENDAR MONTH AND THE PRIOR CALENDAR MONTH MUST BE USED IN DETERMINING INCOME.

IF EARNINGS FROM AT LEAST TWO PAY PERIODS WITHIN THE CURRENT CALENDAR MONTH AND THE PRIOR CALENDAR MONTH HAVE NOT BEEN PROVIDED WITH THE APPLICATION, SIMPLIFIED REPORT, REDETERMINATION, OR CHANGE REPORT, REQUEST VERIFICATION OF WAGES FOR THE CURRENT AND PRIOR CALENDAR MONTH.

EXCEPTION: ONLY ONE PAY PERIOD IS REQUIRED FOR INCOME WHICH IS PAID ON A MONTHLY BASIS.

DO NOT REJECT THE APPLICATION OR CLOSE THE CASE FOR FAILURE TO PROVIDE VERIFICATION, IF VERIFICATION OF EARNINGS IS PROVIDED THAT MEETS THE REQUIREMENTS.

● THE DATE OF THE APPLICATION,

● THE DATE THE REDETERMINATION IS RECEIVED,

● THE DATE A SIMPLIFIED REPORT IS RECEIVED,

● THE DATE THE VERIFICATION IS REQUESTED,

● THE DATE OF THE MOST RECENT CHECK STUB, IF MORE CURRENT VERIFICATION IS PROVIDED or is available on *** Experian,

NOTE: IF A CHECK STUB IS MORE CURRENT THAN THE DATE OF THE REQUEST FOR VERIFICATION, THE DATE ON THE NEW CHECK STUB WOULD BECOME THE CURRENT MONTH. If a pay date verified through *** Experian is more current than the application date, the most recent pay date would become the current month.

EXAMPLE 1: APPLICATION RECEIVED AUGUST 25 AND NO VERIFICATION PROVIDED. INTERVIEW CONDUCTED AUGUST 30 AND VERIFICATION OF WAGES REQUESTED SAME DAY FOR JULY AND AUGUST WAGES. CHECK STUB DATED SEPTEMBER 8 IS PROVIDED, THEREFORE, THE CURRENT MONTH BECOMES SEPTEMBER AND THE PRIOR MONTH BECOMES AUGUST. USE AUGUST AND SEPTEMBER WAGES.

EXAMPLE 2: Application received August 25 and no verification provided. Interview conducted *** September 2 and verification of wages requested same day. Pay date September 1 is available, therefore, the current month becomes September and the prior month becomes August. Use August and September wages.

● THE DATE THE CLIENT REPORTS A CHANGE if benefits will increase because of the change, or

● The date a client reports a subsequent change which results in an increase in benefits if the initial report was not acted upon because it would have resulted in a decrease in benefits.

THESE INSTRUCTIONS APPLY TO FLUCTUATING AND STABLE INCOME.

IF UNEARNED INCOME DOES NOT FLUCTUATE, VERIFY AND BUDGET THE MONTHLY AMOUNT.

II. PROCEDURES

B-661-SNAP - PR DETERMINING ELIGIBILITY AND BENEFITS

ENTER COUNTABLE INCOME IN LITE

B-661-1-SNAP - PR Determining Earned Income

IF THE HOUSEHOLD PROVIDES VERIFICATION OF WAGES FROM AT LEAST TWO PAY PERIODS WHICH ARE REPRESENTATIVE OF INCOME FOR THE CURRENT CALENDAR MONTH AND PRIOR CALENDAR MONTH WHEN THE APPLICATION, REDETERMINATION, OR SIMPLIFIED REPORT IS RECEIVED, OR THE CHANGE IS REPORTED, NO ADDITIONAL WAGE VERIFICATION MUST BE REQUESTED, UNLESS THE VERIFICATION RECEIVED IS QUESTIONABLE.

IF VERIFICATION OF EARNINGS FROM AT LEAST TWO REPRESENTATIVE PAY PERIODS WITHIN THE CURRENT CALENDAR MONTH AND THE PRIOR CALENDAR MONTH HAVE NOT BEEN PROVIDED, REQUEST VERIFICATION OF ALL WAGES RECEIVED FROM THE CURRENT CALENDAR MONTH AND THE PRIOR CALENDAR MONTH. THE DATE THE VERIFICATION IS REQUESTED IS THE DETERMINING FACTOR ON WHICH MONTHS TO REQUEST THE VERIFICATION.

EXAMPLE: CLIENT APPLIES ON JULY 7 AND DOES NOT PROVIDE WAGE VERIFICATION. CLIENT IS INTERVIEWED ON JULY 20; THEREFORE, WAGES RECEIVED FROM JUNE 1 - JULY 20 SHOULD BE REQUESTED. JUNE IS THE PRIOR CALENDAR MONTH AND JULY IS THE CURRENT CALENDAR MONTH. IF CLIENT PROVIDES AT LEAST TWO CHECK STUBS THAT ARE REPRESENTATIVE BETWEEN JUNE 1 – JULY 20, USE THOSE PAY PERIODS TO ESTIMATE EARNINGS.

EXAMPLE: CLIENT SUBMITS REDETERMINATION FORM ON JUNE 20 FOR A JULY REDETERMINATION. CLIENT IS INTERVIEWED ON JUNE 21. WAGES FROM MAY 1 - JUNE 21 SHOULD BE REQUESTED. THE CLIENT PROVIDED CHECK STUBS DATED MAY 26, JUNE 16, AND JULY 7 THAT ARE REPRESENTATIVE. SINCE THE CLIENT HAS PROVIDED MORE CURRENT EARNINGS, USE PAY PERIODS OF JUNE 16 AND JULY 7.

YEAR-TO-DATE (YTD) INFORMATION CAN BE USED TO CALCULATE THE AMOUNT OF A MISSING PAY PERIOD TO HELP DETERMINE IF CHECK STUBS PROVIDED ARE REPERESENTATIVE OF EARNINGS. TO DETERMINE THE GROSS AMOUNT OF MISSING PAYCHECKS, EACH CALCULATION MUSTBE DONE SEPARATELY.

EXAMPLE: THE CLIENT APPLIES ON 3/1. SHE IS PAID WEEKLY ON FRIDAYS. SHE HAS CHECK STUBS FROM 2/25 AND 2/11. SHE IS MISSING THE CHECK STUB FROM 2/18.

For households occupying a residence that has a monthly rent structure, allow the amount of the monthly rent obligation in the monthly shelter deduction, regardless of when the rent is actually paid. Use the most recent month's bills for projecting expenses, unless the household anticipates a change. Agency Name Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-700 Immunization Document No./Name B-710-FITAP Immunization Effective Date May 1, 2023

1 of 8 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Sufficient evidence of immunity or immunization against vaccine-preventable diseases recommended by the Office of Public Health schedule must be provided for each recipient under 18 years of age. Sufficient evidence that such an immunization program is up-to-date or in progress may be substituted for proof of immunity or immunization.

Immunizations must be verified at:

● initial application,

● when assistance is requested for an additional child,

● at redetermination, and

● at the midpoint of a 24 month certification period.

The client must be advised of the immunization requirement in writing and allowed 10 days to complete the needed activities and submit verification. If the client fails to cooperate or provide sufficient verification of requested immunization for any child, the client is not eligible for assistance.

EXCEPTIONS: The immunization requirement does not apply if the client: ● submits a written statement from a physician stating that the immunization procedure is inadvisable or contraindicated for medical reasons, or

● *** * verbally states an ** objection to the procedure based on religious grounds.

B-711-FITAP - PO IMMUNIZATION SCHEDULE

The child should obtain immunizations according to the schedule listed in the chart below which is recommended by the Office of Public Health.

The Office of Public Health, OPH allows exceptions to the Immunization Schedule. Each child’s individual circumstances must be considered. A child may not have had all the immunizations listed for his age and may not be required to have all the immunizations listed. A statement from a medical provider (hospital, clinic, health unit, physician, etc.) that a child is up-to-date or in progress with their immunization requirement is sufficient.

Determine the current age of the child. To be in compliance with immunization requirements, immunizations should be administered within 30 days of their birthday based on the child’s age shown in the chart below.

Subsequent routine Td boosters are recommended every 10 years.

Time sensitive vaccines:

Hib is an abbreviation for Haemophilus Influenza Type B and may be written as Hib Titer, Act Hib, PedVax Hib, or given as combination with HepB (Comvax). No Hib is given after 60 months of age. If Hib vaccines were manufactured by Merck and administered at 2 and 4 months of age, a dose at 6 months is not required.

RV is an abbreviation for Rotavirus Vaccine. The first dose of the RV Vaccine can be administered between 8 weeks of age and 15 weeks of age. The RV cannot be administered later than 8 months (32 weeks) of age. If Monavalent RV1 is administered at 2 months and 4 months of age, a dose at 6 months is not required. Pentavalent RV5 is administered at 2 months, 4 months and 6 – 8 months.

Remaining vaccines recommended:

HepA is an abbreviation for Hepatitis A Vaccine. HepA is recommended for all children 12 months through 18 years of age.

HepB is an abbreviation for Hepatitis B Vaccine. HepB is routinely recommended for all children up to 19 years of age.

DTaP is an abbreviation for Diphtheria, Tetanus and acellular Pertussis. The following vaccines are acceptable as DTaP equivalents: DTP, DTaP, DT, Td, or any combination including these, such as DTP-Hib, DTP-HBV, DTaP-Hib, etc.

3 of 8

IPV is an abbreviation for Inactivated Poliovirus Vaccine. The following vaccines are acceptable as equivalents: OPV, eIPV, or any combination including these such as DTP-IPV, etc.

PCV is an abbreviation for Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine. All children should receive a 3 dose primary series and a booster if vaccination begun at or before 6 months of age; a 2 dose primary series and a booster if vaccination is begun between 7 and 11 months of age; a 2 dose series and no booster if vaccination is begun between 12 and 23 months of age. If vaccination is initiated at or after 24 months of age, the child should receive 1 dose of PCV. Children 24 through 59 months of age should receive a single dose of PCV13. Children with underlying medical conditions, a single supplemental PCV13 is recommended following primary series. PCV vaccination is required as part of the Daycare/Head Start Immunization Requirement for children less than 24 months of age.

MMR is an abbreviation for Measles, Mumps and Rubella. The following vaccines are acceptable as MMR equivalents: MMR, Measles + Mumps + Rubella, or any combination that includes these, such as MMRV, MMR-Varicella, etc.

VAR is an abbreviation for Varicella. All susceptible children who are at least 12 months old through 18 years of age are eligible.

Tdap is an abbreviation for Tetanus and Diphtheria Toxoids and Acellular Pertussis Vaccine.

HPV is an abbreviation for Human Papillomavirus Vaccine. HPV vaccine is a 2 dose series for ages 9-14 years and a 3 dose series for ages 15-26 years. The first dose is administered between 11-12 years. The second dose is administered 6-12 months after the first dose. If the series was started at 15-26 years, then the third dose is administered at least 12 weeks after the second dose, but no earlier than 24 weeks after the first dose.

MCV is an abbreviation for Menningococcal Conjugate Vaccine. This vaccine should be administered to all children 11-12 years of age, with a booster dose on/after age 16. Only one dose is required if it is given on or after age 16.

Seasonal vaccine:

Flu is an abbreviation for the Influenza Vaccine. Routine annual influenza vaccination is recommended for all children 6 months – 18 years; however, it is not required for a child to be eligible for assistance.

4 of 8 Example:

A redetermination is completed in August 2015. There are 3 children in the assistance unit.

Sharon is 16 months old. According to the schedule it is recommended that she have 4 DTaP vaccines, 4 Hib vaccines, 3 IPV vaccines, 3 HepB vaccines, 4 PCV vaccines, 3 RV vaccines, 1 MMR vaccine, 1 VAR vaccine, and 1 HepA vaccine to be up to date on immunizations. Her immunization card shows that she has received all vaccines required for her age.

Susan is 9 years old and is enrolled in school. Although Susan is enrolled in school, the client is not sure that she has received all required immunizations. According to the schedule, it is recommended that she have 5 DTaP vaccines, 4 Hib vaccines, 4 IPV vaccines, 3 HepB vaccines, 4 PCV vaccines, 3 RV vaccines, 2 MMR vaccines, 2 VAR vaccines, and 2 HepA vaccines to be up to date on immunizations. Her immunization card shows that she has had 4 DTaP vaccines, 3 IPV vaccines, 2 MMR vaccines, 4 Hib vaccines, 3 HepB vaccines, and 1 VAR vaccine. The client provides a recent statement from the Health Unit that she has completed the immunization process. Although she has not received all the vaccines listed, the statement from the Health Unit is sufficient to verify immunizations are considered to be complete. Susan is considered to be in compliance with the immunization requirement and the statement should be accepted without further verification.

Thomas is 12 years old and client states he is enrolled in school and has received all required immunizations. No further verification is necessary.

For additional information concerning recommended immunizations, refer to https://www.cdc.gov/vaccines.

B-712-FITAP - PO VERIFICATION

Verification sources may include hospital, clinic, health unit, school, medical records, private physician's records, Request for Verification of Immunization form (OFS IM), or Louisiana Immunization Network for Kids Statewide (LINKS).

B-712-1- FITAP - PO Louisiana Immunization Network for Kids Statewide (LINKS) Participants

The Louisiana Department of Health, Office of Public Health, Immunization Program provides an internet website that allows designated users to view immunization records for patients in the LINKS Central Registry. The website is: https://linksweb.oph.dhh.louisiana.gov. If a client moves within Louisiana, any participating provider, parish health unit, or designated user in the parish office may retrieve a child’s immunization record. All children’s immunization records may not appear on the website because a provider may not participate in the LINKS Program or a parent may not want to share their child’s information.

5 of 8 The LINKS website provides the following information: child’s full name, date of birth, gender, mother’s maiden name, guardian’s first name (when applicable), address, phone number, immunization record and other information which may determine eligibility for free vaccines.

If the LINKS Patient Vaccination Summary printout indicates “up-to-date” or “due now,” the child is considered to be in compliance with the immunization requirement. The LINKS printout should be accepted without further verification.

An explanation of the LINKS terms Due Now, Past Due and Up-to-Date are as follows:

● Due Now - As of today’s date, the patient’s age falls between the recommended minimum age and recommended maximum age for this dose and the absolute minimum interval has been met since last dose.

● Past Due - As of today’s date, the recommended maximum age or the recommended maximum for this dose has passed. (30 days after the date due which is the child’s birthday).

● Up-to-Date - As of today’s date, the patient is not due or past due.

B-712-2-FITAP - PO Non-LINKS Participants

Refer to B-712-2-PR for the procedure staff must follow regarding Non-LINKS Participants.

II. PROCEDURES

At initial application, when assistance is requested for an additional child, redetermination, and at the midpoint of a 24-month certification period:

● advise the client of the immunization requirement,

● discuss and determine with the client each child's immunization status to determine what action is necessary on the part of the client to meet the requirement:

o For school aged children, accept the client's statement made verbally that the child has had all required immunizations if the client states that the child is currently enrolled in school. Document this information in Case Notes.

o For all other children, review LINKS. For example, does the client need to make an appointment to have the child immunized or does the client only need to submit verification of the child's immunization record?

● advise the client in writing of any actions needed to meet the requirement, and

● give the client 10 days to complete the needed activities and submit verification.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B - Eligibility Factors (FITAP) Section No./Name B-800 FITAP Relationship Document No./Name B-810 FITAP Eligibility Requirement Effective Date November 1, 2022

1 of 2

I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

A child must live in the home of a parent (Refer to B-0510 FITAP) or one of the following qualified relatives (either biological or adoptive) * as follows:

● grandfather or grandmother (extends to great-great-great)

● brother or sister (including half brother and half sister)

● uncle or aunt (extends to great-great)

● first cousin, including first cousin once removed (child of a first cousin)

● nephew or niece (extends to great-great)

● stepfather or stepmother

● stepbrother or stepsister

Relationship extends to the legal spouse of the above listed relatives even after the marriage is terminated by death or divorce.

The relationship requirement is met when the child lives with any of the above named relatives. Legal custody is not a factor in determining relationships.

Legal adoption terminates all prior legal relationships. The biological parent and biological relatives remain qualified relatives due to the blood relationship.

Descendants of stepsiblings are not qualified relatives.

A First Cousin Once Removed who is the descendent of a Great Uncle or Aunt is not within the required degree of relationship to be a qualified relative.

II. PROCEDURES

LITE determines eligibility for degree of relationship by using the data entered from the Relationship Type is drop-down list on the Relationship – Details screen for each member.

Document relationship in LITE on the Relationship – Details screen and the Relationship – Establishing Family Tree screen. **

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Verify relationship of each child to the qualified relative at certification and when adding a child.

B-821-FITAP - PO HOW TO VERIFY RELATIONSHIP TO PARENT

Relationship of a child to his parent(s) is primarily verified through a birth certificate. If the birth certificate is not available, other documents may be used if they include the name of the child and the parent(s). These documents may include:

● baptismal certificate,

● documents from the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) and/or identifying information provided in correspondence from a Voluntary Agency,

● licensed midwife records, or

● medical records.

Note: A birth card which does not include the full name of the child, full name of the mother and/or father is not sufficient verification of relationship. Other supporting documentation as outlined above and at B-822-FITAP must be obtained.

If the father's name does not appear on the birth certificate, the determination of his relationship to the child may be established by one or more of the following:

● a court judgment which declares the man to be the child's father;

● documentation that the child receives financial benefits based on circumstances of the father, i.e., Social Security, VA, military allotment;

● documentation that the child is claimed by the man as his dependent child for income tax purposes;

● paternity test results that verify the man to be the father; or

● the man is named by the mother and:

o the man verbally acknowledges paternity to the agency, or o the man signs an acknowledgement of paternity, or o at least two references or collaterals state in writing that the man has acknowledged to them that he is the child's father.

2 of 4 B-822-FITAP - PO HOW TO VERIFY RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER QUALIFIED RELATIVE

Once the parental relationship has been established, use documentary proof to establish the child's relationship to the qualified relative. In addition to the documents listed in section B-821-FITAP, the following may be used:

● family bible,

● church records,

● U.S. Census records,

● insurance policies over 3 years old, or

● legal document executed by the court, such as a custody order, which states the qualified relative's relationship to the child.

If none of the above documents is available, the relationship of the qualified relative to the child may be established by securing:

● the qualified relative's written statement as to how he is related to the child, and

● a written statement attesting to the relationship from another individual in a position to know the facts of the situation.

Determine how the collateral is knowledgeable of the client's situation and document this *** in Case Notes. If the collateral is not interviewed in the parish office, contact the collateral by telephone to obtain the documentation of how he knows of the relationship of the qualified relative to the child.

To request verification of Relationship, select ‘Pending Verification’ or ‘Client Statement’ on the Relationship – Details screen for those relationships that have not been verified. Example: Mother applies for herself and two children. The agency has a birth certificate for the first child only. LITE is updated to reflect the birth certificate contained in OnBase for that child. However, verification is still needed for the second child. Data collection in LITE on the Relationship – Details chart would be updated as follows:

Between the 1st child and 2nd child – Relationship verification coding should be ‘Reliable Reference.’ If ‘Pending Verification’ is selected as the relationship verification between the two children, LITE will also request verification for the 1st child. This would be incorrect as there is already a birth certificate on file for the 1st child.

NOTE: Conversion codes (data from legacy systems) must be reviewed and updated accordingly. LITE cannot determine correct relationships and eligibility if ‘Conversion Value’ is not updated to reflect the correct household situation.

* Paternity Establishment and Support Enforcement (PESE)

The PESE interface allows access to Vital Records to receive and verify birth record information that assists in establishing relationship for program applicants. Staff is allowed to view birth record information if provisioned in the Case Access role. Staff may use PESE to establish the relationship status and/or age of household members. PESE must be reviewed prior to requesting verification of relationship. PESE information can be accessed in LITE by two methods: by using the PESE On- Demand button in the ‘Case Info’ right navigation panel in the case record or by clicking the PESE button from the ‘Internal Links’ left navigation panel on the LITE Home screen. The PESE On-Demand button is displayed on the following screens within a case record in LITE from the ‘Case Info’ right navigation panel:

• Person – Details • Relationship – Details, and • Person Demographics – Details

To access the PESE via the On-Demand button, the Person - Details, Relationship - Details, or the Person Demographics - Details screens to conduct a search, the worker must:

• Click the PESE On-Demand button from the ‘Case Info’ right navigation panel to display the PESE website’s Search screen with the results pre-populated for the individual whose details are being reviewed. • If staff have not received authorization to access PESE, clicking the On-Demand button will result in being redirected to the PESE website with the following error messaged displayed: “You are not authorized to access this site. Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 –Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B - Eligibility Factors (FITAP) Section No./Name B-800 FITAP Relationship Document No./Name B-840 FITAP Temporary Certification (Presumptive Eligibility FITAP Only) Effective Date November 1, 2022

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

If documentary verification of relationship cannot be obtained within 30 days of the application, do not deny the certification if:

 relationship can be temporarily established through collateral contacts,

 there is no reason to believe that the alleged relationship does not exist, and

 there is no reason to believe that documentation cannot be secured within three months.

Eligibility of the child in such a situation cannot extend longer than three months unless the relationship can be documented.

II. PROCEDURES

* For Relationship Verification, select Pending Verification (for FITAP only cases) or Client Statement (for cases with an associated pending or active SNAP program) which will trigger the 10 day Request for Verification.

NOTE: Do not extend the due date to “trick” the system or take any further action unless the requested verification is received, or the case is ready to be temporarily certified.

Once verifications are received and processed, if the client fails to verify relationship and they are otherwise eligible, update “Pending Verification/Client Statement” to “Presumptive Eligibility FITAP Only” and authorize the case.

LITE will recognize verification of Relationship as “postponed” once the case is authorized with “Presumptive Eligibility FITAP Only” as the Relationship Verification type. LITE will assign a 12- month certification period unless the Certification Thru date is matched to SNAP.

The Notice of Decision will inform the client that they will receive temporary FITAP benefits for three months. If eligibility cannot be established in three months, additional benefits cannot be provided. If the client provides verification prior to the end of the three-month temporary period, the Relationship Verification type must be updated and authorized in LITE. Benefits may be extended past the three months if eligibility has been met.

LITE will close the case automatically at the end of the 3rd month at cut-off if Relationship Verification is still marked “Presumptive Eligibility FITAP Only.” **

Agency Name Office of Family Support (OFS) Chapter No./Name 04 – Family Assistance Manual (FAM) Part No./Name B. Eligibility Factors (FITAP) Section No./Name B-900 Residency (FITAP) Document No./Name B-910-FITAP Eligibility Requirement Dates Issue December 20, 1997 Effective December 20, 1997

1 of 1

CLIENTS MUST RESIDE IN LOUISIANA TO BE ELIGIBLE FOR BENEFITS.

The following persons meet the residency requirement:

● Any person currently living in Louisiana who intends to make a home here and whose stay is not for temporary purposes.

● Other persons living in the state at the time of application who entered the state with a job commitment or an intention to seek employment (regardless of current employment status), and are not receiving assistance from another state.

Homeless families are considered to meet the residency requirement if the above requirements are met. Refer to B-521 (DOCNO = B-520).

NOTE: The child is a resident if his caretaker is a resident.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-900-FITAP-SNAP Residency Document No./Name B-920-FITAP Verification/Documentation Effective Date January 1, 2023

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

RESIDENCY MUST BE VERIFIED AT APPLICATION AND AT ANY OTHER TIME RESIDENCY IS QUESTIONABLE.

B-921-FITAP - PO HOW TO VERIFY RESIDENCY

USE SOURCES SUCH AS AN UNEXPIRED DRIVER’S LICENSE/STATE IDENTIFICATION CARD, INCLUDING A REAL ID OR RECENT RENT, MORTGAGE, OR UTILITY RECEIPTS TO VERIFY RESIDENCY. A RENT, MORTGAGE, OR UTILITY RECEIPT MUST LIST THE SAME RESIDENTIAL ADDRESS REPORTED ON THE APPLICATION REGARDLESS OF WHEN SUBMITTED.

SOCIAL SECURITY ADMINISTRATION (SSA) AND/OR SUPPLEMENTAL SECURITY INCOME (SSI) RECORDS RECEIVED THROUGH SOLQ OR CLEARANCE SUMMARY ARE ACCEPTABLE DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE TO VERIFY RESIDENCY IF NO OTHER PROOF IS AVAILABLE. THE IDENTIFYING INFORMATION, INCLUDING THE NAME, ADDRESS, AND DATE OF BIRTH LISTED ON THE SSA/SSI RECORD, MUST MATCH THE INFORMATION PROVIDED ON THE APPLICATION. IF THERE IS ANY DISCREPANCY BETWEEN THE INFORMATION PROVIDED ON THE APPLICATION AND THE SSA/SSI RECORD, RESIDENCY MUST BE VERIFIED THROUGH OTHER MEANS.

AN UNEXPIRED ON-DEMAND OMV/LA WALLET INTERFACE RESULT IS ACCEPTABLE VERIFICATION OF AN INDIVIDUAL’S RESIDENCY.

PAY CHECK STUBS OR AN OFS 87 (CURRENT, PAST OR ANTICIPATED WAGE VERIFICATION LETTER) THAT ARE NO MORE THAN 12-MONTHS OLD MAY ALSO BE USED TO VERIFY RESIDENCY.

* NOTE: THE ADDRESS LISTED ON THE CHECK STUBS OR THE OFS 87 MUST MATCH THE ADDRESS CURRENTLY BEING REPORTED AND BE NO MORE THAN 12-MONTHS OLD TO SERVE AS VERIFICATION OF RESIDENCY. **

WHEN RESIDENCY CANNOT BE VERIFIED WITH READILY AVAILABLE EVIDENCE:

 CONTACT THE LANDLORD, NEIGHBORS, RELATIVES, OR OTHER SOURCES OF RELIABLE INFORMATION DESIGNATED BY THE HOUSEHOLD OR

 MAKE A SCHEDULED HOME VISIT TO OBSERVE PERSONAL EFFECTS AND LIVING ARRANGEMENTS.

RESIDENCY MUST BE VERIFIED *** AT APPLICATION, REDETERMINATION, AND AT ANY OTHER TIME RESIDENCY IS QUESTIONABLE.

EXCEPTIONS: It is not necessary to verify residency in unusual cases (such as homeless households, some migrant farm worker households, newly arrived households) where verification is not possible, or if the household is categorically eligible.

Postpone verification of residency if necessary to meet expedited service timeframes.

B-921-SNAP - PO HOW TO VERIFY RESIDENCY

THE IDENTIFYING INFORMATION, INCLUDING THE NAME, ADDRESS, AND DATE OF BIRTH LISTED ON THE SSA/SSI RECORD, MUST MATCH THE INFORMATION PROVIDED ON THE APPLICATION. IF THERE IS ANY DISCREPANCY BETWEEN THE INFORMATION PROVIDED ON THE APPLICATION AND THE SSA/SSI RECORD, RESIDENCY MUST BE VERIFIED THROUGH OTHER MEANS.

AN UNEXPIRED ON-DEMAND OMV/LA WALLET INTERFACE RESULT IS ACCEPTABLE VERIFICATION OF AN INDIVIDUAL’S RESIDENCY.

A PERMANENT ID CANNOT BE USED TO VERIFY RESIDENCY. IF AN INDIVIDUAL HAS A PERMANENT ID, VERIFICATION OF RESIDENCY MUST BE REQUESTED.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-900 FITAP-SNAP Residency Document No./Name B-930-FITAP Moves In and Out of State Effective Date May 1, 2023

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

A PERSON CANNOT PARTICIPATE AS A MEMBER OF MORE THAN ONE HOUSEHOLD OR IN MORE THAN ONE *** STATE IN ANY MONTH.

***

II. PROCEDURES

* WHEN AN APPLICANT HAS RECEIVED BENEFITS IN ANOTHER STATE WITHIN SIX MONTHS PRIOR TO THE APPLICATION DATE, VERIFY THE EFFECTIVE CLOSURE DATE, OR THE DATE THE APPLICANT AND/OR MEMBERS OF THE APPLICATION WERE REMOVED FROM THE OUT OF STATE CERTIFICATION.

IF BENEFITS WERE AUTHORIZED FOR THE MONTH OF APPLICATION VERIFY IF BENEFITS HAVE BEEN RETURNED OR CANCELED BY THE OTHER STATE.

OUT-OF-STATE-INQUIRIES

THE ANALYST MUST CONTACT THE STATE AGENCY TO REQUEST CLOSURE OF THE ACTIVE FITAP CASE DUE TO THE APPLICANT NOW RESIDING AND APPLYING FOR BENEFITS IN LOUISIANA.  THE ANALYST SHOULD ATTEMPT TO CONTACT THE STATE BY PHONE IN ORDER TO REPORT THE APPLICANT IS NOW RESIDING AND APPLYING FOR BENEFITS IN LOUISIANA.

 IF THE PHONE ATTEMPT IS UNSUCCESSFUL, AN OFS 82 (OUT-OF-STAE INQUIRY) FORM MUST BE FAXED TO THE STATE AGENCY.

VERIFICATION OF THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF CLOSURE FOR THE OUT-OF-STATE FITAP CASE MUST BE REQEUSTED FROM THE APPLICANT.

 IN ORDER FOR LITE TO REQUEST THE VERIFICATION FROM THE APPLICANT, BOTH A “BENEFIT BEGIN DATE” AND “BENEFIT END DATE” MUST BE INPUT ON THE OUT OF STATE BENEFIT DETAILS SCREEN.

 THE “BENEFIT BEGIN DATE” AND “BENEFIT END DATE” SHOULD MATCH.

 IF A “BENEFIT END DATE” IS NOT POPULATED, LITE WILL NOT REQUEST THE VERIFICATION AS REQUIRED.

 “PENDING VERIFICATION” MUST BE SELECTED FOR THE “TERMINATION VERIFICATION” FIELD.

 IF THE OFS 82 IS NOT RETURNED BY THE OTHER STATE AND THE APPLICANT DOES NOT PROVIDE VERIFICATION OF THE EFFECTIVE DATE OF CLOSURE FOR THE OUT-OF-STATE SNAP CASE, ANOTHER INQUIRY SHOULD BE MADE WITH THE INTERACTIVE VOICE RESPONSE SYSTEM ON DAY 30. IF THE CASE IS STILL REPORTED AS ACTIVE, THE APPLICATION SHOULD BE DENIED OR THE MEMBER REMOVED FOR RECEIPT OF BENEFITS OUT-OF-STATE.

 * If the applicant reported that their SNAP case is closed in the other state and both the applicant and the worker are unable to verify that the SNAP case is closed in the other state, the applicant’s statement that the SNAP case is closed may be accepted if duplicate participation is not considered questionable. **

EXCEPTION: Residents in an approved shelter for battered women and children may participate twice during the month of application if they participated first with the person who abused or threatened them with abuse. The abused person must go directly from the household to the shelter.

NOTE: Receipt of Nutrition Assistance Program (NAP) benefits from Puerto Rico, American Samoa, or the Mariana Islands during the same month as SNAP benefits are received is not considered duplicate participation because NAP benefits are considered inaccessible in the mainland United States.

When all household members move to another state, close the case and send a concurrent notice to the last known address.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

OFS 082 Form/ Instructions Out-of-State Inquiry

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name B – Eligibility Factors Section No./Name B-900-FITAP Residency Document No./Name B-940-FITAP Temporary Visits Out of State Effective Date May 1, 2023

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Clients do not lose their residence status because of temporary absences from the state when the client intends to return.

II. PROCEDURES

* When notified that the client is temporarily out of state contact the client to discuss:

● the client's circumstances,

● the client’s reason for not returning,

● the client’s plans for returning,

● the client’s evidence of maintenance of residency in Louisiana and intent to return.

Good cause for absence from the home should be explored. Refer to policy B-520-FITAP. If it is determined that good cause exists the client may receive benefits while out of state according to the time frames established in policy B-520-FITAP. Update LITE to reflect the information received as well as the good cause reason established.

In the 6th month, contact the client to determine if they have returned to the state. If the client has not returned they are no longer eligible for benefits.

EXCEPTION: Temporary absence does not apply to migrants or itinerant workers. Once the person leaves the state they must not be considered a resident of the state.

II. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C-Case Processing(SNAP) Section No./Name C-100-SNAP Household Determination (SNAP) Document No./Name C-110-SNAP Household Definitions Effective Date June 27, 2011

1 of 1 C-111-SNAP RESERVED

C-112-SNAP HOUSEHOLDS

A SNAP household is a person or a group of persons living together who usually purchase and prepare food together.

This includes a person who * is away from home for employment purposes only, ** has not established permanent residence elsewhere, returns home at least one day each month, and is considered a member of the household by the household. * This also includes a person who is away from the home temporarily for a vacation, has not established permanent residence elsewhere, and is considered a member of the household by the household. **

C-112-1-SNAP Public Assistance (PA) Household

● All members receive FITAP or KCSP.

● Some members receive FITAP, KCSP and all other members receive SSI, including SSI essential

persons.

● All members receive SSI, including SSI essential persons.

C-112-2-SNAP Non-Public Assistance (NPA) Household

● All others not classified as PA.

C-113-SNAP HEAD OF THE HOUSEHOLD

The head of the household is a member of the household who usually has primary financial responsibility. The worker determines which member will be head of the household except as specified in C-113-1-SNAP. The case is certified in this name.

C-113-1-SNAP Designation of "Adult Parent of Child(ren)" as Head of Household

Households which include an adult parent with children must be offered the option of selecting the head of household. These households will be allowed to select an adult parent of children in the household as the head when all adult household members making application agree to the selection. The household may designate the head of household at each certification, but the designation may not change during a certification period unless the household composition changes. If the adult members fail to agree, the worker must designate the head.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 04 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-100 FITAP-SNAP Household Determination Document No./Name C-120-FITAP Who Is Included in the Assistance Unit Effective Date October 1, 2017

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The following persons living in the home must be included in the assistance unit with the exceptions noted below:

C-121-FITAP PO WHO MUST BE INCLUDED

● The dependent child, including the minor unmarried parent,

● The dependent child's siblings under age 18, including half siblings and legal step siblings,

● The parents of the dependent children who are included,

● The legal stepparent of the dependent child, and

● The minor unmarried parent's child(ren).

Upon determination of who may or must be included, two-parent eligibility must be considered as per C-1510-FITAP.

EXCEPTIONS:

● The person is an SSI recipient or an SSI eligible with suspended payments. (Not included in Federal Participation Rate)

● The person does not meet the citizenship requirement. (Not included in Federal Participation Rate)

● The parental relationship has been terminated through adoption.

● The person does not meet the enumeration requirements. (Included in Federal Participation Rate)

● The parent is a convicted offender per C-140-FITAP. (Included in Federal Participation Rate)

● The child is provided either federal or state foster care payments. (Included in Federal Participation Rate)

● The person is disqualified due to an intentional program violation. (Included in Federal Participation Rate)

● The person is a fleeing felon or a probation/parole violator. (Refer to document C-140-FITAP.) (Included in Federal Participation Rate)

● A qualified relative other than a parent if the parent does not live in the home and if the qualified relative does not have minor children in the home. If the qualified relative is married, the spouse must also be included. (Included in Federal Participation Rate)

● The caretaker relative, including a minor unmarried parent, may be certified when all of the children in the home receive SSI and the caretaker relative and the children would be eligible if the children were not SSI recipients. The SSI child(ren) is not subject to the FITAP requirement of immunization, school attendance, or parenting skills training. (Included in Federal Participation Rate)

● A woman who is pregnant when there is no eligible child in the home. If the father of the unborn child or the spouse of the pregnant woman is in the home, he must be included. The baby must be expected to be born within 3 months. (Included in Federal Participation Rate)

NOTE: Pregnancy and expected date of delivery must be verified by a statement from a medical facility such as a hospital, clinic, health unit or a physician's office.

If Due Date Is: Then Certify Effective: April January May February June March July April August May September June October July November August December September January October February November March December

Upon determination of who may or must be included, two-parent eligibility must be considered as per C-1510-FITAP.

● The biological parent whose legal relationship to the child has been terminated through adoption may be included as a qualified relative other than a parent. (Included in Federal Participation Rate)

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 04 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-100-FITAP-SNAP Household Determination Document No./Name C-120-SNAP Who Is Included in the Household Effective Date October 1, 2017

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

C-121-SNAP WHO MUST BE INCLUDED

Certify the following people as a SNAP household:

1. A person who lives alone.

2. A group of people living together who usually purchase food and prepare meals together.

3. A person or group of people who live with others but usually purchase and prepare food separately from the others. Note: It does not matter who actually purchases and prepares the food, as long as the food is purchased and prepared separately.

4. A person or group of people who live with others but intend to purchase and prepare food separately after certification.

5. A person or group of people who are disabled residents of an authorized group living arrangement and who receive benefits under Title II or Title XVI of the Social Security Act.

6. A narcotic addict or alcoholic, and their children, residing and participating in a drug or alcohol treatment program.

7. A resident in a public or private non-profit facility that serves battered women and children. Consider people temporarily residing in shelters for battered women and children as individual household units if they apply for and receive SNAP.

8. A resident of federally subsidized housing for the elderly.

9. A person age 60 or over (and * his or her ** spouse) who resides with others but is unable to purchase and prepare food separately from the others because of permanent disability or disability considered permanent under the Social Security Act. (Refer to C-1523-SNAP.) The gross income of * the ** other household members (excluding * the ** elderly person and * his or her ** spouse) cannot exceed 165% of the * poverty ** limit for the number of * the ** other people.

The elderly person must:

● verify the other's income, and

● prove his disability if questionable.

Agency Name Office of Family Support (OFS) Chapter No./Name 04 – Family Assistance Manual (FAM) Part No./Name C. Case Processing (FITAP) Section No./Name C-100 FITAP Household Determination (FITAP) Document No./Name C-130-FITAP Separate Assistance Units Dates Issue December 1, 2009 Effective December 1, 2009

1 of 2

When two or more family groups live together, each must be certified for a separate grant.

A family group consists of:

● Minor children who are siblings, including half and step siblings, and

● Parents (natural, adoptive, or step) of these children or eligible qualified relatives

Siblings and their parents are a family group. Children who are not siblings are separate family groups.

A person may be payee of two or more grants, but may be included in only one grant. ***

Examples of Assistance Units:

● A man and woman live in non-legal union and both have children of prior unions, but have no children together. The woman and her children are one family group and the man and his children are a separate family group. Certify each group separately.

● In the same example, if the man and woman have a child of their union in addition to the children of their separate unions, the entire family group must be included in one grant.

● A man and woman are not legally married, and have only children of their union. The family would be eligible for a single FITAP payment, if all other eligibility requirements are met. Either the man or the woman could be payee of the grant and both parents would be included as FITAP parents.

● A man and woman are legally married, each having children of a prior union. All of the eligible children and their parent(s) must be included in one certification. Either of the parents may be payee for all of the eligible children. If they have a child together, that child must be included in the certification.

● A mother, her minor daughter, her minor daughter's child and another grandchild live in the home. The mother, daughter and daughter's child must be included in one certification and the mother must be payee of a separate grant for her other grandchild.

● A mother, her two minor children, one of whom is a minor unmarried parent, and the minor unmarried parent's child live in the home. The minor unmarried parent receives SSI. The mother, her minor child who is not the minor unmarried parent and the child of the minor unmarried parent must be included in one certification.

● A mother, her minor child, her nephew and a grandchild live in the home. The mother and her child must be included in one certification and the mother must be payee of a second grant for her nephew and of a third grant for her grandchild.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C-Case Processing (SNAP) Section No./Name C-100-SNAP Household Determination (SNAP) Document No./Name C-130-SNAP Separate Households Effective Date June 27, 2011

1 of 3 Do not certify the following people as a separate household if they live together.

● Parents and children age 21 or younger (natural, adopted, or step).

EXCEPTION: Parents and their children may apply separately if one of the parents meets the criteria in number 9 of section C-121-SNAP of C-120-SNAP.

● A child (other than a natural, adopted, or stepchild) under 18 and adult household members with parental control of the child. A child is considered to be under parental control if the child is financially or otherwise dependent on an adult member of the household. The worker must make that determination.

EXCEPTIONS:

o The household may choose to consider a foster child as a boarder instead of a household member.

o Allow a child under 18 who purchases and prepares meals separately to apply separately if the child is:

 married and living with a spouse or

 the parent of a minor child living in the home.

● Spouses as defined in A-110-FITAP/SNAP.

NOTE: Consider parents, children, and spouses, as described above, to be living together even when one person:

● is away from home for employment purposes only, has not established permanent residence elsewhere, and returns home at least one day a month. * ● is away from the home temporarily for a vacation and has not established permanent residence elsewhere. **

Certify the following persons as separate households unless they fall into one of the three previous categories:

● A roomer who pays for lodging but not meals. ● A live-in attendant.

C-131-SNAP SEPARATE HOUSEHOLD STATUS CHART

Definition of household: A person or group of persons living together who usually purchase food and prepare meals together.

Can Separate Household Status be granted? Circumstances Yes / No Parents and children living together, purchasing and preparing meals separately Child 21 or under No Child 22 or over Yes Child under 18 living with adults who are not their parents, and purchasing and preparing meals separately Unmarried with no children & under parental control of adult household member No Living with their minor child or married and living with their spouse

Note: Minors who live with adults other than their parents, who are married and living with spouse or their minor child are not considered to be under the parental control of the adult household member. Yes Not under parental control of adult household member Yes Spouses living together purchasing and preparing meals separately (See A-110-SNAP for definition of spouse.) No

Note: A person age 60 or over (and spouse) who resides with others, but is unable to purchase and prepare meals separately from the others because of a disability can be certified as a separate household, regardless of the fact that the person’s meals are not purchased and prepared separately. The gross income of other household members cannot exceed 165% of the net income limit for the number of other people. (See C-120-SNAP)

C-132-SNAP CHILDREN WHO LIVE IN MORE THAN ONE HOME

C-132-1-SNAP Joint Custody

If a child lives in more than one home because the child’s parents, or the persons acting as parents, do not live together and they share joint custody, the child may be included in the SNAP household for either home. If the parents, or persons acting as parents, agree about which household will receive SNAP benefits for the child, they should be given the opportunity to make the choice concerning which case should include the child. However, if they cannot agree, the agency will make the decision. In most instances, the child will be included in the SNAP household where he lives the majority of the time.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C-Case Processing (SNAP) Section No./Name C-100-SNAP Household Determination (SNAP) Document No./Name C-130-SNAP Separate Households Effective Date June 27, 2011

3 of 3 Example: Parents have joint custody. The child stays with his mother the majority of the time and with his father every other weekend and two weeks during the summer. The father applies for SNAP benefits. Since joint custody exists:

● If the mother does not receive SNAP benefits, the child can be included in the father’s SNAP household.

● If the mother receives SNAP benefits, the child can be included in the father’s SNAP household only if the child is not included in the mother’s SNAP household and the mother approved the inclusion of the child in the father’s SNAP household. In this situation, the mother makes the decision because the child lives with her the majority of the time.

C-132-2-SNAP Sole Custody

When joint custody does not exist and the child lives with one parent, or with a person acting as a parent, and visits periodically in the home of the other parent, he is not a member of the SNAP household of the home in which he visits.

Example: Parents do not have joint custody. The child lives with his mother and visits in his father’s home every other weekend and two weeks during the summer. The father applies for SNAP benefits. The child cannot be included in his father’s SNAP household since the child only visits in the father’s home.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 04 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-100 FITAP-SNAP Household Determination Document No./Name C-140-FITAP Who Is Not Included in the Assistance Unit Effective Date October 1, 2017

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Do not include the following in the assistance unit:

● SSI recipients. Remove a FITAP family member from the grant when the person is certified for SSI. Do not count income or resources belonging only to the SSI recipient.

● INDIVIDUALS FLEEING TO AVOID PROSECUTION, CUSTODY OR CONFINEMENT AFTER CONVICTION FOR COMMITTING A CRIME OR ATTEMPTING TO COMMIT A CRIME THAT WOULD BE CLASSIFIED AS A FELONY (OR HIGH MISDEMEANOR IN NEW JERSEY) UNDER THE LAW OF THE PLACE FROM WHICH THE INDIVIDUAL IS FLEEING. This does not apply with respect to conduct of an individual, for any month beginning after the President of the United States grants a pardon with respect to the conduct. REFER TO E-240-FITAP.

● INDIVIDUALS VIOLATING A CONDITION OF PROBATION OR PAROLE IMPOSED UNDER A FEDERAL OR STATE LAW. THE DETERMINATION THAT A PERSON HAS VIOLATED HIS OR HER PROBATION OR PAROLE CAN ONLY BE MADE BY THE LOUISIANA PAROLE BOARD OR THE COURT SYSTEM. This does not apply with respect to conduct of an individual, for any month beginning after the President of the United States grants a pardon with respect to the conduct. REFER TO E-240-FITAP.

● Individuals found guilty of having made a fraudulent statement or representation with respect to residence in order to receive assistance simultaneously from two or more states are ineligible for a ten year period that begins on the date the individual is convicted in Federal or State Court. This does not apply if the President of the United States grants a pardon with respect to the conduct which was the subject of the conviction.

***

II. PROCEDURES

Add the eligible household member(s) to LAMI and exclude ineligible members from the FITAP household using the appropriate LAMI Inclusion/Exclusion Code and Inclusion/Exclusion Reason Code on the Register/Maintain Members by Case Screen.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms associated with this policy.

IV. REFERENCES

‘‘Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996’’. H. R. 3734 -34; H. R. 3734 – 35

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Do not include the following in the certified SNAP household:

• Non-household members who reside with the certified SNAP household.

Non-household members are:

o Roomers,

o Live-in attendants,

o Students who are ineligible, or

o Others sharing living quarters but purchasing and preparing meals separately.

• Disqualified persons during their period of disqualification. (SSN, IPV, work registration or ABAWD work requirement)

• Boarders. Boarders cannot receive SNAP separately from the household with whom they are living.

• Ineligible aliens who reside with the household. This includes members who are excluded because the alien does not wish INS to be contacted to verify his immigration status.

• Institutional residents who receive more than half their meals from an institution that is not authorized to accept SNAP.

EXCEPTION: This does not include people eligible as members of group living arrangements; residents of alcohol/narcotic centers together with their children; shelters for battered women and children; federally subsidized housing for the elderly; or individuals who are residents of public or private non-profit shelters for homeless persons.

• New household members who are certified in another household. Do not add these people to the new case until they are removed from the old one.

EXCEPTION: Residents in shelters for battered women and children can receive up to 2 allotments in 1 month if:

o the former household's allotment was based on a household size that included the woman and children, and

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-100-FITAP-SNAP Household Determination Document No./Name C-170-SNAP Authorized Representative Effective Date August 15, 2022

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The head of the household or other responsible household member may name a non-household member as an Authorized Representative (AR) to apply for benefits for the household. The authorized representative is someone who may act on the household’s behalf to obtain and use benefits for the household and conduct business with the agency for the household. The authorized representative has the same rights and responsibilities as the client.

Explain that the household will be held responsible if an over issuance occurs because an authorized representative gives incorrect information.

C-171-SNAP - PO RESTRICTIONS ON AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE

Persons disqualified from SNAP because of an Intentional Program Violation (IPV), may serve as authorized representative only if the agency has determined that no one else is available to serve as an authorized representative.

If no one else is available to act as authorized representative, Economic Stability (ES) employees and retailers authorized to accept the Louisiana Purchase Automated Benefit Card may serve as authorized representative only if the ES Manager gives written approval.

Under no circumstances shall an employee who is an authorized representative on a case take any action on that case. This includes, but is not limited to, certification action, interim changes, and requests for new EBT cards.

The agency may limit the number of households an authorized representative may represent in order to prevent program abuse. However, such limitations must only be set on a case-by-case basis with supervisory approval after cause has been established. If the parish office cannot establish cause and continues to suspect program abuse, the case should be referred for fraud investigation using normal procedures.

C-172-SNAP - PO AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE APPLYING FOR HOUSEHOLD

When the head of household or another household member cannot apply, a non-household member may be designated as the authorized representative. This person must be:

 An adult.

 Designated in writing by the head of the household or another responsible household member. This designation must include the name and address of the person chosen as an authorized representative, the signature of the household member making the choice, and the date. Designation made by a blind head of household requires 2 witnesses.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-100-FITAP-SNAP Household Determination Document No./Name C-170-SNAP Authorized Representative Effective Date August 15, 2022

2 of 4

If the designation is made by a household member who cannot sign his name, his mark must be witnessed by someone other than the authorized representative.

An authorized representative may be designated by completion of:

 the authorized representative section on the CAFÉ Self Service (SSP) application, simplified report or change report,

 the authorized representative item on form OFS 4APP, or OFS 4MR,

 the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) 4AR, or

 a written statement signed by the head of household, the spouse, or another responsible member of the household. The document must be scanned and indexed into OnBase.

Note: An individual who has a General Power of Attorney for the head of household may act as authorized representative without an additional written statement signed by the head of household.

Note: If the head of the household completes an application in CAFÉ SSP and names an authorized representative, this is considered designated in writing.

* Note: If the head of household or other responsible household member completes a no form application and a telephonic signature for their household, and names an authorized representative, the naming of the authorized representative is considered a written designation.

 Aware of the household circumstances. Except for drug/alcoholic treatment centers or group living facilities acting as authorized representative, the client is liable for any overissuance resulting from inaccurate information that the authorized representative gave.

The authorized representative applying for the household must sign the application.

If an AR applies for the household, the identities of both the authorized representative and the head of the household must be verified.

EXCEPTION: If it is necessary to meet expedited service time limits, you may verify identity only of the authorized representative being interviewed.

Note: If the AR completes a No Form interview and the telephonic signature on behalf of the household, written designation signed by the head of household, or another responsible household member is required. To request the written designation, send a Free Form Contact Letter and attach a SNAP 4AR to the request. **

3 of 4

C-173-SNAP - PO DISQUALIFICATION OF AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE

If the local office obtains evidence that an authorized representative has misrepresented a household's circumstances, knowingly provided false information, or made improper use of benefits, the local office must disqualify the authorized representative from participating as an authorized representative for up to one year.

Use form SNAP 13A to notify the household and the authorized representative 30 days prior to the date of disqualification.

C-174-SNAP - PO AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

Enter the name and address of the authorized representative in the case record. Document on the Form 4APP or file the written statement in the case record.

If a person disqualified for intentional program violation, is appointed, document that no one else is available to be an authorized representative. Document in the narrative. Documentation is required when an ES employee or retailer employees are approved as authorized representative.

II. PROCEDURES

C-171-SNAP - PR RESTRICTIONS ON AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE

To determine if an AR is disqualified due to an IPV sanction the following steps should be taken:  Navigate to LITE.  Select ‘Search’ from the Main Navigation Bar.  Select ‘Case’ from the Sub-Navigation Tab.  Select the magnifying glass on the Case – Search Summary Page.  Enter the individual’s identifying information on the Case – Search pop up screen.  Click ‘search’. o If the individual is known to LITE case search results will display on the bottom of the page o If the individual is not known to LITE, the results will be blank validating that the individual does not have an intentional program violation (IPV)  Check the box next the individual.  Click ‘submit’.  Click ‘search’ on the Case – Search/Summary screen, after the individual’s case identification number (CID) populates  Click the CID hyperlink on the Case – Search/Summary screen.  Select inquiry (read only mode) on the ‘Initiate Data Collection Page’.  Click Next.  Click others tab in the Data Collection Page submenu.  Select ‘compliance’ from the drop down menu.

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

THE ‘SCAN DATE’ IN ONBASE SHOULD BE USED AS THE DATE OF RECEIPT ON DOCUMENTS RECEIVED BY MAIL OR FAX THROUGH THE DOCUMENT PROCESSING CENTER (DPC) WHEN DETERMINING THE APPLICATION DATE OR THE DATE VERIFICATION IS RECEIVED. THE PSI: CAPTURE SYSTEM CAPTURES THE SCAN DATE/TIME AND FAX DATE/TIME WHICH IS THE ACTUAL DATE THE DOCUMENT WAS RECEIVED AT THE DPC.

II. PROCEDURES

IF THE ‘SCAN DATE’ IS AFTER 4:30 PM ON A WORKDAY, THE DATE OF RECEIPT WILL BE FOLLOWING WORKDAY. THE ‘SCAN DATE’ CAN BE LOCATED BY VIEWING ‘KEYWORDS’ WHEN SCROLLING DOWN TO THE BOTTOM OF THE FORM.

NOTE: THE ‘SCAN DATE’ CANNOT BE CHANGED BY USERS.

DOCUMENTS RECEIVED IN A DCFS OFFICE OR FAXED DIRECTLY TO THE DCFS OFFICE SHOULD BE DATE STAMPED BY THE RECEIVING OFFICE ON THE DATE OF RECEIPT PRIOR TO SCANNING THE DOCUMENTS INTO ONBASE VIA PSI: FUSION. IF A DOCUMENT IS SCANNED LOCALLY BY THE PARISH OFFICE, A ‘SCAN DATE, WILL NOT BE DISPLAYED. WHEN INDEXING THE DOCUMENT, STAFF SHOULD UPDATE THE ‘DOCUMENT DATE’ TO INDICATE THE DATE OF RECEIPT IN ONBASE. THE ‘DOCUMENT DATE’ SHOULD MATCH THE DATE STAMPED BY THE RECEIVING OFFICE. STAFF SHOULD USE THE ‘DOCUMENT DATE’ WHEN DETERMINING RECEIPT OF A DOCUMENT WHEN THERE IS NO ‘SCAN DATE’.

DOCUMENTS RECEIVED VIA EMAIL FROM THE CLIENT DIRECTLY TO THE WORKER OR TO THE OFFICE GENERIC EMAIL ADDRESS SHOULD BE SENT TO ONBASE BY USING THE HYLAND VIRTUAL PRINT OPTION. THIS INCLUDES SENDING THE EMAIL ITSELF AND THE VERIFICATION TO ONBASE. TO COMPLETE A VIRTUAL PRINT, ONBASE SHOULD BE OPEN. THE HYLAND SOFTWARE VIRTUAL PRINT CAN BE ACCESSED BY SELECTING ‘FILE’ ON THE DOCUMENT AND SELECTING ‘PRINT’. ONCE THE PRINT BOX IS POPULATED, CHANGE THE PRINTER OPTION TO ‘HYLAND SOFTWARE VIRTUAL PRINTER’, THEN SELECT PRINT. WHEN INDEXING THE DOCUMENT, STAFF SHOULD UPDATE THE ‘DOCUMENT DATE’ TO INDICATE THE DATE OF RECEIPT OF THE EMAIL IN ONBASE. THE ‘DOCUMENT DATE’ SHOULD MATCH THE DATE THE EMAIL WAS RECEIVED.

NOTE: THE ‘POSTMARK DATE’ WILL ONLY BE USED TO DETERMINE IF A FAIR HEARING REQUEST IS TIMELY RECEIVED FROM THE CLIENT BY THE AGENCY.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

THERE ARE NO FORMS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS POLICY.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C-Case Processing (FITAP) Section No./Name C-1100-FITAP-SNAP Verification Document No./Name C-1120-FITAP Sources of Verification Effective Date June 1, 2016

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

C-1121-FITAP * - PO ** DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE

DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE IS WRITTEN CONFIRMATION OF A HOUSEHOLD'S CIRCUMSTANCES, SUCH AS CHECK STUBS, CONTRIBUTION STATEMENTS, UTILITY BILLS, ETC.

USE DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE AS THE PRIMARY SOURCE OF VERIFICATION. OBTAIN VERIFICATION FROM THE HOUSEHOLD OR OTHER SOURCE.

DO NOT REQUIRE ANY SINGLE TYPE OF DOCUMENT. ACCEPT ANY REASONABLE DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE IF THE VERIFICATION PROVES THE HOUSEHOLD'S STATEMENTS.

***

DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE MAY BE CONSIDERED INSUFFICIENT IF IT DOES NOT PROVIDE AN ACCURATE PICTURE OF THE HOUSEHOLD'S SITUATION OR APPEARS TO BE FALSIFIED.

***

C-1122-FITAP * - PO ** COLLATERALS

COLLATERALS ARE THIRD PARTY VERIFICATION OF A HOUSEHOLD'S CIRCUMSTANCES.

* THE COLLATERAL MUST BE ABLE TO VERIFY EACH PERSON WHO LIVES IN THE HOME AND THE ADDRESS WHERE THE FAMILY LIVES. **

IT MAY BE NECESSARY TO CONTACT A COLLATERAL SOURCE TO DETERMINE ELIGIBILITY WHEN AN ELIGIBILITY DECISION CANNOT BE MADE BASED ON:

● THE CLIENT'S STATEMENT,

● DOCUMENTS PROVIDED BY THE CLIENT,

● INFORMATION OBTAINED FROM PUBLIC RECORDS, OR

● WHEN OTHER NECESSARY DOCUMENTARY INFORMATION CANNOT BE OBTAINED.

C-1122-1-FITAP * - PO ** Selection of a Collateral Source

2 of 4 Collateral sources may be selected by the client or the worker. WHEN THE CLIENT SUGGESTS A COLLATERAL, THE WORKER SHOULD EVALUATE THE RELIABILITY OF THIS PERSON. IF THE WORKER QUESTIONS WHETHER THE COLLATERAL IS ABLE TO PROVIDE ACCURATE INFORMATION, THE WORKER SHOULD SELECT ANOTHER COLLATERAL.

The client may withdraw his application if he does not want the worker to make necessary collateral contacts.

The client's consent is not required prior to contacting a collateral.

***

C-1122-2-FITAP * - PO ** Confidentiality

AVOID TELLING THE COLLATERAL THAT THE CLIENT HAS APPLIED FOR OR IS RECEIVING ASSISTANCE.

***

C-1122-3-FITAP * - PO ** Evaluation of Collateral Information

WHEN THE COLLATERAL CONTRADICTS INFORMATION PROVIDED BY A CLIENT, DO NOT MAKE A DECISION BASED SOLELY ON INFORMATION PROVIDED BY THE COLLATERAL.

***

C-1122-4-FITAP * - PO ** Documentation

Confirm the collateral statement in writing ***. Record the collateral's name, phone number, and address.

***

C-1122-5-FITAP * - PO ** Questionable Information

CONSIDER THE CLIENT'S STATEMENTS ON THE APPLICATION, *** SIMPLIFIED REPORT, OR DURING THE INTERVIEW * TO BE ** QUESTIONABLE IF THEY:

● ARE CONTRADICTORY.

EXAMPLE: CLIENT STATES THAT HE HAS HAD NO INCOME FOR SEVERAL MONTHS BUT HIS BILLS ARE PAID.
