3 of 4

● DO NOT AGREE WITH INFORMATION IN THE CASE RECORD.

EXAMPLE: CLIENT PROVIDES AN EMPLOYER STATEMENT SHOWING A 40 HOUR WEEK WHEN CASE RECORD DOCUMENTATION SHOWS FREQUENT OVERTIME.

● DO NOT ADEQUATELY EXPLAIN THE HOUSEHOLD'S CIRCUMSTANCES.

EXAMPLE: APPLICANT STATES THAT HE HAS NOT PAID RENT OR UTILITIES FOR SEVERAL MONTHS, BUT HE HAS NOT BEEN EVICTED OR HAD HIS UTILITIES DISCONNECTED.

● DO NOT AGREE WITH INFORMATION OBTAINED FROM THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY.

EXAMPLE: APPLICANT STATES THAT THEY ARE NOT WORKING BUT CURRENT WAGES ARE REPORTED BY THE WORK NUMBER.

***

II. PROCEDURES

* C-1121-FITAP - PR DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE **

* USE ALTERNATE SOURCES OF VERIFICATION IF DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE CANNOT BE OBTAINED OR IS NOT SUFFICIENT TO MAKE A FIRM DETERMINATION OF ELIGIBILITY OR BENEFIT LEVEL.

RECORD THE DATE RECEIVED ON ALL DOCUMENTS SUBMITTED TO THE AGENCY BY USING A DATE STAMP. THE ENVELOPE AND THE DOCUMENT MUST BE FILED INTO ONBASE. WHEN ORIGINAL DOCUMENTS SUCH AS BIRTH CERTIFICATES, MARRIAGE LICENSES, SOCIAL SECURITY CARDS, CHECK STUBS, ETC. ARE SUBMITTED, THE WORKER MUST MAKE A COPY OF THE DOCUMENT, RECORD THE RECEIPT DATE ON THE COPY, AND RETURN THE ORIGINAL DOCUMENT TO THE CLIENT.

C-1122-FITAP - PR COLLATERALS

THERE ARE NO PROCEDURES ASSOCIATED WITH THIS POLICY.

C-1122-1-FITAP - PR Selection of a Collateral Source

SELECT AS A COLLATERAL SOURCE A PERSON WHO IS IN A POSITION TO PROVIDE ACCURATE THIRD PARTY VERIFICATION OF THE ISSUE IN QUESTION AND WHO DOES NOT HAVE A VESTED INTEREST IN THE CLIENT'S SITUATION. RELATIVES SHOULD ONLY BE USED WHEN OTHER COLLATERALS ARE NOT AVAILABLE.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C-Case Processing (FITAP) Section No./Name C-1100 FITAP Verification (FITAP) Document No./Name C-1130-FITAP Responsibility For Obtaining Verification Effective Date July 1, 2011

1 of 2 C-1131-FITAP WORKER RESPONSIBILITY

THE WORKER IS RESPONSIBLE FOR:

● EVALUATING THE CLIENT'S CAPABILITY FOR PROVIDING OR OBTAINING NEEDED

INFORMATION,

● INFORMING THE HOUSEHOLD IN WRITING OF WHAT THE CLIENT MUST DO OR WHAT

INFORMATION IS NEEDED,

● ALLOWING AT LEAST 10 DAYS FOR THE CLIENT TO PROVIDE THE INFORMATION OR

VERIFICATION OR TO ADVISE THE WORKER THAT HE IS UNABLE TO SECURE THE

REQUESTED INFORMATION. IF THE 10TH DAY FALLS ON A WEEKEND OR HOLIDAY, THE

DUE DATE BECOMES THE FOLLOWING WORKDAY.

***

● OFFERING ASSISTANCE TO THE CLIENT TO OBTAIN THE NEEDED INFORMATION OR TO

IDENTIFY AND SECURE ALTERNATE INFORMATION WHEN THE INFORMATION

ORIGINALLY REQUESTED CANNOT BE OBTAINED,

● ASSISTING THE CLIENT IN DESIGNATING A COLLATERAL CONTACT, IF REQUESTED BY

THE CLIENT,

● EVALUATING THE ACCURACY AND ADEQUACY OF VERIFICATIONS, TO ENSURE THAT

EVIDENCE IS ENOUGH TO MAKE A VALID DECISION OF ELIGIBILITY AND BENEFIT LEVEL,

● ACCEPTING REASONABLE DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE GIVEN BY THE CLIENT OR REASONABLE COLLATERAL SOURCES DESIGNATED BY THE CLIENT. DO NOT INSIST ON ONE TYPE OF VERIFICATION AND EXCLUDE OTHER REASONABLE SOURCES.

C-1132-FITAP CLIENT RESPONSIBILITY

THE CLIENT HAS PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY FOR PROVIDING DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE NEEDED FOR PROOF OF THE HOUSEHOLD'S CIRCUMSTANCES.

DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE MAY BE PROVIDED IN PERSON, THROUGH THE MAIL, THROUGH ELECTRONIC TRANSMISSION (SUCH AS FAX) OR THROUGH AN AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE.

IF DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE IS NOT AVAILABLE OR SUFFICIENT, THE CLIENT MUST DESIGNATE A THIRD PARTY SOURCE FOR THE INFORMATION OR PERMIT A HOME VISIT.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C-Case Processing (FITAP) Section No./Name C-1100 FITAP Verification (FITAP) Document No./Name C-1130-FITAP Responsibility For Obtaining Verification Effective Date July 1, 2011

2 of 2 C-1133-FITAP HOME VISITS

HOME VISITS ARE WORKER CONTACTS AT THE HOUSEHOLD'S RESIDENCE TO VERIFY THE HOUSEHOLD'S CIRCUMSTANCES.

MAKE A HOME VISIT WHEN THERE ARE QUESTIONS WHICH CANNOT BE OTHERWISE RESOLVED REGARDING HOUSEHOLD COMPOSITION, INCOME, MANAGEMENT OR OTHER FACTORS WHICH COULD AFFECT ELIGIBILITY OR BENEFIT LEVEL.

MAKE HOME VISITS DURING THE USUAL WORK HOURS, UNLESS THE CLIENT REQUESTS A VISIT OUTSIDE REGULAR WORK HOURS BECAUSE OF EMPLOYMENT, ETC.

Advance scheduling of the home visit is not required.

OBSERVE THE HOUSEHOLD'S LIVING ARRANGEMENTS, BELONGINGS, AND LIFESTYLE.

DO NOT ENGAGE IN ANY PRACTICES WHICH MIGHT BE CONSIDERED AS HARASSMENT TO THE CLIENT, AND AVOID ANY APPEARANCE OF MAKING A SEARCH OF THE CLIENT'S HOME.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C-Case Processing (SNAP) Section No./Name C-1100- Verification (SNAP) Document No./Name C-1130-SNAP Responsibility For Obtaining Verification Effective Date July 1, 2011

1 of 2 C-1131-SNAP WORKER RESPONSIBILITY

THE WORKER IS RESPONSIBLE FOR:

● EVALUATING THE CLIENT'S CAPABILITY FOR PROVIDING OR OBTAINING NEEDED INFORMATION,

● INFORMING THE HOUSEHOLD IN WRITING OF WHAT THE CLIENT MUST DO OR WHAT INFORMATION IS NEEDED,

● ALLOWING AT LEAST 10 DAYS FOR THE CLIENT TO PROVIDE THE INFORMATION OR VERIFICATION OR TO ADVISE THE WORKER THAT HE IS UNABLE TO SECURE THE REQUESTED INFORMATION. IF THE 10TH DAY FALLS ON A WEEKEND OR HOLIDAY, THE DUE DATE BECOMES THE FOLLOWING WORKDAY.

***

● OFFERING ASSISTANCE TO THE CLIENT TO OBTAIN THE NEEDED INFORMATION OR TO IDENTIFY AND SECURE ALTERNATE INFORMATION WHEN THE INFORMATION ORIGINALLY REQUESTED CANNOT BE OBTAINED,

● ASSISTING THE CLIENT IN DESIGNATING A COLLATERAL CONTACT, IF REQUESTED BY THE CLIENT,

● EVALUATING THE ACCURACY AND ADEQUACY OF VERIFICATIONS, TO ENSURE THAT EVIDENCE IS ENOUGH TO MAKE A VALID DECISION OF ELIGIBILITY AND BENEFIT LEVEL,

● ACCEPTING REASONABLE DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE GIVEN BY THE CLIENT OR REASONABLE COLLATERAL SOURCES DESIGNATED BY THE CLIENT. DO NOT INSIST ON ONE TYPE OF VERIFICATION AND EXCLUDE OTHER REASONABLE SOURCES.

C-1132-SNAP CLIENT RESPONSIBILITY

THE CLIENT HAS PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY FOR PROVIDING DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE NEEDED FOR PROOF OF THE HOUSEHOLD'S CIRCUMSTANCES.

DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE MAY BE PROVIDED IN PERSON, THROUGH THE MAIL, THROUGH ELECTRONIC TRANSMISSION (SUCH AS FAX) OR THROUGH AN AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE.

IF DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE IS NOT AVAILABLE OR SUFFICIENT, THE CLIENT MUST DESIGNATE A THIRD PARTY SOURCE FOR THE INFORMATION OR PERMIT A HOME VISIT.

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

DOCUMENT INFORMATION AS A CASE NOTE TO SUPPORT ALL DECISIONS ABOUT ELIGIBILITY AND BENEFIT AMOUNT. DOCUMENT THE INFORMATION IN ENOUGH DETAIL SO THAT ALL COMPUTATIONS AND WORKER DECISIONS CAN BE UNDERSTOOD.

II. PROCEDURES

DOCUMENT THE FOLLOWING:

● MANDATORY VERIFICATIONS,

● WHY CERTAIN INFORMATION IS QUESTIONABLE,

● HOW QUESTIONABLE INFORMATION IS CLEARED,

ADEQUATE DOCUMENTATION OF VERIFICATION CONSISTS OF RECORDING THE:

● TYPE OR SOURCE OF VERIFICATION,

● DATE OF VERIFICATION, AND

● LOCATION OF VERIFICATION, IF NOT FILED IN THE SAME CASE RECORD.

DOCUMENT EVERY CASE ACTIVITY *** * IN CAFÉ, ** INCLUDING A VERY BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTIVITY.

USE NARRATIVE ENTRIES TO RECORD INFORMATION WHICH IS NOT RECORDED ON FORMS OR WHICH NEEDS MORE EXPLANATION.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

THERE ARE NO FORMS OR INSTRUCTIONS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS POLICY.

IV. REFERENCES

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C-Case Processing (FITAP) Section No./Name C-1300 FITAP Cooperation (FITAP) Document No./Name C-1310-FITAP Cooperation Requirements Effective Date October 6, 2014

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

THE CLIENT MUST COOPERATE IN THE PROCESS OF DETERMINING ELIGIBILITY BY COMPLETING AN APPLICATION, BEING INTERVIEWED, AND PROVIDING REQUIRED INFORMATION.

DO NOT ASK THE CLIENT TO PROVIDE INFORMATION WHICH IS CLEARLY IMPOSSIBLE TO SECURE, SUCH AS CHECK STUBS FOR A CLIENT WHO IS PAID IN CASH OR THE ADDRESS OF A PERSON THE CLIENT CANNOT LOCATE.

IF THE WORKER HAS FULFILLED HIS RESPONSIBILITIES, BUT THE CLIENT FAILS TO PROVIDE INFORMATION HE AGREED TO PROVIDE WHICH IS NECESSARY TO COMPLETE THE ELIGIBILITY DETERMINATION PROCESS, TAKE ACTION TO DENY THE APPLICATION OR CLOSE THE CASE USING ADVERSE ACTION PROCEDURE.

C-1311-FITAP - PO APPLICATIONS

TIMELY SCHEDULE AN APPLICATION APPOINTMENT.

C-1312-FITAP- PO REDETERMINATIONS

IF THE HOUSEHOLD FAILS TO SUBMIT A TIMELY REAPPLICATION, CLOSE THE CASE ON THE DAY AFTER THE TIMELY REAPPLICATION DUE DATE.

C-1313-FITAP- PO OTHER ELIGIBILITY REVIEWS

THE HOUSEHOLD MUST COOPERATE IN ANY SUBSEQUENT REVIEW OF ITS ELIGIBILITY, INCLUDING REVIEWS GENERATED BY:

● REPORTED CHANGES.

II. PROCEDURES

THE WORKER MUST:

● INFORM THE HOUSEHOLD IN WRITING OF WHAT THE CLIENT MUST DO OR WHAT INFORMATION IS NEEDED,

● ALLOW AT LEAST 10 DAYS FOR THE CLIENT TO PROVIDE THE INFORMATION OR VERIFICATION OR TO ADVISE THE WORKER THAT HE IS UNABLE TO SECURE THE REQUESTED INFORMATION. IF THE 10TH DAY FALLS ON A WEEKEND OR HOLIDAY, THE DUE DATE BECOMES THE FOLLOWING WORKDAY.

2 of 3 AT CERTIFICATION OR REDETERMINATION, WHEN THERE ARE LESS THAN 10 DAYS LEFT IN THE PROCESSING PERIOD, THE APPLICATION/REDETERMINATION MUST NOT BE DENIED ON OR BEFORE THE 30TH DAY FOR FAILURE TO PROVIDE VERIFICATION BUT MUST REMAIN IN PENDING/SUSPENDED STATUS. THE APPLICATION /REDETERMINATION MUST NOT BE DENIED/CLOSED FOR FAILURE TO PROVIDE VERIFICATION PRIOR TO THE DUE DATE.

● IF PARTIAL VERIFICATION IS PROVIDED, A SECOND REQUEST IS NOT NECESSARY.

● OFFER ASSISTANCE TO THE CLIENT TO OBTAIN THE NEEDED INFORMATION OR TO IDENTIFY AND SECURE ALTERNATE INFORMATION WHEN THE INFORMATION ORIGINALLY REQUESTED CANNOT BE OBTAINED.

C-1311-FITAP - PR APPLICATIONS

IF THE APPLICANT FAILS TO KEEP HIS SCHEDULED APPLICATION APPOINTMENT, ENTER THE REJECTION CODE FOR FAILURE TO KEEP AN APPOINTMENT USING DISPOSITION REASON 07 AND REJECTION CODE 04 AND DISPOSITION THE CASE ON THE DAY OF THE MISSED INTERVIEW APPOINTMENT. THE NOTICE SUPPRESSION FIELD MUST NOT BE COMPLETED. AN AUTOMATED NOTICE OF MISSED INTERVIEW WILL BE SENT TO THE APPLICANT THE FOLLOWING WORKDAY TO NOTIFY THE APPLICANT THAT THEIR SCHEDULED INTERVIEW APPOINTMENT WAS MISSED AND IT IS THEIR RESPONSIBILITY TO CONTACT THE AGENCY TO SCHEDULE ANOTHER APPOINTMENT TO BE INTERVIEWED. * IF THE APPLICANT CONTACTS THE AGENCY DURING THE 30 DAY APPLICATION PERIOD, A SECOND INTERVIEW MUST BE SCHEDULED USING AN OFS 18C. THIS INCLUDES A REQUEST THROUGH THE CUSTOMER SERVICE CENTER ON THE 30TH DAY AFTER THE PARISH OFFICE IS CLOSED. ** IF NO FURTHER ACTION IS TAKEN LAMI WILL AUTOMATICALLY REJECT THE CASE ON THE 30TH DAY FOLLOWING THE APPLICATION DATE (OR THE FOLLOWING WORKDAY IF THE 30TH DAY FALLS ON A WEEKEND OR HOLIDAY) AND CHANGE THE CASE STATUS TO CLOSED.

IF THE APPLICANT FAILS TO RESPOND TO THE REQUEST FOR THE INFORMATION OR VERIFICATION BY THE DUE DATE NOTED ON THE FORM OFS 18C *** AND DOES NOT REQUEST ADDITIONAL TIME IN WHICH TO FURNISH THE INFORMATION, DENY THE APPLICATION ON THE DAY FOLLOWING THE DUE DATE FOR RECEIPT OF THE INFORMATION.

IF THE CLIENT MISSES THE SCHEDULED APPOINTMENT, OR IF THE APPLICANT FAILS TO PROVIDE ALL INFORMATION NEEDED TO COMPLETE THE APPLICATION BY THE 30th DAY FROM THE ORIGINAL APPLICATION DATE, THE CLIENT MAY REAPPLY WITHIN 30 DAYS AFTER THE DATE OF DENIAL WITHOUT COMPLETING ANOTHER APPLICATION. SEE C-630- FITAP, SECTION C-638-FITAP, FOR FUTHER INFORMATION ON REUSE OF THE APPLICATION.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-1300-FITAP-SNAP Cooperation Document No./Name C-1310-SNAP Cooperation Requirements Effective Date January 1, 2023

1 of 5 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

THE CLIENT MUST COOPERATE IN THE PROCESS OF DETERMINING ELIGIBILITY BY COMPLETING AN APPLICATION, BEING INTERVIEWED if required, AND PROVIDING REQUIRED INFORMATION.

DO NOT ASK THE CLIENT TO PROVIDE INFORMATION WHICH IS CLEARLY IMPOSSIBLE TO SECURE, SUCH AS CHECK STUBS FOR A CLIENT WHO IS PAID IN CASH OR THE ADDRESS OF A PERSON THE CLIENT CANNOT LOCATE.

IF THE WORKER HAS FULFILLED HIS RESPONSIBILITIES, BUT THE CLIENT FAILS TO PROVIDE INFORMATION HE AGREED TO PROVIDE WHICH IS NECESSARY TO COMPLETE THE ELIGIBILITY DETERMINATION PROCESS, TAKE ACTION TO DENY THE APPLICATION OR CLOSE THE CASE USING ADVERSE ACTION PROCEDURE.

C-1311-SNAP - PO APPLICATIONS

TIMELY SCHEDULE AN APPLICATION APPOINTMENT.

C-1312-SNAP - PO REDETERMINATIONS

IF THE HOUSEHOLD FAILS TO SUBMIT A TIMELY REAPPLICATION, CLOSE THE CASE ON THE DAY AFTER THE TIMELY REAPPLICATION DUE DATE.

C-1313-SNAP - PO OTHER ELIGIBILITY REVIEWS

THE HOUSEHOLD MUST COOPERATE IN ANY SUBSEQUENT REVIEW OF ITS ELIGIBILITY, INCLUDING REVIEWS GENERATED BY:

 REPORTED CHANGES, or

 as part of a Quality Control (QC) or Federal Quality Control (QC) review.

If QC reports a change in income discovered during the QC review, action should only be taken if the change results in a benefit increase or the income exceeds the gross income limit. Action is not taken if the change would result in decreased benefits. The information is not considered verified upon receipt since additional information would be required.

Clients who fail to cooperate with QC will be referred to the local office in order for the local office to assist in getting the client to cooperate. QC notifies the local office that a client has failed to cooperate with the QC review process by sending the Quality Control Failure to Cooperate Notification (QC 9FTC). The QC 9FTC informs the local office that QC’s attempts to contact/locate the household were unsuccessful and requests assistance in contacting/locating the client.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-1300-FITAP-SNAP Cooperation Document No./Name C-1310-SNAP Cooperation Requirements Effective Date January 1, 2023

2 of 5

Upon receipt of the QC 9FTC, the worker must contact the household by telephone within 5 days and advise the household they must cooperate with QC. If the household cannot be reached by telephone, send a Client Contact Letter (OFS 18C), advising the household to contact the local office within 10 days to discuss cooperating with the QC review process.

 If the worker speaks to the client or a responsible household member and informs the household of the requirement to cooperate with QC, the worker must complete the “TO BE COMPLETED BY THE PARISH OFFICE” section of the QC 9FTC originally sent by QC. The worker must return the form to the QC reviewer the same day contact is made with the household.

 If the household fails to respond to the OFS 18C request for contact to discuss cooperating with the QC review process, no action is needed. The client’s failure to respond will continue to be considered a failure to cooperate with QC and will not result in case closure.

Quality Control (QC) notifies the local office that a household has refused to cooperate with the QC review process by sending the Quality Control Refusal to Cooperate Notification (QC 9RTC).

*** The worker must * take the following actions within two workdays of receiving the QC 9RTC:

 Send an advance notice of adverse action informing the household their case will be closed unless they cooperate with QC,  Complete the “TO BE COMPLETED BY THE PARISH OFFICE” section of the QC 9RTC originally sent by QC and return to the QC reviewer the same day the case action is completed,  Scan a copy of the completed QC 9RTC to OnBase. **  Contact the QC reviewer immediately or before the expiration of the advance notice of adverse action, if during the advance notice of adverse action period, the household indicates willingness to cooperate. If the expiration of the advance notice of adverse action period falls on a weekend or holiday, treat the following workday as the expiration day.

The worker must enter a case note documenting all activities.

Households who refuse to cooperate with QC will be disqualified, resulting in case closure. If QC indicates that the household refused to cooperate and the case is closed for refusal to cooperate with QC, the household may reapply but eligibility cannot be re-established until the member cooperates with the QC reviewer unless the time frame allowed for completion of the QC review has passed.

The time frame allowed for completion of a State QC review is 125 days from the end of the Federal Fiscal Year, which ends on September 30. The time frame allowed for completion of a Federal QC review is 9 months from the end of the Federal Fiscal Year.

3 of 5 If the case is closed because the household refused to cooperate with the State QC review in one Federal Fiscal Year and the household reapplies after February 2 of the following Federal Fiscal Year, the household may be certified, if all eligibility factors are met, and a referral to the State QC reviewer will not be necessary.

If the case is closed because the household refused to cooperate with the Federal QC review in one Federal Fiscal Year and the household reapplies after June 30 of the following Federal Fiscal Year, the household may be certified, if all eligibility factors are met, and a referral to the Federal QC reviewer will not be necessary.

If a case is closed for refusal to cooperate with QC, and the client reapplies, the worker MUST refer the household to the appropriate QC reviewer if the time frame allowed for completion of the review has not passed. If the client subsequently fails to cooperate with QC, the application must be rejected for refusal to cooperate with QC.

Example – State QC reviewer notifies the worker that client refused to cooperate with QC on May 4. If the client reapplies for SNAP before February 2 (125 days from the end of the FFY), the household MUST cooperate with the State QC reviewer and meet all eligibility requirements prior to certification. If the client reapplies February 3 or after, the household does not need to cooperate with the State QC reviewer prior to certification.

II. PROCEDURES

THE WORKER MUST:

 INFORM THE HOUSEHOLD IN WRITING OF WHAT THE CLIENT MUST DO OR WHAT INFORMATION IS NEEDED,

 ALLOW AT LEAST 10 DAYS FOR THE CLIENT TO PROVIDE THE INFORMATION OR VERIFICATION OR TO ADVISE THE WORKER THAT HE IS UNABLE TO SECURE THE REQUESTED INFORMATION. IF THE 10TH DAY FALLS ON A WEEKEND OR HOLIDAY, THE DUE DATE BECOMES THE FOLLOWING WORKDAY.

AT CERTIFICATION OR REDETERMINATION, WHEN THERE ARE LESS THAN 10 DAYS LEFT IN THE PROCESSING PERIOD, THE APPLICATION/REDETERMINATION MUST NOT BE DENIED ON OR BEFORE THE 30TH DAY FOR FAILURE TO PROVIDE VERIFICATION BUT MUST REMAIN IN PENDING/SUSPENDED STATUS. THE APPLICATION/ REDETERMINATION MUST NOT BE DENIED/CLOSED FOR FAILURE TO PROVIDE VERIFICATION PRIOR TO THE DUE DATE.

 IF PARTIAL VERIFICATION IS PROVIDED, A SECOND REQUEST IS NOT NECESSARY.

THIS INCLUDES A REQUEST THROUGH THE CUSTOMER SERVICE CENTER ON THE 30TH DAY AFTER THE PARISH OFFICE IS CLOSED. IF NO FURTHER ACTION IS TAKEN, LAMI WILL AUTOMATICALLY REJECT THE CASE ON THE 30th DAY FOLLOWING THE APPLICATION DATE (OR THE FOLLOWING WORKDAY IF THE 30th DAY FALLS ON A WEEKEND OR HOLIDAY) AND CHANGE THE CASE STATUS TO CLOSED.

IF THE APPLICANT FAILS TO RESPOND TO THE REQUEST FOR THE INFORMATION OR VERIFICATION BY THE DUE DATE NOTED ON THE FORM OFS 18C AND DOES NOT REQUEST ADDITIONAL TIME IN WHICH TO FURNISH THE INFORMATION, DENY THE APPLICATION ON THE DAY FOLLOWING THE DUE DATE FOR RECEIPT OF THE INFORMATION.

IF THE CLIENT MISSES THE SCHEDULED APPOINTMENT, OR IF THE APPLICANT FAILS TO PROVIDE ALL INFORMATION NEEDED TO COMPLETE THE APPLICATION BY THE 30th DAY FROM THE ORIGINAL DATE, THE CLIENT MAY REAPPLY WITHIN 30 DAYS AFTER THE DATE OF DENIAL WITHOUT COMPLETING ANOTHER APPLICATION. SEE C-630-SNAP, SECTION C-638-SNAP, FOR FURTHER INFORMATION ON REUSE OF THE APPLICATION.

C-1312-SNAP - PR REDETERMINATIONS

CLOSE THE CASE ON THE LAST WORKDAY OF THE LAST MONTH OF CERTIFICATION IF:

 THE CLIENT FAILS TO KEEP A REDETERMINATION APPOINTMENT WITHOUT GOOD CAUSE AFTER SUBMITTING A TIMELY REAPPLICATION, OR

 THE CLIENT FAILS TO PROVIDE REQUIRED VERIFICATION.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-1300-FITAP-SNAP Cooperation Document No./Name C-1310-SNAP Cooperation Requirements Effective Date January 1, 2023

5 of 5 C-1313-SNAP - PR OTHER ELIGIBILITY REVIEWS

When QC notifies the parish office that the household refused to cooperate with QC, the worker must sanction the household. Sanctions are entered on the Non-Compliance Details screen by selecting “Yes” to the question, “Is anyone in the household currently out of compliance or has ever been out of compliance with program requirements?”. Click the ‘NEXT’ button to navigate to the Non-Compliance – Details screen. On the Non-Compliance –Details screen, the worker selects the ‘Name’ of the Person sanctioned, enters the ‘Start/Change Date, the ‘Reported On’ date, the Non-Compliance Violation Type - ‘SNAP QC’, enters the Non-Compliance Reason - ‘Refused to Cooperate with QC (Federal) or (State)’, enters the ‘Decision Date’, and clicks the ‘ADD Non-Compliance’ button.

When eligibility is run, an automated Notice of Decision (OFS 16) is sent informing the household that their case is closed and unless they cooperate with QC by the expiration of the advance notice of adverse action, their case will remain closed.

If the household reapplies when sanctioned for refusal to cooperate with QC, the worker must send an email to the QC reviewer advising that the client reapplied. If the client subsequently fails to cooperate with QC, the application must be rejected for refusal to cooperate with QC. The sanction/non-compliance should already be entered on the individual household member, therefore when eligibility is run and the case is authorized, an automated OFS 16 will be sent informing the client their application was rejected because they refused to cooperate with QC.

Example – The client refused to cooperate with QC on April 9 and the worker entered the sanction information on the Non-Compliance – Details screen and the case closed effective May. The client reapplied on May 7 and agreed to cooperate with QC. The worker sent an email to the QC reviewer advising the client reapplied. The QC reviewer notified the worker on May 31 that the client refused to cooperate with QC. The application was rejected after eligibility was run using Denial/Closure Reason – Failure due to non-cooperation with Quality Control. An automated OFS 16 was sent to the household informing of the application rejection due to the households’ refusal to cooperate with QC.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

* OFS 016 Form / Instructions Automated Notice of Decision ** OFS 018 Form / Instructions Notice of Decision OFS 018C Form / Instructions Client Contact Letter QC 9FTC Form / Instructions Quality Control Failed to Cooperate Notification QC 9RTC Form / Instructions Quality Control Refuse to Cooperate Notification

IV. REFERENCES

7CFR 273.2(d)(2) LAC 67:III Chapter 19

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 04 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-1500 FITAP Incapacity Determination/SNAP Disability Document No./Name C-1510-FITAP Incapacity Determination Effective Date January 1, 2019

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

To be determined incapacitated, a person must have a medically determined physical or mental illness or impairment.

The incapacity shall be:

● supported by competent medical evidence,

● of such a debilitating nature as to substantially reduce or eliminate the parent’s ability to support or care for the child, and

● expected to last for at least 30 days.

In making the determination of ability to support the child, the limited employment opportunities of disabled individuals shall be taken into account.

The incapacity decision is based primarily upon socioeconomic and medical information. The client’s age, education, work experience, vocational training and other social factors are evaluated to determine the level of work the person can perform.

Amputations, asthma, diabetes, epilepsy, fractures, hemorrhoids, hernia, menopausal syndrome, mental deficiency, obesity, post-surgical complications, psychoneurosis, uterine fibroids, and varicose veins are not considered incapacitating unless:

● approval is for a temporary period for treatment and rehabilitation, or

● the condition cannot be corrected by treatment without undue risk to the client, or

● the client cannot engage in a useful occupation because of the impairment.

Refer the client for SSI and Louisiana Rehabilitation Services (LRS) if the incapacity warrants referral and is expected to last at least six months. Use form SSI3 when referring to SSI. Indicate on form OFS 90S when the referral was made.

Establish incapacity in one of the following ways:

● Receipt of RSDI based on disability of the person,

● Local office decision, or

● Incapacity decision by the FITAP/STEP Program Consultant.

2 of 4 II. PROCEDURES

LOCAL OFFICE DECISION

Make a local office decision if one of the following situations exists:

● Temporary or Total Incapacity

If the disability prevents all work activity and will last at least 30 days but no more than six months, the worker may make the incapacity decision with supervisory approval.

If the client remains temporarily disabled after a six-month period, obtain additional medical information which includes the expected duration of incapacity. The local office may extend approval of the temporary incapacity decision for no more than five (5) additional months for a total of eleven months.

Document the decision with the forms OFS 90, 90AD, 90S, or other report that includes the diagnosis, ability to work, and duration of incapacity. When any condition is expected to last longer than three months, the form OFS 90S is required to be completed.

● Hospitalized Person

A person who is continuously hospitalized meets the condition of incapacity. The worker must:

o Verify by hospital records and

o Secure medical information.

If incapacity is not clearly established for a local office decision to be made based on documentation that indicates temporary or total (permanent) incapacity or continuous hospitalization, submit form OFS 90S packet to the FITAP/STEP Program Consultant.

FITAP/STEP PROGRAM CONSULTANT DECISION

The following steps should be taken when requesting an incapacity decision from the FITAP/STEP Program Consultant:

● Obtain medical information from a licensed medical professional, clinic, hospital, DDS or other source of medical information or treatment.

● Use medical information provided by the client, if current and sufficient. The verification provided must be comparable to the information obtained in the form OFS 90, 90AD, 90D.

3 of 4 ● When requesting medical records from a free source, use form 90D, Request to Physician or Medical Facility for Medical Data. Use form OFS 90DDS to request information from DDS.

***

● When the client is participating in LRS, obtain a copy of the training plan from LRS.

● If a client has a pending Worker's Compensation suit, do not request a medical report from the client's attorney or ask the client to obtain it. However, accept and use it if the client voluntarily presents it.

***

● Obtain social information from the client or his representative for completion of the form OFS 90S. Document worker observation on the form OFS 90S.

● Obtain information regarding SSI status from SIEVS Option Q. Include reason for rejection if application was denied.

● Send form OFS 90 packet to the Regional FITAP/STEP Program Consultant. The form OFS 90 packet includes:

o forms OFS 90, 90A, 90AD, 90D, or 90DDS current medical information completed by medical professionals, o previous forms OFS 90 and medical information, o medical reports provided by medical professionals, o form OFS 90S - social information completed by worker, o form OFS 90X - route slip, o form OFS 90DDS if information obtained from DDS, o any useful information or copies of records from any social service provider.

The incapacity decision made by the FITAP/STEP Program Consultant should not exceed twelve months, as current medical information should be obtained and evaluated at that time.

REVIEW OF FITAP/STEP PROGRAM CONSULTANT DECISION

The local office may request a review of the FITAP/STEP Program Consultant decision if:

● the local office staff disagrees with the decision, or

● new medical or social information is available.

Obtain supervisory approval and resubmit the form OFS 90 packet with a cover memo giving the reason for the submission and any additional information.

1 of 2 Consider as disabled for SNAP purposes and entitled to special consideration when determining eligibility and benefits any person who is:

1. receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security benefits based on disability or blindness; or

2. receiving federally or state-administered supplemental benefits under section 1616(a) of the Social Security Act (Optional State Supplementation) provided that the eligibility to receive the benefits is based upon the SSI disability or blindness criteria; or

3. receiving federally or state-administered supplemental benefits under Section 212(a) of Pub. L. 93-66 (Mandatory Minimum State Supplementation); or

4. receiving disability retirement benefits from a governmental agency because of a disability considered permanent under the Social Security Act (refer to C-1520-SNAP, section C-1523- SNAP); or

5. a veteran with a disability rated by the Veteran's Administration (VA) as total or paid as total by the VA under Title 38 of the United States Code; or

6. a veteran considered by the VA to be in need of regular aid and attendance or permanently housebound under Title 38 of the United States Code; or

7. a surviving spouse of a veteran and considered by the VA to be in need of regular aid and attendance or permanently housebound or a surviving child of a veteran and considered by the VA to be permanently incapable of self-support under Title 38 of the United States Code; or

8. a surviving spouse or surviving child of a veteran and is receiving or has been approved to receive compensation for a service-connected death or pension benefits for a nonservice- connected death under Title 38 of the United States Code and has a disability considered permanent under the Social Security Act (refer to C-1520-SNAP, section C-1523-SNAP); or

9. receiving an annuity payment under Section 2(a)(1)(iv) of the Railroad Retirement Act of 1974 and is determined to be eligible to receive Medicare by the Railroad Retirement Board; or section 2(a)(1)(v) of the Railroad Retirement Act of 1974 and is determined to be disabled based upon the SSI criteria; or

10. eligible for SSI benefits based on presumptive eligibility and SSI emergency allowance payments; or

11. eligible for disability benefits from SS, SSI or VA, but not receiving a check because of 100 percent recoupment; or

1 of 3 C-1521-SNAP VERIFICATION OF DISABILITY

C-1521-1-SNAP When to Verify

Verify disability at certification, redetermination, and when changed.

C-1521-2-SNAP Methods of Verification

For persons to be considered disabled as identified in C-1510-SNAP, Nos. 1, 2 and 3, the household must provide proof that the disabled person is receiving disability benefits.

For persons to be considered disabled as identified in C-1510-SNAP, Nos. 4 and 8, use the Social Security Administration's (SSA) most current list of disabilities considered permanent under the Social Security Act. (Refer to C-1523-SNAP.)

For persons to be considered disabled as identified in C-1510-SNAP, No. 5 the household must present a statement from the VA which clearly indicates that the disabled individual is receiving VA disability benefits and that the disability is rated as total or paid at the total rate by VA.

For persons to be considered disabled as identified in C-1510-SNAP, Nos. 6 and 7, proof by the household that the disabled person is receiving VA disability benefits is sufficient.

For persons to be considered disabled as identified in C-1510-SNAP, No. 9 the household must provide proof that the person receives a Railroad Retirement disability annuity from the Railroad Retirement Board and has been determined to qualify for Medicare.

C-1522-SNAP DOCUMENTATION OF DISABILITY

Document verification of disability.

C-1523-SNAP LIST OF DISABILITIES CONSIDERED PERMANENT UNDER THE SOCIAL SECURITY ACT

1. Arthritis of One Major Joint In Each Upper Extremity 2. Disorders of the Spine (Arthritis Manifested By Ankylosis or Fixation at 30 degrees or more) 3. Statutory Blindness, Except If Due to Cataracts or Detached Retina - Markedly Reduced Ability to See Objects Not Correctable by Surgery, Other Treatment, or Glasses 7. Loss of Visual Efficiency (Visual Efficiency of Better Eye After Best Correction 20 Percent or Less) 8. Hearing Impairments (Hearing Not Restorable by a Hearing Aid)

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Independence (EI) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-200-FITAP-SNAP Clearances Document No./Name C-210-SNAP National Accuracy Clearinghouse (NAC) Effective Date September 1, 2026

1 of 10 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The National Accuracy Clearinghouse (NAC) is a nationwide data matching system designed to enhance program integrity by providing state agencies with a tool to screen for duplicate participation in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) so that an individual does not receive SNAP benefits in more than one state at any time. NAC ensures that timely action is taken to reduce incorrect SNAP, including Louisiana Combined Application Project (LaCAP), benefit issuances when an individual applies for SNAP in another state. NAC can only be used to prevent duplicate participation in SNAP. Information from the NAC cannot be used to determine eligibility for Family Independence Temporary Assistance Program (FITAP) or Kinship Care Subsidy Program (KCSP) cases. All states and territories are required to utilize NAC. It will be implemented in a phased approach over a 5-year period.

C-211-SNAP – PO NAC PROCESS OVERVIEW

NAC is queried for all household members at application, redetermination, and when adding a new household member. The state that submits a query in NAC is considered the Initiating State. The state that has the NAC Match is considered the Matching State. A NAC Match means that an individual has been identified as currently receiving benefits in one state and is applying for benefits in another state. Louisiana can be either the Initiating State or the Matching State. In either situation, if a NAC Match of duplicate participation is identified, action must be taken to clear the match. When Louisiana is the Initiating State, a query is submitted to the NAC Web Application during application, redetermination, or when adding a new household member, which may result in a NAC Match being found for duplicate participation in another state. A query is completed through the Clearance Summary or On-Demand.

Identity, residency, and Social Security Numbers (SSN) must be verified prior to conducting a query in NAC. If all three are not verified initially in Data Collection, the Clearance Summary will not run the query. Once the identity, residency, and Social Security Number are verified for the head of household and the SSNs verified for all other household members, a NAC On-Demand query must be sent to receive NAC results in the Clearance Summary for the head of household and/or household members.

When NAC finds a match, the NAC Web Application will create a Match Record in the NAC Web Application with a unique ‘Match ID’ to identify it. NAC will send both the Initiating and Matching states an email notification of the match, which includes the ‘Match ID’ that is linked to the Match Record. If no match is found, the NAC Web Application notifies the Initiating State that no match was found. If an On-Demand query is run and there is no match found, a case note must be made indicating that the NAC query was conducted and no match was found. The worker will continue the eligibility determination process in accordance with policy.

When Louisiana is the Matching State, an email notification is sent from the NAC Web Application indicating a NAC Match was found advising that an individual who is receiving SNAP in Louisiana is applying for benefits in another state. This may mean the household has moved to another state

2 of 10 without closing their case in Louisiana making their Louisiana residency questionable. Current residency in Louisiana must be verified prior to denying or closing the case if the member is the head of household or excluding the household member if the member is not the head of household.

An email notification from the NAC Web Application is sent to SNAP.NAC@la.gov mailbox that Fraud and Recovery Unit (FRU) support staff will receive. The email advises that an individual has applied for benefits in that state and will include the ‘Match ID’ and the ‘Match Date’. FRU support staff is responsible for monitoring the email box and notifying staff that a NAC match has been received by creating a NAC Task. Refer to C-213-PR for FRU’s responsibilities when Louisiana is the Matching State and a NAC Match is received.

C-212-SNAP – PO NAC TERMINOLOGY

The terms below assist when processing a case with a NAC Match.

• NAC Web Application – the system used by participating NAC states regarding duplicate SNAP participation to view and search information on matches, make necessary updates, and take actions. • NAC Match – indicates an individual is receiving benefits in another state. NAC matches for active SNAP participants are received daily from the NAC Web Service. • Match Record – created when NAC finds a match for duplicate participation in another state. • Match ID – an identifier to allow States to communicate with each other about the match outside the NAC Web Application (such as by email) without using Personally Identifiable Information (PII). • Match Date – the date a NAC Match was received. • Initiating State – the state that receives a NAC Match indicating possible duplicate participation as a result of a client applying for benefits or adding a new household member in Louisiana. • Matching State – the state that receives a NAC Match indicating possible duplicate participation from the initiating state or directly from the NAC Web Application as a result of a new applicant or the addition of a new household member. • NAC Data Matching Elements – can be used to search for SNAP participants in the NAC Web Application; these elements are the participant’s name, date of birth, and SSN. • Participant ID or Individual ID – A unique identifier for a participant or applicant that each State will connect a match to the appropriate individual in their own State system; this is the Person ID (PID) in LITE. • Vulnerable Individual – a person who would be endangered by the circulation of their information as a result of a domestic violent situation. Ex. Individual living in a battered woman’s shelter or identifies as fleeing from domestic violence. • Invalid Match – involves participants who are not receiving or applying for benefits in more than one state and may occur if there has been an error in the information submitted to the NAC or in cases of identity theft.

3 of 10 • Initial Action Taken – the first action taken by the Initiating State and Matching State to resolve a match; must be completed within ten days of receiving a match notification of possible duplicate participation. The Initial Action Taken options change depending on whether the state is the Initiating State or the Matching State. • Initial Investigation – task status when FRU staff enter details for match results reported from the NAC Web Application. • No Interface Triggered – If NAC was not able to be called because identity, residency, or SSN was not verified, then the record will appear on Clearance Summary as “No Interface Triggered”. • Final Disposition Taken – the final result after the Initiating or Matching state has resolved a match of possible duplicate participation. C-213-SNAP – PO PROCESSING EXPEDITED CASES WITH NAC MATCH

Expedited timeframe does not apply:

• If a NAC Match is received and it is verified that benefits are currently being receiving benefits in another state, by either a household member or the entire household. o If it is verified a ‘matched’ individual is receiving benefits in another state, the individual must be excluded from the case and expedited benefits issued to the remaining members of the household.

Expedited timeframe applies:

• If a NAC Match is found and it is verified a household member is not receiving benefits in another state, expedited benefits must be issued. • If a NAC Match is found but is not able to be resolved timely, expedited benefits must be issued. • If the worker is unable to submit a NAC query due to postponed verification, the household is eligible to receive expedited benefits for the initial and second month, if applicable. o If during the 30-day processing period, residency and Social Security Number are verified, the NAC query is submitted and a match is found, the worker must follow procedures in C- 212-SNAP PR, for a NAC Match.

If the household fails to respond to the OFS 14 NAC notice within 10 days, or if the State determines the matched individual is receiving benefits in another State, the Notice of Decision must be sent. While the notice is sent to the head of household, only the ‘matched’ individuals are denied and not the remaining household members.

The Monthly Bulk Match (MBM) Report runs every second Tuesday of each month around 6:00 am ET. This report looks at all SNAP participants in all participating States’ most recent bulk upload and cross references to find individuals already receiving SNAP benefits that were not found through a

4 of 10 query match. Each month, after the MBM report runs, FRU staff will receive an email notification advising the MBM report is available and the number of matches found. If there were zero matches found, an email is sent advising of no matches. If matches are indicated in the email, select the ‘View MBM Report’ button in the email to navigate to the NAC Web Application. Use the ‘Match ID’ link on the MBM Report to access the match details. Refer to section C-213-SNAP – PR for procedures.

II. PROCEDURES

C-211-SNAP – PR ACCESSING THE NAC WEB APPLICATION

Staff must access the NAC Web Application to update or view NAC Match details. This can be completed via the link provided in the NAC Match email notification or through the “NAC” Task in LITE by selecting the ‘Match ID’ link. After selecting the link from one of these options, staff will be directed to the USDA eAuthentication (eAuth) website Customer Login screen and must complete the following steps:

• Select the option Login.gov, • Enter the Email address and Password associated with your eAuth account, • Select ‘Sign-In’, and enter the one-time code sent via text message, • Select ‘Submit’ to access the NAC Web Application. o Selecting ‘Submit’ navigates staff to the Find a SNAP Participant screen in the NAC Web Application.

Within the Find a SNAP Participant screen, staff can conduct searches for an individual to verify if there is duplicate participation in SNAP in other states. Staff must use caution when conducting a search on the Find a SNAP Participant screen because if there is no existing match, a new match will be created as a result of the search. To conduct a search for an individual SNAP participant on the Find a SNAP Participant screen and view a Match Record, staff must:

• Enter the Last Name, Date of Birth, Social Security Number, Participant ID (PID in LITE), and a Search Reason (New Application, New Household Member, Recertification, or Other) then select ‘Search’, • If a match is not found, the following message will display: “No Matches Found – There are no match records for this participant.” Matches are only on exact values. Information entered incorrectly will result in no match results. • If a match is found, the SNAP Participants Search Results will display the ‘Match ID’, ‘Matching State’, and ‘Vulnerable Individual’ information. o Note: It is possible to have multiple matches for a single individual. • Select the ‘Match ID’ link in the SNAP Participants Search Results to navigate to the Match Record screen. • Enter response details for either the ‘Initial Action’ or ‘Final Disposition’, and • Select ‘Save Changes’.

5 of 10 Staff can also access the NAC Web Application to search for an open match and make updates to the ‘Match Record’. To conduct a search for an open match and update the ‘Match Record’ in the NAC Web Application, staff must:

• Navigate to the NAC Web Application, • Select the ‘Find An Existing Match’ tab in the top navigation panel, and • On the Find an Existing Match screen, select one of the following search options: o Match ID o Participant ID o Case Number o Last Name, Date or Birth, and Social Security Number. • The Match Record screen displays the Vulnerable and Invalid Status questions, the Initial Action details, and the Final Disposition details as fields to be updated. • If the individual is flagged as a Vulnerable Individual, an alert will populate. Click Continue to proceed. • The Match Record screen also displays read-only information for the Matching State and Initiating State that includes the SNAP Participant Information, Match Information, and Contact Information of each state included in the Match Record. • Select ‘Save Changes’ to complete the update once all the required updates have been entered on the Match Record. o An automatic email notification is sent to notify the Initiating/Matching State of changes made to the Match Record.

Note: A combination of Invalid Match and entering ‘Final Disposition’ information will result in the closure of the Match once both States provide their ‘Final Disposition’. Once closed, the Match Record cannot be updated and can only be viewed in Read-Only mode.

The ‘Initial Action Taken’ and ‘Final Disposition Taken’ options displayed depend on whether the Louisiana is the Initiating State or the Matching State.

• ‘Initial Action Taken’ o Initiating State options are: ▪ Notice Sent - a SNAP Participation Match in Another State (OFS 14 NAC) notice is sent to the household to inform the client of the NAC match. ▪ Client Provided Required Verification – the client submitted the requested verification to verify Louisiana residency.

o Matching State options: ▪ Notice Sent - a SNAP Participation Match in Another State (OFS 14 NAC) notice is sent to the household to inform the client of the NAC match. ▪ Client Verified Move out of State – verification received from the client verifying the household no longer resides in Louisiana.

6 of 10 • ‘Final Disposition Taken’ o Initiating State options are: ▪ Benefits Approved – the case has been approved and benefits issued. ▪ Benefits Denied – the case has been denied. o Matching State options: ▪ Benefits Terminated – the case has been closed and the client is no longer receiving benefits. ▪ Benefits Unchanged – no action was taken to terminate benefits.

C-212-SNAP – PR LOUISIANA AS THE INITIATING STATE

When Louisiana is the Initiating State, a query is submitted to the NAC Web Application when completing an application, a redetermination, adding a household member, or when calling NAC On- Demand. During Data Collection, the NAC query is automatically submitted after verifying the identity, residency, and Social Security Number of the head of household and the Social Security Numbers of additional household members when continuing from the Person Demographics – Details screen.

If a NAC Match is found, the NAC Match will be displayed in the Clearance Summary. Information received from the NAC Match is automatically added to the Out-of-State Benefits – Details screen in LITE by creating a new record. This results in an automatic case note generated stating “Out-of- State record added for individual (PID) due to NAC match.” LITE automatically populates the following information in the Out-of-State Benefits – Details screen:

• Benefit Begin Date - "Recent Benefit Issuance Date" from the NAC Match results, which is the last date of benefit issuance. • Benefit End Date - "Participant Closing Date" from the NAC Match results which may or may not provide the benefit termination date if benefits are continuing to be received. • Reported On - The date the NAC Match was found. This date might be before or after the Benefit Begin Date. • Benefit Received in Other State – the program type will be SNAP. • State - State ID for the state from where the benefits were received • Termination Verification – Verification option will be "Pending Due to NAC Match.”

If a record already exists on the Out-of-State Benefits - Details screen that overlaps with the new record from the NAC Match, the new record is added. Exact duplicate information is not be added to the Out-of-State Benefits – Details screen.

Additionally, when a NAC Match is found, a NAC Match – Initiating State task is automatically created and assigned to the worker (case owner) in ‘Initial Investigation’ status. The task is created when a NAC Match is found at intake, redetermination, or when a new member is added to a SNAP household. Action must be taken on the task within ten days.

The worker (case owner) must complete the following actions once the interview is complete:

• Run Eligibility Determination and Benefit Calculation (EDBC). LITE will automatically send the SNAP Participation Match in Another State (OFS 14 NAC), to inform the household of the NAC Match. An automatic case note is generated stating, "Notice of Match Result generated for individual (PID) due to a NAC match." The case is pended for the missing verification listed on the OFS 14 NAC. The household must provide the verification within 10 days. o Access the NAC Web Application and update the ‘Initial Action’ to “Notice Sent”. If “Notice Sent” is selected, the “Initial Action Date” is populated. o Click “Save Changes”.

• If verification of terminated out-of-state benefits is received and the Matching State terminated the benefits or the Matching State has not updated NAC Web Application, take the following actions: o Access LITE and navigate back to the work item and Data Collection. o Update the Out-of-State Benefits – Details screen with Termination Verification of "NAC - Termination Verified". An automatic case note is generated stating “Out-of-State Benefits updated to ‘NAC – Termination Verified’ for individual (PID).” ▪ Run EDBC and authorize the case. The case will be approved for benefits. ▪ The NAC Match – Initiating State task status is automatically updated to ‘Final Disposition Needed’. o Access the NAC Web Application and update the: ▪ ‘Initial Action Taken’ to “Client provided Required Verification”, ▪ Date received, and ▪ ‘Final Disposition’ of "Benefits Approved". o Manually update the NAC Match – Initiating State Task status to "Completed” in LITE.

• If verification of receipt of out-of-state benefits is received and the Matching State did not terminate the benefits or the Matching State has not updated NAC Web Application, take the following actions: o Access LITE and navigate back to the work item and Data Collection. o Remove the ‘Benefits End Date’ from the Out-of-State Benefits – Details screen. o The Termination Verification can remain blank and the system automatically closes the case or excludes the individual. An automatic case note is generated stating, “Individual (PID) excluded due to Out-of-State benefits – NAC Match.” ▪ Run EDBC and authorize the case. The case is denied or closed if the household member is the head of household. The member is excluded if the member is not the head of household. ▪ The NAC Match – Initiating State Task status is automatically updated to ‘Final Disposition Needed’. o Access the NAC Web Application with the ‘Final Disposition’ as "Benefits Denied", and o Manually update the NAC Match – Initiating State Task status to "Completed."

C-213-SNAP – PR LOUISIANA AS THE MATCHING STATE

When Louisiana is the Matching State, the NAC Web Application sends an email notification to the LDH NAC mailbox advising that an applicant has applied for benefits in another state.

The email address, SNAP.NAC@la.gov, has been created to accept email notifications received from the NAC Web Application. FRU staff monitor the email box and notify the staff that a NAC match has been received by creating the NAC Match for Matching State – Initiate Action Task. An automatic case note is created that displays “NAC match received from another state for individual (PID).”

FRU staff must complete the following steps to create a NAC Match for Matching State – Initiate Action task in LITE: • Navigate to the LITE Worker Portal Home screen and click the ‘Dashboard’ tab from the top navigation panel. • Select the new ‘Create NAC Task’ button on the Staff Summary screen. The ‘Create NAC Task’ pop-up displays. • Enter the ‘Match ID’, ‘Match Date’, and ‘Assigned Worker’ and select ‘SAVE AND CLOSE’ to create the NAC Match for Matching State – Initiate Action Task, o The NAC Match for Matching State – Initiate Action task is manually assigned to a FRU worker with a due date of five days after the date the match was found. • Locate the task on the Staff Summary screen or conduct a Work Item - Task search using the ‘Match ID’ and click ‘Start Work Item. The NAC Task pop-up displays. • Select the ‘Match ID’ link in the pop-up to access the NAC Web Application. Use the ‘Match ID’ to locate the match and obtain the ‘Case ID’ and “Individual (Participant) ID’. • Navigate back to LITE and the NAC Task pop-up and enter the ‘Case ID’ and the ‘Individual ID’ and select ‘SAVE AND CLOSE’. The NAC Match for Matching State – Initiate Action Task will automatically close and the NAC Match – Matching State Task will be created. The NAC Match – Matching State Task will be assigned as follows: o If the case is active with no pending work items (application, Simplified Report, redetermination, Change Report), the task will be assigned to FRU staff. o If the case is active with pending work items, the task will be assigned to the worker who is the case owner.

9 of 10 For cases that are active with no pending work items, FRU staff must complete the following steps:

STEP 1: Select the “Start Work Item” for the NAC Match – Matching State Task on the dashboard and navigate to Initiate Data Collection to initiate a Change Report with the new NAC flag . STEP 2: Navigate to the Person Demographics screen and update residency verification to “NAC Match – Pending Verification”. An automatic case note is generated stating “Pending verification of Residency due to a NAC match for individual (PID).” STEP 3: Run EDBC. The case (whether SNAP or LaCAP) is pended for the missing NAC verification. If the SNAP case has an associated FITAP or KCSP case, benefits will be pended based on existing eligibility rules when residency is not verified.

STEP 4: Ensure LITE sends the OFS 14 NAC that includes an Advance Notice of Adverse Action to request residency verification for the individual included in the NAC Match. The household must provide the verification of residency by the due date listed on the OFS 14 NAC (13 days). An automatic case note is generated stating “Notice of Match Results and Adverse Action generated for individual (PID) due to a NAC Match.”

NOTE: A Request for Verification will be sent for the FITAP/KCSP case and an OFS 14 NAC will be sent only for the SNAP case. If the worker does determine that the client moved out of state, then the FITAP case can be terminated based on the residency requirement, but an OFS 14 NAC must not be sent.

STEP 5: Access the NAC Web Application and update the ‘Initial Action’ to ‘Notice Sent’.

If verification of the Louisiana residency is received: • Update the Residency Verification field to the appropriate selection based on the verification received. An automatic case note is generated stating “Residency updated to ‘Meets residency requirement’ for individual (PID).” • Run EDBC and authorize the case. The case is approved for benefits. • The NAC Task status is automatically updated to ‘Final Disposition Needed’. • Navigate to the NAC Web Application and update the Final Disposition to "Benefits Unchanged". • Manually update the NAC Task status to “Completed” in LITE.

If verification of the Out-of-State Residency is not received: • If the Head of Household, the LITE batch process will automatically close the case if the household member is the head of household. An automatic case note is generated stating, “Case closed for failure to provide verification due to NAC Match.” • If a household member, manually authorize the case because the LITE batch process will not automatically exclude a household member. The LITE batch process will result in a Case Authorization Error task advising to authorize the case.

1 of 6 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

C-220-FITAP - PO CLEARANCE SUMMARY

THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY CONSISTS OF A CLEARANCE SUMMARY SCREEN AND A CLEARANCE SUMMARY POP-UP SCREEN. THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY POP-UP SCREEN IS THE INITIAL SOURCE FOR ALL CLEARANCES ON THE INIITAL SCREEN IN DATA COLLECTION DURING INTAKE, REDETERMINATION, AND SIMPLIFIED REPORT CASE MODES. THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY SCREEN IS USED TO VIEW HISTORICAL DATA BY INDIVIUDALS WHO ARE CONDUCTING A CASE REVIEW. IT ALSO ALLOWS FOR CHANGES TO THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY STATUS. CLEARANCES HELP DETECT UNREPORTED INFORMATION AND SERVES AS VERIFICATION FOR CERTAIN INCOME.

THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY IS RUN AUTOMATICALLY AT APPLICATION, SIMPLIFIED REPORT, AND REDETERMINATION.

• THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY POP-UP SCREEN IS AVAILABLE AND ACCESSED BY SELECTING THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY ICON ON THE RIGHT HAND NAVIGATION PANEL AT THE BEGINNING OF THE DATA COLLECTION - INDIVIDUAL INFORMATION MODULE. THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY POP-UP SCREEN ALLOWS USERS TO VERIFY THE INFORMATION RECEIVED FROM OTHER INTERFACE SOURCES WHILE ALLOWING THE WORKER TO NAVIGATE THROUGH THE DRIVER FLOW TO COLLECT THE NECESSARY DATA.

• AT APPLICATION OR REDETERMINATION, IF THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY POP-UP SCREEN IS VIEWED BEFORE THE COMPLETION OF THE DATA COLLECTION - INDIVIDUAL INFORMATION MODULE, NO CLEARANCES WILL BE PRESENT ON THE POP-UP SCREEN. THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY POP-UP SCREEN IS TRIGGERED AFTER THE WORKER COMPLETES THE PROGRAM REQUEST SCREEN AND AVAILABLE DURING THE DATA COLLECTION- HOUSEHOLD INFORMATION MODULE.

• THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY POP-UP SCREEN, WHEN TRIGGERED AT ELIGIBILITY-WRAP UP WILL BE USED TO UPDATE THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY STATUS. THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY POP-UP SCREEN ALLOWS THE USER TO MARK THE STATUS OF THE CLEARANCES ASSOCIATED WITH THE CASE AS EITHER “CLEARED”, “REJECTED” OR “CLOSED”. THIS IS DETERMINED BY THE WORKER BASED ON THE ELIGIBILITY RESULTS.

• LASES

USE INFORMATION FOUND ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY. IF CHILD SUPPORT PAYMENTS HAVE BEEN RECEIVED IN THE PAST 12 MONTHS, THEN THE LAST 12 MONTHS OF PAYMENTS WILL BE DISPLAYED. TAX INTERCEPTS ARE NOT INCLUDED IN THE PAYMENT SHOWN ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY.

• VETERAN’S ADMINISTRATION (VA) BENEFITS

DISCUSS WITH THE HOUSEHOLD. ARE ANY PAYMENTS FROM AGENT ORANGE? IF THE HOUSEHOLD REPORTS THERE ARE NO AGENT ORANGE PAYMENTS, USE THE INFORMATION FOUND ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY.

• FEDERAL DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE EMPLOYMENT

OBTAIN VERIFICATION FROM THE HOUSEHOLD.

• INTERSTATE PARTICIPATION IN A PUBLIC ASSISTANCE PROGRAM IN ANOTHER STATE.

CONTACT THE STATE DEPARTMENT AND DISCUSS WITH THE HOUSEHOLD.

• PRISONER MATCH

IF THE RELEASE DATE IS NOT DISPLAYED, CONTACT THE FACILITY TO DETERMINE IF THE INDIVIDUAL IS STILL INCARCERATED.

IF THE PRISON NAME AND ADDRESS, CONTACT NAME, AND FACILITY PHONE NUMBER ARE UNAVAILABLE, CONTACT THE CLIENT TO DISCUSS.

ONCE ALL HITS HAVE BEEN CLEARED, UPDATE THE STATUS TO “CLEARED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY, AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE. REFER BELOW FOR USE OF CODES “REJECTED,” “CLOSED,” AND “CLEARED.”

AT APPLICATION

• IF THE APPLICATION IS REJECTED AND HITS WERE NOT CLEARED, UPDATE THE STATUS TO “REJECTED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY, AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE.

• IF THE APPLICATION IS REJECTED AND HITS HAVE BEEN CLEARED, INFORMATION OBTAINED THROUGH THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY MUST BE USED TO UPDATE ANY ASSOCIATED CASE INFORMATION. UPDATE THE STATUS TO “CLEARED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE.

6 of 6 NOTE: IT IS NOT NECESSARY TO GO BACK IN TO DATA COLLECTION TO MARK CLEARANCE SUMMARY AS REJECTED FOR AUTO DENIALS FOR FAILURE TO PROVIDE POSTPONED VERIFICATION.

AT SIMPLIFIED REPORT

• IF THE CASE IS CLOSED AND HITS WERE NOT CLEARED, UPDATE THE STATUS TO “CLOSED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY, AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE.

• IF THE CASE IS CLOSED AND HITS HAVE BEEN CLEARED, INFORMATION OBTAINED THROUGH THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY MUST BE USED TO UPDATE ANY ASSOCIATED CASE INFORMATION. UPDATE THE STATUS TO “CLEARED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE.

AT REDETERMINATION

• IF THE CASE IS CLOSED AND HITS WERE NOT CLEARED, UPDATE THE STATUS TO “CLOSED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY, AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE.

• IF THE CASE IS CLOSED AND HITS HAVE BEEN CLEARED, INFORMATION OBTAINED THROUGH THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY MUST BE USED TO UPDATE ANY ASSOCIATED CASE INFORMATION. UPDATE THE STATUS TO “CLEARED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE.

NOTE: IT IS NOT NECESSARY TO GO BACK INTO DATA COLLECTION TO CLEAR CLEARANCE SUMMARY FOR AUTO CLOSURES.

At Addition of a Household Member per C-840-FITAP:

Using the Case Change/Change Report case mode workflow, the new member must be added to LITE and clearances run. Clear all hits according to procedures listed above. Once all hits have been cleared, update the Change Action Case Mode status to “Cleared” on the Clearance Summary and click Confirm.

DOCUMENT ALL ACTIVITIES IN LITE.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms associated with this policy.

6 of 7 Contact the person listed in the eDRS panel to verify that the disqualification is valid. Refer to F-350-SNAP for information regarding clearing eDRS hits.

ONCE ALL HITS HAVE BEEN CLEARED, UPDATE THE STATUS TO “CLEARED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY, AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE. REFER BELOW FOR USE OF CODES “REJECTED,” “CLOSED,” AND “CLEARED.”

AT APPLICATION

• IF THE APPLICATION IS REJECTED AND HITS WERE NOT CLEARED, UPDATE THE STATUS TO “REJECTED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY, AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE.

• IF THE APPLICATION IS REJECTED AND HITS HAVE BEEN CLEARED, INFORMATION OBTAINED THROUGH THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY MUST BE USED TO UPDATE ANY ASSOCIATED CASE INFORMATION. UPDATE THE STATUS TO “CLEARED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE.

NOTE: IT IS NOT NECESSARY TO GO BACK IN TO DATA COLLECTION TO MARK CLEARANCE SUMMARY AS REJECTED FOR AUTO DENIALS FOR FAILURE TO PROVIDE POSTPONED VERIFICATION.

AT SIMPLIFIED REPORT

• IF THE CASE IS CLOSED AND HITS WERE NOT CLEARED, UPDATE THE STATUS TO “CLOSED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY, AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE.

• IF THE CASE IS CLOSED AND HITS HAVE BEEN CLEARED, INFORMATION OBTAINED THROUGH THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY MUST BE USED TO UPDATE ANY ASSOCIATED CASE INFORMATION. UPDATE THE STATUS TO “CLEARED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE.

AT REDETERMINATION

• IF THE CASE IS CLOSED AND HITS WERE NOT CLEARED, UPDATE THE STATUS TO “CLOSED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY, AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE.

• IF THE CASE IS CLOSED AND HITS HAVE BEEN CLEARED, INFORMATION OBTAINED THROUGH THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY MUST BE USED TO UPDATE ANY ASSOCIATED CASE INFORMATION. UPDATE THE STATUS TO “CLEARED” ON THE CLEARANCE SUMMARY AND CLICK SAVE AND CLOSE.

Note: It is not necessary to go back into Data collection to clear clearance summary for auto closures. It is also not necessary to check clearance summary when interim changes are reported. Refer to policy C-820-SNAP

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Independence (EI) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-200-FITAP-SNAP Clearances Document No./Name C-240-SNAP National Directory of New Hires Effective Date September 1, 2026

1 of 5 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

C-240-SNAP – PO NATIONAL DIRECTORY OF NEW HIRES (NDNH)

THE FOOD AND NUTRITION ADMINISTRATION (FNA) REQUIRES STATE AGENCIES TO VERIFY SUPPLEMENTAL NUTRITION ASSISTANCE PROGRAM (SNAP) APPLICANT WAGE DATA THROUGH THE NATIONAL DIRECTORY OF NEW HIRES (NDNH) TO DETERMINE SNAP ELIGIBILITY AND BENEFIT AMOUNTS AT THE TIME OF CERTIFICATION AND RECERTIFICATION. THE NDNH PROCESS IS AN AUTOMATED PROCESS AND MATCHES ARE HANDLED THROUGH THE LOUISIANA INTEGRATED TECHNOLOGY FOR ELIGIBILITY (LITE). LITE DETERMINES IF THE SNAP HOUSEHOLD WAS REQUIRED TO REPORT NEW EMPLOYMENT IF THE APPLICATION DATE IS WITHIN 60 DAYS OF THE DATE OF HIRE. LDH MUST REPORT TO FNA PERFORMANCE OUTCOMES ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE STATE’S USE OF THE NDNH MATCH RESULTS.

C-241-SNAP - PO CLAIM DETERMINATION

EACH OFFICE MUST KEEP TRACK OF ALL OVERISSUANCES THAT ARE DISCOVERED DUE TO NDNH MATCHES.

II. PROCEDURES

C-240-SNAP - PR NATIONAL DIRECTORY OF NEW HIRES (NDNH)

Household Required To Report

IF LITE DETERMINES THAT EMPLOYMENT FROM THE MATCH WAS REQUIRED TO BE REPORTED BECAUSE THE HIRE DATE WAS 60 DAYS PRIOR TO THE APPLICATION DATE:

• LITE WILL CREATE A NDNH CHANGE REPORT WORK ITEM AND ASSIGN IT TO THE CASE OWNER. • THE NEW NDNH FLAG WILL DISPLAY ON THE NDNH CHANGE REPORT WORK ITEM. • CLICK THE NDNH FLAG TO OPEN THE NDNH INCOME MATCH POPUP. IF THE USER CLICKS THE 'START WORK ITEM' BEFORE CLEARING THE NDNH FLAG, THE FOLLOWING WARNING MESSAGE WILL DISPLAY:

“PLEASE SELECT THE NDNH FLAG AND CLEAR THE INCOME BEING REPORTED BY THE NATIONAL DIRECTORY OF NEW HIRE (NDNH) MATCH RESULT.”

THE “NDNH INCOME MATCH” POP-UP SCREEN WILL DISPLAY THE “NDNH INCOMES LIST” DETAILING NEW EMPLOYMENT DATA FOR THE HOUSEHOLD AND THE EXISTING LITE “INCOME – SUMMARY”. THE WORKER MUST SELECT “CLEARED”, “AUTOMATE”, OR “DEFERRED” TO CLEAR THE NDNH MATCH:

2 of 5 • SELECT “CLEARED” IF THE EMPLOYMENT IS ALREADY KNOWN AND HAS BEEN PREVIOUSLY CLEARED AND CLICK ‘SAVE’. o ONCE ‘SAVE’ IS SELECTED, THE FOLLOWING WARNING MESSAGE WILL DISPLAY, “YOU CHOSE TO CLEAR A JOB THAT WAS REQUIRED TO BE REPORTED. ARE YOU SURE YOU WANT TO CLEAR THIS JOB?” SELECT ‘SAVE’ AGAIN TO CONTINUE. • SELECT “DEFERRED” IF ACTION SHOULD BE TAKEN ON THE CHANGE DURING THE NEXT SR OR REDETERMINATION AND CLICK ‘SAVE’. o ONCE ‘SAVE’ IS SELECTED, THE FOLLOWING WARNING MESSAGE WILL DISPLAY, “YOU CHOSE TO DEFER A JOB THAT WAS REQUIRED TO BE REPORTED. ARE YOU SURE YOU WANT TO DEFER THIS JOB?” SELECT ‘SAVE’ AGAIN TO CONTINUE. • ENTER A DETAILED CASE NOTE TO EXPLAIN WHY “CLEARED” OR “DEFERRED” WAS SELECTED.

NOTE: IF “CLEARED IS SELECTED, NO FURTHER ACTION IS REQUIRED. IF “DEFERRED” IS SELECTED, ACTION MUST BE TAKEN AT THE NEXT SR OR REDETERMINATION.

• SELECT “AUTOMATE” IF THE EMPLOYMENT NEEDS TO BE CLEARED. IF “AUTOMATE” IS SELECTED, THE NIGHTLY BATCH IN LITE WILL AUTOMATICALLY: o INSERT INCOME ($0.00) FOR THE EMPLOYER INDICATED ON THE NDNH MATCH WITH ‘PENDING VERIFICATION’ ON THE EARNED INCOME DETAILS SCREEN INCLUDING THE FIELDS BELOW. ▪ INDIVIDUAL ID: PERSON ID FROM NDNH ▪ START DATE: HIRE DATE FROM NDNH ▪ REPORT DATE: SYSTEM DATE ▪ INCOME TYPE: WAGES ▪ PAY FREQUENCY: MONTHLY ▪ INCOME SOURCE: EMPLOYER NAME ON THE NDNH FILE IS THE INCOME BEING BUDGETED ONLY DUE TO THE NATIONAL DIRECTORY OF NEW HIRE (NDNH) MATCH? ‘YES’ ▪ EMPLOYER NAME: EMPLOYER NAME FROM NDNH ▪ AMOUNT PER HOUR: $0 ▪ NO. OF HOURS MONTHLY: 1 ▪ VERIFICATION: PENDING VERIFICATION ▪ CALCULATE AVERAGE BY: PAY PER FREQUENCY o GENERATE AN OFS 14 (VERSION A) INCLUDING A WAGE VERIFICATION FORM (OFS 87) REQUESTING EMPLOYMENT VERIFICATION WITH A DUE DATE OF 10 DAYS FROM THE DATE OF THE NOTICE.

IF VERIFICATION IS RECEIVED, THE WORKER MUST CLICK ‘START WORK ITEM’ ON THE NDNH CHANGE REPORT WORK ITEM, CLEAR THE NDNH MATCH, UPDATE THE APPROPRIATE FIELDS ON THE EARNED INCOME DETAILS AND EARNED INCOME PAYMENTS SCREENS, RUN EDBC, AND AUTHORIZE THE CASE. LITE WILL SEND A NOTICE OF DECISION EXPLAINING THE ACTION TAKEN ON THE CASE.

3 of 5 NOTE: IF CASE AUTHORIZATION IS ATTEMPTED WITHOUT CLEARING ALL NDNH MATCHES, THE ERROR MESSAGE “PLEASE CLEAR THE INCOME REPORTED BY NDNH MATCH RESULTS” WILL DISPLAY.

IF VERIFICATION IS NOT RECEIVED BY THE DUE DATE ON THE OFS 14, RUN EDBC AND AUTHORIZE THE CASE. LITE WILL SEND A NOTICE OF DECISION TO PROPOSE CLOSURE OF THE CASE.

HOUSEHOLD NOT REQUIRED TO REPORT

IF LITE DETERMINES THAT EMPLOYMENT FROM THE MATCH WAS NOT REQUIRED TO BE REPORTED, LITE WILL SEND THE OFS 14 (VERSION B) INCLUDING AN OFS 87 FOR EACH HOUSEHOLD MEMBER WITH NEW EMPLOYMENT ON THE NDNH MATCH RESULTS. THE OFS 14 WILL INCLUDE QUESTIONS TO DETERMINE WHETHER VERIFICATION OF THE INCOME FROM THE EMPLOYER MUST BE PROVIDED OR IF ANY FURTHER ACTION IS NECESSARY. IF IT IS DETERMINED THAT VERIFICATION MUST BE PROVIDED, THE OFS 14 WILL INSTRUCT THE HOUSEHOLD TO RETURN THE OFS 87 COMPLETED BY THE EMPLOYER OR CHECK STUBS AND PROVIDE A DUE DATE OF TEN DAYS FROM THE NOTICE MAIL DATE. THE OFS 14 (VERSION B) WILL ALSO INFORM THE HOUSEHOLD OF THE WAYS THE OFS 87 OR CHECK STUBS CAN BE SUBMITTED.

IF THE HOUSEHOLD RETURNS THE EMPLOYMENT VERIFICATION, THE WORKER MUST:

• CREATE A CHANGE REPORT FROM INITIATE DATA COLLECTION AND NAVIGATE TO THE EARNED INCOME – SUMMARY SCREEN, • ADD REPORTED INCOME, o NOTE: “YES” SHOULD BE SELECTED TO THE QUESTION “IS THE INCOME BEING BUDGETED ONLY DUE TO THE NATIONAL DIRECTORY OF NEW HIRE (NDNH) MATCH?” • CLICK THE “NDNH INCOME MATCH” LINK, • UPDATE THE NDNH STATUS TO “CLEARED”, • CLICK ‘SAVE’, • RUN EDBC, AND • AUTHORIZE THE CASE. o NOTE: IF THE NDNH MATCH RESULTS ARE NOT CLEARED, THE FOLLOWING WARNING MESSAGE WILL DISPLAY ON THE INCOME QUESTIONS SCREEN, EARNED INCOME SUMMARY SCREEN, AND THE CASE AUTHORIZATION SCREENS, “PLEASE CLEAR THE INCOME BEING REPORTED BY THE NATIONAL DIRECTORY OF NEW HIRE (NDNH) MATCH RESULTS”.

IF THE HOUSEHOLD DOES NOT RETURN INCOME VERIFICATION, THE NDNH MATCH RESULTS WILL BE DEFERRED AND MUST BE CLEARED AT THE NEXT SR OR REDETERMINATION.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-300-FITAP-SNAP Identity Document No./Name C-310-SNAP Eligibility/Verification Requirement Effective Date April 1, 2024

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

C-311-SNAP - PO INITIAL CERTIFICATION

Verify the identity of the person interviewed.

If an authorized representative applies for the household, verify the identities of both the authorized representative and the head of the household.

The OMV/LaWallet interface * and the Paternity Establishment and Support Enforcement (PESE) interface must be checked prior to requesting verification of identity from the person being interviewed.

EXCEPTION: If it is necessary to meet expedited service time limits, you may verify identity only of the authorized representative being interviewed. Verification of the identity of the head of the household may be postponed.

C-312-SNAP-PO REDETERMINATION

If a redetermination interview is conducted, verify the identity of the person interviewed if the person has not been identified before. The OMV/LaWallet and PESE interfaces must be checked prior to requesting verification of identity from the person being interviewed.

C-313-SNAP-PO RECEIPT OF THE LOUISIANA PURCHASE AUTOMATED BENEFIT CARD

Verify the identity of the head of household, spouse, any other responsible household member, or authorized representative receiving the Louisiana Purchase Automated Benefit Card.

II. PROCEDURES

The OMV/LaWallet and PESE interfaces ** must be checked prior to requesting verification of identity from the person being interviewed at application and redetermination. See C-320-SNAP How to Verify Identity.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCATIONS

There are no forms and instructions associated with this policy.

IV. REFERENCES

District/Section Economic Stability Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-300-SNAP Identity Document No./Name C-320-SNAP How To Verify Identity Effective Date December 1, 2025

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Identity may be verified through readily available documentary evidence, or if this is unavailable, through a collateral contact. Examples of acceptable documentary evidence which the applicant may provide include, but are not limited to:

• Driver's license,

• State ID,

• OMV/LA Wallet Interface,

• Paternity Establishment and Support Enforcement (PESE) Interface,

• Military ID,

• Work or school ID,

• ID for health benefits or for another assistance or social services program,

• Voter's registration card,

• Paycheck stubs or OFS 87 (Current, Past Or Anticipated Wage Verification Letter),

Note: These documents may only be used if the date on the document is within the past 12 months.

• U.S. Passport card,

• U.S. military discharge papers,

• Birth certificate, or

• Matricula Consular ID card, also known as Matricula Consular de Alta Seguridad (MCAS) or Certificate of Consular Registration. Note: This form of identity verification is not sufficient verification of legal immigration status or benefit eligibility.

Do not accept a Social Security card as sole proof of identity unless no other proof is available.

Social Security Administration (SSA) and/or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) records received through SOLQ or Clearance Summary are acceptable documentary evidence to verify identity. The identifying information, including the name, address, and date of birth, listed on the SSA/SSI record must match the information provided on the application. If there is any discrepancy between the

II. PROCEDURES

The identity of the person being interviewed must be verified using the OMV/LA Wallet interface prior to requesting verification of identity.

When identity of the Head of Household is verified by Social Security Administration (SSA) and/or Supplemental Security Income (SSI) records received through SOLQ or Clearance Summary use verification code “Other State, Federal or Local Agency” on the Person – Details page.

When identity is verified by documentary evidence, a copy of the identity verification must be filed in the document repository system.

If verification of identity cannot be located in the document repository system, verification of identity must be obtained. Identity that was previously verified using the on-demand OMV/LA WALLET interface does not have to be re-verified when a new application is processed.

LITE retains the OMV/LA Wallet Search results in the Interface Module.

When identity of the Head of Household, any other responsible household member, and/or Authorized Representative is verified using the on-demand OMV/LA Wallet interface in LITE follow the procedures below. Identity of the Head of Household or other responsible household member is verified and documented on the Person - Details page. Identity of the Authorized Representative is verified and documented on the Individual Interviewed - Details page.

To verify identity through OMV, click on the OMV icon on the right navigation panel in Data Collection on either the Person Details page or the Individual Interviewed – Details page in LITE. • A popup displays allowing the worker to enter the individual’s Driver’s License number, Audit number, First Name and Last Name. • Click “Search” to display and review results and verify the individual's identity. • If identity is verified, click the “Verified” button. “OMV Verified” automatically populates as the identity verification on the Person Details page. • If identity is not verified, click the “Not Verified” button.

To verify identity through LA Wallet, click on the LA Wallet icon on the right navigation panel in Data Collection on either on the Person Details page or the Individual Interviewed – Details page in LITE. • A popup displays allowing the worker to obtain a four digit verification code. • Click “Get Code” to display the verification code. • Provide the verification code to the individual to enter in the LA Wallet application on their mobile device.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C-Case Processing (FITAP) Section No./Name C-500 FITAP Management (FITAP) Document No./Name C-520-FITAP When To Consider Management Effective Date September 1, 2012

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

EXAMINE FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT AT EACH APPLICATION * ONLY IF THE APPLICANT REPORTS ZERO INCOME OR THE EXPENSES REPORTED ARE EQUAL TO OR EXCEED THE INCOME REPORTED AND IF MANAGEMENT IS QUESTIONABLE WHEN COMPLETING A SIMPLIFIED REPORT OR REDETERMINATION. ** IF REPORTED EXPENSES EXCEED REPORTED INCOME AT * REDETERMINATION, ** MANAGEMENT MUST BE DISCUSSED WITH THE HOUSEHOLD.

MANAGEMENT MUST BE EXPLORED WHEN A SIMPLIFIED REPORT IS PROCESSED ONLY IF:

● CIRCUMSTANCES HAVE CHANGED SINCE THE LAST CASE ACTION AND MANAGEMENT IS NOW QUESTIONABLE (SUCH AS THE HOUSEHOLD REPORTS LOSS OF INCOME)

OR

● MANAGEMENT WAS NOT ADEQUATELY EXPLAINED AND DOCUMENTED AT THE PREVIOUS APPLICATION OR REDETERMINATION.

II. PROCEDURES

* THERE ARE NO PROCEDURES ASSOCIATED WITH THIS POLICY.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

OFS 4MW Form/Instructions Management Review Worksheet

IV. REFERENCES

There are no references associated with this policy. **

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C-Case Processing (FITAP) Section No./Name C-500-FITAP-SNAP Management Document No./Name C-530-FITAP How To Evaluate Management Effective Dates May 1, 2022

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

*** THE MANAGEMENT REVIEW – * DETAILS SCREEN IN LITE IS AN ** *** INTERVIEWING TOOL THAT * IS USED TO DOCUMENT THE DISCUSSION OF ** HOW A HOUSEHOLD MANAGES THEIR EXPENSES IN RELATION TO THEIR NET INCOME. COMPLETION *** IS REQUIRED FOR ALL HOUSEHOLDS THAT REPORT ZERO INCOME OR THE EXPENSES REPORTED ARE EQUAL TO OR EXCEED THE REPORTED * INCOME.

THE OFS 4MW, MANAGEMENT REVIEW WORKSHEET, MAY BE USED AS A GUIDE TO DISCUSS MANAGEMENT.

II. PROCEDURES

● REVIEW THE CASE TO SEE IF THERE IS ENOUGH INCOME TO MEET THE HOUSEHOLD'S EXPENSES. CONSIDER HOW THE CLIENT PAYS FOR FOOD, SHELTER, UTILITIES, CLOTHING, DAY-TO-DAY EXPENSES, AND ALL OTHER REGULAR BILLS. LOOK FOR CLUES TO UNREPORTED EXPENSES, INCOME, OR RESOURCES.

● DETERMINE IF THE HOUSEHOLD HAS MULTIPLE SOURCES OF INCOME SUCH AS INCOME FROM TIPS, COMMISSIONS, OVERTIME, OR BONUSES.

● WHEN A HOUSEHOLD BORROWS MONEY FROM FRIENDS OR RELATIVES, DETERMINE IF THE LOANS ARE TEMPORARY, IF THE CLIENT INTENDS TO REPAY THE LOAN, AND WHEN REPAYMENT WILL BEGIN.

● DETERMINE IF A HOUSEHOLD'S EXPENSES ARE PAID DIRECTLY BY ANOTHER SOURCE, SUCH AS HUD RENTAL ASSISTANCE, THE SALVATION ARMY, INSURANCE, OR ANOTHER PERSON OUTSIDE THE HOUSEHOLD.

● DETERMINE WHETHER INFORMATION GIVEN IN THE PAST IS CONSISTENT WITH THE CURRENT SITUATION AND IF RELIABLE ASSUMPTIONS FOR FUTURE PERIODS CAN BE MADE BASED ON THE INFORMATION.

● DETERMINE IF ANY BILLS ARE UNPAID, WHEN THE CLIENT LAST PAID THESE BILLS AND WHEN THEY ** EXPECT TO PAY THEM AGAIN.

● EVALUATE FACTS SUCH AS AGE, EDUCATION, DISABILITY AND FORMER SOURCES OF INCOME.

● EXPLORE POTENTIAL SOURCES OF INCOME AND RESOURCES FOR EACH PERSON.

● HOME VISITS MAY HELP THE WORKER EVALUATE THE CLIENT'S SITUATION.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS
