6 of 18 DOCUMENT THE CASE WITH A CASE NOTE INDICATING THAT THE HOUSEHOLD REQUESTED WITHDRAWAL OF THE APPLICATION AND ALL OTHER CASE ACTIVITY.

If the reported change results in disqualification due receipt of lottery or gambling winnings of $4500 or more won in a single game or before taxes or other withholdings, the case must be closed. LITE will send Advance Notice of Adverse Action informing the household the case will close due to substantial lottery or gambling winnings.

For cases in LITE, the worker must enter the amount of the winnings as a resource so that LITE will close the SNAP case and send a Notice of Decision.

An automatic case note will be created by LITE explaining that the case closed due to receipt of the substantial lottery or gambling winnings.

Example 1: Johnny wins a jackpot at the casino in the amount of $10,000 before taxes on March 1. The casino took $1000 in taxes before giving Johnny $9000. Johnny purchases a vehicle with the $9000. Johnny reported the winnings on April 10, which is the date he is required to report. Even though Johnny no longer has the $9000, his SNAP case must be disqualified. The worker would enter $10,000 on the resource screen for Johnny so that the household is disqualified.

Example 2: Johnny wins a jackpot at the casino in the amount of $5,000 before taxes or other withholdings on March 1. The casino took $500 for taxes and $2500 due to a child support garnishment giving Johnny $2000. Johnny reported the winnings on April 10, which is the date he is required to report. Johnny put the remaining $2000 in his savings account. Even though Johnny has only $2000 remaining and is below the resource limit, his SNAP case must be disqualified because his winnings before taxes and other withholdings was $5000.

C-821-2-SNAP - PR Increasing Benefits

IF THE REPORTED CHANGE RESULTS IN AN INCREASE IN BENEFITS, REQUEST VERIFICATION, IF NECESSARY. ALLOW THE HOUSEHOLD 10 DAYS TO PROVIDE THE REQUIRED VERIFICATION. IF THE 10TH DAY FALLS ON A WEEKEND OR HOLIDAY, THE DUE DATE BECOMES THE FOLLOWING WORKDAY.

• IF THE VERIFICATION IS RECEIVED BY THE DUE DATE GIVEN ON THE REQUEST FOR VERIFICATION, INCREASE BENEFITS EFFECTIVE THE MONTH AFTER THE CHANGE WAS REPORTED. AUTHORIZE SUPPLEMENTAL BENEFITS IF NECESSARY. SEND CONCURRENT NOTICE.

• IF VERIFICATION IS NOT RECEIVED BY THE DUE DATE, BUT IS LATER PROVIDED, INCREASE BENEFITS EFFECTIVE THE MONTH AFTER THE VERIFICATION IS RECEIVED. SEND CONCURRENT NOTICE.

7 of 18 • IF THE HOUSEHOLD DOES NOT PROVIDE VERIFICATION, DO NOT TAKE ACTION TO INCREASE BENEFITS. NO FURTHER ACTION WILL BE REQUIRED.

• A NOTE SHOULD BE INCLUDED IN THE REQUEST FOR VERIFICATION, THAT BENEFITS CANNOT BE INCREASED UNTIL THE VERIFICATION HAS BEEN PROVIDED.

IF THE REPORTED CHANGE RESULTS IN AN INCREASE IN BENEFITS AND IS REPORTED ON THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT IN THE MONTH PRIOR TO THE REPORT MONTH, INCREASE BENEFITS EFFECTIVE THE MONTH AFTER THE CHANGE IS REPORTED IF THE VERIFICATION IS RECEIVED BY THE DUE DATE GIVEN ON THE REQUEST FOR VERIFICATION. AUTHORIZE SUPPLEMENTAL BENEFITS, IF NECESSARY.

(SEE C-850-SNAP/FITAP FOR PROCEDURES TO DETERMINE IF THE FIRST MONTH BENEFITS ARE AFFECTED).

AN OFS 18C SHOULD NOT BE SENT TO REQUEST VERIFICATION FOR INFORMATION REPORTED ON THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT. THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT IS CONSIDERED THE REQUEST FOR VERIFICATION AT SIMPLIFIED REPORT. THE 5TH OF THE SR MONTH IS THE DUE DATE FOR THE REQUESTED VERIFICATION.

EXAMPLE: A JUNE SIMPLIFIED REPORT IS RECEIVED IN THE OFFICE ON MAY 30. THE CLIENT REPORTS THAT PREVIOUSLY VERIFIED CONTRIBUTIONS HAVE DECREASED FROM $350 PER MONTH TO $100 PER MONTH. NO VERIFICATION IS PROVIDED.

• IF THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT IS RECEIVED IN MAY AND VERIFICATION IS PROVIDED IN MAY OR NO LATER THAN JUNE 5TH, INCREASE BENEFITS EFFECTIVE JULY. ISSUE SUPPLEMENTAL BENEFITS FOR JUNE.

• IF THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT IS RECEIVED IN MAY AND VERIFICATION IS PROVIDED IN JUNE, BUT AFTER THE 5TH OF THE MONTH, INCREASE BENEFITS EFFECTIVE JULY. NO SUPPLEMENTAL BENEFITS ARE ISSUED FOR JUNE.

• IF THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT IS RECEIVED IN MAY AND VERIFICATION IS NOT PROVIDED, DO NOT REQUEST VERIFICATION. THE $350 CONTRIBUTIONS WILL CONTINUE TO BE BUDGETED.

IF THE REPORTED CHANGE RESULTS IN AN INCREASE IN BENEFITS AND IS REPORTED ON THE REDETERMINATION APPLICATION IN THE MONTH PRIOR TO THE REDETERMINATION MONTH, INCREASE BENEFITS EFFECTIVE THE REDETERMINATION MONTH IF THE VERIFICATION IS RECEIVED BY THE DUE DATE GIVEN ON THE REQUEST FOR VERIFICATION. AUTHORIZE SUPPLEMENTAL BENEFITS, IF NECESSARY. (SEE DOCUMENT C-850-SNAP/FITAP FOR PROCEDURES TO DETERMINE THE FIRST MONTH BENEFITS ARE AFFECTED.)

EXAMPLE 1: MAY REDET APPLICATION IS RECEIVED IN THE OFFICE ON APRIL 20 REPORTING A CHANGE THAT WILL RESULT IN AN INCREASE IN BENEFITS. VERIFICATION IS REQUESTED AND RECEIVED TIMELY. THE WORKER PROCESSES THE CASE ON APRIL 26. THE BENEFIT INCREASE WOULD BE EFFECTIVE FOR MAY. THE CASE IS RECERTIFIED EFFECTIVE JUNE.

EXAMPLE 2: A MAY REDETERMINATION APPLICATION IS RECEIVED IN THE OFFICE ON APRIL 20 REPORTING A CHANGE THAT WILL RESULT IN AN INCREASE IN BENEFITS. VERIFICATION IS REQUESTED AND RECEIVED TIMELY. THE WORKER PROCESSES THE CASE ON MAY 15. THE CHANGE RESULTS IN AN INCREASE IN BENEFITS THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN EFFECTIVE MAY. A SUPPLEMENT MUST BE ISSUED FOR MAY AND THE CASE RECERTIFIED EFFECTIVE JUNE.

EXAMPLE 3: A MAY REDETERMINATION APPLICATION IS RECEIVED IN THE OFFICE ON APRIL 20 REPORTING A CHANGE THAT WILL RESULT IN AN INCREASE IN BENEFITS. THE WORKER REQUESTS VERIFICATION ON APRIL 20. VERIFICATION IS RECEIVED ON MAY 10. THE CHANGE IS EFFECTIVE JUNE SINCE THE VERIFICATION WAS NOT RECEIVED TIMELY. THE CASE IS RECERTIFIED EFFECTIVE JUNE.

EXAMPLE 4: A MAY REDETERMINATION APPLICATION IS RECEIVED IN THE OFFICE ON APRIL 11 REPORTING A CHANGE THAT WILL RESULT IN A DECREASE IN BENEFITS (THE CLIENT'S SON HAS MOVED OUT OF THE HOME). THE WORKER PROCESSES THE CASE ON APRIL 11 AND SENDS A NOTICE OF ADVERSE ACTION. THE BENEFITS WILL DECREASE EFFECTIVE MAY. THE CASE IS RECERTIFIED EFFECTIVE JUNE.

EXAMPLE 5: A MAY REDETERMINATION APPLICATION IS RECEIVED IN THE OFFICE ON APRIL 26 REPORTING A CHANGE THAT WILL RESULT IN A DECREASE IN BENEFITS. THE WORKER PROCESSES THE CASE IN THE REDETERMINATION MONTH ON MAY 15. THE CHANGE IS EFFECTIVE JUNE AND THE CASE IS RECERTIFIED EFFECTIVE JUNE.

C-821-3-SNAP - PR Information Insufficient to Determine Eligibility and Benefit Level

IF THE REPORTED INFORMATION IS INSUFFICIENT TO DETERMINE ELIGIBILITY AND BENEFIT LEVEL, DO NOT CLEAR INFORMATION ON SIEVS, LDET, Experian, OR BENDEX. CONTACT THE HOUSEHOLD BY TELEPHONE TO DISCUSS THE REPORTED CHANGE. IF THE HOUSEHOLD CANNOT BE REACHED, SEND A SEMI-AUTOMATED FFCCL - CLIENT CONTACT LETTER, (18C-FF) IN LITE, REQUESTING THAT THE HOUSEHOLD CONTACT THE DEPARTMENT TO DISCUSS THE REPORTED CHANGE. ALLOW TEN CALENDAR DAYS FOR THE HOUSEHOLD TO CONTACT THE DEPARTMENT. IF THE 10th DAY FALLS ON A WEEKEND OR HOLIDAY, THE DUE DATE BECOMES THE FOLLOWING WORKDAY.

IF THE HOUSEHOLD CONTACTS THE DEPARTMENT, OBTAIN THE INFORMATION NECESSARY TO DETERMINE THE EFFECT OF THE CHANGE ON THE BENEFITS.

C-822-1-SNAP - PR Residential Address Change

When a residential address is updated in LITE and Next is clicked, an end date will automatically populate for all existing shelter expenses without end dates. A Free Form Client Contact Letter (FFCCL) is automatically generated and sent to the household requesting new shelter expense information and verification. The household will be allowed 10 days to provide the information. If the 10th day falls on a weekend or holiday, the due date becomes the following workday.

A pending shelter cost task is automatically generated with a due date of 10 days. The task documents that new shelter costs information has been requested resulting from a residential address change.

If the household provides the requested shelter expense information:

• click start work item on the task to proceed to data collection, • navigate to shelter expenses, • add the new shelter expenses, run eligibility and authorize the case.

If the household does not provide the requested information:

• click start work item on the task to proceed to Data Collection, • navigate to shelter expenses, • run eligibility and authorize the case.

If benefits are reduced or ended resulting from changes in shelter costs, a Notice of Adverse Action (NOAA) will be generated and sent to the household.

C-822-2-SNAP - PR Returned Mail

IF MAIL IS RETURNED FROM THE U.S. POSTAL SERVICE AS UNDELIVERABLE THAT INCLUDES A FORWARDING ADDRESS, CONTACT THE HOUSEHOLD TO CONFIRM THAT THE MAILING ADDRESS ON THE RETURNED MAIL IS CORRECT. C-823-SNAP - PR INCOME CHANGES

1. Household reports a change which would not increase benefits.

If a household reports a change in employers and the effect on the benefits is not obvious, complete a manual budget based on the client’s statement of his new wages. If the household income has increased but remains below 130% of the federal poverty level for the household size limit for the household size and benefits would decrease, do not take action to reduce benefits. Document in CAFÉ that the change was reported and the household remained eligible. A copy of the manual budget should be saved in document repository system.

2. One check stub was received to report new income or a new hourly wage.

• The worker must determine the effect of the change. A change in student status is not a reportable change. • If the client meets another exemption to student policy, the wages should be removed since this would result in an increase. • If the loss of wages would result in the client being an ineligible student and would result in a decrease in benefits, no action is taken unless the client provides verification of termination at the time of the reported change.

4. A client begins receiving SSI and sends a copy of the award letter. Since the award letter originated from SSA, it would be considered verified upon receipt. Action should be taken on the SNAP case and the income budgeted after expiration of NOAA.

5. A client reports that he has begun receiving SSI. No verification from SSA has been received. The increase in income would not be considered verified upon receipt since the information did not come from the primary source. If the reported income does not exceed the applicable gross income limit, the change should be documented and no action should be taken on the case. Verification of the income should not be requested.

3. A household reports that she moved and had a change in rental and utility expenses, as well as a change in household composition. The effect of all reported changes must be determined. If the benefits would increase based on all reported changes, the changes must be documented and action taken on all of the changes reported. The change in household composition is considered verified upon receipt. Shelter costs are not required to be verified unless questionable. If the shelter expense is questionable and verification was not provided and benefits would decrease, do not take action on the changes since all questionable changes were not verified. Document the changes reported and reason for not taking action. If the shelter expense is not questionable, the change is considered verified upon receipt; therefore, action must be taken on all reported changes.

WHEN A FITAP CASE IS REVIEWED BECAUSE OF A GRANT REVIEW AND CHILD SUPPORT INCOME IS VERIFIED THROUGH LASES, THIS IS VERIFIED UPON RECEIPT AND MUST BE BUDGETED IN THE SNAP CASE. REFER TO CHAPTER 4, POLICIES B-1270 AND B-620-8-2.

C-825-4-SNAP - PR Information Reported by Quality Control (QC)

1. Quality Control (QC) notifies the local office that a household has refused to cooperate with the QC review process by sending the Quality Control Refusal to Cooperate Notification (QC 9RTC).

A report of non-cooperation received from QC is considered a change that is verified upon receipt. Follow policy in C-1313-SNAP and send advance notice of adverse action informing the household their case will be closed on the expiration of the advance notice of adverse action unless they cooperate with QC. The worker must complete the “TO BE COMPLETED BY THE PARISH OFFICE” section of the QC 9RTC originally sent by QC and return to the QC reviewer the same day the case action is completed. If during the advance notice of adverse action period the client indicates willingness to cooperate, contact the QC reviewer immediately or before the

2. QC notifies the local office that a household has failed to cooperate with the QC review process by sending the Quality Control Failure to Cooperate Notification (QC 9FTC). The QC 9FTC informs the local office that QC’s attempts to contact/locate the client were unsuccessful and requests assistance in contacting/locating the client.

Upon receipt of the QC 9FTC, the worker must contact the household by telephone within 5 days and advise the household that they must cooperate with QC. If the household cannot be reached by telephone, send a Client Contact Letter (OFS 18C), advising the household to contact the local office within 10 days to discuss cooperating with the QC review process.

• If the worker, speaks to the client or a responsible household member and informs the household of the requirement to cooperate with QC, the worker must complete the “TO BE COMPLETED BY THE PARISH OFFICE” section of the QC 9FTC originally sent by QC. The worker must return the form to the QC reviewer the same day contact is made with the household.

• If the household fails to respond to the OFS 18C request for contact to discuss cooperating with the QC review process, no action is needed. The client’s failure to respond will continue to be considered a failure to cooperate with QC and will not result in case closure.

3. QC reports a change in income discovered during the QC review.

Action should only be taken if the change results in a benefit increase or the income exceeds the gross income limit. Action is not taken if the change would result in decreased benefits. The information is not considered verified upon receipt since additional information would be required.

The worker must enter a case note documenting all activities.

THIS SHOULD BE TREATED AS IF THE CLIENT HAD REPORTED THE CHANGE. A DECISION MUST BE MADE BASED UPON THE CLIENT’S STATEMENT AS THIS INFORMATION IS NOT CONSIDERED VERIFIED AT THIS POINT.

C-825-7-SNAP - PR Louisiana Department of Health (LDH)

THE LOUISIANA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (LDH) RECEIVES DAILY FILES FROM THE LOUISIANA VITAL RECORDS REGISTRY (VRR) OF DECEASED INDIVIDUALS VIA LITE. LDH RUNS A MATCH BETWEEN DECEASED INDIVIDUALS AND INDIVIDUALS WHO RECEIVE SNAP AND THE ASSOCIATED FITAP OR KCSP.

LITE WILL AUTOMATICALLY UPDATE THE CASE OF EACH DECEASED INDIVIDUAL REPORTED THROUGH THE MATCH, EXCLUDE THE MEMBER SEND THE APPROPRIATE NOTICE TO THE HOUSEHOLD, IF REQUIRED, AND GENERATE AN AUTOMATED CASE NOTE IN LITE. However, a notice will not be generated for SNAP single person household cases since a notice is not required when all household members are deceased.

C-826-SNAP - PR RESOURCE CHANGES

Example:

A client reports receipt of a large lump sum payment from Worker’s Compensation. The payment puts her well over the resource limit.

• If the client provides verification of the resource, the change must be acted upon if the household is not categorically eligible.

• If verification is not provided, no action is taken. Document the report including the reason the change was not acted upon, but take no further action. Receipt of a resource is not a reportable change.

EXAMPLE: OBSERVE HOUSEHOLD MEMBER WORKING AT A NEW JOB OR LEARN OF THE BIRTH OF A HOUSEHOLD MEMBER.

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

IN SOME ADVERSE ACTION SITUATIONS, THE CLIENT IS ENTITLED TO 13-DAY ADVANCE NOTICE. THIS PERIOD IS DETERMINED BY COUNTING 13 DAYS FROM THE DATE THE NOTICE IS MAILED, CONSIDERING THE DAY AFTER THE DATE THE NOTICE IS MAILED AS THE FIRST DAY. THE ACTION MUST NOT BE TAKEN DURING THE ADVANCE NOTICE PERIOD WHICH EXPIRES AT 4:30 P.M. ON THE 13TH DAY. IF THE 13TH DAY FALLS ON A WEEKEND OR HOLIDAY, TREAT THE FOLLOWING WORKDAY AS THE 13TH DAY. OTHER ADVERSE ACTIONS ARE EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY.

C-831-SNAP - PO ADVERSE ACTIONS THAT REQUIRE ADVANCE NOTICE

EXCEPT AS SPECIFIED IN C-832 BELOW, SEND 13-DAY ADVANCE NOTICE OF ADVERSE ACTION TO REDUCE BENEFITS OR CLOSE A CASE.

C-832-SNAP - PO ADVERSE ACTIONS THAT ARE EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY

IN THE FOLLOWING SITUATIONS, 13-DAY ADVANCE NOTICE IS NOT REQUIRED. A CONCURRENT NOTICE IS SENT TO THE CLIENT WHEN:

1. THE AGENCY DISQUALIFIES A HOUSEHOLD MEMBER BECAUSE OF AN INTENTIONAL PROGRAM VIOLATION AND THE BENEFITS OF THE REMAINING HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS ARE REDUCED OR ENDED BECAUSE OF THE DISQUALIFICATION. FORM FR 15A IS SENT BY THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT AND A CONCURRENT NOTICE OF REDUCTION IS SENT BY LITE.

2. THE WORKER REDUCES OR ENDS BENEFITS AT THE END OF A NORMAL PERIOD OF CERTIFICATION WHEN THE HOUSEHOLD TIMELY REAPPLIES.

3. A CLIENT HAS BEEN CERTIFIED IN ANOTHER STATE AND THAT FACT HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED.

4. THE CLIENT SIGNS A STATEMENT REQUESTING CLOSURE OR REDUCTION IN BENEFITS AND WAIVING THE RIGHT TO ADVANCE NOTICE.

5. BENEFITS ARE REDUCED OR TERMINATED EFFECTIVE THE MONTH FOLLOWING THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT MONTH AS A RESULT OF CHANGES REPORTED THROUGH THE SIMPLIFIED REPORTING PROCESS.

EXCEPTION: ADVANCE NOTICE IS REQUIRED PRIOR TO IMPOSING A SANCTION FOR FLEEING FELON RESTRICTIONS, PROBATION/PAROLE VIOLATIONS, Adults convicted of certain felonies as stated in E-221-1-SNAP-PO, AND FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS, SUCH AS VOLUNTARY QUIT and refusal to comply with QC.

E-MAIL CORRESPONDENCE IS CONSIDERED A SIGNED, WRITTEN REPORT IF IT IS SENT BY THE HEAD OF THE HOUSEHOLD OR OTHER RESPONSIBLE HOUSEHOLD MEMBER FROM THE E-MAIL ADDRESS THAT THE HOUSEHOLD HAS PREVIOUSLY REPORTED AS THEIR E-MAIL ADDRESS.

7. MASS CHANGES.

8. The worker determines, based on reliable information, that the household has moved or will be moving out of the state prior to the next monthly issuance. Send the notice of closure to the last known address.

9. The client applied for PA and SNAP at the same time and has been getting SNAP while waiting for approval of the PA grant. In these cases, the client was notified at the time of certification that his SNAP allotment would be reduced if the grant was approved.

10. The client was a certified resident in a drug or alcohol treatment center or a group living arrangement which loses its state certification or FNA disqualifies it as a retailer.

11. The expedited household provides postponed verification which reduces or terminates benefits.

Do not send notice to the household concurrent with taking the action when:

1. All members of a household have died. The EBT card must be cancelled. A replacement EBT card must not be issued.

2. The client's allotment changes from month to month during the certification period because of changes expected at time of certification. In these cases, the client was informed at the time of certification what his allotment would be each month of the certification period.

3. The agency recoups benefits from a client who previously received a repayment demand letter.

4. The Fraud and Recovery Section converts a cash payment to allotment reduction because the household failed to make agreed payments on a claim.

IF THE HOUSEHOLD DOES NOT WAIVE ITS RIGHT TO CONTINUED BENEFITS, BENEFITS SHALL CONTINUE AT THE SAME LEVEL UNTIL THE END OF THE CERTIFICATION PERIOD OR UNTIL THE RESOLUTION OF THE HEARING, WHICHEVER IS FIRST.

C-833-2-SNAP - PO Concurrent Notice of Adverse Action

IF THE CLIENT REQUESTS A FAIR HEARING WITHIN 13 DAYS OF THE MAILING DATE OF A NOTICE WHICH WAS SENT CONCURRENT WITH THE ACTION, REINSTATE BENEFITS TO THE PREVIOUS LEVEL WITHIN 5 DAYS FROM THE DATE OF RECEIPT OF THE HOUSEHOLD'S REQUEST FOR A FAIR HEARING UNLESS THE CLIENT WAIVES HIS RIGHT TO CONTINUED BENEFITS. IF THE REQUEST FOR A FAIR HEARING IS SUBMITTED BY MAIL, IT MUST BE POSTMARKED BY THE 13TH DAY AFTER THE CONCURRENT NOTICE WAS SENT. IF THE 13TH DAY FALLS ON A WEEKEND OR HOLIDAY, TREAT THE FOLLOWING WORKDAY AS THE 13TH DAY.

IF THE HOUSEHOLD DOES NOT WAIVE ITS RIGHT TO CONTINUED BENEFITS, BENEFITS WILL BE REINSTATED AT THE PRIOR LEVEL AND CONTINUE UNTIL THE END OF THE CERTIFICATION PERIOD OR UNTIL THE RESOLUTION OF THE HEARING, WHICHEVER IS FIRST.

THIS APPLIES IF ACTION WAS TAKEN TO REDUCE OR END BENEFITS BASED SOLELY ON WRITTEN INFORMATION FROM THE HOUSEHOLD.

NOTE: REINSTATEMENT OF BENEFITS IS NOT APPLICABLE FOR CHANGES OR CLOSURES MADE AT THE END OF A NORMAL PERIOD OF CERTIFICATION.

3. Supplemental - additional benefits provided to a household during a month when benefits have already been issued. Supplemental benefits can only be issued for the current benefit month to correct an administrative error, or because of administrative limitations, such as the computer being down on cut-off date.

If restoration is due and there is an existing claim, send two copies of form 20CD documenting the restoration to the Fraud and Recovery Section for review. If approved, the claim will be offset with the amount of the restored benefits and the balance, if any, will be refunded to the household by Fraud and Recovery.

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The amount of benefits is based on assistance unit size and countable income.

Prorated benefits are paid from the date of application unless the case was closed in error.

● If the prorated budgetary deficit is $.01 through $9.99, no benefits are paid.

● If the prorated budgetary deficit is $10 or more, the benefit amount is the prorated budgetary deficit rounded down to the nearest dollar.

*** * Refer to C-840-FITAP, section C-841 for benefit issuance when adding a person to an existing grant.

II. PROCEDURES

LITE will determine ** the budgetary deficit by subtracting countable earned plus countable unearned income from the appropriate FITAP flat grant amount. *** * The benefit amount will be determined by rounding down the full budgetary deficit or the prorated budgetary deficit amount.

● If the full budgetary deficit is $.01 through $9.99, no benefits are paid.

● If the full budgetary deficit is $10.00 or more, the benefit amount is the budgetary deficit rounded down to the nearest dollar.

C-921-FITAP - PR COMPUTING THE PRORATED BUDGETARY DEFICIT

If the budgetary deficit is not a whole dollar amount, LITE will use the following formula to compute the prorated budgetary deficit:

(Prior to rounding down)

Amount of budgetary deficit X (31 - Date of Application)

30

Example: On October 8th, Mrs. Jones applies for FITAP for herself and her three minor children. She has countable unearned income of $174.35.

Mrs. Jones meets the eligibility test. Her October benefit amount is computed as follows:

Flat Grant (4)

$568.00 Less Countable Income - 174.35 Budgetary Deficit = $393.65

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-900-FITAP-SNAP Issuing Benefits Document No./Name C-930-SNAP Issuing Methods Effective Date April 1, 2026

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

LITE authorizes benefits on a monthly basis to ongoing cases during the first 23 calendar days of each month as follows:

Last Digit of Social Security Number (SSN) (unless the head of the household is Elderly or any member of the household is Disabled): SNAP benefits are available after 5 a.m. on the: The head of the household is Elderly or any member is Disabled

(1st-4th of every month) 0 5th of every month 1 7th of every month 2 9th of every month 3 11th of every month 4 13th of every month 5 15th of every month 6 17th of every month 7 19th of every month 8 21st of every month 9 23rd of every month

Benefits may also be authorized automatically by LITE when:

• certifying a case,

• recertifying a timely reapplication after cutoff,

• authorizing the second month’s benefits on an expedited case with postponed verification that is provided after cutoff, or

• a Manual Issuance request is entered in LITE by the local office or by State Office.

LITE benefit issuance is batch oriented and benefits are authorized the same day for all actions.

Benefits issued through a Manual Issuance are available either the same day or the following day after the issuance request is entered in LITE. Examples of Manual Issuance reasons include:

• authorizing the first month’s benefits for a new certification period when a redetermination is completed after the end of the redetermination month.

2 of 4 • authorizing second month's benefits on an expedited case with postponed verification that is provided timely, but the case closes in error,

• meeting time limits for case actions,

• authorizing replacement benefits,

• authorizing supplemental benefits, or

• restoring benefits for prior months.

C-931-SNAP – PO STATE OFFICE ISSUING METHOD

All regular benefits are automatically authorized by State Office each month.

State Office assigns benefit dates 1 through 23 as indicated in the above chart.

If the household's SSI/Social Security income or work registration status changes, the benefit date would also be reassigned.

C-932-SNAP – PO MANUAL ISSUANCE

When benefits must be issued on the same day or the following day, follow procedures outlined in C- 932-SNAP-PR.

Do not authorize benefits before the month for which they are intended, except when first and second months' SNAP benefits must be authorized simultaneously. (See C-933-SNAP - PO).

Do not authorize benefits for more than 12 months in the past.

C-933-SNAP – PO SIMULTANEOUS AUTHORIZATION OF FIRST AND SECOND MONTHS' BENEFITS

Households applying for SNAP benefits after the 15th of the month may have their first and second months’ benefits authorized at the same time if determined eligible for both months under certain circumstances.

NOTE: Migrant or seasonal farm workers eligible to receive the full month's benefits in the first month of the certification period will not be authorized simultaneous benefits.

3 of 4

C-933-1-SNAP – PO Non-Expedited Cases Certified In the First or Second Month

Households applying for SNAP benefits after the 15th of the month must have their first and second months' benefits authorized at the same time if:

• The household has completed the application process and has provided all required verification, and

• The household has been determined eligible to receive benefits for the initial month of application and the following month.

C-933-2-SNAP – PO Expedited Cases

Households applying for benefits after the 15th of the month and determined expedited shall have their first and second months' benefits authorized at the same time regardless of whether or not verification has been postponed.

II. PROCEDURES

C-931-SNAP – PR STATE OFFICE ISSUING METHOD

State Office automatically issues and deposits benefits on the client’s Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card based on the appropriate mail code.

C-932-SNAP – PR MANUAL ISSUANCE

When benefits must be issued outside of the automatic process, the following procedures should be followed:

• Complete form SNAP 38 with the household, if replacing benefits. (See Document C-940-SNAP- PO.)

• Determine if the benefit month is older than 12 months. If it is, a manual issuance cannot be completed.

• Complete form OFS 35 to request a Manual Issuance of SNAP benefits .

• Obtain supervisory approval for Manual Issuance of benefits.

• Request that the Manual Issuance be entered in LITE.

• Document the activity in LITE.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 04 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name C – Case Processing Section No./Name C-900-FITAP-SNAP Issuing Benefits Document No./Name C-940-SNAP Replacing Benefits Effective Date September 10, 2019

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

C-941-SNAP REPLACEMENT OF FOOD DESTROYED IN A HOUSEHOLD MISFORTUNE

Replacement benefits can be authorized if food purchased with * SNAP benefits is ** destroyed in a household misfortune.

Prior to authorizing replacement benefits, review the case record *** and other applicable documentation to determine:

● if the benefit was correctly authorized;

● if the household has timely reported the destruction of the food in a household misfortune and

● if the household has timely executed the form SNAP 38.

The household must:

1. Report verbally or in writing the loss of the food within 10 calendar days of the household misfortune.

2. Execute the form SNAP 38 within 10 calendar days of the report of the household misfortune.

NOTE: If the 10th day falls on a weekend or holiday, treat the following workday as the 10th calendar day.

The worker must:

1. Determine that food purchased with food benefits was destroyed in a household misfortune or disaster, such as, but not limited to, a fire or flood. If food was destroyed due to a power outage, the power must have been out for at least 24 hours. Verify this through:

o a collateral contact,

o documentation from a community organization including, but not limited to, the Red Cross or fire department, or

o a home visit. ***

2. Mail the form SNAP 38 if the *** household *** is unable to come to the office because of:

o age, handicap, or distance from the office, and

o is unable to appoint an authorized representative. ***

2 of 3 3. Authorize replacement benefits within two days of the date the form SNAP 38 is received by the local office or within 10 days of the report of the household misfortune, whichever is later.

NOTE: If the signed form SNAP 38 is received within the 10-day limit, replacement benefits can be authorized in the month following the month of the misfortune.

4. Document the replacement in the case record.

There is no limit on the number of replacement benefits authorized to replace food destroyed in a household misfortune.

The value of the replacement benefit will be in the amount equal to the value of the food destroyed in the misfortune up to a maximum of one month's allotment for that SNAP household unless the loss includes food purchased with restored benefits which will be replaced in the amount of the loss up to the full value of the restoration.

Example: A one person household reports losing $200 worth of food purchased with SNAP benefits. The household received $150.00 in SNAP benefits. The maximum allotment for a one person household is $192. Since the household only received $150, the replacement amount cannot exceed the monthly allotment the household received of $150.

Deny the request for a replacement benefit if:

● the household did not report the loss within 10 days of the household misfortune;

● the form SNAP 38 was not executed within 10 days of the report of the household misfortune; or

● available documentation indicates that the household's request for replacement appears to be fraudulent.

Inform the household of the right to a fair hearing to contest the denial or delay of a replacement benefit. Do not make replacements while the denial or delay is being appealed.

II. PROCEDURES

The worker for the case must verify the loss and issue replacement benefits, if the form SNAP 38 is mailed and returned.

If client resides in a parish different from the worker’s parish, advise the client to visit their local office to sign the form SNAP 38. The worker in the local office * who received ** the form SNAP 38 must verify the loss and issue replacement benefits.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name E-Special Households (FITAP) Section No./Name E-100 FITAP Joint Special Households (FITAP) Document No./Name E-110-FITAP Sponsored Aliens Effective Date May 1, 2011

1 of 3 E-111-FITAP DEFINITION

A sponsor is a person or organization who executed an affidavit of support pursuant to Section 213A of the Immigration and Nationality Act on behalf of an alien, who is not the spouse or child of the sponsor, as a condition of the alien's entry into the U. S.

NOTE: NOT ALL ALIENS MUST OBTAIN A SPONSOR BEFORE BEING ADMITTED INTO THE U.S.

E-112-FITAP ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENT

When an alien is sponsored by an individual count the income and resources of the alien's sponsor and sponsor's spouse, if living in the home, in determining the eligibility and level of benefits of the alien.

This applies until such time as the alien:

● achieves Unites States Citizenship through naturalization, or

● has worked 40 qualifying quarters of coverage, and in the case of any such qualifying quarter creditable for any period beginning after December 31, 1996, did not receive any federal means- tested public benefits.

Exception: The battered alien, the alien parent of a battered child and the child of a battered alien parent are not subject to alien sponsor provisions for up to 12 months.

E-113-FITAP RESPONSIBILITY TO PROVIDE INFORMATION

THE ALIEN IS RESPONSIBLE FOR OBTAINING ALL INFORMATION FROM THE SPONSOR AND FOR REPORTING ALL CHANGES IN THE SPONSOR'S SITUATION ACCORDING TO THE RULES FOR REPORTING CHANGES.

DENY THE ALIEN'S APPLICATION IF HE REFUSES TO COOPERATE.

E-114-FITAP * RESERVED **

***

E-115-FITAP INCOME

CONSIDER ALL OF THE SPONSOR'S AND SPONSOR'S SPOUSE'S IF LIVING WITH THE SPONSOR, GROSS COUNTABLE INCOME AS AVAILABLE TO THE ALIEN'S HOUSEHOLD MINUS ONLY THE FOLLOWING DEDUCTIONS:

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name E-Special Households (FITAP) Section No./Name E-100 FITAP Joint Special Households (FITAP) Document No./Name E-110-FITAP Sponsored Aliens Effective Date May 1, 2011

2 of 3

● The lesser of:

o 20% of the total earned income, or o $175.00

● The appropriate Need Standard for the sponsor, spouse, and any other persons living in the home whom the sponsor claims or could claim as a dependent for Federal income tax purposes.

● Total amounts the sponsor or spouse pays to anyone not living in the household but whom the sponsor or spouse claims or could claim as a dependent for Federal income tax purposes.

● Total verified alimony or child support the sponsor or spouse pays to persons not living in the household.

Budget the amount remaining as unearned income available to the alien.

If a person sponsors more than one alien, prorate the amount of counted income evenly among the sponsored aliens.

Note: If the alien switches sponsors during the certification period, then deemed income/resources would be recalculated based on the required information about the new sponsor as soon as possible after the information is supplied by the alien and verified by the local office.

E-116-FITAP SPONSOR'S LIABILITY IN OVERISSUANCES

SPONSORS AND ALIENS ARE JOINTLY LIABLE FOR OVERISSUANCES RESULTING FROM INCORRECT INFORMATION PROVIDED BY THE SPONSOR UNLESS THE SPONSOR CAN SHOW GOOD CAUSE OR THAT HE WAS NOT AT FAULT FOR THE ERROR. GOOD CAUSE EXISTS IF INFORMATION CHANGES WITHOUT THE KNOWLEDGE OF THE SPONSOR OR IF THE SPONSOR IS OR WAS UNABLE TO REPORT DUE TO ILLNESS, ABSENCE, ETC.

E-117-FITAP VERIFICATION

THE ALIEN SHOULD HAVE A DOCUMENT INDICATING THE SECTION OF THE LAW UNDER WHICH HE WAS ADMITTED. IF THE ALIEN CANNOT OBTAIN THE NEEDED INFORMATION, THE WORKER MAY CONTACT UNITED STATES CITIZENSHIP AND IMMIGRATION SERVICES AT:

U. S. CITIZENSHIP AND IMMIGRATION SERVICES 2424 EDENBORN AVENUE SUITE 300 METAIRIE, LA 70001-1845

1 of 7 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

* NOT ALL ALIENS MUST OBTAIN A SPONSOR BEFORE BEING ADMITTED INTO THE UNITED STATES. **

E-111-SNAP - * PO DEFINITIONS **

A sponsor is a person who signed * a legally binding affidavit of support or similar agreement on or after December 19, 1997 **, agreeing to support an alien as a condition of his entry into the U.S. This includes the sponsor's spouse who lives with him even if they were not married when the affidavit was signed.

* Deeming is a process in which the Analyst or other assigned worker, in determining a non-citizen’s eligibility for SNAP and benefit allotment, counts a portion of the income and resources of a non- citizen’s sponsor as income and resources available to the non-citizen. **

E-112-SNAP - * PO ** ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENT

When an alien is sponsored by an individual, * a portion of ** the income and resources of the alien's sponsor and sponsor's spouse * are deemed available to the aliens eligible for SNAP when ** determining the eligibility and level of benefits of the alien's household ***.

● * Deeming ** applies until the alien:

o becomes a citizen through naturalization, ***

o has worked 40 qualifying quarters of Social Security coverage,

Note: Beginning January 1, 1997, a quarter in which the alien received federal means-tested benefits is not counted as a qualifying quarter of coverage.

o * loses Lawfully Admitted for Permanent Residence status and leaves the U. S.,

o obtains in removal proceedings a new grant of adjustment of status as relief from removal, or

o the sponsor dies. **

● * Deeming ** does not apply to:

o Aliens who are not required to have a sponsor such as refugees, and asylum grantees, * persons granted withholding of deportation, Amerasians, trafficking victims, SIVs, and Cuban or Haitian entrants. **

o The battered alien, the alien child of a battered alien and the alien parent of a battered child are not subject to alien deeming provisions for up to 12 months. * The 12-month exemption can be extended for an additional 12 months if the alien verifies that the battery is recognized:

 by a court,  administrative order, or  by the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), and  the agency determines that the battery has substantial connection to the need for benefits. **

o Any alien under 18 years of age.

o * Aliens whose sponsor has not signed a legally binding affidavit of support or signed an affidavit of support prior to December 19, 1997.

o Ineligible members who are ineligible due to Immigration Status. **

o Aliens who are entitled to an indigence exemption.

The immigrant is entitled to an indigence exemption from deeming if the immigrant’s household income, including cash or in-kind assistance provided by the sponsor or others, does not exceed 130 percent of the poverty income limit for the household’s size.

The * USCIS ** must be notified any time a sponsored alien has been determined indigent, * unless the alien opts out of the indigence determination. ** The notification must include the names of the sponsor and sponsored aliens.

Prior to determining whether an alien is indigent, explain the purpose of the determination to the alien and provide the alien the opportunity to refuse the determination. If the household refuses the determination, do not complete the indigence determination.

Inform the sponsored alien of the consequences of refusing this determination and the consequences of failure to provide such consent. If the sponsored alien fails to provide

E-113-SNAP - * PO ** RESPONSIBILITY TO PROVIDE INFORMATION

THE ALIEN IS RESPONSIBLE FOR OBTAINING ALL INFORMATION FROM THE SPONSOR AND FOR REPORTING ALL CHANGES IN THE SPONSOR'S SITUATION ACCORDING TO THE RULES FOR REPORTING CHANGES.

The alien is responsible for providing the names (or other identifying factors) of other aliens for whom the alien's sponsor has signed an agreement to support.

Determine how many of such other aliens are Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program applicants or participants.

If such information about other aliens for whom the sponsor is responsible is not provided, count all the deemed income and resource amounts until the information is provided.

DENY THE ALIEN'S APPLICATION IF HE REFUSES TO COOPERATE.

E-113-1-SNAP - * PO ** Awaiting Verification of Sponsor Information

The alien will be ineligible to participate until all information/verification needed to determine that portion of the alien sponsor's income and resources which is countable to the alien is provided.

Determine the eligibility of any remaining household members. Consider as available the income and resources of the ineligible alien excluding the income and resources of the alien's sponsor (and sponsor's spouse) in determining the eligibility and benefit level of the remaining household members.

If the sponsored alien refuses to cooperate in providing and/or verifying needed information, other adult members of the alien's household must provide and/or verify the information required.

If the same sponsor is responsible for the entire household, the entire household is ineligible until the needed sponsor information is provided and/or verified.

If the disqualified alien later provides the information, process the information as a reported change.

E-121-FITAP DEFINITION

A STRIKER IS ANYONE INVOLVED IN A STRIKE OR CONCERTED STOPPAGE OF WORK BY EMPLOYEES (INCLUDING A STOPPAGE BY REASON OF THE EXPIRATION OF A COLLECTIVE- BARGAINING AGREEMENT) AND ANY CONCERTED SLOWDOWN OR OTHER CONCERTED INTERRUPTION OF OPERATIONS BY EMPLOYEES.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name E – Special Households Section No./Name E-100-FITAP-SNAP Joint Special Households (FITAP and SNAP) Document No./Name E-120-SNAP Strikers Effective Date January 1, 2010

1 of 2 E-121-SNAP DEFINITION

A STRIKER IS ANYONE INVOLVED IN A STRIKE OR CONCERTED STOPPAGE OF WORK BY EMPLOYEES (INCLUDING A STOPPAGE BY REASON OF THE EXPIRATION OF A COLLECTIVE- BARGAINING AGREEMENT) AND ANY CONCERTED SLOWDOWN OR OTHER CONCERTED INTERRUPTION OF OPERATIONS BY EMPLOYEES.

A person's status as a striker ends only when he returns to the job, retires, quits, is locked out, or is fired, regardless of the length of the strike.

EXCEPTION: A federal, state, or local government employee who participates in a strike against such government and is dismissed from his job will be considered to have voluntarily quit without good cause.

E-122- SNAP PERSONS NOT CONSIDERED STRIKERS

A person is not considered a striker if he is

● exempt from work registration on the day before the strike for any reason other than employment (such as care of a child).

● not participating in the strike, but cannot work because of the strike. Example: airline pilots strike, and baggage handlers cannot work because there is no work.

● afraid to cross the picket line because of threatened harm.

● locked out of his job by employers, including a person who was considered a striker before the lockout.

E-123- SNAP ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS

A household with strikers is ineligible for supplemental nutrition assistance unless the household was eligible the day before the strike and is eligible at the time of application.

Treat the day prior to the strike as if it were the date of application. All points of eligibility must have been met as of that day for the household's current eligibility to be considered.

E-124- SNAP RESOURCES

If resources are over the maximum limit either the day before the strike or currently, the household is ineligible.

2 of 2 E-125- SNAP INCOME

E-125-1- SNAP Prestrike Eligibility

Use the income of all household members (including the striker) as of the day before the strike. If the household is ineligible, deny the household.

If the household would have been eligible before the strike, compute current eligibility. However, such households must not receive an increased allotment as a result of the decreased income of the striking member.

E-125-2- SNAP Current Eligibility

● Compare the striker's income on the day before the strike with his current income (including union benefits and part-time jobs). Count the higher of the two incomes.

● Add the striker's higher income to the current income of other household members.

If the household is not currently eligible, deny the household.

If the household is eligible based on current income and income before the strike, determine if the household meets all other eligibility criteria. Other eligibility criteria must be considered the same as income, i.e., the household must be eligible both currently and before the strike.

E-126- SNAP WORK REGISTRATION

A striker must comply fully with the work registration requirement. He does not have to accept employment at a location subject to a strike or lock-out. If a strike is prohibited under either the Taft- Hartley or Railway Labor Acts, the agency considers this a continuing offer of suitable employment to the striker. Failure by the striker to return to this employment, for any reason, is failure to comply with work registration requirements. This makes the entire household ineligible.

E-127- SNAP VERIFICATION

The worker may contact union and company officials to find out the probable length of the strike and to verify wages from the struck company, striker's benefits, or other help from the union.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name E-Special Households (SNAP) Section No./Name E-200-SNAP SNAP Special Households (SNAP) Document No./Name E-210-SNAP Boarders Effective Date September 1, 2013

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

E-211-SNAP - PO DEFINITION

A boarder is a person or a group of persons living with a household and paying reasonable compensation for meals and lodging.

Reasonable compensation is an amount equal to or exceeding:

● the amount of the full allotment for the appropriate size boarder household if the boarder eats more than two meals a day with the SNAP household, or

● two-thirds of the full allotment for the appropriate size boarder household if the boarder eats two meals or less a day with the SNAP household.

Note: To determine reasonable compensation, count only the amount paid for meals, if it can be separated from lodging. If the amount cannot be separated from lodging, evaluate the total payment.

Foster care individuals placed in the home of relatives or other individuals or families by a federal, state, or local government foster care program, are considered boarders.

Boarders are ineligible to participate in SNAP independent of the household providing the board.

A household may choose to include or exclude the boarder as a household member.

E-211-1-SNAP - PO Persons Not Allowed as Boarders

The following persons shall not be granted boarder status and must participate as members of the household:

● children who are under 18 years old and are under the parental control of an adult in the household,

● parents and children (21 years of age or younger) of household members unless one of the parents is age 60 or over and disabled and meets the criteria found in number nine of C-121- SNAP,

● spouses of household members, and

● persons furnished both meals and lodging but paying less than reasonable compensation. These persons are considered household members of the household providing meals.

2 of 4 BOARDER EXAMPLES

Example 1: Mr. A. pays the household monthly for room and board. Three meals per day are provided by the household. The amount paid for meals cannot be distinguished from the portion paid for lodging. Mr. A. pays an amount which exceeds the full *** allotment for a one person household; therefore, he is considered a boarder.

Example 2: Mr. B. pays the household monthly for room and board. Three meals per day are provided by the household. Mr. B. pays an amount for meals which exceeds the full *** allotment for a one person household; therefore, he is considered a boarder.

Example 3: Mr. C. pays the household monthly for room and board. Three meals per day are provided by the household. Half of the payment is for meals and half for board. The amount paid for meals is less than the full *** allotment for one person; therefore, Mr. C. is not considered a boarder.

Example 4: Mr. D. pays the household monthly for room and board. The amount paid for meals can be distinguished from the amount paid for lodging. The household provides two meals per day. The amount Mr. D. pays for meals exceeds two-thirds of the full *** allotment for one person; therefore, he is considered a boarder.

E-212-SNAP - PO BOARDERS AS SNAP HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS

If the client chooses to include a boarder as a SNAP household member:

● count all income and resources of the boarder and allow deductions as appropriate, but

● do not count the payment from the boarder as income to the SNAP household because it is considered money transferred between SNAP household members.

If the boarder is a foster care individual and is included as a SNAP household member, count the foster care payments.

E-213-SNAP - PO BOARDERS NOT IN THE SNAP HOUSEHOLD

If the boarder is not included as a SNAP household member:

● do not count his income and resources, but

● count the payment from the boarder, including contributions made directly to the household toward the household's shelter expenses, as self-employment income for the household.

Exception: If the boarder is a foster care individual not included in the SNAP household, do not count the foster care payments.

3 of 4

E-213-1-SNAP - PO Cost of Doing Business

Determine the gross income the SNAP household receives from the boarder and deduct the cost of doing business.

For boarders, the cost of doing business cannot exceed the total payment for meals and lodging and must equal either:

● the monthly SNAP allotment for a household size that is equal to the number of boarders, or

● the actual verified cost of providing room and meals, if the actual costs exceed the monthly SNAP allotment for that number of boarders. If actual costs are used, only separate and identifiable costs of providing room and meals to boarders shall be allowed.

Note: When there are two or more boarders in a household, whether they are one household or separate households, the value of the full allotment for a household size equal to the number of boarders is deductible.

II. PROCEDURES

E-211-SNAP - PR DEFINITION

There are no procedures for this policy.

E-212-SNAP - PR BOARDERS AS SNAP HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS

Boarders included as a SNAP household member must be included with the appropriate inclusion code and reason on LAMI.

E-213-SNAP - PR BOARDERS NOT IN THE SNAP HOUSEHOLD

Boarders not included as a SNAP household member are not added to LAMI.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms and instructions associated with this policy.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name E – Special Households Section No./Name E-200-FITAP-SNAP Special Households Document No./Name E-220-SNAP Disqualified Members and Households Effective Date August 1, 2024

1 of 9 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

E-221-SNAP - PO MEMBERS DISQUALIFIED BECAUSE OF SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBERS, INELIGIBLE ALIENS, FAILURE TO ATTEST TO CITIZENSHIP OR ALIEN STATUS, ABAWDs FAILURE TO MEET THE ABAWD WORK REQUIREMENT * AND FAILURE TO RESPOND TO A NATIONAL ACCURACY CLEARINGHOUSE (NAC) MATCH.

E-221-1-SNAP - PO Reasons for Disqualification

The agency disqualifies a member of a household who:

• Fails to provide or apply for a Social Security Number,

• Is an ineligible alien (including aliens awaiting sponsor information or proof of sponsor information),

• Fails to sign the application attesting to citizenship or alien status,

• Is an ABAWD who fails to meet the ABAWD work requirement or

• Fails to respond to a NAC Match

E-221-2-SNAP - PO Resources

Count all nonexempt resources of the disqualified member.

Do not count the disqualified member when determining which resource limit applies to the household.

E-221-3-SNAP - PO Income and Earned Income Deductions

E-221-3-1-SNAP - PO Income

Prorate the disqualified person's countable income equally among all members (including the disqualified person). This is called pro rata share. Include all but the disqualified member's share in the household budget.

Example: In a five person household, two are disqualified and one of them has income; therefore, 3/5 of the disqualified person's income is counted.

Exception: The full amount of child support income received by the disqualified person for children in the SNAP household must be counted and not prorated. The income must be budgeted on the youngest child’s unearned income screen in LITE. **

2 of 9

E-221-3-2-SNAP - PO Earned Income Deduction

Determine the part of the disqualified member's earned income that is counted in the household. Add this amount to other earned income. Apply the earned income deduction to the total.

E-221-4-SNAP - PO Household Deductions

E-221-4-1-SNAP - PO Standard Deduction

Allow the full standard deduction to the household.

E-221-4-2-SNAP - PO Utility Standard

Allow the full appropriate utility allowance to the household.

E-221-4-3-SNAP - PO Dependent Care and Other Shelter Costs

Prorate expenses billed to or paid by the disqualified member equally among everyone. Subtract the disqualified person's prorated share and allow the remaining deductions for the household. Count in full if deductions are billed to or paid by a member who is not disqualified.

E-221-5-SNAP - PO Medical/Excess Shelter Deductions

E-221-5-1-SNAP - PO Medical

Do not count medical bills of a disqualified member. If the disqualified member is billed for or pays medical bills of an eligible household member who is eligible for a medical deduction, prorate this expense.

E-221-5-2-SNAP - PO Uncapped Excess Shelter

The household is not eligible for this special provision if the disqualified member is the only person who is elderly or disabled. If another member in the household is elderly or disabled, the household is entitled to the special deduction.

E-221-6-SNAP - PO Income Test and Household Size

The household must pass both the gross and net income eligibility tests if the disqualified member was the only elderly or disabled person in the household.

Do not count the disqualified member in determining the household's income limits or the amount of the household's allotment.

3 of 9

E-221-7-SNAP - PO Adverse Action

Give advance notice of adverse action to the household before disqualifying a person during a certification period. This notice must explain why the disqualification is occurring, what the person must do to become qualified, and the eligibility and benefits of remaining members. A concurrent notice of adverse action must be sent when disqualifying a person at the end of the certification period.

E-221-8-SNAP - PO Ending Disqualification

Add the disqualified member to the household the month after he complies with the missing requirement.

Continue budgeting the disqualified member's income, but do not continue prorating his income when he is added to the household.

If there is an interruption in the household's certification, continue the disqualification until the person complies with the missing requirement.

E-221-9-SNAP - PO Verification

The disqualified person's circumstances, including income and resources, are subject to the same verification requirements as any other member.

E-221-10-SNAP - PO Child Support Payment/Deduction

The amount of child support paid or expected to be paid would be divided evenly among the household members, including the ineligible member and all of the ineligible member's share would be * included in ** the household income when determining gross income eligibility. If the household is eligible, the same prorated amount would be allowed as a deduction.

The agency disqualifies a member found to have committed IPV

• through an administrative disqualification hearing,

4 of 9 • by signing a waiver of right to an administrative disqualification hearing,

• by a court of appropriate jurisdiction, or

• by a disqualification consent agreement in cases referred for prosecution.

The agency disqualifies an individual for work registration requirements when he has:

• refused to register for work,

• failed to participate in an Employment and Training Program,

• refused to accept an offer of employment,

• refused to provide sufficient information to determine his employment status or job availability, or

• voluntarily quit a job or reduces their work effort and, after the reduction, works less than 30 hours per week and makes less than the federal minimum wage multiplied times 30 hours per week.

The agency disqualifies a member who is fleeing to avoid prosecution, custody or confinement after conviction for committing a crime or attempting to commit a crime that is a felony under the law of the place from which the individual is fleeing (or a high misdemeanor in New Jersey). Refer to E-240- SNAP.

The agency disqualifies a member who is violating a condition of probation or parole imposed under a federal or state law. The determination that a person has violated his or her probation or parole can only be made by the Louisiana Parole Board or the court system. Refer to E-240-SNAP.

The agency disqualifies a member who has been convicted as an adult for a felony that occurred after February 7, 2014, for one of the following crimes:

• Aggravated sexual abuse under section 2241 of title 18, United States Code;

• Murder under section 1111 of title 18, United States Code;

• Sexual exploitation and other abuse of children under chapter 110 of title 18, United States Code;

• A Federal or State offense involving sexual assault, as defined in section 40002(a) of the Violence Against Women Act of 1994 (42 U.S.C. 13925(a)); or

• The individual is not in compliance with the terms of their sentence.

The disqualified person's circumstances, including income and resources, are subject to the same verification requirements as any other member. The remaining members may participate if eligible. See Section F-300-SNAP for IPV penalties and Section B-1400-SNAP for Work Registration Requirements penalties.

E-222-2-SNAP - PO Resources

Count all nonexempt resources of a disqualified member.

E-222-3-SNAP - PO Income and Deductions

Count all income and expenses of a disqualified member.

E-222-4-SNAP - PO Medical Deductions and Uncapped Shelter Deductions

The household is entitled to medical deductions and an uncapped shelter deduction even if the disqualified person is the only elderly or disabled person in the household.

E-222-5-SNAP - PO Income Test and Household Size

The household must still pass both the gross and net income tests if the disqualified person is the only elderly or disabled person in the household.

Do not count the disqualified person in the household's size for determining the resource or income limits or the amount of the allotment.

E-222-6-SNAP - PO Adverse Action

Do not give advance notice of adverse action when disqualifying a member for Intentional Program Violation. Send a concurrent notice.

Send advance notice of adverse action during the certification period when disqualifying a member for work registration requirements non-compliance, fleeing felon restrictions, probation/parole violation, and for a conviction as an adult for a felony that occurred after February 7, 2014 listed above. A concurrent notice of adverse action must be sent when disqualifying a person at the end of the certification period.

Add the disqualified member to the household the month after his disqualification ends. See B-1463 - SNAP for ending the disqualification of an individual for noncompliance with work registration requirements. Continue budgeting the disqualified member's income.

NOTE: Once a disqualification penalty has been imposed against a currently participating household member, the period of disqualification continues uninterrupted until completed regardless of the eligibility of the disqualified member's household.

E-222-8-SNAP - PO Verification

The disqualified person's circumstances, including income and resources, are subject to the same verification requirements as any other member.

E-222-9-SNAP - PO Child Support Payment *** Deduction

The total amount of child support paid or expected to be paid would be allowed as a *** deduction.

II. PROCEDURES

E-221-SNAP-PR MEMBERS DISQUALIFIED BECAUSE OF SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBERS, INELIGIBLE ALIENS, FAILURE TO ATTEST TO CITIZENSHIP OR ALIEN STATUS, ABAWDS FAILURE TO MEET THE ABAWD WORK REQUIREMENT * AND FAILURE TO RESPOND TO A NATIONAL ACCURACY CLEARINGHOUSE (NAC) MATCH **

If the member is disqualified for failure to provide a Social Security Number, to exclude the member in LITE,

1. Access the Person Demographic – SSN Application page for the person failing to provide a Social Security Number. 2. Select No for the question “Has a SSN been provided for this person”. 3. Select Refusal/Good Cause Not Established for question “Reason SSN not applied for”.

The member will be disqualified when eligibility is determined and the case authorized. LITE will send an automatic notice of decision.

If the member is disqualified for ineligible aliens, failure to attest to citizenship, or alien status to exclude the member in LITE,

1. Access the member’s Alien Details Page 2. Select “No” for the question “Do you to DCFS contacting United States Citizen and Immigration Services (USCIS) to verify your immigration status?” 3. Select a verification type from the Immigration Status Verification drop-down menu.

If the member is disqualified for Intentional Program Violation (IPV) on an active case, the Fraud and Recovery Unit will enter the sanction on the Non-Compliance Details Page in LITE by,

1. Selecting the name of the member with an IPV from the drop-down menu, 2. Entering the Non-Compliance Dates, 3. Selecting the Non-Compliance Violation Type from the drop-down menu, 4. Selecting Non-Compliance Reason from the drop-down menu, 5. Entering a decision date and, 6. Clicking the Add Non-Compliance button.

The Fraud and Recovery Unit will send an email marked High Priority to the Parish Office where the worker assigned to the case is housed via the generic email address, with a request that the email be acknowledged when read. The worker must run EDBC, authorize the case, and cancel the notice. The member will be disqualified when eligibility is determined and the case authorized. A copy of the email received from the Fraud and Recovery Unit must be filed in OnBase, and a case note made stating when the case was authorized.

Note: After all actions have been completed, an email must be sent to the Fraud and Recovery Unit advising that the IPV sanction has been imposed. See F-350-SNAP PR.

If the member is disqualified for SNAP Work Registration for non-compliance with Work Registration Requirements, refer to B-1462-SNAP PR.

If the member is disqualified for Fleeing Felon Restrictions, Probation/Parole Violations, or certain convicted felons as identified in E-222-1-SNAP-PO, to exclude the member,

1. Access the LITE Person Demographics Summary Screen. 2. Click the edit pencil next to the member to be disqualified. 3. Click continue on the Person Demographics - Details Screen. 4. Click continue on the Person Demographics - SSN Application Screen. 5. Click continue on the Person Demographics – Conviction. 6. Enter the Conviction Information for the member. 7. Click Next

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name E – Special Households Section No./Name E-200-FITAP-SNAP Special Households Document No./Name E-230-SNAP Elderly or Disabled Effective Date October 15, 2022

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

E-231-SNAP - PO WHO IS CONSIDERED ELDERLY

Persons 60 and older are defined as elderly. This includes persons who are 59 years old when they apply but who will become 60 on or before the last day of the month of application.

E-232-SNAP - PO WHO IS CONSIDERED DISABLED

See C-1500-SNAP.

E-233-SNAP - PO SPECIAL PROVISIONS FOR ELDERLY OR DISABLED HOUSEHOLDS

Households which contain elderly or disabled persons are entitled to special provisions.

● Special household status - elderly persons aged 60 or older who are disabled (and the spouse of such persons) who live and eat with others, and are unable to purchase and prepare meals separately because of a permanent disability, may be granted separate household status from the other persons provided the other persons' gross income does not exceed 165% of the net income limit for the number of other persons living in the household (See B-642-3-SNAP).

● Institutional residents – elderly persons who are residents of federally subsidized housing for the elderly may be eligible for SNAP even if the institution provides more than half of their meals.

● Income tests - households with elderly or disabled members are exempt from the gross income test.

● Medical deduction - Deduct medical expenses in excess of $35 incurred by elderly or disabled members. It is not necessary for each elderly or disabled member to have expenses in excess of $35.

● Excess shelter - households with elderly or disabled members receive an uncapped shelter deduction for the full monthly amount of expenses which exceed 50% of the household's monthly income after the allowed deductions.

● Resources – * Refer to B-1030-SNAP for the maximum resource limit for households with ** *** at least one member in the household who is elderly or disabled.

E-234-SNAP - PO VERIFICATION

If eligibility for separate household status is questionable, the household must provide information the agency needs to establish if the person is elderly or disabled.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name E-Special Households (FITAP and SNAP) Section No./Name E-200-FITAP-SNAP Special Households (FITAP and SNAP) Document No./Name E-240-FITAP Fleeing Felons and Probation and Parole Violators Effective Date August 1, 2016

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY AN INDIVIDUAL DETERMINED TO BE A FLEEING FELON OR PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATOR IS INELIGIBLE TO RECEIVE FITAP BENEFITS. DCFS HAS THE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY FOR VERIFYING AN INDIVIDUAL’S FLEEING FELON AND PROBATION AND PAROLE VIOLATOR STATUS.

E-241-FITAP FLEEING FELON

DCFS MAY ESTABLISH THAT AN INDIVIDUAL IS A FLEEING FELON WHEN A FEDERAL, STATE, OR LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER ACTING IN HIS OFFICIAL CAPACITY PRESENTS AN OUTSTANDING FELONY ARREST WARRANT TO DCFS TO OBTAIN INFORMATION ON THE LOCATION OF AND OTHER INFORMATION ABOUT THE INDIVIDUAL NAMED IN THE WARRANT. THE FELONY ARREST WARRANT MUST CONFORM TO ONE OF THE FOLLOWING NATIONAL CRIME INFORMATION CENTER UNIFORM OFFENSE CLASSIFICATION CODES:

 ESCAPE (4901),  FLIGHT TO AVOID (PROSECUTION, CONFINEMENT, ETC.) (4902), OR  FLIGHT-ESCAPE (4999).

REFER TO CHAPTER 7, E-510 FOR INFORMATION THAT CAN BE RELEASED TO LAW ENFORCEMENT PERSONNEL.

E-242-FITAP PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATOR

TO BE CONSIDERED A PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATOR, FEDERAL, STATE, OR LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT MUST DETERMINE THAT THE INDIVIDUAL VIOLATED A CONDITION OF HIS OR HER PROBATION OR PAROLE IMPOSED UNDER FEDERAL OR STATE LAW, AND ARE ACTIVELY SEEKING THE INDIVIDUAL TO ENFORCE THE CONDITIONS OF THE PROBATION OR PAROLE AS OUTLINED BELOW.

FEDERAL, STATE, OR LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT AUTHORITIES ARE ACTIVELY SEEKING AN INDIVIDUAL WHEN THE LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY:

● INFORMS DCFS THAT IT INTENDS TO ARREST AN INDIVIDUAL FOR A PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATION WITHIN 20 DAYS OF SUBMITTING A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ABOUT THE INDIVIDUAL TO DCFS;

● PRESENTS A FELONY ARREST WARRANT TO DCFS; OR

APPLICATION PROCESSING SHOULD NOT BE DELAYED BEYOND NORMAL PROCESSING TIME STANDARDS, IF AWAITING VERIFICATION FROM THE LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY TO DETERMINE THE STATUS OF THE PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATOR. REFER TO CHAPTER 4, C-600-FITAP.

II. PROCEDURES

IF AN INDIVIDUAL HAS BEEN DETERMINED TO BE A FLEEING FELON OR A PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATOR, THE INDIVIDUAL IS INELIGIBLE TO RECEIVE FITAP BENEFITS. IF THE FLEEING FELON OR A PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATOR IS A MEMBER OF THE HOUSEHOLD, THE WORKER MUST TAKE ACTION TO REMOVE THE MEMBER EVEN IF THIS RESULTS IN A DECREASE IN BENEFITS.

IF AN APPLICANT REPORTS THAT A MEMBER OF THE HOUSEHOLD IS A PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATOR, CONTACT THE LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY AND ALLOW THE LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY 20 DAYS TO RESPOND TO A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ABOUT THE CONDITIONS THE PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATION, AND WHETHER THE LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY INTENDS TO ACTIVELY PURSUE THE INDIVIDUAL.

● IF THE LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY DOES NOT INDICATE THAT IT INTENDS TO ARREST THE INDIVIDUAL FOR THE PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATION WITHIN 30 DAYS OF THE REQUEST FOR VERIFICATION, THE WORKER SHALL DETERMINE THAT THE INDIVIDUAL IS NOT CONSIDERED A PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATOR AND DOCUMENT THIS DETERMINATION WITH A CASE NOTE.

● IF THE LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY INDICATES THAT IT DOES INTEND TO ARREST THE INDIVIDUAL FOR THE PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATION WITHIN 30 DAYS OF REQUEST FOR VERIFICATION DO NOT TAKE ANY ACTION ON THE CASE UNTIL THE 30-DAY PERIOD HAS EXPIRED. ONCE THE 30-DAY PERIOD HAS EXPIRED, THE WORKER SHALL VERIFY WITH THE LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY WHETHER IT HAS ATTEMPTED TO ARREST THE PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATOR.

IF DCFS RECEIVES VERIFICATION THAT AN INDIVIDUAL IS A FLEEING FELON, EXCLUDE THE INDIVIDUAL USING INCLUSION/EXCLUSION CODE AND REASON 02/05.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS THERE ARE NO FORMS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS POLICY. IV. REFERENCES 7 CFR 273.11

E-241-SNAP FLEEING FELON

DCFS MAY ESTABLISH THAT AN INDIVIDUAL IS A FLEEING FELON WHEN A FEDERAL, STATE, OR LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER ACTING IN HIS OFFICIAL CAPACITY PRESENTS AN OUTSTANDING FELONY ARREST WARRANT TO DCFS TO OBTAIN INFORMATION ON THE LOCATION OF AND OTHER INFORMATION ABOUT THE INDIVIDUAL NAMED IN THE WARRANT. ● ESCAPE (4901),

1 of 18 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

An individual is considered a resident of an institution when the institution provides the resident with the majority of their meals (over 50% of three meals daily) as part of the institution’s normal services. Residents of institutions are not eligible for participation in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) unless the facility meets at least one of the five exceptions to the institution provision listed below.

1. Residents of federally subsidized housing for the elderly, built under either Section 202 of the Housing Act of 1959 or Section 236 of the National Housing Act.

2. Narcotic addicts or alcoholics who for the purpose of regular participation in a drug or alcohol treatment and rehabilitation program reside at a facility or treatment center and the facility is an approved facility ***.

3. Disabled individuals who are residents of group living arrangements and the facility is an approved facility ***.

4. Individuals or individuals with their children temporarily residing in a shelter for battered persons. Such persons shall be considered individual household units for the purposes of applying for and participating in SNAP.

5. Residents of public or private non-profit shelters for homeless persons.

If the facility does not provide more than 50% of meals, the facility is not considered an institution for SNAP purposes. Residents may apply for and receive SNAP if they are otherwise eligible.

Staff must discuss whether the facility provides more than half of the individual’s meals when an applicant reports living in a facility.

E-251-SNAP - PO DRUG/ALCOHOL TREATMENT FACILITY

Drug addicts or alcoholics and their children, who reside at a facility that provides more than half their meals and is an approved public or non-profit drug or alcohol treatment facility for the purpose of participating in a drug or alcohol treatment or rehabilitation program, may be eligible for (SNAP) benefits, if all other eligibility factors are met. Eligibility is determined by the same income and resource standards as other households. Residents must be certified as one-person households unless their children live with them, in which case the children must be included in their household. The resident is exempt from work registration. If the facility provides less than half of the resident’s meals, the resident is not considered institutionalized and may be otherwise eligible.

The drug/alcohol treatment facility must act as the authorized representative. The resident and authorized representative must both sign the application unless the resident designates the facility as the authorized representative on another document.

2 of 18 Residents in a drug/alcohol treatment facility that does not meet or no longer meets the criteria to be considered an approved drug/alcohol treatment facility and provides more than half of the resident’s meals are not eligible for SNAP benefits. Residents certified for SNAP benefits when the facility no longer meets the criteria to be considered an approved drug/alcohol treatment facility and provides more than half of the resident’s meals are not entitled to advance notice of adverse action. A concurrent notice is sent when the case is closed.

E-251-1-SNAP - PO Eligibility Requirements of a Drug/Alcohol Treatment Facility

In order for a drug/alcohol treatment facility to be approved to receive SNAP benefits, the facility must apply for approval by completing an Application for Drug/Alcohol Treatment Facility to Receive Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Benefits (SNAP 41DA) and provide required verification. The application must be submitted to LDH SNAP State Office via fax, mail, or email LA.SNAP.LDH@LA.GOV . The LDH SNAP State Office staff will determine if the facility meets the criteria to receive SNAP benefits for their residents.

The drug/alcohol treatment facility must provide verification that it meets the following criteria to be considered an approved drug/alcohol treatment facility:

• Certified as a retailer by USDA, Food and Nutrition Service, or

• Tax-exempt organization as verified by a current valid Internal Revenue Service exemption and certified by the Louisiana Department of Health, Office for Behavioral Health as:

o Receiving funding under part B of title XIX of the Public Health Service Act, or

o Eligible to receive funding under part B of title XIX of the Public Health Service Act even if no funds are being received, or

o Operating to further the purposes of part B of title XIX of the Public Health Service Act, to provide treatment and rehabilitation of drug addicts and/or alcoholics.

Refer to E-251-1-SNAP – PR for LDH SNAP State Office Responsibilities.

E-251-2-SNAP - PO Drug/Alcohol Treatment Facility Responsibilities

The facility must:

• Apply for the resident.

• Act as the Authorized Representative (AR).

As the AR, the facility must also:

o Ensure the facility is listed as the AR for all residents receiving SNAP benefits who reside at the facility.

o Complete a Change Report through the CAFÉ Customer Portal, if the facility is not listed as the resident’s AR or unsure if the facility is listed as the AR.

• Buy and prepare food for eligible residents and their children. The facility may redeem benefits by using the resident’s EBT card to purchase food from an authorized retailer or by being an authorized retailer and using their point of sale (POS) device at the facility.

• Buy meals delivered to the individual residents and their children.

• Ensure that no more than one-half of the resident’s SNAP allotment is obtained prior to the 16th of the month.

• Report any change or overissuance. Increase in income that causes the resident to exceed the gross income limit for that resident’s household size, must be reported by the 10th of the following month, in which the income exceeded the gross income limit. The facility is liable for any misrepresentation or intentional program violation, which it knowingly committed to obtain SNAP benefits for the resident.

• Report if the facility no longer meets the criteria to be considered an approved drug/alcohol treatment facility to LDH SNAP State Office within 10 days.

• Provide a Drug/Alcohol Treatment Facility Monthly Roster of Residents Receiving SNAP Benefits (SNAP 45DA) or a list of current residents who are receiving SNAP benefits to LDH SNAP State Office by the 5th of each month for the previous month. The list must be signed by a responsible official attesting to the validity of the list. An unsigned list or a facility stamped signature is not acceptable. Failure to send the list will result in the facility becoming ineligible to receive SNAP benefits and the residents will no longer be eligible for SNAP benefits.

NOTE: The facility may use the SNAP 45DA to report the current residents who receive SNAP or the facility may create an acceptable substitute if the list contains the same information as the SNAP 45DA.

4 of 18 The facility must give the resident his Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) Card when the resident leaves the facility.

The facility must:

• Provide the departing resident his full allotment if no SNAP benefits have been spent on his behalf, regardless of when during the month the resident leaves, or

• Provide the departing resident one-half his monthly SNAP allotment if SNAP benefits have already been spent on his behalf and the resident leaves the facility on or before the 15th of the month.

NOTE: The departing resident does not receive any SNAP benefits if he leaves the facility after the 15th of the month and benefits have already been used.

• Advise the resident to report his new address by completing a Change Report through the CAFÉ Customer Portal or by contacting the local parish LDH office within 10 days from the resident’s departure.

• Inform LDH SNAP State Office of all residents who have left the facility unannounced so that the resident’s EBT card can be deactivated. Include the resident’s name and Case Identification Number (CID). This must be provided within 10 days of the resident’s departure. The facility must return the resident’s EBT card to LDH SNAP State Office by the end of the month that the resident left the facility if the EBT card has not been provided to the departing resident.

E-252-SNAP - PO GROUP LIVING ARRANGEMENT

Disabled or blind residents who meet the SNAP definition of "Elderly or Disabled Member" may be certified for SNAP benefits under group living arrangements if they live in an approved group living arrangement as defined below and the facility provides more than half of the resident’s meals. (Refer to A-110-SNAP for elderly or disabled definition.) Eligibility is determined by the same income and resource standards as other households. If the facility provides less than half of the resident’s meals, the resident is not considered institutionalized and may be otherwise eligible.

The residents of group living arrangements may apply:

• for themselves,

• through an authorized representative of their choosing, or

• through an authorized representative employed by the center.
