5 of 18 The residents in the group living arrangement facility decide if they want to apply as a group, as individuals, or through an authorized representative. If a member of the group wants to apply on his own, the facility's decision to let him apply is based on the resident's physical and mental ability to handle his own affairs. Accept applications from any individual the facility allows to apply as a one- person household or for any group of residents applying as a household, regardless of whether one or all have an authorized representative. If the resident applies on his own behalf, he is liable for any overissuance. If the residents apply on their own behalf, the largest household size allowed is 16.

If the facility applies as the authorized representative, the resident is treated as a one-person household. The resident and authorized representative must both sign the application unless the resident designates the authorized representative on another document.

When the facility loses its status as authorized representative or no longer meets the definition of an approved group living arrangement facility and provides more than half of the resident’s meals and the resident is not certified on his own behalf, the resident is not entitled to advance notice of adverse action. Send concurrent notice explaining the termination and when it will become effective.

E-252-1-SNAP - PO Eligibility Requirements of a Group Living Arrangement

In order for a group living arrangement facility to be approved to receive SNAP benefits, the facility must apply for approval by completing an Application For Group Living Arrangement Facility to Receive Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Benefits (SNAP 41GLA) and provide required verification. The application must be submitted to LDH SNAP State Office via fax, mail or email LA.SNAP.LDH@LA.GOV. LDH SNAP State Office staff will determine if the facility meets the criteria to receive SNAP benefits for their residents.

An approved group living arrangement is defined as a public or private nonprofit residential facility, serving no more than 16 residents that is:

• Certified as a retailer by USDA, Food and Nutrition Service, or

• Licensed by the Louisiana Department of Health, Health Standards Section.

Nonprofit status may be verified by obtaining a current valid Internal Revenue Service exemption.

Refer to E-252-1-SNAP – PR for LDH SNAP State Office Responsibilities.

E-252-2-SNAP - PO Group Living Arrangement Facility Responsibilities

When the facility acts as the authorized representative, the facility must:

• Apply for the resident.

E-253-SNAP - PO PREPARED MEAL SERVICES

E-253-1-SNAP - PO Eligibility Requirements

Eligible clients may use the EBT Card to purchase prepared meals through non-profit communal dining or meal delivery services approved by USDA-FNS.

• Meal delivery services - Eligible household members must be 60 years of age or over, or housebound, physically handicapped, or unable to prepare their own meals. The eligible member's spouse is also eligible.

• Communal dining - Eligible household members must be 60 years of age or over or receiving SSI. The eligible member's spouse is also eligible.

E-254-SNAP - PO RESIDENTS IN SHELTERS FOR BATTERED WOMEN

E-254-1-SNAP - PO Eligibility Requirements

Residents in approved shelters for battered women and children may receive SNAP benefits. They must meet the same income and resource standards as other households.

The special requirements for residents in shelters for battered women apply to persons living in private or public nonprofit residential facilities that usually serve meals.

If the shelter does not serve meals it is not classified as an institution, but the residents may receive SNAP benefits as individual household units or as part of a group of individuals like any other household.

Residents in shelters for battered women may apply for SNAP benefits and use SNAP benefits on their own behalf. They may also appoint a shelter representative or another person to act as authorized representative.

E-254-2-SNAP - PO Approved Centers

Shelters for battered women and children must be public or private nonprofit residential facilities that serve battered women and children. If a facility serves other people, part of the facility must be set aside on a long-term basis to serve only battered women and children.

E-254-3-SNAP - PO Buying Meals

Individual households may use their SNAP benefits to buy meals prepared for them at a shelter approved by USDA.

E-254-4-SNAP - PO Processing Applications

The usual processing standards and usual verification and documentation requirements apply to residents in shelters for battered women.

E-254-5-SNAP - PO Expedited Time Limits

The EBT Card and benefits must be available by the close of business on the sixth calendar day after the application date.

E-254-7-SNAP - PO Determination of Eligibility

Determine eligibility for shelter residents based on their income, resources, and expenses. Consider resources inaccessible if they are jointly owned with members of the former household and access to the resources depends on the consent of the joint owner.

Consider room payments to the shelter as shelter expenses for the resident.

E-254-8-SNAP - PO Adverse Action

Resident households have the same rights to notices of adverse action, fair hearing, and lost benefits as other households.

E-254-9-SNAP - PO Work Registration

Register residents in shelters for battered women and children for work unless otherwise exempt.

II. PROCEDURES

E-251-SNAP - PR DRUG/ALCOHOL TREATMENT FACILITY

Residents of an approved public or non-profit drug or alcohol treatment facility participating in a treatment or rehabilitation program may be eligible for SNAP benefits, if all other eligibility factors are met.

Determine eligibility by the same income and resource standards as other households.

Certify residents as one-person households. Include the children if they are living at the facility with their parent(s).

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

* E-271-SNAP - PO ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS

Households composed entirely of people who are applying for or receiving SSI may apply for SNAP at the Social Security Administration office unless they already have a SNAP application pending.

These clients are not required to go to a parish office to complete the application or reapplication process. If more information is needed from the household, contact them by home visit, telephone, or mail.

E-272-SNAP – PO INITIAL APPLICATION

The Social Security Administration accepts and completes the SNAP application during the SSI interview and forwards it to the agency ** *** within one workday after the application is received.

The Social Security Administration forwards

● the application,

● a transmittal sheet, and

● any verification the Social Security Administration has received.

When additional verification is received by the Social Security Administration after the application has been forwarded to the * agency, the Social Security Administration sends the additional verification.

NOTE: The application date is the date the Social Security Administration receives the application.

E-272-1-SNAP - PO Expedited Service

SSI households are entitled to the same expedited procedures as other households except expedited time limits begin with the date the application is received by the agency. ** ***

The Social Security Administration:

● screens the application for expedited services on the day the application is received,

● marks "Expedited Processing" on the 1st page of the application if the household appears to be eligible, and

● forwards the application to the * agency.

The client may also take the application to the agency. **

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name E – Special Households Section No./Name E-200-FITAP-SNAP Special Households Document No./Name E-280-SNAP Categorically Eligible Households Effective Date October 1, 2025

1 of 6 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

E-281-SNAP - PO HOUSEHOLDS CONSIDERED TRADITIONAL CATEGORICALLY ELIGIBLE

Households are considered traditional categorically eligible for SNAP benefits when all members receive or are authorized to receive benefits from:

• FITAP,

• STEP,

• KCSP, or

• SSI

A recipient of benefits includes:

• an individual receiving benefits through the FITAP, STEP, KCSP, or SSI programs, or

• an individual authorized to receive FITAP, STEP, KCSP, or SSI but the benefits have not yet been paid, or

• an individual determined eligible to receive zero benefits, i.e., a person whose benefits are being recouped, or

• a FITAP recipient whose benefits are less than $10 and therefore does not receive any cash benefits, or

• A payee for KCSP is considered a recipient of KCSP. Do not consider households containing persons entitled only to Medicaid as categorically eligible.

E-281-1-SNAP - PO BROAD-BASED CATEGORICALLY ELIGIBLE HOUSEHOLDS

Broad-Based Categorically Eligible (BBCE) households are eligible for SNAP benefits when the household receives a non-cash TANF/MOE funded benefit or service. Upon certification of a BBCE household, the TANF Non-Cash Services Fact Sheet (OFS 4BBCE) is sent to notify the household that they are authorized to receive non-cash TANF/MOU services.

Resources for all members included in the broad-based categorically eligible household are excluded from eligibility determination. Resource questions do not need to be cleared when processing applications, Simplified Reports, or redeterminations. Verification of resources for BBCE households do not need to be requested.

2 of 6 If the household is determined to be BBCE, the household is subject to the gross income test of 200% of the federal poverty limit instead of 130% of the federal poverty limit. Households that are exempt from the gross income limit must still meet the gross income test of 200% of the federal poverty limit to be considered BBCE.

Upon authorization of a case, LITE will determine if the household is BBCE based on the criteria in E- 282-PO. LITE will automatically:

• Exclude resources reported. • Determine eligibility based on the gross income test of 200% of the FPL instead of 130%. • Select ‘Yes’ to the question, “Is this household broad-based categorically eligible?” • Send the TANF Non-Cash Services Fact Sheet (OFS 4BBCE) automatically to notify the household that they have been authorized to receive non-cash TANF/MOU funded services. • Create a case note indicating that BBCE has been conferred to the household. The case note will read: “Household has been determined Board-Based Categorically Eligible.”

E-282-SNAP - PO DETERMINING TRADITIONAL CATEGORICAL ELIGIBILITY AND BROAD- BASED CATEGORICAL ELIGIBILITY (BBCE)

Do not consider a household traditional categorically eligible or BBCE if:

• any member of that household is disqualified for an Intentional Program Violation.

• the head of household is disqualified for failure to comply with work registration requirement.

• any member of that household is disqualified for fleeing felon restrictions or probation/parole violation,

• any member of that household is disqualified for being convicted of a crime cited in E-221-1-SNAP – PO and not in compliance with the terms of their sentence,

• the household was disqualified due to receipt of substantial lottery or gambling winnings. If the household reapplies after losing eligibility due to these winnings, the household would not be considered categorically eligible and must meet the income and resource limit. The case would be processed under regular SNAP rules. This requirement only applies to the first time a household is certified following the loss of eligibility due to substantial lottery or gambling winnings.

Do not consider the following individuals a member of the household when determining traditional categorical eligibility or BBCE:

• an ineligible alien,

• an ineligible student,

E-283-SNAP - PO TRADITIONAL CATEGORICALLY ELIGIBILITY FACTORS

Households which are traditional categorically eligible are considered to have met the following SNAP eligibility factors without additional verification:

• Resources,

• Social Security Numbers,

• Sponsored Alien Information, and

• Residency.

These households also do not have to meet the gross and net income limits. Verify income not counted for FITAP, KCSP, or SSI.

Verify factors (authorization to receive FITAP, KCSP, STEP, and/or SSI) used to determine categorical eligibility, if questionable. See E-281-SNAP – PO.

These households must meet all other eligibility factors.

E-284-SNAP - PO CHANGES

Process changes as outlined in C-800-SNAP except for changes in the eligibility factors listed in E- 283-SNAP – PO.

E-285-SNAP - PO BENEFITS

Benefits for traditional categorically eligible and BBCE households shall be based on net income as for any other household. One and two person households will receive a minimum benefit as defined in C-920-SNAP.

Traditional categorically eligible and BBCE households of 3 or more persons for which income exceeds the level at which benefits are paid shall be denied.

E-287-SNAP - PO CERTIFIED HOUSEHOLDS

Certified households which become traditional categorically eligible because of receipt of SSI benefits shall be eligible for the medical and uncapped shelter deductions from:

• the beginning of the period for which the SSI benefits are authorized, or

• the date of the SNAP application, whichever is later.

II. PROCEDURES

E-281-SNAP - PR HOUSEHOLDS CONSIDERED TRADITIONAL CATAGORICALLY ELIGIBLE AND BBCE HOUSEHOLDS

When a BBCE household reports or the agency learns that their gross monthly income exceeds 130% of the FPL for their household size, verification of the household’s income must be requested and once received determine if the change in income affects eligibility. If the household fails to provide the verification, the case must be closed for failure to provide verification.

If a BBCE household’s gross monthly income exceeds 200% of the FPL, the household is no longer eligible for BBCE and also no longer eligible for SNAP. Anytime it is determined that a BBCE household is no longer eligible to be BBCE, the household must be notified in writing that they are no longer eligible for BBCE non-cash TANF funded services. LITE will automatically create a case note and send the Notice of Decision informing the household that the household is no longer BBCE.

• If a BBCE household’s gross monthly income exceeds 130% of the FPL but is below 200% of the FPL, staff must determine if the household’s gross monthly income exceeds the net income limit.

o If the income does not exceed the net income limit, the income must be budgeted, EDBC run, and the case must be authorized. o If the income exceeds the net income limit and it is a one or two-person household, the income must be budgeted and the household will be eligible for the $24 minimum allotment. o If the income exceeds the net income limit and it is a three or more-person household, the income must be budgeted and the household is no longer eligible for SNAP.

If the household was determined to be BBCE in error and the household was notified that they are BBCE, then the household is considered to be BBCE. The household must be notified that they are not BBCE. If benefits were issued in error due to the BBCE determination, all ineligible benefits must be recovered.

5 of 6 E-282-SNAP - PR DETERMINING TRADITIONAL CATEGORICAL ELIGIBILITY

There are no procedures associated with this policy.

E-283-SNAP - PR TRADITIONAL ELIGIBILITY FACTORS

Do not request verification of resources, Social Security Numbers, alien information or residency for a categorically eligible household.

E-284-SNAP - PR CHANGES

Process changes as outlined in C-800-SNAP except for changes in the eligibility factors listed in E-283-SNAP.

Process households in which all members are applying for FITAP, KCSP, or SSI, in accordance with joint processing procedures.

Until a determination is made on the FITAP, KCSP, or SSI application, base the household's eligibility and benefit level on SNAP eligibility criteria. Postpone denying a potentially categorically eligible household until the 30th day in case the household is determined eligible to receive FITAP, KCSP, or SSI benefits.

Advise the household on its notice of denial that it would be to their advantage to notify the local office when SSI benefits are approved.

If the household is later determined eligible to receive FITAP, KCSP, or SSI benefits after the 30th day and is otherwise categorically eligible, provide benefits using the original application along with other pertinent information occurring subsequent to that application.

Do not re-interview the household.

Use any available information to update the application and/or make mail or phone contact with the household or authorized representative to determine any changes in circumstances. If eligibility for FITAP, KCSP, or SSI is determined within the 30-day SNAP processing time, provide benefits back to the date of application. If eligibility for FITAP, KCSP, or SSI is determined after the SNAP application is denied, prorate benefits for the initial month from the effective date of that certification or the date of the SNAP application, whichever is later.

E-287-SNAP - PR CERTIFIED HOUSEHOLDS

Certified households that become traditional categorically eligible because of receipt of SSI benefits shall be eligible for medical and uncapped shelter deductions.

Provide these additional benefits through restoration by using an OFS 35.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name E-Special Households (FITAP) Section No./Name E-300-FITAP FITAP Special Households (FITAP) Document No./Name E-310-FITAP Minor Unmarried Parent Effective Date May 1, 2016

1 of 6 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

A minor parent and the dependent child in his or her care must reside in the household of a parent, legal guardian, or other adult relative, or in an adult-supervised supportive living arrangement in order to receive FITAP cash assistance.

E-311- PO FITAP DEFINITION

A minor unmarried parent is a person who is:

● under 18 years of age, and

● has one or more children or is pregnant.

E-312- PO FITAP REQUIRED LIVING ARRANGEMENT

In order to be eligible for assistance, a minor unmarried parent must reside in the home of a:

● parent,

● legal guardian,

● qualified relative other than a parent age 18 or over, or

● in an adult-supervised supportive living arrangement.

EXCEPTION: If the minor unmarried parent does not meet this requirement an exception may be made if:

● The minor parent has no living parent or legal guardian whose whereabouts are known;

● No living parent or legal guardian allows the minor parent to live in their home;

● The minor parent lived apart from a parent or legal guardian for a period of at least one year before either the birth of the dependent child or the application for FITAP;

● The physical or emotional health or safety of the minor parent or dependent child would be jeopardized if they resided in the same residence with the minor parent's parent or legal guardian;

● There is otherwise good cause for the minor parent and dependent child to receive assistance while living apart from the minor parent's parent, legal guardian, or other adult relative, or in an adult-supervised supportive living arrangement.

Good cause may exist when:

● The adult is temporarily absent from the home.

● The parent or guardian lives out-of-state, is in an institution, or is addicted to drugs or alcohol.

● The minor's return to the parent's or guardian's home would violate their lease or local health or safety standards.

● The minor is in a licensed substance abuse treatment program which would not be available if returned to the parent's or guardian's home.

● The minor alleges that the home of the parent or legal guardian is the scene of illegal activity.

● The minor parent has been emancipated by court order.

● A court order has barred contact between the minor parent and the parent or legal guardian.

● The parent or legal guardian did not provide adequate food, clothing, medical care, or other necessities for the minor parent or the child.

An adult-supervised supportive living arrangement means a private family setting or other living arrangement, other than a public institution, which is maintained as a family setting, as evidenced by the assumption of responsibility for the care and control of the minor unmarried parent and dependent child or the provision of supportive services, such as counseling, guidance, or supervision. This may include:

● foster homes,

● maternity homes, or

● the home of a non-relative age 18 or over who provides supervision for the minor unmarried parent and child.

If the minor unmarried parent is not living in the household of a parent, a legal guardian, or other adult qualified relative, or in an adult-supervised supportive living arrangement:

● Advise the minor of the possible exemptions;

● Assist the minor in obtaining the necessary verifications if one or more of these exceptions is claimed;

4 of 6 When the minor unmarried parent who is not payee reaches age 18 and meets the requirements of a FITAP child, she and her child may remain included in the existing certification if it is advantageous to the family. However, if the former MUP requests an application be taken in her own name for herself and her child, remove them from the existing certification or close the case, whichever is applicable, and determine their eligibility.

When the minor unmarried parent who is not payee reaches 18 and does not meet the requirements of a FITAP child, she and her child must be removed from the certification or the case closed no later than the month after her 18th birthday. She may apply for assistance in her own name and be certified effective the month of her 18th birthday if not included in another grant that month.

E-316- PO FITAP ADULT SUPPORTIVE LIVING ARRANGEMENT AND WHO SHALL BE PAYEE

There are no policies associated with the procedures.

E-316-1- PO FITAP WHO SHALL BE PAYEE

● If the minor unmarried parent lives in the home of a parent or other qualified relative, the parent or relative must be payee for the minor unmarried parent and child.

● If the minor unmarried parent lives in a supportive living arrangement with a legal guardian or adult who is not a qualified relative, the legal guardian or other adult must be a Third Party Payee of the FITAP grant. If living in a group living arrangement, other than a maternity home, the minor parent may be the payee.

● If the minor unmarried parent meets one of the five exceptions outlined in E-312- FITAP, the minor parent may be payee.

E-317- PO FITAP FOSTER CARE

A child whose minor parent is in Title IV-E Foster Care, Category 08, and who lives in the same foster home or child care institution as the minor parent is not eligible for FITAP cash assistance. This child is required to be included in the Foster Care payment.

A child whose minor parent is certified for state-funded Foster Care payments other than Title IV-E is not included in the Foster Care payment and may be eligible for FITAP cash assistance.

There are no procedures associated with this policy.

E-313- PR FITAP WHO MUST BE INCLUDED IN THE ASSISTANCE UNIT

If both minor parents of the dependent child are in the home, an eligibility determination must be made in regards to two-parent households. The household is not eligible for FITAP cash assistance unless at least one parent is determined to be physically or mentally incapacitated or caring for a disabled family member living in the home. (See * C-1510-FITAP **).

E-314- PR FITAP CHILD SUPPORT

If either or both of the parents of the minor unmarried parent are absent from the home, a referral to Child Support Enforcement (CSE) must be made on the absent parents of the minor unmarried parent as well as on the absent parent of the child.

E-315- PR FITAP REACHING AGE 18

When a MUP obtains age 18 and requests an application be taken in her own name for herself and her child, remove them from the existing certification or close the case, whichever is applicable, and determine their eligibility.

She and her child must be removed from the certification or the case closed no later than the month after her 18th birthday. She may apply for assistance in her own name and be certified effective the month of her 18th birthday if not included in another grant that month.

E-316- PR FITAP ADULT SUPPORTIVE LIVING ARRANGEMENT AND WHO SHALL BE PAYEE

There are no procedures associated with this policy.

E-316-1- PR FITAP WHO SHALL BE PAYEE

A minor unmarried parent in a maternity home may be her own payee while in the maternity home if she has no plans to live with a parent or other adult qualified relative after her child is born. The FITAP application is taken in the parish of the maternity home.

If the minor unmarried parent plans to return to the home of a parent or other adult qualified relative after her child is born, the parent, legal guardian or relative must be payee and the application taken in that person's name in their parish of residence.

A FITAP child who enters a maternity home shall remain included in the existing certification if the child plans to return to the home.

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Assign a third party payee when the caretaker relative demonstrates an inability to manage the FITAP benefits.

E-321- * PO ** FITAP WHEN A THIRD PARTY PAYEE IS REQUIRE

Assign a third party payee for the month the caretaker relative is unable to receive FITAP/KCSP benefits due to their death. In this situation, the third party payee must be the person currently caring for the children.

Assign a third party payee when a minor unmarried parent lives in a supportive living arrangement with a legal guardian or adult who is not a qualified relative. See E-310-FITAP, Section * E-316 PO/PR **-FITAP.

E-322-* PO ** FITAP STANDARDS OF SELECTION

The third party payee must:

● not be a member of the OFS staff or a person whose business or personal affairs would create a conflict of interest.

● express an interest in the FITAP family and a willingness to assume the responsibility designated.

● live close enough to the family or have transportation available to allow the family to maintain close contact.

● be reliable.

● have the ability to establish and maintain a positive relationship with the family.

E-323- -* PO ** FITAP LOCATING A THIRD PARTY PAYEE

* There are no policies associated with the procedures. **

E-324- * PO **-FITAP RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE THIRD PARTY PAYEE

* There are no policies associated with the procedures. **

E-325- * PO ** FITAP CONFIDENTIALITY

Release to the third party payee only information pertinent to his responsibility in managing the grant.

● he has sole responsibility for managing the grant in the best interest of the family, based on guidance provided by the client.

● he will not be paid for services provided, nor reimbursed for expenses incurred if he exceeds the amount of the payment in meeting the family's expenses.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name E-Special Households (FITAP) Section No./Name E-300-FITAP FITAP Special Households (FITAP) Document No./Name E-330-FITAP Domestic Violence Effective Date March 1, 2023

1 of 12 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

E-331-FITAP - PO DOMESTIC VIOLENCE OPTION

Policies and procedures outlined in this document have been established to:

● Screen individuals applying for and receiving * cash assistance to identify survivors of domestic violence, sexual harassment, sexual assault, and stalking while maintaining the confidentiality of such individuals;

● Refer such individuals to counseling and supportive services; and

● Temporarily waive, after establishing good cause, certain program requirements which would make it more difficult for such individuals to escape domestic violence, sexual harassment, sexual assault, and stalking or unfairly penalize such individuals who are experiencing or have survived such violence, or individuals who are at risk of further violence.

E-332-FITAP - PO DEFINITIONS ***

Domestic violence is physical, sexual, psychological, economical, and/or emotional abuse of an intimate partner in which a partner uses a variety of tactics to gain and maintain power and control over the other partner.

Sexual harassment is hostile, intimidating, or oppressive behavior based on sex that create an offensive environment.

Sexual assault is an umbrella term that includes sexual activities such as rape, fondling, and attempted rape. A victim of sexual assault is an individual who has been subjected to sexual contact or behavior that occurs without the explicit consent of the recipient.

Stalking is engaging in a course of conduct directed toward a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety or the safety of others; or suffer substantial emotional distress. Stalking includes but is not limited to acts which the stalker directly, indirectly, or through third parties by any action, method, device or means:  follows someone else;  monitors, observes, or surveils another person;  threatens another person;  communicates to or about another person; or  interferes with a person’s property. **

***

2 of 12 E-333-FITAP - PO IDENTIFICATION OF VICTIMS OF *** VIOLENCE

* Identifying survivors of violence includes:  Advising each applicant of the domestic violence waiver provisions, and  Providing the applicant with the OFS Flyer DV if a manual application is received or if the applicant adds a cash program during an interview.

LITE will indicate those applicants that responded through the Self-Service Portal (SSP) in reference to domestic violence.

E-334-FITAP - PO REFERRAL TO COUNSELING AND SUPPORTIVE SERVICES

Individuals experiencing domestic violence should be referred to contact the Louisiana Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-888-411-1333 for free, confidential 24-hour assistance or the National Domestic Violence Hotline via the nationwide number-1-800-799-SAFE (7233) or TTY 1-800-787-3224 or (206) 518-9361 (Video phone only for deaf callers) during the application process.

Individuals experiencing sexual harassment, sexual assault, or stalking should be referred to contact the Louisiana Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-888-995-7273 or text 225-351-SAFE (7233).

These hotlines will connect the individual with a trained crisis support specialist who can talk with them about their safety, their situation and provide immediate intervention, general support, or can give resources to find long-term support.

Individuals may also be referred to and provided information about available community resources for other types of supportive services. This information is available through the Louisiana 211 Statewide Resource Database (LA 211). The database includes shelters for battered individuals, medical services, abuse hot lines, emergency aid for individuals fleeing violence, legal counseling and advocacy, mental health care, counseling, support groups and financial assistance for survivors of crime.

The Louisiana 211 Statewide Network serves all parishes in Louisiana 24 hours a day, seven days a week, helping residents locate available programs and services to meet their needs. Help seekers simply dial 211 from anywhere in Louisiana to reach a “live” navigation specialist, 24/7. Services are available to non-English speakers.

E-335-FITAP - PO VERIFICATION OF DOMESTIC VIOLENCE

Individuals who wish to claim an exemption from program requirements may submit any available documentation to verify their situation. ** This may include, but is not limited to:

● Police, government agency, or court records;

3 of 12 ● Documentation from a shelter worker, legal professional, member of the clergy, medical or mental health professional, or other professional from whom the individual has sought assistance in dealing with violence;

***

● Physical evidence of violence; or

● Other documentation which supports the statement.

If the individual is unable to provide documentation to substantiate the claim, the client's statement must be accepted ***. * It is often unsafe for an individual to seek an order of protection or other official help. The lack of this type of proof alone does not establish that the individual is not a survivor of violence.

***

In no instance should the perpetrator be contacted or given any information regarding the individual’s situation.

E-336-FITAP - PO GOOD CAUSE WAIVER OF PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS

Good cause for a temporary waiver of certain eligibility requirements for victims of violence is established if it is determined that compliance with the requirement would:

● Endanger a family affected by violence;

● Create obstacles for a survivor of violence to escape the situation; or

● Unfairly penalize the survivor for past, present and potential abuse.

Individuals who are identified to be survivors shall be advised that certain eligibility requirements may be temporarily waived upon a determination of good cause for such a waiver. With the individual's consent, the worker shall determine whether good cause exists for a waiver of a program requirement(s). An individual is free to decline an offer of a waiver, or terminate an existing waiver at any time.

E-337-FITAP - PO SPECIFIC PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS WHICH MAY BE WAIVED

Staff shall waive or modify program requirements if the requirement makes it more difficult for the individual to escape violence or places them at risk of further violence. Not every client experiencing or surviving violence will need to have program requirements waived; it is a case-by-case

4 of 12 determination. Consider the family’s current situation and their plan for achieving self-sufficiency when determining whether a waiver of program requirements is appropriate for reasons of violence. **

Program requirements which may be temporarily waived include but are not limited to:

● STEP participation requirement

Non-compliance with work activities may occur frequently in households affected by violence and could be the result of attempts by the * perpetrator to control the actions of the individual. Although an individual’s behaviors may appear to be non-compliant, they could indicate that a client has good cause and warrant further investigation.

A client may be excused from STEP activities if:

o The client has physical injuries caused by abuse or psychological effects of abuse which prohibit working; or

o A work activity is disrupted due to violence, including civil or criminal legal proceedings; or

o The abuser actively interferes with the client's work activity, attendance at work activities or child care arrangements; or

o A work activity location puts the client at risk of further violence; or

o Other circumstances that prevent the client from participating, such as but not limited to:

■ Sabotaging child care arrangements (This may include failing to watch the children as agreed or harassing babysitters),

■ Calling the work site and telling lies about the individual,

■ Verbally harassing the individual at work by telephone or in person,

■ Destroying or hiding clothes needed for classes, interviews, or work,

■ Keeping the individual up all night before interviews or tests,

■ Restricting access to family transportation, or

■ Turning off the alarm clock, etc. **

5 of 12 ● Time-Limited Benefits

Cash benefits for the family may continue after expiration of the 24 or 60-month time-limit if it is established that the * circumstances resulting from the violence result in the client's inability to be self-sufficient.

● Child Support Enforcement (CSE) or Paternity Establishment Cooperation Requirements

Survivors of violence may be excused from cooperation with CSE once good cause has been established if giving information about the noncustodial parent or starting a paternity or child support case might put the individual or their children in further danger of physical, emotional, or sexual abuse. However, the requirement should not be waived if the client wishes to pursue child support.

● Residency

The residency requirement may be waived for a client who is temporarily residing in Louisiana to escape a domestic violence situation.

E-338-FITAP - PO PROGRAM REQUIREMENTS WHICH MAY NOT BE WAIVED

Program requirements which may not be waived include:

● Income requirements; or

● Relationship and living in the home requirements.

E-339-FITAP - PO PRIVACY PROTECTION

Assure that all confidentiality provisions outlined in Chapter 7, Part E are strictly adhered to and advise the client of these protections:

● Inform the client that disclosure of information regarding violence is strictly voluntary;

● Assure the client that in no circumstances will the perpetrator be contacted; and

● Advise the client that it is not necessary that their geographical residence be entered in LITE **. The client may use an alternate mailing address which may be the local DCFS office address.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name E – Special Households Section No./Name E-300-FITAP FITAP Special Households Document No./Name E-340-FITAP Allocation of Income Effective Date March 15, 2022

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The allocation of income is the assignment of countable income of the caretaker relative and/or legal spouse to meet the needs of:

● the caretaker relative and/or legal spouse living in the home when not included due to the citizenship requirement,

● the caretaker relative's child or stepchild who is living in the home when not included due to the citizenship requirement, or

● persons living outside the home who the caretaker relative or legal spouse is under court order to support.

II. PROCEDURES

* Court-Ordered Child Support Expenses Paid

The amount of income to be allocated for persons not living in the home is the amount actually paid up to the amount of the court order. Enter the child support court-ordered amount and expense actually paid on the Expense Screen in LITE.

Required Member – Ineligible Alien

The amount of countable income belonging to the Ineligible Alien must be budgeted and used in consideration of the income eligibility of the Assistance Unit (AU).

However, a portion of the countable income amount is reserved for the Ineligible Alien to use for their own needs. The portion reserved is equal to the flat grant amount for one person. The remaining countable income is allocated to meet the needs of members included in the AU and included in the FITAP budget.

All countable income belonging to an ineligible alien must be entered in LITE. LITE will automatically calculate the allocation of need for the ineligible alien and budget the remaining countable income to determine income eligibility for the AU.

Note: Ineligible Aliens are not eligible to receive the Earned Income Deductions – Child Care Deduction and the $900 Time-Limited Deduction. **

***

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

OFS 002 Form / Instructions FITAP Budget Worksheet

body:
Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name E – Services Households Section No./Name E-400-SNAP Failure to Comply Document No./Name E-410-SNAP Failure to Comply (FTC) Penalty Effective Date January 10, 2022

1 of 5 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

SNAP benefits will not be increased when a household's public assistance (FITAP, KCSP, or SSI) benefits are decreased (reduced, terminated, or suspended) due to the client's failure to comply (FTC) with a requirement of the Public Assistance (PA) program. The purpose of this policy is to reinforce sanctions imposed by the public assistance programs.

The prohibition against increasing the household's SNAP allotment will follow the individual who failed to comply with public assistance requirements. If the sanctioned person leaves the household, the prohibition against increasing the SNAP allotment will end for that household. If the sanctioned person joins another SNAP household before the public assistance sanction ends, the prohibition will apply to the new household.

E-411-SNAP – PO DETERMINATION OF FAILURE TO COMPLY

The individual or household must have been receiving PA at the time of the violation and the PA benefits must have been decreased or terminated because of the client's failure to comply.

The determination of Failure to Comply (FTC) with a FITAP, KCSP, STEP, or SSI program requirement is made by the PA worker. The SNAP worker does not make this determination.

The worker will receive a CAFÉ Alert when the inclusion code/reason for a member on the associated FITAP or KCSP case changes from included to excluded. Any FITAP sanction is considered to be the result of a failure to comply.

To impose a FTC penalty, the agency administering the PA program must advise that a Failure to Comply has occurred.

FTC policy does not apply under the following circumstances:

● While the individual is sanctioned for failure to comply with a SNAP work registration ● requirement, (see B-1440-SNAP) or ABAWD work requirement (see B-1470-SNAP). ● During the period of time the person is being sanctioned under SNAP rules for the same offense that a penalty is being imposed under a PA program. ● When the Social Security Administration does not cooperate in providing the necessary information. ● When the individual was not certified for SNAP at the time the failure to comply occurred in the PA program. ● When a SNAP household applied for PA and was denied or certified for a reduced amount due to failure to comply with a PA requirement.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name E – Services Households Section No./Name E-400-SNAP Failure to Comply Document No./Name E-410-SNAP Failure to Comply (FTC) Penalty Effective Date January 10, 2022

2 of 5 E-412-SNAP – PO FAILURE TO COMPLY (FTC) PENALTY PERIODS

The prohibition against increasing SNAP benefits as a result of the PA sanction will be in effect for the following time periods:

● If a FITAP family is work-eligible and their FITAP benefits are terminated due to a STEP sanction, the FTC penalty will be applied to their SNAP case for the following time periods:

○ STEP Sanction, Occurrence 1 - one month ○ STEP Sanction, Occurrence 2 - two months ○ STEP Sanction, Occurrence 3 - three months

● If a FITAP or KCSP family is not work-eligible and FITAP or KCSP benefits are terminated due to failure to comply with a FITAP or KCSP requirement, the FTC penalty for the SNAP case is for one month. ● If FITAP or KCSP benefits are reduced or terminated due to an IPV sanction, the FTC penalty for the SNAP case is for the length of the IPV sanction.

If SSI benefits are reduced or suspended due to failure to comply with an SSI requirement, the FTC penalty for the SNAP case is 3 months or until SSA no longer reports the failure to comply, whichever occurs first.

E-413-SNAP – PO DETERMINING THE SNAP FAILURE TO COMPLY (FTC) PENALTY AMOUNT

The SNAP FTC penalty amount is equal to the difference between the PA grant prior to the PA sanction and the grant amount after the sanction.

E-414-SNAP – PO OTHER CHANGES

Changes in the household's circumstances unrelated to the PA sanction must be reflected in the SNAP budget. Do not recalculate the SNAP FTC penalty unless the SNAP case is closed and the client reapplies.

If there are other changes in the household which affect the PA grant amount for the same benefit month as the imposition of a IPV sanction, determine the SNAP FTC penalty amount based on what occurred first, the IPV sanction or the household change.

Example: A FITAP recipient is currently receiving a grant for herself and three children. The adult is disqualified due to FITAP IPV sanction. The client also reports the birth of a fourth child. The amount of the SNAP FTC penalty depends on what happened first. If the IPV sanction occurred first, the SNAP FTC penalty amount would be * $84 (the difference between $564 and $484.) If the request to add the child occurred first, the SNAP FTC penalty would be $86 (the difference between $654 and $568.) **

● If FITAP benefits are reduced or terminated due to an IPV sanction, the FTC penalty will be applied to the SNAP case for the length of the IPV sanction.

Example 5: The FITAP grant is closed due to an IPV sanction. The FITAP grant was $484 prior to the sanction. The FTC penalty amount is $484 and is applied to the SNAP budget for the length of the IPV sanction.

● If SSI benefits are reduced or suspended due to failure to comply with an SSI requirement, the FTC penalty will be applied to the SNAP case for 3 months or until SSA no longer reports the failure to comply, whichever occurs first.

Example 6: The FITAP grant is closed due to an SSI sanction. The SSI amount was $841 prior to the sanction. The FTC penalty amount of $841 ** is applied to the SNAP budget for 3 months or until SSA no longer reports the failure to comply, whichever is first.

E-416-SNAP – PO SSI FAILURE TO COMPLY (FTC) PENALTY

If a reduction in SSI benefits is due to a readily identifiable change such as, but not limited to, receipt of additional income, it is not necessary to contact SSA to determine the reason for the change.

If the reason for the reduction or suspension of SSI benefits is not known, verify the reason through SSA documents. If the SSA document or query response does not specifically identify the reduction or suspension as resulting from a Failure to Comply, do not apply a penalty.

Complete a case note to reflect the attempts to verify the reason for the SSI reduction.

Example - An SSI check is reduced. The reason for the reduction is not known. The worker is unable to obtain information from SSA concerning the reason for the reduction. The reduced SSI amount is shown in the SNAP budget and the attempts to verify the reason for the reduction are documented with a case note.

II. PROCEDURES

The case record must be documented or a case note made to reflect the PA program's determination of Failure to Comply. Budget the FTC amount as unearned income for the appropriate sanction period.

When notification is received from the PA program that the household's benefits will be reduced due to an IPV sanction, the SNAP FTC penalty must be imposed at the same time.

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

ALL OVERPAYMENTS/OVERISSUANCES MUST BE REPORTED TO THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT EXCEPT INADVERTENT HOUSEHOLD ERROR CLAIMS AND ADMINISTRATIVE ERROR CLAIMS LESS THAN * $350.00 ** ***.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F – Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-100-FITAP-SNAP Claims Document No./Name F-120-FITAP Worker Action Effective Date February 1, 2023

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

WHEN A CLIENT RECEIVES MORE BENEFITS THAN HE WAS ENTITLED TO RECEIVE, A CLAIM MUST BE SUBMITTED TO THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT NO LATER THAN FORTY-FIVE DAYS AFTER THE END OF THE QUARTER IN WHICH THE OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE WAS DISCOVERED.

II. PROCEDURES

THE FOLLOWING ACTION MUST BE TAKEN WHEN A CLIENT RECEIVES MORE BENEFITS THEN HE WAS ENTITLED TO RECEIVE.

1. CORRECT THE ONGOING BENEFITS AS NEEDED USING STANDARD ADVERSE ACTION PROCEDURES.

2. SEND FORM OFS 20CD TO THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT AFTER DISCUSSING THE OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE WITH THE CLIENT. IF AN INTENTIONAL PROGRAM VIOLATION (IPV) IS SUSPECTED, ATTACH A COPY OF ALL RELEVANT CASE RECORD DOCUMENTS WHICH WERE SIGNED BY THE HOUSEHOLD DURING THE PERIOD OF THE SUSPECTED IPV OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE AS WELL A COPY OF WAGE VERIFICATION. INFORM THE CLIENT THAT:

● A CLAIM WILL BE SUBMITTED TO STATE OFFICE,

● HE WILL BE NOTIFIED OF THE DECISION IN WRITING,

● HE HAS A RIGHT TO APPEAL, AND

● HE MAY CONTACT THE LOCAL OFFICE IF HE HAS ANY QUESTIONS.

3. Send Form OFS 20CF to the Fraud and Recovery Unit when the client's situation changes.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

OFS 20CD Form / Instructions Report of Claim Determination OFS 20CF Form / Instructions Assistance Payments Recovery Case Change Form

IV. REFERENCES

Louisiana Administrative Code – Title 67 Social Services – Subpart 2 – Chapter 15: General Program Administration – Subchapter B. Recovery, §1503

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

WHEN DETERMINING THE AMOUNT OF THE CLAIM INCLUDE ALL MONTHS OF PARTICIPATION IN THE PROGRAM WHEN DETERMINING THE AMOUNT OF THE CLAIM. PARTICIPATION IN THE PROGRAM OCCURS WHEN THE BENEFITS ARE POSTED TO THE EBT ACCOUNT AND THE AVAILABILITY DATE IS REACHED, REGARDLESS OF WHETHER THE BENEFITS ARE ACCESSED BY THE HOUSEHOLD.

F-131-FITAP- PO HOW TO DETERMINE FIRST MONTH OF INELIGIBILITY OR OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE

FOR ERRORS PRESENT AT THE TIME OF CERTIFICATION, THE FIRST MONTH OF AN OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE IS THE FIRST MONTH AN ERROR CAUSES THE CLIENT TO RECEIVE MORE BENEFITS THAN HE WAS ENTITLED TO RECEIVE.

FOR CHANGES OCCURRING WITHIN A CERTIFICATION, THE FIRST MONTH OF AN OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE IS THE MONTH IN WHICH THE CHANGE WOULD HAVE BEEN EFFECTIVE HAD IT BEEN REPORTED AND ACTED UPON IN A TIMELY MANNER.

IF THE CHANGE OCCURRED IN A CASE AND WAS NOT REPORTED TIMELY, BENEFITS SHOULD HAVE BEEN TERMINATED OR REDUCED EFFECTIVE THE EARLIEST POSSIBLE MONTH AFTER THE EXPIRATION OF ADVANCE NOTICE OF ADVERSE ACTION, IF REQUIRED.

THE EFFECTIVE MONTH CANNOT BE LATER THAN THE SECOND MONTH AFTER THE CHANGE OCCURRED.

F-131-1-FITAP- PO Ineligibility or Overpayment/Overissuance Because Household Member is Incarcerated/Drug Related Felony Conviction

IF IT IS DETERMINED THAT A HOUSEHOLD REPORTED THAT A HOUSEHOLD MEMBER WAS LIVING IN THE HOME BUT THE MEMBER WAS ACTUALLY INCARCERATED DURING THE APPLICATION OR REDETERMINATION INTERVIEW, RECOVERY IS NEEDED. THE PERIOD OF RECOVERY BEGINS AT CERTIFICATION FOR AN APPLICATION, AND THE FIRST MONTH OF THE NEW CERTIFICATION FOR A REDETERMINATION.

PRIOR TO OCTOBER 2017 IF IT IS DETERMINED THAT A HOUSEHOLD FAILED TO REPORT A HOUSEHOLD MEMBER HAD BEEN CONVICTED OF A DRUG-RELATED FELONY AT THE APPLICATION OR REDETERMINATION INTERVIEW, RECOVERY IS NEEDED. THE PERIOD OF RECOVERY BEGINS AT CERTIFICATION FOR AN APPLICATION AND THE FIRST MONTH OF THE NEW CERTIFICATION FOR A REDETERMINATION.

EXAMPLE: AN APPLICANT, NOT PREVIOUSLY KNOWN TO * LITE **, SUBMITS AN APPLICATION. THE APPLICATION WAS CERTIFIED PRIOR TO OCTOBER 2017 AND THE WEEKLY DRUG MATCH. THE APPLICANT RECEIVED BENEFITS, HOWEVER, THE APPLICANT

2 of 4 FAILED TO REPORT A DRUG-RELATED FELONY CONVICTION ON THE APPLICATION AND DURING THE INTERVIEW. AFTER THE NEXT WEEKLY MATCH WAS COMPLETED, THE CASE WAS AUTOMATICALLY PLACED IN ACTIVE CLOSURE (AC) STATUS SINCE THE CONVICTION DATE WAS WITHIN THE PAST 12 MONTHS. RECOVERY IS NEEDED FOR ALL BENEFITS ISSUED SINCE THE CLIENT FAILED TO REPORT THE CONVICTION ON HER APPLICATION.

F-132-FITAP- PO INELIGIBILITY OR OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE BECAUSE OF AGENCY DELAY

IF THE CLIENT MADE A TIMELY REPORT OF A CHANGE BUT THE WORKER DID NOT TAKE TIMELY ACTION, THEN THE FIRST OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE MONTH IS THE MONTH THE WORKER SHOULD HAVE MADE THE CHANGE EFFECTIVE.

IF A NOTICE OF ADVERSE ACTION WAS REQUIRED BUT NOT SENT, ASSUME THAT THE MAXIMUM ADVANCE NOTICE PERIOD EXPIRED WITHOUT THE HOUSEHOLD REQUESTING A FAIR HEARING.

II. PROCEDURES

1. DETERMINE THE FIRST MONTH OF OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE FOLLOWING GUIDELINES AND PROCEDURES OUTLINED IN CHAPTER 00, MISCELLANEOUS ISSUANCES MANUAL, PART O, OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE PROCEDURES, O-003.

2. COMPLETE A CORRECTED BUDGET FOR EACH MONTH OF OVERPAYMENT/ OVERISSUANCE. Refer to Chapter 00, Part O, O-004-2 for additional instructions.

3. SUBTRACT THE AMOUNT OF BENEFITS THE HOUSEHOLD SHOULD HAVE RECEIVED FROM THE AMOUNT IT ACTUALLY RECEIVED EACH MONTH. (For FITAP cases with child support collected by Child Support Enforcement (CSE), see No. 6.)

4. ADD TOGETHER THE AMOUNTS OF OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE FOR EACH MONTH.

5. DO NOT REDUCE THE AMOUNT OF AN OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE IN ONE MONTH BY THE AMOUNT OF AN UNDERPAYMENT/UNDERISSUANCE WHICH OCCURRED IN ANOTHER MONTH. REPORT UNDERPAYMENTS/ UNDERISSUANCES SEPARATELY BY:

● Submitting a memo to the Fraud and Recovery Unit. (Refer to Chapter 7, Section G)

IN CASES WHICH HAVE BOTH AN UNDERPAYMENT/UNDERISSUANCE AND OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE, STATE OFFICE WILL OFFSET ONE AGAINST THE OTHER.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 04 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F – Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-100-FITAP-SNAP Claims Document No./Name F-130-SNAP How To Determine Amount of Claim Effective Date June 1, 2025

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

WHEN DETERMINING THE AMOUNT OF THE CLAIM, INCLUDE ALL MONTHS OF PARTICIPATION IN THE PROGRAM ***. PARTICIPATION IN THE PROGRAM OCCURS WHEN THE BENEFITS ARE POSTED TO THE EBT ACCOUNT AND THE AVAILABILITY DATE IS REACHED, REGARDLESS OF WHETHER THE BENEFITS ARE ACCESSED BY THE HOUSEHOLD.

F-131-SNAP- PO HOW TO DETERMINE FIRST MONTH OF INELIGIBILITY OR OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE

FOR ERRORS PRESENT AT THE TIME OF CERTIFICATION, THE FIRST MONTH OF AN OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE IS THE FIRST MONTH AN ERROR CAUSES THE CLIENT TO RECEIVE MORE BENEFITS THAN HE WAS ENTITLED TO RECEIVE.

FOR CHANGES OCCURRING WITHIN A CERTIFICATION, THE FIRST MONTH OF AN OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE IS THE MONTH IN WHICH THE CHANGE WOULD HAVE BEEN EFFECTIVE HAD IT BEEN REPORTED AND ACTED UPON IN A TIMELY MANNER.

IF THE CHANGE OCCURRED IN A CASE AND WAS NOT REPORTED TIMELY, BENEFITS SHOULD HAVE BEEN TERMINATED OR REDUCED EFFECTIVE THE EARLIEST POSSIBLE MONTH AFTER THE EXPIRATION OF ADVANCE NOTICE OF ADVERSE ACTION, IF REQUIRED.

THE EFFECTIVE MONTH CANNOT BE LATER THAN THE SECOND MONTH AFTER THE CHANGE OCCURRED. For households included in Simplified Reporting, the effective month cannot be later than the third month after the household’s total gross monthly income exceeded the gross income limit for their household size.

F-131-1-SNAP- PO Ineligibility or Overpayment/Overissuance Because Household Member is Incarcerated/Drug Related Felony Conviction

IF IT IS DETERMINED THAT A HOUSEHOLD REPORTED THAT A HOUSEHOLD MEMBER WAS LIVING IN THE HOME BUT THE MEMBER WAS ACTUALLY INCARCERATED DURING THE APPLICATION OR REDETERMINATION INTERVIEW or when the simplified report was received, RECOVERY IS NEEDED. THE PERIOD OF RECOVERY BEGINS AT CERTIFICATION FOR AN APPLICATION, the first month following the simplified report month for simplified reports, AND THE FIRST MONTH OF THE NEW CERTIFICATION FOR A REDETERMINATION.

PRIOR TO OCTOBER 2017 IF IT IS DETERMINED THAT A HOUSEHOLD FAILED TO REPORT A HOUSEHOLD MEMBER HAD BEEN CONVICTED OF A DRUG-RELATED FELONY AT THE APPLICATION OR REDETERMINATION INTERVIEW, RECOVERY IS NEEDED. THE PERIOD OF RECOVERY BEGINS AT CERTIFICATION FOR AN APPLICATION AND THE FIRST MONTH OF THE NEW CERTIFICATION FOR A REDETERMINATION.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 04 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F – Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-100-FITAP-SNAP Claims Document No./Name F-130-SNAP How To Determine Amount of Claim Effective Date June 1, 2025

2 of 3 EXAMPLE: AN APPLICANT, NOT PREVIOUSLY KNOWN TO LITE, SUBMITS AN APPLICATION. THE APPLICATION WAS CERTIFIED PRIOR TO OCTOBER 2017 AND THE WEEKLY DRUG MATCH. THE APPLICANT RECEIVED BENEFITS, HOWEVER, THE APPLICANT FAILED TO REPORT A DRUG-RELATED FELONY CONVICTION ON THE APPLICATION AND DURING THE INTERVIEW. AFTER THE NEXT WEEKLY MATCH WAS COMPLETED, THE CASE WAS AUTOMATICALLY PLACED IN ACTIVE CLOSURE (AC) STATUS SINCE THE CONVICTION DATE WAS WITHIN THE PAST 12 MONTHS. RECOVERY IS NEEDED FOR ALL BENEFITS ISSUED SINCE THE CLIENT FAILED TO REPORT THE CONVICTION ON HER APPLICATION.

F-132-SNAP- PO INELIGIBILITY OR OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE BECAUSE OF AGENCY DELAY

IF THE CLIENT MADE A TIMELY REPORT OF A CHANGE BUT THE WORKER DID NOT TAKE TIMELY ACTION, THEN THE FIRST OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE MONTH IS THE MONTH THE WORKER SHOULD HAVE MADE THE CHANGE EFFECTIVE.

IF A NOTICE OF ADVERSE ACTION WAS REQUIRED BUT NOT SENT, ASSUME THAT THE MAXIMUM ADVANCE NOTICE PERIOD EXPIRED WITHOUT THE HOUSEHOLD REQUESTING A FAIR HEARING.

II. PROCEDURES

1. DETERMINE THE FIRST MONTH OF OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE FOLLOWING GUIDELINES AND PROCEDURES OUTLINED IN CHAPTER 00, MISCELLANEOUS ISSUANCES MANUAL, PART O, OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE PROCEDURES, O-003.

2. COMPLETE A CORRECTED BUDGET FOR EACH MONTH OF OVERPAYMENT/ OVERISSUANCE. Refer to Chapter 00, Part O, O-004-3 for additional instructions.

Do not apply the earned income deduction to earned income the household did not timely report

3. SUBTRACT THE AMOUNT OF BENEFITS THE HOUSEHOLD SHOULD HAVE RECEIVED FROM THE AMOUNT IT ACTUALLY RECEIVED EACH MONTH.

4. ADD TOGETHER THE AMOUNTS OF OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE FOR EACH MONTH.

5. DO NOT REDUCE THE AMOUNT OF AN OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE IN ONE MONTH BY THE AMOUNT OF AN UNDERPAYMENT/UNDERISSUANCE WHICH OCCURRED IN ANOTHER MONTH.

6. REPORT UNDERPAYMENTS/UNDERISSUANCES SEPARATELY BY * SENDING AN EMAIL TO THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT AT DCFS.FRAUD@LA.GOV. THE EMAIL MUST INCLUDE ALL REQUIRED VERIFICATION AND SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION TO

3 of 3 SUPPORT THE CLAIM. THE SUBJECT LINE OF THE EMAIL MUST READ “CLAIM NEEDED for [program]” FOLLOWED BY THE CASE IDENTIFICATION NUMBER (CID). EXAMPLE: CLAIM NEEDED FOR SNAP– CID 000000000. **

7. IN CASES WHICH HAVE BOTH AN UNDERPAYMENT/UNDERISSUANCE AND OVERPAYMENT/OVERISSUANCE, STATE OFFICE WILL OFFSET ONE AGAINST THE OTHER.

8. The LITE Claims Calculator will subtract the amount of any expunged benefits in the household's EBT account. 9. For issuance prior to EBT, exclude any months in which the household did not participate and any months over six years prior to the date of discovery or before March 1, 1979. III. Agency Name Office of Family Support (OFS) Chapter No./Name 04 – Family Assistance Manual (FAM) Part No./Name F. Case Maintenance (FITAP) Section No./Name F-100-FITAP Claims (FITAP) Document No./Name F-140-FITAP When Local Office Handles Repayment Dates Issue December 30, 2005 Effective January 1, 2006

1 of 1

When a client offers repayment on a claim, review the Recovery Account System to determine whether there is an active account.

If a claim has been established on the Recovery Account System, repayment can be made:

● Through EBT with the Louisiana Purchase Automated Benefit Card by debiting the account (refer to Chapter 3, * J-150, ** Electronic Repayment Of Claims)

● By check or money order made payable to DSS, Office Of Family Support. Mail the payment in an envelope to the Fraud And Recovery Section, P.O. Box 91147, Baton Rouge, La. 70821-9147.

If there is not an established claim on the Recovery Account System, repayment can be made by sending to Fraud And Recovery:

● A check or money order, made payable to DSS, Office Of Family Support, and

● A completed form OFS 20CD.

Electronic repayment of benefits must not be used when there is a voluntary return of benefits and there is no established claim.

Repayment should not be accepted if the amount to be repaid is below the threshold for recovery. (refer to Miscellaneous Issuances Manual O-004.).

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 − Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F − Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-100-SNAP Claims Document No./Name F-140-SNAP When Local Office Handles Repayment Effective Date March 1, 2023

1 of 1 I.

STATEMENT OF POLICY

When a client offers repayment on a claim that has been established on the Recovery Account System, accept checks or money orders made payable to Department of Children and Family Services. Mail payment in an envelope to Fraud And Recovery Unit, P. O. Box 1421, Baton Rouge, LA 70821- 1421 .

Form 20CD must have been submitted and a claim established on the Recovery Account System BEFORE repayment can be accepted.

II. PROCEDURES

Claim repayments can be made through EBT with the La. Purchase Automated Benefit Card by debiting the account. (Refer to Chapter 3, Document J-150 Electronic Repayment Of Claims.)

No more than five persons in each office can accept La. Purchase Automated Benefit Cards for repayment.

Before accepting repayment of a claim, *** * email The Fraud and Recovery Unit (FRU) at DCFS.Fraud@la.gov to determine if the client has an active recovery account. Include the client’s name, Social Security Number, CID and the Claim Number, if a claim was completed in the Claims Calculator. FRU will respond within three workdays of the date of the request. If there is an active debt, FRU will include in the email the balance of the debt.**

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

OFS 20CD Form / Instructions Report of Claim Determination

IV. REFERENCES

LAC-Title 67: Part III., Subpart 3. Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Chapter 19 Certification of Eligible Households, Subchapter P. Recovery of Over-Issued SNAP Benefits

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F – Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-200-FITAP-SNAP Corrective Payments/Restoration Document No./Name F-210-FITAP Entitlement Effective Date January 1, 2023

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

There is no statement of policy.

II. PROCEDURES

Correct all underpayments within 5 workdays from the date the loss is discovered regardless of:

● when they occurred, ● why they occurred, or ● the amount of the underpayment.

EXCEPTION: DO NOT AUTHORIZE PAYMENT/RESTORATION IF THE HOUSEHOLD HAS A PENDING OR ACTIVE RECOVERY ACCOUNT. *** * EMAIL THE UNDERPAYMENT TO THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT (FRU) AT DCFS.FRAUD@LA.GOV. REFER TO THE PREVIOUS OVERPAYMENT AND INCLUDE THE CLIENT’S NAME, SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER, and CID. WITHIN THREE WORKDAYS OF THE DATE OF REQUEST, FRU WILL NOTIFY THE WORKER VIA EMAIL OF THE BALANCE OF THE DEBT, THE AMOUNT THAT WILL BE APPLIED TO THE DEBT, AND THE AMOUNT OWED TO THE CLIENT IF FUNDS REMAIN. THE AMOUNT OF THE RESORATION WILL BE THE AMOUNT THAT FRU INDICATED IN THEIR RESPONSE AS THE AMOUNT THAT IS OWED TO THE HOUSEHOLD. FRU WILL ADJUST THE DEBT ACCORDINGLY IN THE RECOVERY ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

OFS 20CD Form / Instructions Report of Claim Determination

IV. REFERENCES

Louisiana Administrative Code - Title 67 Social Services - Subpart 3 - Chapter 19: Certification of Eligible Households - Subchapter P **

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F – Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-200-FITAP-SNAP Corrective Payments/Restoration Document No./Name F-210-SNAP Entitlement Effective Date January 1, 2023

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Households are entitled to restoration within 5 workdays from the date the loss is discovered, even if currently ineligible, when:

● a loss of benefits was caused by an agency error,

● a loss was caused by an administrative disqualification for IPV which was later reversed, or

● federal regulations state that the household is entitled to restoration.

Households are not entitled to restored benefits for client errors.

Restoration is authorized for not more than 12 months prior to whichever occurred first:

● the date the agency received a request for restoration from the household,

● the date the agency is notified or otherwise discovers a loss has occurred,

● the date court action was initiated if judicial action is the first action taken by the household to obtain restoration, or

● the date the household requested a fair hearing to contest an adverse decision, if no request for restoration was received.

II. PROCEDURES

* If there is no recovery account, the form OFS 35 must be completed and submitted to the supervisor for review, approval, and system input. **

*** DO NOT AUTHORIZE PAYMENT/RESTORATION IF THE HOUSEHOLD HAS A PENDING OR ACTIVE RECOVERY ACCOUNT. * EMAIL THE UNDERPAYMENT TO THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT (FRU) AT DCFS.Fraud@la.gov. REFER TO THE PREVIOUS OVERPAYMENT AND INCLUDE THE CLIENT’S NAME, SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER, CID, AND THE CLAIM NUMBER, IF THE CLAIM WAS COMPLETED IN THE CLAIMS CALCULATOR. Form OFS 20CD outlining the circumstances which necessitated the restoration should be attached to the EMAIL when there is a recovery account. WITHIN THREE WORKDAYS OF THE DATE OF REQUEST, FRU WILL NOTIFY THE WORKER VIA EMAIL OF THE BALANCE OF THE DEBT, THE AMOUNT THAT WILL BE APPLIED TO THE DEBT, AND THE AMOUNT OWED TO THE CLIENT IF FUNDS REMAIN. THE AMOUNT OF THE RESTORATION WILL BE THE AMOUNT THAT FRU INDICATED IN THEIR RESPONSE AS THE AMOUNT THAT IS OWED TO THE HOUSEHOLD. FRU WILL ADJUST THE DEBT ACCORDINGLY IN THE RECOVERY ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM. **

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F – Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-200-FITAP-SNAP Corrective Payments/Restoration Document No./Name F-220-FITAP Local Office Responsibilities Effective Date January 15, 2023

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

* All FITAP overpayments shall be subject to collection either by recoupment or recovery with the exception of inadvertent household error claims and administrative error claims of less than $125 for nonparticipating households.

Action will be taken to recover all claims for participating households and claims which are determined to be the result of intentional program violation.

II. PROCEDURES

● CORRECT THE ONGOING BENEFITS AS NEEDED. NOTE: SUPPLEMENTAL BENEFITS MAY BE AUTHORIZED FOR THE CURRENT MONTH.

● ASK THE HOUSEHOLD TO PROVIDE MORE INFORMATION IF THE CASE RECORD DOES NOT DOCUMENT THE HOUSEHOLD'S ELIGIBILITY. IF THE HOUSEHOLD CANNOT PROVIDE THE NECESSARY INFORMATION, DO NOT CONSIDER THAT A LOSS OCCURRED.

● DETERMINE THE MONTH THE LOSS BEGAN.

● COMPUTE FOR EACH MONTH THE AMOUNT OF BENEFITS THE HOUSEHOLD SHOULD HAVE RECEIVED BEGINNING WITH THE FIRST MONTH OF THE LOSS.

AUTHORIZE BENEFITS FOR THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE ACTUAL AND CORRECT AMOUNT OF BENEFITS WITHIN 5 WORK DAYS FROM THE DATE THE LOSS IS DISCOVERED UNLESS THE CLIENT OWES A CLAIM FOR AN OVERPAYMENT. IF THERE IS A PENDING OR ACTIVE RECOVERY ACCOUNT, THE CORRECTIVE PAYMENT/RESTORATION WILL BE APPLIED FIRST TO THE OUTSTANDING CLAIM. REPORT THE UNDERPAYMENT TO THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT (FRU) BY EMAIL AT DCFS.FRAUD@LA.GOV. THE EMAIL SHOULD INCLUDE THE CLIENT’S NAME, SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER, and CID. WITHIN THREE WORKDAYS FROM THE DATE OF THE REQUEST, FRU WILL EMAILA RESPONSE INCLUDING THE BALANCE OF THE DEBT, THE AMOUNT TO BE APPLIED TO THE DEBT, AND THE AMOUNT OWED TO THE CLIENT IF THERE ARE REMAINING FUNDS.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

OFS 20CD Form / Instructions Report of Claim Determination

IV. REFERENCES

Louisiana Administrative Code - Title 67 Social Services - Subpart 3 - Chapter 19: Certification of Eligible Households - Subchapter P **

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F – Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-200-FITAP-SNAP Corrective Payments/Restoration Document No./Name F-220-SNAP Local Office Responsibilities Effective Date January 15, 2023

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

* Staff in the local office are responsible for issuing corrective payments. Please see section II for the local office responsibilities.

II. PROCEDURES

● CORRECT THE ONGOING BENEFITS AS NEEDED.

NOTE: SUPPLEMENTAL BENEFITS MAY BE AUTHORIZED FOR THE CURRENT MONTH.

● ASK THE HOUSEHOLD TO PROVIDE MORE INFORMATION IF THE CASE RECORD DOES NOT DOCUMENT THE HOUSEHOLD'S ELIGIBILITY. IF THE HOUSEHOLD CANNOT PROVIDE THE NECESSARY INFORMATION, DO NOT CONSIDER THAT A LOSS OCCURRED.

● DETERMINE THE MONTH THE LOSS BEGAN.

● COMPUTE FOR EACH MONTH THE AMOUNT OF BENEFITS THE HOUSEHOLD SHOULD HAVE RECEIVED BEGINNING WITH THE FIRST MONTH OF THE LOSS.

● Exclude months before the 12-month time limit and calculate the loss for each month after the date of the initial loss until the month the loss is corrected or the household is found ineligible.

● AUTHORIZE BENEFITS FOR THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE ACTUAL AND CORRECT AMOUNT OF BENEFITS WITHIN 5 WORKDAYS FROM THE DATE THE LOSS IS DISCOVERED UNLESS THE CLIENT OWES A CLAIM FOR AN OVERPAYMENT. IF THERE IS A PENDING OR ACTIVE RECOVERY ACCOUNT, THE CORRECTIVE PAYMENT/RESTORATION WILL BE APPLIED FIRST TO THE OUTSTANDING CLAIM. REPORT THE UNDERPAYMENT TO THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT (FRU) BY EMAIL AT DCFS.Fraud@la.gov. THE EMAIL SHOULD INCLUDE THE CLIENT’S NAME, SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER, CID, AND CLAIM NUMBER, IF A CLAIM WAS COMPLETED ON THE CLAIMS CALCULATOR. WITHIN THREE WORKDAYS FROM THE DATE OF THE REQUEST, FRU WILL EMAIL A RESPONSE INCLUDING THE BALANCE OF THE DEBT, THE AMOUNT TO APPLIED TO THE DEBT, AND THE AMUNT OWED TO CLIENT IF THERE ARE REMAINING FUNDS. Form 20CD outlining the circumstances which necessitated the restoration should be attached to the memo.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

OFS 20CD Form / Instructions Report of Claim Determination **

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F – Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-200-FITAP-SNAP Corrective Payments/Restoration Document No./Name F-260-FITAP Providing Corrective Payments/Restoration Effective Date January 1, 2023

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

ALL BENEFITS OWED THE CLIENT WILL BE ISSUED AT THE SAME TIME. ***

II. PROCEDURES

Corrective payments for FITAP and KCSP will be made by * completing the manual issuance screen in LITE. ** *** For FITAP and KCSP, separate entries must be made for each benefit month covered.

* EXCEPTION: DO NOT AUTHORIZE PAYMENT/RESTORATION IF THE HOUSEHOLD HAS A PENDING OR ACTIVE RECOVERY ACCOUNT. EMAIL THE UNDERPAYMENT TO THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT (FRU) AT DCFS.Fraud@la.gov. REFER TO THE PREVIOUS OVERPAYMENT AND INCLUDE THE CLIENT’S NAME, SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER, and CID. WITHIN THREE WORKDAYS OF THE DATE OF REQUEST, FRU WILL NOTIFY THE WORKER VIA EMAIL OF THE BALANCE OF THE DEBT, THE AMOUNT THAT WILL BE APPLIED TO THE DEBT, AND THE AMOUNT OWED TO THE CLIENT IF FUNDS REMAIN. THE AMOUNT OF THE RESTORATION WILL BE THE AMOUNT THAT FRU INDICATED IN THEIR RESPONSE AS THE AMOUNT THAT IS OWED TO THE HOUSEHOLD. FRU WILL ADJUST THE DEBT ACCORDINGLY IN THE RECOVERY ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM.

FITAP, KCSP, AND SNAP BENEFITS WILL BE POSTED TO THE RECIPIENT'S EBT ACCOUNT THE DAY AFTER THE CORRECTIVE PAYMENT/RESTORATION IS INPUT IN LITE.

FOR HOUSEHOLDS THAT DO NOT POSSESS A LOUISIANA EBT CARD, ISSUE A NEW CARD. **

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

OFS 35 Form / Instructions Request for Special-Manual Issuance Cash Assistance-SNAP Benefits

IV. REFERENCES

C-110 Employee Responsibilities J-140 Restoration

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F – Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-200-FITAP-SNAP Corrective Payments/Restoration Document No./Name F-260-SNAP Providing Corrective Payments/Restoration Effective Date January 1, 2023

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

ALL BENEFITS OWED THE CLIENT WILL BE ISSUED AT THE SAME TIME.

II. PROCEDURES

Restoration of SNAP benefits will be made by *** * completing the manual issuance screen in LITE. All benefits due to the household should be entered as a lump sum regardless of the benefit months covered.

EXCEPTION: DO NOT AUTHORIZE PAYMENT/RESTORATION IF THE HOUSEHOLD HAS A PENDING OR ACTIVE RECOVERY ACCOUNT. EMAIL THE UNDERPAYMENT TO THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT (FRU) AT DCFS.Fraud@la.gov. REFER TO THE PREVIOUS OVERPAYMENT AND INCLUDE THE CLIENT’S NAME, SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER, CID, ANDTHE CLAIM NUMBER, IFA CLAIME WAS COMPLETED IN THE CLAIMS CALCULATOR. Form OFS 20CD outlining the circumstances which necessitated the restoration should be attached to the EMAIL when there is a recovery account. WITHIN THREE WORKDAYS OF THE DATE OF REQUEST, FRU WILL NOTIFY THE WORKER VIA EMAIL OF THE BALANCE OF THE DEBT, THE AMOUNT THAT WILL BE APPLIED TO THE DEBT, AND THE AMOUNT OWED TO THE CLIENT IF FUNDS REMAIN. THE AMOUNT OF THE RESTORATION WILL BE THE AMOUNT THAT FRU INDICATED IN THEIR RESPONSE AS THE AMOUNT THAT IS OWED TO THE HOUSEHOLD. FRU WILL ADJUST THE DEBT ACCORDINGLY IN THE RECOVERY ACCOUNT MANAGEMENTSYSTEM.

FITAP, KCSP, AND SNAP BENEFITS WILL BE POSTED TO THE RECIPIENT'S EBT ACCOUNT THE DAY AFTER THE CORRECTIVE PAYMENT/RESTORATION IS INPUT IN LITE.

FOR HOUSEHOLDS THAT DO NOT POSSESS A LOUISIANA EBT CARD, ISSUE A NEW CARD.

If the household to be issued restoration no longer resides in Louisiana, the benefits will be entered IN LITE as for any other household. Procedures in section I-132 of the EBT Handbook should be followed to allow the household access to the benefits.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

OFS 20CD Form / Instructions Report of Claim Determination

IV. REFERENCES

7 CFR 273.17 **

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F-Case Maintenance (FITAP) Section No./Name F-300-FITAP Intentional Program Violations (FITAP) Document No./Name F-310-FITAP Definitions Effective Date January 1, 2016

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

INTENTIONAL PROGRAM VIOLATION (IPV) OCCURS WHEN A CLIENT, FOR THE PURPOSE OF ESTABLISHING OR MAINTAINING ELIGIBILITY OR FOR INCREASING OR PREVENTING A REDUCTION IN BENEFITS, INTENTIONALLY:

● MAKES A FALSE OR MISLEADING STATEMENT, OR MISREPRESENTS, CONCEALS, OR WITHHOLDS FACTS; OR

● COMMITS AN ACT INTENDED TO MISLEAD OR MISREPRESENT, CONCEAL OR WITHHOLDS FACTS; OR

● Propounds a falsity.

INTENTIONAL PROGRAM VIOLATION ALSO OCCURS WHEN A CLIENT USES AN EBT CARD IN A WAY THAT IS PROHIBITED BY THE PROGRAM AND THE AGENCY HAS DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE TO SUPPORT A CHARGE OF PROHIBITED USE OF AN EBT CARD. Prohibited use includes:

o The use of cash benefits in a electronic benefit transfer transaction in any of the following places in a liquor store, gambling casino or gaming establishment, any retail establishment that provides adult oriented entertainment in which performers disrobe or perform in an unclothed state for entertainment purposes, any adult bookstore, adult paraphernalia store, or sexually oriented business, any tattoo, piercing, or commercial body art facility, any nail salon, jewelry store, amusement or video arcade, any bail bonds company, any night club, bar, tavern, or saloon, any cruise ship, psychic business, or any establishment where persons under age 18 are not permitted are prohibited.

o The purchase of an alcoholic beverage, a tobacco product, a lottery ticket or jewelry with an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card is prohibited.

* Note: Policy is applicable for all cash cases (FITAP/KCSP). **

II. PROCEDURES

There are no procedures associated with this policy.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms associated with this policy.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F – Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-300-FITAP-SNAP Intentional Program Violations Document No./Name F-330-FITAP Penalties Effective Date May 1, 2018

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS FOUND TO HAVE COMMITTED IPV ARE INELIGIBLE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE PROGRAM:

● FOR ONE YEAR FOR THE FIRST VIOLATION;

● FOR TWO YEARS FOR THE SECOND VIOLATION; AND

● PERMANENTLY FOR THE THIRD VIOLATION.

* Note: Disqualifications resulting from the illegal use of an Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) card will result in case closure. **

***

Individuals found guilty of having made a fraudulent statement or representation with respect to residence in order to receive assistance simultaneously from two or more states are ineligible for a 10 year period that begins on the date the individual is convicted in Federal or State Court. This does not apply if the President of the United States grants a pardon with respect to the conduct which was the subject of the conviction.

Note: Policy is applicable for all cash cases (FITAP/KCSP).

II. PROCEDURES

There are no procedures associated with this policy.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms associated with this policy.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4-Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F-Case Maintenance (SNAP) Section No./Name F-300-SNAP Intentional Program Violations (SNAP) Document No./Name F-330-SNAP Penalties Effective Date December 1, 2013

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS FOUND TO HAVE COMMITTED IPV ARE INELIGIBLE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE PROGRAM:

● for six months for the first violation (offenses 6/83 - 9/96),

● for twelve months for the first violation (offenses 10/96 and thereafter),

● for twelve months for the second violation (offenses 6/83 - 9/96),

● for twenty-four months for the second violation (offenses 10/96 and thereafter),

● permanently for the third violation.

Note: One or more IPV disqualifications which occurred prior to the June 1,1983 implementation of these penalties and addressed under the provisions of the Food Stamp Act of 1977 and 1980 amendments must be considered as only one previous disqualification when determining the penalty to impose.

Individuals found guilty of an Intentional Program Violation because of making a fraudulent statement or representation with respect to identity or residence in order to receive multiple benefits simultaneously shall be disqualified for ten years.

Individuals found by a court to have used or received SNAP in a transaction involving the sale of a controlled substance shall be disqualified from the program:

● for one year for the first finding occurring 9/94 through 9/96,

● for two years for the first finding occurring 10/96 and thereafter,

● permanently for the second finding.

Individuals found by a court to have used or received SNAP in a transaction involving the sale of firearms, ammunition or explosives shall be permanently disqualified from the program.

Individuals convicted of trafficking SNAP benefits of $500 or more shall be permanently disqualified.

If the court imposes a penalty, the period of disqualification is in accordance with the court order.

II. PROCEDURES

* There are no procedures associated with this policy.
