Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F – Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-300-FITAP-SNAP Intentional Program Violations (IPV) Document No./Name F-340-FITAP Referrals For IPV Effective Date January 1, 2023

1 of 5 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT WILL REVIEW ALL COMPLAINTS, FROM THE PUBLIC AND DCFS STAFF, TO DETERMINE IF THERE ARE VALID REASONS TO SUSPECT AN INTENTIONAL PROGRAM VIOLATION ON THE PART OF THE SUSPECTED VIOLATOR.

F-341-FITAP - PO PARISH OFFICE RESPONSIBILITY

IPV DISQUALIFICATION ALERTS ARE SENT TO EACH ECONOMIC STABILITY OFFICE VIA THE GENERIC EMAIL ADDRESS ADVISING THAT AN IPV DETERMINATION HAS BEEN MADE.

F-342-FITAP - PO FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT RESPONSIBILITY

WHEN THERE ARE VALID REASONS TO SUSPECT IPV, THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT WILL PURSUE AN ADMINISTRATIVE IPV DETERMINATION OR CRIMINAL IPV DETERMINATION.

F-342-1-FITAP – PO Imposition of the Disqualification

THERE IS A DEFINED PERIOD OF TIME TO NOTIFY A DISQUALIFIED MEMBER.

F-343-FITAP - PO DCFS BUREAU OF APPEALS’ RESPONSIBILITY

REFERRALS ARE MADE TO THE DCFS BUREAU OF APPEALS WHEN WARRANTED.

II. PROCEDURES

F-341-FITAP - PR PARISH OFFICE RESPONSIBILITY

THE LOCAL OFFICE:

● INFORMS THE HOUSEHOLD OF THE DISQUALIFICATION PENALTIES FOR COMMITTING IPV EACH TIME THE HOUSEHOLD APPLIES FOR BENEFITS,

● REPORTS OVERISSUANCES ON FORM OFS 20CD WITH A COPY OF SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS CONTAINING A RECOMMENDATION TO THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT THAT IPV IS SUSPECTED, AND

● REFERS CASES OF ALLEGED IPV TO THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT FOR INVESTIGATION AS INSTRUCTED BY OFS 40 INSTRUCTIONS.

ONCE THE HEARING PROCESS BEGINS FOR A COMBINED FAIR HEARING AND AN ADMINISTRATIVE DISQUALIFICATION HEARING, THE LOCAL OFFICE:

2 of 5 o REPORTS SUBSEQUENT CHANGES IN CLIENT’S CASE STATUS, BENEFIT AMOUNT, ADDRESS, OR OTHER CIRCUMSTANCE TO DCFS BUREAU OF APPEALS, AND

o REPORTS THESE SUBSEQUENT CHANGES DURING THE HEARING TO THE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGE.

IF IPV HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED, FRAUD AND RECOVERY NOTIFIES THE LOCAL OFFICE THAT A PERSON HAS COMMITTED AN IPV WITH AN ALERT SENT TO THE GENERIC EMAIL ADDRESS, AND ENTERS IPV DECISIONS ON THE * LITE SANCTION SCREEN.

NOTE: THE LOCAL OFFICE MUST CHECK THE GENERIC EMAIL INBOX REGULARLY FOR NEW IPV SANCTION EMAILS FROM THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT.

● IF THE CASE IS ACTIVE, THE WORKER MUST AUTHORIZE THE CASE TO IMPOSE THE DISQUALIFICATION. LITE WILL GENERATE ADEQUATE NOTICE TO THE HOUSEHOLD PROVIDING BENEFIT AMOUNT AFTER THE APPROPRIATE PERSON IS DISQUALIFIED.

● IF THE CASE IS INACTIVE AND THE SANCTION PERIOD HAS NOT ENDED, UPON AUTHORIZATION AT CERTIFICATION, GENERATE A NOTICE TO THE HOUSEHOLD ADVISING OF ELIGIBILITY AND BENEFIT LEVEL WITH THE DISQUALIFIED MEMBER'S NEEDS OMITTED.

A COPY OF THE EMAIL RECEIVED FROM THE FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT MUST BE FILED IN ONBASE, AND A CASE NOTE MADE STATING WHEN THE CASE WAS AUTHORIZED. **

ONCE A DISQUALIFICATION PENALTY HAS BEEN IMPOSED, THE PERIOD OF DISQUALIFICATION CONTINUES UNINTERRUPTED UNTIL COMPLETED REGARDLESS OF THE ELIGIBILITY OF THE DISQUALIFIED MEMBER'S HOUSEHOLD FOR THE REMAINDER OF THE DISQUALIFICATION PERIOD.

F-342-FITAP - PR FRAUD AND RECOVERY UNIT RESPONSIBILITY

WHEN A CASE IS REFERRED TO FRAUD AND RECOVERY, FRAUD AND RECOVERY:

● REFERS THE CASE FOR PROSECUTION, OR

● REFERS THE CASE TO DCFS BUREAU OF APPEALS FOR AN ADMINISTRATIVE DISQUALIFICATION HEARING IF THE CLIENT DOES NOT SIGN THE WAIVER OF RIGHT TO AN ADMINISTRATIVE DISQUALIFICATION HEARING, AND:

o THE FACTS OF THE INDIVIDUAL CASE DO NOT WARRANT CIVIL OR CRIMINAL PROSECUTION THROUGH THE APPROPRIATE COURT SYSTEMS; OR

3 of 5 o THE CASE WAS PREVIOUSLY REFERRED FOR PROSECUTION, AND WAS DECLINED BY THE APPROPRIATE LEGAL AUTHORITY; OR

o THE CASE WAS PREVIOUSLY REFERRED FOR PROSECUTION AND NO ACTION WAS TAKEN WITHIN A REASONABLE PERIOD AND THE REFERRAL WAS FORMALLY WITHDRAWN BY FRAUD AND RECOVERY, OR

● PURSUES COLLECTION WHEN IPV CANNOT BE ESTABLISHED, OR

● INITIATES COLLECTION ON CLAIMS PENDING AN ADMINISTRATIVE DISQUALIFICATION HEARING.

IF IPV HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED, FRAUD AND RECOVERY MUST:

● INITIATE COLLECTION ACTION FOR IPV CLAIMS,

● ISSUE FORM FR 15A AND HEARING DECISION (IF APPLICABLE) TO THE PERSON TO BE DISQUALIFIED. THE HEARING DECISION MUST BE PROVIDED TO THE HOUSEHOLD MEMBER WITHIN 90 DAYS OF THE DATE THE HOUSEHOLD MEMBER WAS NOTIFIED IN WRITING THAT A HEARING HAD BEEN SCHEDULED. SEND THE PARISH OFFICE A COPY OF THE FORM FR 15A AND HEARING DECISION (IF APPLICABLE).

● ENTER IPV DECISIONS ON THE * LITE ** SANCTION SCREEN. ENTER THE *** VIOLATION OCCURRENCE, SANCTION REASON, DECISION DATE AND BEGIN DATE ON THE MEMBER SANCTION SCREEN. THE SANCTION END DATE IS AUTOMATICALLY POPULATED BASED ON THE VIOLATION OCCURRENCE TIME PERIOD.

o IF THE CASE IS ACTIVE, SEND AN IPV DISQUALIFICATION ALERT FOR WORKER ACTIVITIES. THE WORKER WILL * AUTHORIZE THE CASE TO IMPOSE THE DISQUALIFICATION AND LITE WILL GENERATE ADEQUATE NOTICE TO THE HOUSEHOLD PROVIDING BENEFIT AMOUNT AFTER THE APPROPRIATE PERSON IS DISQUALIFIED.

o IF THE CASE IS INACTIVE AND THE SANCTION PERIOD HAS NOT ENDED, UPON AUTHORIZATION AT CERTIFICATION, GENERATE A NOTICE TO THE HOUSEHOLD ADVISING OF ELIGIBILITY AND BENEFIT LEVEL WITH THE DISQUALIFIED MEMBER'S NEEDS OMITTED.

NOTE: LITE TRACKS THE DISQUALIFICATION PERIOD AND AUTHORIZES ** THE CASE TO ADD THE MEMBER BACK TO THE CASE AT THE END OF THE SANCTION PERIOD. A SYSTEM NOTICE WILL BE SENT WHEN THE MEMBER IS ADDED BACK TO THE CASE.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F – Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-300-FITAP-SNAP Intentional Program Violations (IPV) Document No./Name F-340-FITAP Referrals For IPV Effective Date January 1, 2023

4 of 5 F-342-1-FITAP - PR Imposition of the Disqualification

THE DISQUALIFICATION MUST BE IMPOSED AS FOLLOWS:

● WITHIN 45 DAYS OF THE DATE THE PERSON WAS FOUND GUILTY OR SENTENCED BY THE COURT IF NO OTHER DATE WAS SPECIFIED BY THE COURT; OR ● WITHIN 45 DAYS OF THE DATE THE PERSON SIGNED THE COURT DISQUALIFICATION CONSENT AGREEMENT; OR

● Effective no later than the first day of the second month following the date of the notice (Form FR 15A).

THE PERIOD OF DISQUALIFICATION CONTINUES UNINTERRUPTED UNTIL COMPLETED REGARDLESS OF THE ELIGIBILITY OF THE DISQUALIFIED MEMBER'S HOUSEHOLD FOR THE REMAINDER OF THE DISQUALIFICATION PERIOD.

F-343-FITAP - PR DCFS BUREAU OF APPEALS’ RESPONSIBILITY

WHEN A CASE IS REFERRED BY FRAUD AND RECOVERY, THE DCFS BUREAU OF APPEALS MUST:

● REVIEW AND PREPARE THE DEPARTMENT’S CASE.

A FAIR HEARING AND AN ADMINISTRATIVE DISQUALIFICATION HEARING MAY BE COMBINED INTO A SINGLE HEARING IF THE FACTUAL ISSUE ARISE OUT OF THE SAME OR RELATED CIRCUMSTANCES AND THE HOUSEHOLD RECEIVES PRIOR NOTICE THAT THEY WILL BE COMBINED.

IF THE HEARINGS ARE COMBINED FOR THE PURPOSE OF SETTLING THE AMOUNT OF THE CLAIM AT THE SAME TIME AS DETERMINING WHETHER AN IPV OCCURRED, THE HOUSEHOLD MAY NOT SUBSEQUENTLY APPEAL THE AMOUNT OF THE CLAIM.

● SEND NOTICE TO THE HOUSEHOLD THAT THE APPEAL REQUEST HAS BEEN DENIED WITH A COPY OF THE SUMMARY OF EVIDENCE AND COPY OF ALL DOCUMENTS REFERENCED.

● SEND ADVANCE NOTICE OF THE HEARING TO THE HOUSEHOLD BY EITHER FIRST- CLASS MAIL OR CERTIFIED MAIL-RETURN RECEIPT REQUESTED AT LEAST 30 DAYS PRIOR TO THE DATE OF THE HEARING WITH A COPY OF THE SUMMARY OF EVIDENCE AND A COPY OF ALL DOCUMENTS REFERENCED.

5 of 5 ● SEND THE DOCUMENT PACKET TO THE DIVISION OF ADMINISTRATIVE LAW, WHO WILL CONDUCT THE HEARING, ARRIVE AT A DECISION, AND NOTIFY THE HOUSEHOLD AND THE DCFS BUREAU OF APPEALS.

Note: Division of Administrative Law will recommend a decision for FITAP/KCSP cases and DCFS will issue the final decision.

● RESCHEDULE THE HEARING WITH THE DIVISION OF ADMINISTRATIVE LAW ON BEHALF OF THE CLIENT IF REQUESTED.

● SUBMIT A NEW APPEAL REQUEST TO THE DIVISION OF ADMINISTRATIVE LAW ON BEHALF OF THE CLIENT IF REQUESTED.

● WITHIN 80 DAYS OF THE DATE THE HOUSEHOLD MEMBER IS NOTIFIED IN WRITING THAT A HEARING HAS BEEN SCHEDULED, THE DCFS BUREAU OF APPEALS MUST NOTIFY FRAUD AND RECOVERY OF THE DECISION.

NOTE: A PENDING ADMINISTRATIVE DISQUALIFICATION HEARING FOR IPV DOES NOT AFFECT THE PERSON'S OR THE HOUSEHOLD'S RIGHT TO BE CERTIFIED AND PARTICIPATE IN THE PROGRAM.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

OFS 20CD Form / Instructions Report of Claim Determination OFS 40 Form / Instructions Fraud Investigation Referral FR-015A Form / Instructions Intentional Program Violation Disqualification Notice

IV. REFERENCES

TANF-ACF-PI-2006-03 (Collecting and Repaying Overpayments Made to Families under the Aid to Families with Dependent Children (AFDC) Program and the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) Program) (Replaces TANF-ACF-PI-2000-2) E-510 Disqualification Process Responsibilities/ Procedures

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name F – Case Maintenance Section No./Name F-300-FITAP-SNAP Intentional Program Violations Document No./Name F-350-SNAP Electronic Disqualified Recipient System (eDRS) Effective Date March 15, 2022

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

F-351-SNAP - PO eDRS

The Electronic Disqualified Recipient System (eDRS) is a nationwide database of individuals who have been disqualified from SNAP participation due to an Intentional Program Violation (IPV). The eDRS database is composed of data supplied by State agencies and is maintained by the Food and Nutrition Service (FNS). If an individual is disqualified in one State because of an IPV determination, the individual is disqualified in every State. Disqualification penalties are cumulative. When a State determines that an individual is guilty of an IPV, the information is entered into eDRS. In Louisiana, Fraud and Recovery Unit staff enters the IPV disqualification into eDRS. FNS requires that all State agencies use eDRS data to screen all adult (age 18 or older) SNAP applicants prior to initial certification of benefits to ensure applicants are not currently disqualified from program participation and to match all new adult household members to eDRS data before the member is added to the household’s case.

F-352-SNAP - PO eDRS IN CLEARANCE SUMMARY (CS)

eDRS data is included in the CS at application, redetermination, and Simplified Report (SR). The * eDRS icon is used to complete the eDRS clearance for new household members not already included in the CS. When an adult household member is not included in the CS, an on demand search must be completed. The on demand eDRS clearance will be completed using the eDRS icon which is available in data collection of a LITE work item.

F-353-SNAP - PO VERIFY eDRS DATA

The Computer Matching and Privacy Protection Act of 1988 requires that the State agency may not take any adverse action to terminate, deny, or reduce benefits for an applicant or recipient based on the information produced by a Federal computer matching program unless the information has been independently verified by the State agency. Therefore, if there is an eDRS hit for any adult SNAP household member, staff must verify the hit with staff in the State where the disqualification originated. The contact information for staff to verify the disqualification will be displayed in the eDRS clearance results. The disqualification verification may be a verbal or written statement from the disqualifying State agency attesting to the existence of documentation. Document the name of the contact person from the disqualifying State and the discussion of the disqualification as a detailed case note. The disqualifying State should provide information regarding the disqualification, including if an Administrative Disqualification Hearing (ADH) was conducted, if the household waived the ADH, if the court made the determination, or if the household signed an agreement in lieu of prosecution. This information is needed to be able to enter the correct disqualification information on LITE. ** Written verification must be saved into OnBase.

2 of 4 F-354-SNAP - PO IPV DISQUALIFICATION

Only Fraud and Recovery Staff are authorized to enter IPV sanctions on members in * LITE.

The individual is ineligible to participate in SNAP for a set period of time based on past IPV disqualifications and the reason for the disqualification. Remaining eligible household members are not affected by the IPV disqualification.

In any case where the verification is not received from the disqualifying State contacted in time to process the case, including expedited and regular applications, staff should process the application/case without the verification, if otherwise eligible. If the State subsequently receives independent verification that the client or household member is ineligible, staff must review the information and immediately disqualify the ineligible members allowing advance notice. A claim must be established to collect any benefits that were issued in error.

The information must be reviewed and immediately entered into LITE and the appropriate notice sent.

An eDRS hit does not prevent the SR from being considered complete. Therefore, if the household submits a complete SR, process the SR. The IPV disqualification must be entered on LITE allowing advance notice.

An eDRS hit does not prevent the redetermination from being extended, if otherwise eligible. The redetermination must be completed and the IPV disqualification must be entered in LITE allowing advance notice.

When an SR or redetermination is completed, the IPV disqualification must be entered the following workday so that LITE will send out the automated notice of decision regarding the SR or the redetermination and will also send out the notice regarding the IPV disqualification. When a case is dispositioned more than once on the same day, LITE will cancel the first notice that is sent. Households must be sent a notice regarding all case actions completed.

When an eDRS hit is discovered on a certified case and the IPV disqualification was not already imposed on the case on LITE, a claim must be established to recover ineligible benefits outlined in Chapter 4, Section F-100.

If there is an IPV disqualification already imposed in LITE and there is an eDRS hit found and Louisiana is the imposing state, determine if the hit and the disqualification penalty on LITE match. If they do, no further action is necessary. If they do not match, contact Fraud and Recovery to discuss the mismatch.

If there is an IPV disqualification already imposed in LITE and there is an eDRS hit found and the disqualification was determined by another State, determine if the hit and the disqualification penalty in LITE ** match. If they do, no further action is necessary. If they do not match, update the disqualification based on the verification obtained from the disqualifying state.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name J – Charts Section No./Name J-300-SNAP SNAP Income Eligibility Chart Document No./Name J-300-SNAP Income Eligibility Chart Effective Date October 1, 2025

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

SNAP eligibility is limited to households whose incomes are determined to meet the income limits in the Income Eligibility Chart. Households having at least one member who is 60 years of age or older, or receives SSI, or Social Security Disability, or Veteran's (rated or paid as total) Disability payments are only required to meet the Maximum Net Monthly Income Eligibility Standard. All other households are required to meet the Maximum Gross and Maximum Net Monthly Income Standards. Broad- Based-Categorically Eligible (BBCE) households are required to meet the Maximum Gross Monthly Income Standard of 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) instead of 130% of the FPL.

The SNAP Income Eligibility Chart is as follows:

HH Size Maximum Gross Maximum Gross Maximum Net Monthly Income Maximum Monthly Income Eligibility Standard 130% of Poverty Monthly Income Eligibility Standard 200% of Poverty Monthly Income Eligibility Standard 100% of Poverty Elderly Disabled Separate Household 165% of Poverty SNAP Allotment 1 $1696 $2609 $1305 $2152 $298 2 $2292 $3525 $1763 $2909 $546 3 $2888 $4442 $2221 $3665 $785 4 $3483 $5359 $2680 $4421 $994 5 $4079 $6275 $3138 $5177 $1183 6 $4675 $7192 $3596 $5934 $1421 7 $5271 $8109 $4055 $6690 $1571 8 $5867 $9025 $4513 $7446 $1789 9 $6463 $9942 $4972 $8203 $2007 10 $7059 $10859 $5431 $8960 $2225 11 $7655 $11775 $5890 $9717 $2443 12 $8251 $12692 $6349 $10474 $2661 13 $8847 $13609 $6808 $11231 $2879 14 $9443 $14525 $7267 $11988 $3097 15 $10039 $15442 $7726 $12745 $3315 Each additional member +$596 +$917 +$459 +$757 $218

A household may have gross and net income which does not exceed the gross and net income limits, but the net income may result in a zero SNAP allotment. These households are not eligible for benefits.

A one and two-person traditional categorically eligible household and a BBCE household that is over the net income limit is eligible to receive the minimum SNAP allotment.

Dependent Children: 18 year old child(ren) who fail to participate are excluded from the grant until they participate. Dependent Children: Use excl. code/reason 02/17 (Parenting Skills exclusion) to remove the child for failure to participate.

Dependent Children: Apply FTC policy. If the FITAP grant remains open, FTC income equals the difference between the grant with the child included and the grant after the child has been excluded. Budget the FTC income as long as the child is excluded from the FITAP grant due to failure to comply with drug testing. If the FITAP case closed as a result of the child’s exclusion, the FTC income equals the amount of the FITAP grant prior to closure. Budget FTC income for one month only if the FITAP case is closed due to the child’s exclusion.

FITAP Not Work Eligible: If the recipient fails to participate in the drug screening, testing, education, treatment, and rehabilitation program close the case for at least one month or until compliance, whichever is later.

If the applicant fails to participate, reject the application. FITAP Not Work Eligible: Enter disposition reason 06, closure code 87.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 - Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name M - Kinship Care Subsidy Program Section No./Name M-100-KCSP Kinship Care Subsidy Program Document No./Name M-110-KCSP Introduction Effective Date January 6, 2022

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The Kinship Care Subsidy Program (KCSP) provides cash assistance for eligible children who reside with qualified relatives other than parents.

A child may meet the eligibility requirements for both FITAP and KCSP but may only receive assistance in one of these programs for a given month. Although a client may specify the program for which the client is applying (FITAP or KCSP), a request for either is considered a request for any cash assistance for which the family may be eligible. It is the worker’s responsibility to determine eligibility and benefit level for both programs. If the client is eligible for both programs, an explanation of the benefits and requirements in each program must be given to the client.

When a child is determined eligible in both programs, the client must choose the program through which she wishes to receive assistance. The case * notes must be documented to reflect this choice. A qualified relative may receive both FITAP and KCSP at the same time, but only for different children. A child may not be included in both a FITAP and a KCSP assistance unit for the same month.

M-111-KCSP - PO ASSISTANCE UNIT

The child who receives SSI or foster care payments is not eligible for KCSP benefits.

The assistance unit shall include all children in the home for whom the qualified relative receives KCSP. The children are not required to be related to each other. Additionally, there is no requirement that all related children and siblings must be included in the KCSP certification.

M-111-1-KCSP PO KCSP-Eligible Child Included in FITAP Certification

If a KCSP-eligible child is included in a FITAP certification, remove the child from the FITAP certification prior to KCSP certification. Advance Notice of Decision to reduce or terminate FITAP benefits is not required if the KCSP grant plus the reduced FITAP grant, if any, will exceed the former FITAP grant amount. In these situations, a concurrent Notice should be sent to the household and the KCSP certification must be effective the month following the last month the child receives FITAP benefits.

If the KCSP qualified relative is also the payee for a FITAP grant, a separate assistance unit is required for KCSP. In these situations, the qualified relative payee will have a Primary Grant for FITAP and a Multiple Grant for KCSP. **

II. PROCEDURES

KCSP Eligibility Ends

If the child is determined eligible for FITAP benefits, certify the FITAP grant or add the child to an existing FITAP grant effective the month following the last month of receipt of KCSP benefits.

The amount of the KCSP subsidy payment is $450 ** per eligible child per month.

1 of 8 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

M-211-KCSP – PO QUALIFIED RELATIVE REQUIREMENTS

The child must live in the home of one of the following qualified relatives (either biological or adoptive):

• grandfather or grandmother (extends to great-great-great)

• brother or sister (including half brother and half sister)

• uncle or aunt (extends to great-great)

• first cousin, including first cousin once removed (child of a first cousin)

• nephew or niece (extends to great-great)

• stepbrother or stepsister

The legal spouse of the above listed relatives even after the marriage is terminated by death or divorce meets the criteria as a qualified relative.

M-212-KCSP - PO ELIGIBLE CHILD REQUIREMENTS

Eligibility requirements for the child receiving KCSP are similar to the FITAP requirements. FITAP policies, procedures, and forms apply in KCSP unless stated otherwise.

M-213-KCSP - PO CHANGES REPORTED/ MATCHES FROM OTHER ENTITIES

Louisiana Department of Health (LDH), Louisiana Vital Records Division will submit a daily file that identifies deceased individuals matching a member of a pending or active Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and associated Kinship Care Subsidy Program (KCSP) household.

II. PROCEDURES

Even though the qualified relative is not included in the KCSP assistance unit, the qualified relative must meet the following requirements.

• Possess or obtain within one year of certification: custody, guardianship, or provisional custody by mandate of the eligible child(ren) who is living in the home.

Legal custody may be custody awarded by the court or provisional custody by mandate of eligible children living in the home.

2 of 8 Provisional custody by mandate is a notarized authorization made by the child’s custodial parent(s) or by the grandparent(s) who has been awarded legal custody, to a person of legal age to provide for the care, custody, and control of a minor child. Certain requirements must be met for the execution of the provisional custody by mandate document. Refer to section M-211-1.

Custody, guardianship, and provisional custody by mandate must be verified through court records or other reliable documents such as the form, KCSP 4K.

Note: If custody, guardianship, or provisional custody by mandate is not obtained within one year of initial certification, the child is no longer eligible for KCSP benefits. The year begins with the initial month of certification and continues for 11 months thereafter, regardless of program or custody status. (For example: A household certified in May 2026 may be determined eligible for May 2026 thru April 2027. But, the household must obtain court-ordered custody or provisional custody by mandate for all subsequent months of eligibility after April 2027.)

LITE will send a Case Action Task: No Custody by the 10th month after the child has received the KCSP without provisional custody by mandate or legal custody.

• Have an annual family income of less than 150% of the federal poverty threshold, in accordance with the size of the qualified relative’s family.

• Have neither of the eligible child’s parents residing in the applicant’s household.

• Assign to the state any rights to child support from any other person and cooperate with CSE in obtaining child support for the child unless good cause is established.

• Receive no SSI or foster care payments for the child(ren) for which they are applying for KCSP.

Verifying and Documenting Relationship

The LITE Relationship – Details screen allows the user to document the relationships of each household member to each other. Select an appropriate option from the Relationship Type is drop- down list to document the relationship of each child to the caretaker relative. All Qualified Relatives and some Non-Qualified Relatives are included in the drop-down. Select Other Related if the degree of relationship is not available in the drop-down.

After completing all relationship details for individuals living in the home based on the client’s statement during the interview, click Family Tree to capture additional relationship details. The Relationship – Establishing Family Tree pop-up screen displays. The worker will use the Relationship – Establishing Family Tree popup screen as a tool to help establish relationship, document relationship details for each child, and request relationship verification.

3 of 8 Select an appropriate option from the Relationship Verification drop-down list. Relationship Verification is mandatory for KCSP cases.

To request verification of Relationship, the user must select either Pending Verification or Client Statement (which is invalid for KCSP) on the Relationship – Details screen for those relationships that have not been verified. The names of relatives entered in Person 1 and Person 2 will populate on the Request for Verification if Pending Verification or Client Statement is selected in the Verification column for that row of the Family Tree.

Click Save after selecting the type of relationship and type of verification on the Relationship – Details screen.

Once the verification is received, the user must return to the Relationship – Details screen and the Relationship – Establishing Family Tree pop-up screen and select the appropriate type of verification that was provided by the client. Enter the number of the document in the Document Type/Number column. The Document Type/Number field only accepts numbers.

For example:

• If a birth certificate is received, the user must select Birth Certificate/Baptismal Certificate on the Relationship – Details screen and the Relationship – Establishing Family Tree pop-up screen, and enter the birth certificate number in the Document Type/Number column.

• If a court document is received, the user must select Court Records on the Relationship – Details screen and the Relationship – Establishing Family Tree pop-up screen, and enter the court docket number in the Document Type/Number column.

Refer to the Relationship and Verification for FITAP and KCSP Quick Reference Guide for additional guidance.

M-211-1-KCSP - PR Provisional Custody by Mandate

The conferring of provisional custody by mandate is made by the parent(s) who has custody of the child at the time custody is granted to the qualified relative(s). In order to establish which parent(s) has custody it must first be determined if there is a current custody court order or if the parents were legally married at the time of the child’s birth. Obtain verification of current custody order and/or legal marriage. The father’s name on the child’s birth certificate does not establish custody, as it does not verify marriage of the parents. If the parents were legally married at the time of birth, both parents must grant provisional custody by mandate to the qualified relative(s), unless the court has granted sole custody to one parent. Only the parent(s) with legal custody can grant provisional custody by mandate to a person of legal age. A minor parent cannot confer provisional custody by mandate unless the minor has been emancipated.

The conferring of provisional custody by mandate can also be made by the grandparent(s) who has been awarded custody of the child, at the time custody is granted to the qualified relative(s) of legal age. The grandparent(s) awarded custody may not confer provisional custody by mandate to a parent or other person previously denied custody by court order. Obtain verification of current custody order.

The KCSP 4K correspondence in LITE includes a cover letter to the qualified relative, a form sample with instructions, and a blank KCSP 4K form for each child meeting one of the conditions.

The client must completes the form in the presence of a notary. Receipt of the notarized copy of the KCSP 4K must be documented in case notes and the document saved in OnBase. LITE must be updated to reflect the date the document was executed and the date document expires.

M-211-2-KCSP - PR Interim Termination of Provisional Custody by Mandate

The parent(s) or grandparent(s) who had custody of the child at the time Provisional Custody by Mandate was granted to the qualified relative may revoke the Provisional Custody by Mandate at any time by written statement. The statement should include appropriate dates along with the name of the child(ren), the name of the parent(s) or grandparent(s), and the name of the person who was granted Provisional Custody by Mandate. The statement should be signed by the parent(s) or grandparent(s), and notarized.

8 of 8 M-213-KCSP - PR CHANGES REPORTED/MATCHES FROM OTHER ENTITIES

When a KCSP member of an associated SNAP case is identified as deceased, a LITE task is created and assigned to the case owner’s dashboard for review. If the automatic disposition fails, action must be taken in LITE within two business days depending on the household composition.

• If the KCSP qualified relative (payee of the grant) is reported as deceased, the KCSP grant shall be closed. Reason for closure will be Head of Household is deceased. Confirm that an automated concurrent Notice of Decision (OFS 16) is sent. Case notes should be well documented.

• If the only KCSP-eligible child is reported as deceased, the KCSP case must be updated to include the child’s date of death. Running EDBC and authorizing will close the KCSP grant due to no eligible child in the household. Confirm that an automated concurrent Notice of Decision (OFS 16) is sent. Case notes should be well documented.

• If multiple KCSP eligible children are reported as deceased, each identified member’s date of death must be added to the case. Running EDBC and authorizing will exclude the identified members. Confirm that an automated advance notice of adverse action, Notice of Decision (OFS 16), is sent if the household is determined to be ineligible or there is a decrease in benefits. Case notes should be well documented.

Note: For KCSP households receiving SNAP, these households must also comply with requirements and take action in accordance with change processing procedures as defined in C-820 FITAP/SNAP.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability Part No./Name M – Kinship Care Subsidy Program Section No./Name M-300 KCSP Kinship Care Financial Eligibility Requirements Document No./Name M-310 KCSP Financial Eligibility Effective Date January 6, 2022

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

In determining financial eligibility for KCSP, the child must first meet the Child’s Income Test. If the child passes this test, a determination must then be made on the child’s eligibility considering the family income.

*** * These tests are automatically applied in the LITE system ** at application, redetermination and when a change in income or household composition occurs.

M-311-KCSP - PO CHILD’S INCOME TEST

In determining the child’s eligibility for KCSP, consider only the child’s income. If the income is less than * $450, the requirement is met.

M-312-KCSP - PO FAMILY INCOME TEST

To qualify for payment through the KCSP program, the family’s annual income must be less than 150% of the federal poverty threshold, in accordance with the size of the family applying for the subsidy. The federal poverty guidelines are updated annually. (Refer to document M-410-KCSP)

II. PROCEDURES

M-312-KCSP - PR FAMILY INCOME TEST

For KCSP, the caretaker relative’s family is defined to include:

● the eligible child, ● the qualified relative, ● the legal spouse of the qualified relative, ● the minor children of the qualified relative, and ● anyone else residing in the home for whom the qualified relative claims financial responsibility.

NOTE: On the LITE Relationship – Details screen, include all family members defined above. In the KCSP Relationship Information section, state whether the caretaker relative is financially responsible for each member.

Who Is Not Included in the Filing Unit

For KCSP, the caretaker relative’s Family Size does not include a family member who is a:

 SSI recipient. **

1 of 1 I. * STATEMENT OF POLICY

It is the responsibility of all DCFS ** staff to report *** known or suspected instances of abuse and neglect of a child receiving FITAP. Instances of abuse and neglect include situations where a child experiences:

● physical or mental injury, ● sexual abuse or exploitation, or ● negligent treatment or maltreatment

under circumstances which indicate that the child's health or welfare is threatened.

II. * PROCEDURES

DCFS staff members must report instances of child abuse or neglect as described above by calling the Child Abuse/Neglect Hotline at 1-855-4LA-KIDS (1-855-452-5437). Once the report is submitted, the staff member should ask the intake person on the hotline for the Intake Number.

Document Case Notes to indicate a telephone report was made to the Child Abuse/Neglect Hotline and include the Intake Number.

Ch.C. Acts 1991, No. 235, §1, eff. Jan. 1, 1992.

The STEP program uses a case management approach to ensure that clients receive the necessary services and guidance to become self-sufficient while ensuring client accountability and responsibility.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P 100-STEP Introduction Document No./Name P-120-STEP Purpose and Objectives Effective Date October 01, 2008

1 of 1 The purpose of the Strategies to Empower People Program (STEP) is to provide opportunities for work-eligible recipients of FITAP to receive job preparation, work and supportive services to enable them to leave the program and become self-sufficient.

To accomplish this STEP will:

● Encourage, assist and require work-eligible recipients of FITAP to fulfill their responsibilities to support their children by preparing for, accepting and retaining employment. ● Provide individuals with the opportunity to acquire the skills necessary to qualify for employment. ● Provide the necessary supportive services, including *** child care and medical assistance, so that individuals can participate and accept employment. ● Promote coordination of services at all levels of government and in the business community in order to make a wide range of services available and to maximize the use of existing resources. ● Emphasize accountability for both participants and service providers.

P-211-STEP - PO ORGANIZATION OF THE STEP PROGRAM

The STEP program is designed so persons applying for services will have a similar experience when seeking those services at any Economic Stability (ES) office throughout the state.

P-212-STEP - PO INTAKE WORKFLOW

Work-eligible FITAP applicants enter the STEP program after they are certified for FITAP cash assistance.

P-213-STEP - PO STAFF DUTIES

The duties specific of the Intake Worker, the Case Maintenance Worker, and the STEP Case Management Worker are defined below.

Intake

The Intake Worker shall follow departmental procedures during the intake process while processing applications for SNAP, FITAP, and KCSP.

Case Maintenance

The Case Maintenance Worker shall follow departmental procedures during ongoing eligibility-related activities for SNAP, FITAP, and KCSP.

STEP Case Management

The STEP Coach, also known in LITE as the STEP Case Manager, shall follow departmental procedures during ongoing STEP case management.

P-211-STEP- PR ORGANIZATION OF THE STEP PROGRAM

2 of 4 P-213-STEP - PR STAFF DUTIES

Depending on the office size and organization of staff, some of these duties may overlap.

Intake

The Intake Worker is responsible for determining eligibility for FITAP and any associated KCSP and SNAP benefits.

During the intake process the applicant shall:

● be interviewed for FITAP, KCSP, and/or SNAP benefits. ● complete the Needs Assessment, ● discuss additional services/referrals needed, ● be given the form, STEP 2, Responsibilities of Mandatory Work-Eligible Recipients of Cash Assistance Programs – STEP Participation Requirements, ● be given the form, OFS DD1 IS, Direct Deposit/SVC Informational Sheet, ● discuss and arrange supportive services needed to participate in work activities, and ● continue to participate in an approved activity, if self-initiated.

The Intake Worker should explain the general components of FITAP, STEP, and other programs for which they may be eligible. Once the Needs Assessment has been completed and the client indicates which program he would like to apply for, the Intake Worker obtains eligibility information and performs all eligibility-related activities.

The Intake Worker must explain clearly to the work-eligible applicant that participation in the STEP program is a requirement to receive FITAP benefits. It is important that the applicant understands that he must participate in an approved employment or training activity for continued eligibility for FITAP and know that he has the option to choose STEP Supportive Service payments through Direct Deposit or Stored Value Card. At certification, the STEP 2 and OFS DD1 IS will be system generated and mailed to the client.

The Intake Worker should clearly explain that the goal of assistance is to help the applicant to become employed and to transition off of benefits within his 24-month time limit. After certification of FITAP benefits, the client will be referred to a STEP Case Manager located in the client’s parish or region.

The Intake Worker will manually refer the applicant to the STEP program during the application period if the client needs to cure a STEP sanction. Work-eligible FITAP applicants will be automatically referred to the STEP program upon certification.

3 of 4

Case Maintenance

The FITAP Case Maintenance Worker will perform ongoing eligibility-related activities for STEP and all associated programs. This includes processing redeterminations, SRs, and interim changes. The Case Maintenance Worker will coordinate with the STEP Coach to also process STEP Sanction Requests, Work Registration code changes, budgeting of earned income, approval or denial of time limit extensions, and establish incapacity determinations for clients who report a disability, incapacity, or an exemption if they are needed to care for a family member who is disabled or incapacitated.

STEP Case Management

The STEP Coach is responsible for ongoing case management for families who are striving toward becoming employed and moving toward self-sufficiency. This includes but is not limited to the following:

● Coaching the client to motivate and prepare them for educational and work activities, such as, but not limited to: defining their educational and work goals, learning how to overcome personal barriers, developing resumes and completing job applications, improving interpersonal skills, learning work ethics, identifying client interests that will lead to choosing an appropriate career/job, learning interview skills, identifying workplace supports and/or educating a client with disabilities to ask for reasonable accommodations on the job; ● Identifying appropriate Community Based Organizations and local businesses to provide work activities for clients. The Coach will assess the work force needs of the Community Based Organization and/or business and provide services and coaching that will enhance these skills in clients. Coaches will also continually assess Community Based Organizations and local businesses to assure work force needs have not changed and to ensure clients are properly matched in work activities; ● Working with applicants who need to cure a STEP sanction; ● Completing the Family Assessment ***; ● Completing the Family Success Agreement on certified FITAP families; ● Contacting the client to monitor progress; ● Following up with providers and employers; ● Arranging supportive services, including child care and transportation; ● Obtaining the client’s preferred payment option and either enrolling the client in the SVC process or entering their Direct Deposit information in the system; ● Authorizing payment for all supportive services; ● Being knowledgeable about local or community resources, including educational and employment opportunities; ● Updating the Family Success Agreement; ● Ongoing assessment, follow-up, and problem resolution; ● Providing referrals to help meet the client’s needs; ● Identifying innovative service solutions;

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People Program (STEP) Section No./Name P-200-STEP Administration Document No./Name P-220-STEP Tax Credits Effective Date July 1, 2021

1 of 6 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Tax credits for hiring clients who qualify can be used as an incentive for employers. For participants who find employment, tax credits can ease the transition from welfare-to-work.

P-221-STEP PO EMPLOYER TAX CREDITS

P-221-1 - PO Work Opportunity Tax Credit

The Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC) is one tool in a diverse toolbox of flexible strategies designed to help move people into gainful employment and obtain on-the-job experience. It joins other tax credits, education, and workforce training and development programs that help American workers with * barriers to ** employment prepare for good jobs; *** * ease ** their transition from job to job; benefit from the creation of effective regional economic development strategies; and create high performance workplaces.

The new employee must belong to one of the nine target groups listed below:

A. IV-A (TANF) Recipient

A member of a family that is receiving or recently received Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF), or benefits under a successor program for any 9 months during the 18-month period ending on the hire date.

B. Veteran

A veteran who is a member of a family that is receiving or recently received SNAP benefits (formerly known as Food Stamps) for at least a 3-month period during the past 15 months; and for individuals who begin to work for an employer after May 25, 2007, the veteran group is expanded to include "disabled veterans" who are entitled to compensation for a service-connected disability and who, during the one-year ending on the hiring date, were: a) discharged or released from active duty in the U.S Armed Forces, or b) unemployed for a period or periods totaling at least 6 months.

C. Ex-Felon

An ex-felon is an individual who has been convicted of a felony under any statute of the United States or any state; and has a hire date which is not more than one year after the last date on which the applicant was so convicted or was released from prison or is a convicted felon who is participating in a pre-release program.

D. Empowerment Zone/Enterprise Community/Rural Renewal County (EZ/EC/RRC)

An 18-39 year old resident of one of the federally designated Empowerment Zone (EZ), Enterprise Communities (EC) or Rural Renewal County (RRC) or Rural Renewal Empowerment Zone.

2 of 6

E. Vocational Rehabilitation Referral

Applicant * has ** a physical or mental disability which results in a substantial handicap to employment; and was referred to the employer upon completion of, or while receiving, rehabilitative services pursuant to an individualized written plan of employment (IWPE) under a state plan for vocational rehabilitation services approved under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (as amended, 1998), a vocational rehabilitation program for veterans or an employment network under the Ticket to Work program. Proof of participation in any of these programs is required.

F. Supplemental Nutritional Assistance Program (SNAP) Recipient

A member of a family that is receiving or recently received Supplemental Nutritional Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits (formerly known as Food Stamps), and is at least 18, but not yet 40 years old, on the hire date, Individual is a member of a family receiving assistance under a food stamp program for the 6-month period ending on the hire date; or receiving such assistance for at least 3 months of the 5-month period ending on the hire date.

G. Supplemental Security Income (SSI) Recipient

An individual receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits for any month ending within the 60-day period ending on the hire date.

H. Long-Term Family Assistance Recipient

An individual who is a member of a family that received Temporary Assistance to Needy Families (TANF) or benefits under a successor program for at least 18 consecutive months ending on the hire date or has received family assistance for a total of at least 18 months (whether or not consecutive) beginning after August 5, 1997 and has a hire date that is not more than two (2) years after the end of the earliest 18-month period or whose TANF eligibility expired under a federal or state law after August 5, 1997, and who was hired within two years after their eligibility expired.

The Louisiana Enterprise Zone Program, * or EZ program ** is a jobs incentive program that provides Louisiana income and franchise tax credits to a new or existing business located in Louisiana creating permanent net new full-time jobs, and hiring at least 50% of those net new jobs from one of four targeted groups. The benefit provides:

● Either a one-time $3,500 or $1,000 *** tax credit for each net new job created, and

● A rebate of state sales and use taxes paid on qualifying materials, machinery, furniture, and/or equipment purchased or a 1.5% refundable investment tax credit on the total capital investment, excluding tax exempted items. The rebate shall not exceed $100,000 per net new job.

This incentive program is open to any Louisiana * businesses (new or existing) ** *** that will:

Create a minimum of five permanent net new full-time jobs within 24 months of their project start date or increase their current nationwide workforce by 10% within the first 12 months.

● Residents: someone living in ** Enterprise Zone within the state.

● People receiving an approved form of public assistance.

● People lacking basic skills. *** A person performing below a ninth grade proficiency in reading, writing, or mathematics.

● People unemployable by traditional standards.

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The parent or other caretaker relative who is included in the assistance unit must participate in the STEP program unless he/she meets an exemption or has been granted good cause.

They will be given the form STEP 2, Responsibilities of Mandatory Work-Eligible Recipients of Cash Assistance Programs – STEP Participation Requirements, * and the OFS DD1 IS, Direct Deposit/SVC Informational Sheet. If the applicant claims incapacity, a disability, or the need to provide care for a family member living in the home who is incapacitated or disabled, verification must be requested by the FITAP worker. The Family Assessment will be completed on all adult(s)/parent(s) included in the FITAP income unit prior to completion of the Family Success Agreement.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-300- STEP Case Management Process Document No./Name P-320-STEP Home Visits Effective Date August 15, 2022

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Home visiting programs are intended to support families in providing an atmosphere that promotes the healthy progression and development of the family. STEP’s objective is to target services to families and caregivers to improve outcomes, and promote a positive recipient-agency interaction.

Although home visiting programs differ in their approach, published documentation has acknowledged that populations served by a home visit display positive outcomes. High-quality home visiting programs provide family support services that reduce risks and increase beneficial results.

A home visit should have a purpose and desired outcome. STEP’s intent is to provide support to high- risk families with multiple challenges and levels of difficulty. Take this opportunity to listen and allow the participants to share their story.

Why is a home visit beneficial?

 Participants stay in their comfort zone. Meeting in an agency office can be intimidating and talking over the phone can be distancing and impersonal. By having a STEP Coach travel to a STEP’s recipient’s home, participants may be more likely to voice their concerns, speak candidly, and allow the STEP Coach into their lives.

 Closer partnerships, positive communication. Many times when a STEP Coach contacts a participant, it is regarding an issue with low participation. Home visits give participants and their STEP Coaches the opportunity to meet simply to talk and collaborate for the benefit of the participant and their family.

o In-person meetings break the “cycle of blame.” Especially with low-performing STEP recipients, participants and STEP Coaches can begin to blame each other for the failings of the family. Home visits help to put a human face to a name and turn finger pointing into teamwork and understanding.

 The STEP Coach learns more about their participant’s family. Research indicates that the biggest benefit of a home visit is to gain a better understanding of a recipient’s environment and how that environment might affect a STEP family.

 Participants realize they have a network of support. Participants take comfort in knowing that they have someone vested into the success of their family who understands their home situation.

 Participants are more likely to become involved. When participants are more familiar with their STEP Coach, they are more likely to become involved with STEP and more involved in their program activities and volunteering. In this way, a few well-placed home visits can facilitate positive outcomes for all invested in the family unit.

2 of 3 Show your dedication to their success. What message do you send when you show up at their door telling them that you noticed they were not at their assigned site? You are letting the participant know that you care enough to come to them and understand their challenges.

II. PROCEDURES

P-321-STEP - PR CONDUCTING A HOME VISIT

There are proactive steps that STEP Coaches can take to create a sense of structure, consistency, predictability, safety, and hope in their interactions with customers.

While services are delivered in the home of participating families within their ongoing daily routines and activities, safety and respect is at the forefront for all. It is possible that you will go into unfamiliar neighborhoods, entering homes in which not all family members welcome your visit, or entering into apartments or housing developments where you are not welcome. Home visits should occur with the consent of the participant and be scheduled with the appropriate notice.

Human service staff, by the very nature of their job duties, are often placed in the middle of highly volatile situations and therefore it is highly recommended that staff adhere to policy, 15. Safety and Loss Prevention Part No./Name 5. Office Safety Section No./Name 15-530 Threats to Staff or Agency.

P-322-STEP - PR INTERVIEWING TECHNIQUES

Tailor your questions to fit the type of information you need. Encourage STEP recipients’ participation by asking open-ended questions. Use the Goal 4It! Model and motivational interviewing to help the participant to understand their own ideas, interests, and solutions.

P-323-STEP - PR SUPERVISOR AWARENESS

Supervisor approval must be received in advance prior to traveling to conduct off-site visits.

It is recommended to travel in teams or pairs. Supervisors are to ensure there is a “buddy system” in place when at all possible; such as, another STEP Coach or non-traditional employee (i.e. intern).

Where pairing with a team member is not possible: The STEP Coach must discuss with their supervisor and/or manager the reason for the home visit. The discussion shall include a planned date and time. Upon approval, the STEP Coach will check-in with their supervisor before leaving, provide an anticipated return time and check-in again upon return.

Staff must create a plan for home visits and submit to their supervisor for approval prior to conducting a home visit. Home visit results must be documented in the record. The STEP 1 can be used for this purpose. The approved STEP 1 form is to be kept in a supervisor file for audit and tracking purposes.

Upon returning to the agency staff are to record the results of the visit in LITE on the Person Notes screen.

P-325-STEP - PR STAFF REPORTING RESPONSIBILITES

All DCFS staff are mandated reporters. Whenever child abuse/neglect is observed or suspected by DCFS staff within their assigned job responsibilities or staff becomes aware, whether working for the department or while off duty, it shall be immediately reported in accordance with policy reference, 4- 105 Legal Basis for Report and Investigation or Assessment. Refer to DSS Policy Manual, part 5, Legal; Section 6-04, Reporting Suspected Abuse, Neglect or Exploitation of Children if staff have cause to believe that a child’s physical, mental, or emotional health and safety are endangered as a result of abuse or neglect.

The following steps must be adhered to:

 Staff are to immediately report to the DCFS Centralized Intake Child Abuse Reporting Hotline any suspected child abuse/neglect

 Staff shall not screen the information prior to making the report nor conduct a preliminary investigation unless assigned to do so as a result of the intake process.  The reporting worker shall document the report information in any case record within his own caseload when the alleged victim is in his caseload. o Document the specifics of what they witnessed or learned from the participant or the outside party about the alleged abuse/neglect.  The worker shall advise his supervisor of the report.

1 of 5 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

* Family Assessment

A Family Assessment shall be completed with all work-eligible STEP participants in order to assist the STEP Coach in identifying strengths, challenges, interests, skills, prior work experience, and level of employability.

The Family Assessment provides a snapshot in time of what is going on with a participant, their family, and their individual circumstances. It’s used to gather information on what activities will be most helpful to the participant and aids in developing their Family Success Agreement (FSA) Rights and Responsibilities and Family Success Agreement (FSA) Goal Plan. **

***

Unless Good Cause is verified, failure to complete the Family Assessment will result in a STEP sanction. (Refer to P-500-STEP.)

* STEPping Stones to Success

The STEPping Stones to Success shall be used to help STEP Coaches facilitate first-time conversations and follow-up conversations with the participant, in relation to their motivation and readiness to participate. **

II. PROCEDURES

***

* Family Assessment

The Family Assessment is divided into various sections and topics to support a conversation between the STEP Coach and participants to determine the best engagement pathway.

The Family Assessment is designed to:

 allow the participant to indicate their values, goals, strengths, and potholes;  engage the participant;  develop a relationship with the participant;  learn about the family’s current needs and challenges;  guide conversations with families;  determine needed programs, services, and referrals; and  gather information to establish family goals and action plans.

2 of 5 It gives the STEP Coach the flexibility to select a starting topic when engaging the participant in a comprehensive discussion. The conversation must flow based on family needs and goals. The participant’s response is the starting point of the conversation. This format supports a fluid and meaningful conversation with the participant. The STEP Coach must: **

***  * use open-ended questions, where the participant has the opportunity to do most of the talking;  use active listening skills and focus on the participant’s interests, goals, strengths, and challenges; and  engage the participant in a conversation around goals, services, supports, and referrals.

Some examples include:

“I see you feel Frustrated about your current situation. Do you mind telling me more so that I can better understand?”

“I see you would feel successful if STEP helped you Develop healthy relationships. What relationships would you like to improve? Why is that important to you?”

“I see you have a personal goal To further your education. What type of education are you interested in?”

The following section includes topics that the STEP Coach should touch upon during the comprehensive discussion based upon the participant’s responses on the Family Assessment form:

Family Situation

When exploring the family’s current situation, the STEP Coach should consider what services, supports, or exemptions may be needed.

Employment & Work Experience

Based upon the participant’s response, the STEP Coach should explore the participant’s current employment circumstances and work history/experience.

Education & Training

Based upon the participant’s interest, the STEP Coach should explore education and training experience, along with related goals and interest in pursuing this as an engagement activity.

Financial Literacy

Financial literacy services and supports can provide families with the tools for a smoother transition from a benefit-based income to a wage-based income, and keep them from unknowingly entering into financially devastating credit arrangements. It is an essential element to a family achieving financial stability, self-sufficiency, and economic mobility.

Based upon the participant’s interest, the STEP Coach should make a referral to training available in the participant’s local community.

Family Violence

Based upon the participant’s response, the STEP Coach must use the LITE Domestic Violence Questionnaire to further explore any issues that the participant is willing to discuss. The Domestic Violence Questionnaire provides a mandatory script and questions to support screening participants for family violence.

The STEP Coach must provide referral information to the participant, when needed.

Domestic Violence help is available if services are needed:  Louisiana Statewide Hotline. Free. Confidential. 1.888.411.1333  National Domestic Violence Hotline 1.800.799.SAFE (7233)  Text “START” to 88788

Sexual Assault help is available if services are needed:  Louisiana Statewide Hotline: Speak to an Advocate at 1.888.995.7273  Text an Advocate 1.225.351.SAFE (7233)  National Hotline: 1.800.656.HOPE (4673)

Substance Abuse

If the participant discloses that they or a family member have a substance abuse addiction, the STEP Coach must explore whether a referral for a chemical dependency assessment and support is needed.

The FITAP/STEP Regional Consultant can help get the participant connected to services, if the STEP Coach and Supervisor needs assistance.

Emotional, Medical, and Health

Based upon the participant’s response, the STEP Coach must explore whether a referral to social or medical services is needed to professionally assess and support the family’s

5 of 5 STEPping Stones to Success

STEPping Stones to Success presents a broad view of the participant’s strengths and needs. Having a better sense of where participants are starting and the urgency of the challenges they face can help STEP Coaches identify and prioritize which services and opportunities participants may be encouraged to pursue. But Stepping Stones is more than that. It also gives participants a way to reflect on their current circumstances and inform the STEP Coach how motivated they are to take action and how prepared they feel they are to take action. **

1 of 8 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

P-351-STEP *** * PO TIME LIMITS

Each FITAP client is subject to time limited benefits per B-1700-FITAP when they are a parent, other caretaker relative, or the spouse of the parent or caretaker relative, AND they are included in the assistance unit.

A minor parent who receives benefits as a child is not subject to time limited benefits because they are a dependent child. A minor parent who is not a dependent child is subject to both the 24-month and 60-month time limit policy.

Refer to B-1720-FITAP regarding the 24-Month Time Limit requirements and to B-1730-FITAP regarding the 60-Month Time Limit requirements for additional information.

II. PROCEDURES

P-351-STEP - PR TIME LIMITS

Time Limit data can be found in the LITE Benefit Issuance module on the FITAP Time Clock tab. Below is an example of the FITAP Time Clock – Details screen in LITE that tracks time limit data.

During normal case management activities, the STEP Coach must:

 maintain awareness of the participant’s FITAP Time Clock, including their 24 Month Time Clock Counter (State) and 60 Month Time Clock Counter (Federal);  discuss their need for continuation of FITAP benefits to support them while they work on their goals;  ask questions about the family’s situation to determine if there are extenuating circumstances that might warrant an exemption or an extension; and

24 MONTH EXEMPTIONS

There are two types of exemptions that will stop the 24-month time limit clock from counting the month(s) of FITAP benefits for parents. These exemptions include: Incapacitated or Disabled, and $900 Earned Income Disregard. Note: There are no exemptions that stop the 60-month time limit clock from counting the month(s) of FITAP benefits.

Incapacitated or Disabled (STEP)

If the participant is a parent and reports a disability, continuous hospitalization, temporary incapacity, or total incapacity that prevents work activity for at least 30 days but no more than six months, the STEP Coach must request the FITAP Analyst to verify and establish Incapacity in accordance with C- 1510-FITAP.

Once the FITAP Analyst enters a verified disability record and authorizes the change, LITE will assign the value, Incapacitated or Disabled (STEP), for the 24 Month Exemption, and the participant’s receipt of FITAP benefits will not be counted towards the 24 Month Time Clock Counter State for the Benefit Month. The exemption will continue to populate for each Benefit Month as long as the verified disability record exists.

In the example below, the participant was a Parent (other than a Minor Unmarried Parent -MUP), qualified for a 24 Month Exemption based upon incapacity, and had ‘No’ populated for November and December 2022 for the 24 Month Time Clock Counter State. When calculating the number of benefit months, LITE will not count November or December towards the 24-month time limit.

When calculating the number of benefit months, LITE will not count October, November, or December towards the 24-month time limit.

P-351-1-STEP – PR TIME LIMIT EXTENSION REASONS

There are five types of extensions that may allow a STEP participant to continue receiving FITAP benefits beyond the 24-month and/or 60-month time limit. These extensions include:

 Hardship (T5),  Unfavorable Job Factors (T2),  Loss of Job/No Fault (T3),  Pending Appeal (T6), and  Maintain Compliance with FSA (T7).

Note: Maintain Compliance with FSA (T7) is only allowed for the 24-month time limit, and should be granted only when the participant does not qualify for any of the other extension reason types. Hardship (T5)

4 of 8

A hardship has occurred which affects the participant’s ability to obtain employment. These hardship extensions are limited to the period of time the condition or situation is expected to last.

Examples of such hardships include:

 when a parent/caretaker relative is under treatment for a serious addiction and work activity participation is not recommended by the treating organization, or  when adequate child care or transportation is not available, or  a temporary family crisis such as death of a family member, eviction, serious illness or accident has occurred, or  domestic violence situations, or  when a parent is required to provide full-time care to an incapacitated or disabled member of the household, or  incapacity of the parent or other caretaker relative for purposes of applying the 60-month limit.

Unfavorable Job Factors (T2)

Factors relating to job availability are determined to be unfavorable. This extension can be supported in the following ways:

 The STEP Coach’s evaluation of the participant’s education, training, literacy level, skills, and the availability of jobs for which the participant is qualified establishes that the participant is unemployable.  The STEP Coach determines that there are no employers in the commuting area of the participant who will accept applications for employment or will be hiring.

The commuting area is defined as the area around the participant’s home which can be reached within a two-hour round trip by public or private transportation.

Loss of Job/No Fault (T3)

The participant loses their job as a result of factors not related to their job performance.

Pending Appeal (T6)

The participant’s FITAP case remains eligible due to a Fair Hearing request pending a decision by the DCFS Bureau of Appeals.

Note: The STEP Coach and Supervisor must approve the time limit extension until an appeal decision is rendered.

P-351-2-STEP – PR INITIAL EXTENSION DECISIONS

Cases approaching the 24-month and 60-month time limits must be reviewed for consideration of an extension or case closure, including when an extension period is expiring and additional time is needed. When an extension period is expiring and additional time is not needed, an extension determination must be entered in the LITE system indicating a denial and the reason.

In the 22nd and 58th months of FITAP benefits, LITE will generate a Benefit Management task advising the STEP Coach to review the case for time limits. When the FITAP benefit reaches:

 the 22nd month, LITE will generate a Benefit Management task: 24 Month Clock Expire for the appropriate staff member to take action.  the 58th month, LITE will generate a Benefit Management task: Review 60 Month Clock task for the STEP Coach to take action.

The review is to include an assessment of good cause, exceptions, exemptions, or hardships. The STEP Coach will thoroughly document person notes regarding the approaching 24-month time limit with a clear rationale for recommendation of an extension if the client meets one of the extension reasons.

From Others on the main navigation bar select Benefit Issuance for the FITAP Extended Benefits Referral selection to populate. The extension determination is entered in the LITE FITAP Time Limit Decision – Details screen which is located through the FITAP Extended Benefits Referral – Summary screen.

On this screen, the STEP Coach will enter the CID of the member for whom the extension determination is needed then select the Add Extension button in order to reach the FITAP Time Limit Decision – Details screen.

P-351-3-STEP – PR SUBSEQUENT EXTENSION DECISIONS

Subsequent extensions may be completed in the month prior to the last month of an extension period, but no later than the 10th day of the last month of an extension period.

Example: Client has a current extension period of 10/2022 – 3/2023. The subsequent extension determination can be made beginning 2/2023 however no later than 3/10/2023.

At the end of an extension period, subsequent extensions will be determined as outlined in P-351-2- STEP.

There are no Benefit Management tasks associated with subsequent extensions. The Pentaho 24-60 Month Time Limit Tracking report will be used to determine those cases due for an upcoming subsequent extension.

Pentaho contains two reports that should be used to monitor time limits and exemptions.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-300-STEP Case Management Process Document No./Name P-380-Case Staffing Effective Date February 15, 2024

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Case staffing is an opportunity to exchange information about the participant and gain consultation from other professionals. It is a group process in which the STEP Coach, STEP Coach Supervisor, Consultant, and Managers help to identify the participant’s issues, suggest problem resolution strategies, and recommend service options.

What are the benefits of case staffing?

Case staffing provides an approach to identify concerns by bringing together a team to review cases, identify resolution strategies, and recommend solutions. It provides a good opportunity for creative problem solving and resource development.

II. PROCEDURES

The participant’s referral may need a case staffing at any point when it appears they are not making progress towards their goal or have not participated in work activities without good cause. A case staffing can also be done prior to entering a sanction and for participants who may need intensive case management services.

The goal of case staffing is to re-engage the participant into appropriate work activities.

The STEP coach will:

 Gather demographic information about the participant (names, ages of family members, and relationship of household members).

 Document circumstances of the case.

 Document the issues, strengths, concerns, and anticipated duration of issues or concerns. For example: Strengths may be having a high school diploma, stable housing, or reliable transportation. If possible, identify how strengths may help address any barriers such as how the participant’s education may be helpful in obtaining employment.

 Document past or present issues and how they were addressed.

 Document roles and responsibilities of those involved with the participant.

 Document those who attended the staffing.

The team will create a joint action plan with time-frames and expected outcomes.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-300-STEP Case Management Process Document No./Name P-390-STEP Family Success Agreement Effective Date February 15, 2024

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Upon determination of eligibility and after completion of the Family Assessment, work-eligible FITAP recipients shall *** * complete an individual responsibility plan, known as the Family Success Agreement, with the department.

The Family Success Agreement (FSA) is comprised of two parts: a rights and responsibilities agreement, and the mutually-developed goal plan between a STEP participant, on behalf of their family, and the department.

The FSA is the tool used to ensure that STEP participants are engaged in activities and making progress towards their career pathway, full potential, and/or financial independence.

The Agreement advises the participant of their rights and responsibilities, and the results of noncompliance. Additionally, the form requires the participant’s assurances and signature.

Completion of the Agreement is required only once, which occurs after the participant has completed their portion of the Family Assessment. Once the STEP Coach has engaged the participant using the Family Assessment, the participant is ready for goal setting using the FSA Goal Plan.

The FSA Goal Plan is a working document that requires the participant to set:  a long-term goal working towards a career pathway, their full potential, and/or financial independence,  short-term goal(s),  specific action step(s) to achieve their short-term goal(s),  a timeframe for achieving their short-term goal(s),  their definition of success related to achieving the short-term goal(s), and  the supportive services needed to achieve their short-term goal(s).

The FSA and FSA Goal Plan are to be completed in TuaPath.

The FSA Goal Plan may be updated as changes are needed. The initial FSA Goal Plan and all subsequent FSA goal plans will become part of the participant’s agreement.

STEP Coaches will use the agreement and the FSA Goal Plan as tools to:  Help the participant understand that participation in STEP work activities will help them realize their full potential.  Help the participant understand the long-term goal will lead to a career pathway, their full potential, and/or financial independence.  Use Goal4It! techniques to engage and support the participant.  Help the participant understand the short-term goal(s) helps them achieve the long-term goal.  Talk about the participant’s strengths, as determined in the Family Assessment, which can be built upon.

2 of 4  Document the action steps the participant has agreed to do. This is essential to holding the participant responsible for their participation.  Help the participant identify potholes that may disrupt participation and detours to overcome and get through a specific pothole.  Offer suggestions, if the client is open to suggestions, to keep the participant moving towards independence, by reminding those who are seeking a career pathway (who are not job-ready) that short-term goal(s) should eventually lead towards becoming job-ready.  Help disabled participants select short-term goal(s) and activities that will help them stabilize. Short-term goal(s) and work activities may look and feel very different for disabled participants based on their individual needs, but the long-term goal should set them on the path towards financial independence.  Document potholes and detours related to the participant’s goal.  Inform participants of the supports that are available to them.  Ask the participant to identify an accountability partner.  Help participants identify other support systems or resources such as family or friends and how they can be used to ensure success.  Inform participants when their TuaPath time sheets and supporting documents are due.

After an FSA Goal Plan has been signed, the STEP Coach must work with the participants to understand how their benefits will be impacted by their involvement in the goal plan and their engagement in activities that lead to work or self-sufficiency.

STEP Coaches will set the participant’s beginning participation level to meet them where they are. Once appropriate, based upon the participant’s increased education, skills and/or opportunities, the STEP Coach must set the expectation that hours of activities will add up to full-time participation (20- 30 hours per week). The STEP coach must work with the participant to identify the hours of activities that will add to full participation.

The STEP Coach must ensure the participant understands what constitutes job readiness and how it may impact their benefits if employment is not accepted. The STEP Coach must document in Person Notes once the participant’s achieves job-ready status. The participant must find and accept employment once they are job-ready.

STEP Coaches must also closely monitor the participant’s engagement in goal setting, activities, and progress. If the client’s failure to participate is related to required work activities, the STEP Coach should immediately begin a Review and Revise session when the participant is failing to participate as agreed upon, or failing to timely verify their participation hours, progress, or success.

Face to face contact is important to engage participants. STEP Coaches should meet in person for the FSA Goal Plan as often as possible. If a STEP Coach is authorized to travel and meets a client away from their normal work site for an FSA appointment, a manual FSA (STEP 6) may be completed if they do not have online access. The completed manual FSA (STEP 6) must be saved in OnBase and the FSA Goal Plan details must be entered online in TuaPath.
