Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-300-STEP Case Management Process Document No./Name P-390-STEP Family Success Agreement Effective Date February 15, 2024

3 of 4

STEP Coaches are required to document the client’s activities and progress in Person Notes. These notes should be timely entered. The purpose is to ensure participants are receiving opportunities to succeed in the program and proof that the STEP Coach is actively engaging the participant. Instances of good cause must be documented to explain why the participant is not participating.

Unless Good Cause is verified, failure to complete and sign the Family Success Agreement Rights and Responsibilities and/or FSA Goal Plan(s), without good cause, will result in ineligibility for the participant and a STEP sanction (Refer to P-500-STEP).

After an FSA Goal Plan has been signed, compliance in STEP will be measured by the participant’s progress towards achieving their self-sufficiency goals. (See P-500-STEP for additional details.)

If a participant leaves the program and reapplies a new Family Success Agreement Rights and Responsibilities and FSA Goal Plan shall be completed.

II. PROCEDURES

Upon certification, initiate contact with the family within one week to ensure completion of the FSA and FSA Goal Plan within 10 days of FITAP certification.

The FSA Rights and Responsibilities and FSA Goal Plan should be completed face-to-face, but can be completed by phone to avoid a hardship for the participant. Participants may log in and sign their FSA Rights and Responsibilities and FSA Goal Plan electronically. If a manual form is used, it must be mailed to the client for signature. Once the completed manual FSA (STEP 6) is received, it must be saved in OnBase and the FSA Goal Plan details must be entered online in TuaPath.

Key techniques to develop a mutually-developed FSA Goal Plan include:  Involve the participant. First, let the participant define the long-term goal of financial independence for the family. Offer the participant a clear picture of financial independence, if the participant is unsure. Discuss what STEP can do to support this goal.  Focus on the goal. Independence from cash assistance and STEP is often the goal for most families. Getting a job, increasing employment or wages, or establishing disability payments is often the pathway.  Avoid short-term goal(s) that are too large or too complex. Offer or encourage smaller short- term goal(s) that can be achieved quickly or easily, if the client is unsure. As the client achieves goal(s), their confidence will likely grow.  When goal setting, also take into consideration: o What are the participant’s interests? o What are the family’s circumstances? o What was discovered during the Family Assessment? o Are there short-term challenges (potholes) that need to be resolved? o What other types of supports will be available to help while the participant is taking the action steps?

Once the goal(s) and action steps are agreed upon, the participant or STEP Coach would enter these into the FSA Goal Plan using first person voice from the STEP participant’s perspective.

Link each activity or action step to a specific TuaPath Timesheet Activity type.

The FSA Goal Plan may need changes when the participant:  Has changes to the family's situation.  Has an unexpected change (like homelessness or family violence issues).  Achieves a goal or identifies a new goal or new pathway.  Is within two weeks of completing a component or goal (to keep them continually participating).  Gets a job.

Review and Revise sessions must be completed routinely as an ongoing process to measure the participant’s progress, areas of need, supportive services, referrals, etc. These sessions must be documented in Person Notes to track the participant’s process. The FSA Goal Plans may be revised, when needed.

Participants ** should take responsibility for arranging activities, services, and resources whenever possible. These include arranging for child care and transportation, registering for educational activities, and any other activities that lead to self-sufficiency.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-400-STEP Participation Document No./Name P-410-STEP Participation Requirements Effective Date January 1, 2021

1 of 5 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The STEP Program mandates that, to the extent possible, all work-eligible families must actively engage in meaningful activities designed to enable their transition from receipt of FITAP cash assistance to self-sufficiency. Families must demonstrate active and diligent personal responsibility in achieving self-sufficiency through employment and increased workplace literacy or participation in other appropriate activities and development of the Family Success Agreement (FSA). ***

P-411-STEP - PO WORK-ELIGIBLES

A work-eligible family is a FITAP family (including cases which do not receive cash because their benefit would be less than $10) which includes at least one adult under age 60 or a teen head of household, who is not disabled or incapacitated, or who is not caring for a family member who is disabled or incapacitated, as documented by a medical expert. Child-only cases are not considered work-eligible families but are included in the Federal Participation Rate in certain situations (see C- 120-FITAP), section C-121-FITAP).

A work-eligible recipient is an adult under age 60 or a teen head of household who is included in a work-eligible family and who is not disabled or incapacitated, or who is not caring for a family member who is disabled or incapacitated, as documented by a medical expert.

Work-eligible recipients shall be expected to participate in work activities for the minimum number of hours specified by federal law or as required in the FSA ***. No work-eligible recipient shall be exempt from participation in such activities.

Work-eligible recipients shall be granted a temporary exception from participation in work activities until engaged by the STEP * Coach ** in the completion of a Family Assessment and Family Success Agreement.

When an assessment determines that a work-eligible recipient does not possess basic or workplace literacy skills, the recipient shall participate in a combination of employment and educational activities designed to increase basic or workplace literacy skills.

Work-eligible recipients who are pregnant or have a child under age 1 shall participate in Parenting Skills Training. If it is not the recipient’s first pregnancy or first child, and the recipient has completed the current Parenting Skills Training, participation may be allowed in other work activities, if deemed appropriate by the worker.

Work-eligible minor parents who do not have a high school diploma or its equivalent shall attend school or related education classes designed to obtain a high school diploma or its equivalent. Participation in education shall be required in the FSA *** and shall be the primary work activity for these minor parents.

2 of 5 P-412-STEP - PO GOOD CAUSE

Good Cause may be granted to a work-eligible recipient to temporarily excuse the recipient from participation in assigned work activities. Refer to P-531-STEP-PR Good Cause Reasons. Good Cause determinations shall not exceed six months per occurrence. Months in which a Good Cause determination is granted when a payee recipient is deemed temporarily incapacitated, ill, or disabled shall not count toward the recipient’s 24-month time limit.

The FSA *** must be completed when a recipient is granted Good Cause due to incapacity or disability. It should include a plan for the recipient to return to or begin participation in appropriate work activities based on medical documentation of the duration of the incapacity.

P-413-STEP - PO UNIVERSAL ENGAGEMENT

The primary goal of the STEP Program is to ensure that all work-eligible families are actively and universally engaged in meaningful activities designed to enable their transition from receipt of FITAP cash assistance to self-sufficiency. To measure success toward meeting this goal, the * department has implemented a Placement Rate.

The Placement Rate is defined as the percentage of active FITAP families which include an adult in a given month that participate in some type of activity for at least one hour in that same month. Although some of these families may not be work-eligible, they are included in the placement rate calculations because of the manner in which the state performance indicator is calculated.

In an effort to assist all FITAP work-eligible recipients to achieve self-sufficiency, and to achieve the required state performance indicator, it is permissible to place recipients in both countable and non- countable activities. Refer to P-420-STEP. All FITAP work-eligible recipients must be placed in some type of activity in order to achieve the required placement rate of 70%.

In addition to ensuring all work- eligible families are universally engaged in meaningful work activities, the following two categories of recipients should also be universally engaged in meaningful work activities:

● non work-eligible families ● non recipient parents living with a child receiving assistance

Note: Refer to C-120-FITAP, section C-121-FITAP, for parents not included in the assistance unit but living with a child receiving assistance. Non-recipient parents who are an SSI recipient, SSI eligible with suspended payments, or do not meet the citizenship requirement may not be referred to participate in STEP activities or receive STEP Supportive Service payments. **

These families shall be engaged in activities designed to enable their transition to self-sufficiency. These activities can include but are not limited to:

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 04 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-400-STEP Participation Document No./Name P-430-STEP Reporting Hours and Documentation Effective Date January 1, 2021

1 of 6 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The Department, in compliance with federal, state, and/or internal regulations, is mandated to verify and document STEP participation hours.

Participation hours in both contracted and non-contracted activities must be reported. Satisfactory or unsatisfactory attendance must be documented * in Person Notes. **

If it is determined that the client is not participating in accordance with their FSA, *** and if the client is not granted a good cause reason from participation, a STEP sanction is * requested ** (Refer to P-500-STEP).

P-431-STEP - PO CONTRACTED ACTIVITIES

Contracts with service providers must include a provision that the contractor is responsible for collecting and reporting participation hours for participants covered under their contract. The contractor must provide a case management function which will ensure that attendance and progress are monitored. The client may be required to sign in and out as appropriate so that the contractor may collect and report accurate data. A tracking mechanism such as a login/logout time function may be used by the contractor. The contractor must report participation hours to the * DCFS office no less frequently than monthly.

ES contract managers must ensure that contractors adhere to the reporting requirements in their contracts or non-financial agreements. Financial contracts must include a provision to withhold partial payments if participation hours are not reported timely or correctly. Non-financial agreements should include a provision to modify or terminate the agreement if participation hours are not reported timely or correctly.

P-431-1-STEP - PO Information Security

The Department, in compliance with internal regulations, is mandated to secure a participant’s personal information, which is prohibited from being saved or stored on computers and data communication systems owned by and/or administered by DCFS.

P-432-STEP - PO NON-CONTRACTED ACTIVITIES

Work-eligible recipients who are employed or participating in an activity must provide verified participation hours to the STEP Coach. ** Hours must be reported by the due date for each assigned work activity.

Failure of a work-eligible recipient to report participation hours in an activity by the due date for each assigned work activity will result in a STEP sanction.

Hours of participation must be verified by someone who oversees the participant’s work activity.

2 of 6 P-433-STEP - PO DOCUMENTATION FOR EMPLOYMENT ACTIVITIES

Documentation of STEP participation hours in Unsubsidized Employment, Subsidized Public Sector Employment, Subsidized Private Sector Employment, or On-the-Job Training (OJT) must be provided to the STEP Coach at least every six months.

P-434-STEP PO - DOCUMENTATION FOR NON-EMPLOYMENT ACTIVITIES

Documentation of STEP participation hours in Job Search and Job Readiness, Work Experience Program (WEP), Community Service Programs, Vocational Education, Job Skills Training, Education Directly Related to Employment, Secondary/GED, or Provision of Child Care for Community Service must be provided to the STEP Coach no less frequently than monthly.

II. PROCEDURES

Depending on the type of activity, it is the responsibility of either the contractor or the client to report participation hours to the STEP Coach in various timeframes as described below.

As part of the case management process, the STEP Coach must thoroughly explain the reporting requirements to the client, making sure that the client understands the reporting requirements and the penalties for failure to meet these requirements. The STEP Coach must maintain regular contact with the client to ensure that participation is satisfactorily continuing and that no problems are being experienced. Document satisfactory or unsatisfactory attendance in Person Notes.

If the STEP Coach believes the client is not participating in accordance with their FSA, the STEP Coach ** should follow-up with:

● site visits to verify attendance or participation, ● more frequent contacts with the client, ● communication with the contractor or employer, and/or *** ● comparison of participation with simplified reports.

Participation hours in all activities should be considered and/or counted in accordance with the criteria described for each specific work activity in P-420-STEP.

Excused absences are countable up to 16 hours per month but not to exceed 80 hours in a preceding 12-month period. These hours are countable only if the individual was scheduled to participate on those days and only the regularly scheduled amount of daily participation hours in that activity can be counted.

Only the following 10 holidays when recognized by the work site sponsor or training or educational institution can be counted as participation hours for unpaid work activities: New Year’s Day (1 day), Martin Luther King Jr. Day (1 day), Mardi Gras Day (1 day), Good Friday (1 day), Memorial Day (1

3 of 6 day), Independence Day (1 day), Labor Day (1 day), Veteran’s Day (1 day), Thanksgiving (1 day), and Christmas (1 day).

These hours are counted only if the individual was scheduled to participate on those days and only the regularly scheduled amount of daily participation hours in that activity can be counted. For example, if a participant attends a Vocational Educational Training class for four hours per day and the Vocational Institution is closed for Labor Day, four hours of participation will be counted for that participant for that day. Holidays not listed may be counted as an excused absence up to 16 hours per month but not to exceed 80 hours in the preceding 12 month period.

Participation hours can only be rounded on a monthly basis prior to entry * in LITE. Actual daily or weekly hours and minutes must be added until a monthly figure is obtained, and then that amount may be rounded to the nearest participation hour.

P-431-STEP - PR CONTRACTED ACTIVITIES

The client may be required to sign in and out as appropriate so that the contractor may collect and report accurate data. A tracking mechanism such as a login/logout time function may be used by the contractor.

Non-financial agreements should include a provision to modify or terminate the agreement if participation hours are not reported timely or correctly. The STEP Coach ** must inform STEP providers of clients referred for services on form STEP 16R as noted in their contract. ***

A client should not be sanctioned when the contractor does not report participation hours timely or correctly, unless it is later determined that the hours were not reported because the client did not participate or because the client failed to report the hours to the contractor. When a contractor does not timely report hours, the STEP * Coach must contact the contractor to determine why the hours were not reported. If the contractor simply failed to report the hours without justifiable reason, the ES contract manager should be informed and appropriate action should be taken.

P-431-1-STEP - PR Information Security

To ensure compliance with information security by the Louisiana Department of Children and Family Services (DCFS), participant’s personal information such as, but not limited to, resumes, cover letters, and job search applications is prohibited from being saved or stored on computers and data communication systems owned by and/or administered by the contractor. ** Specific questions regarding this guideline should be directed to the appropriate *** * STEP Supervisor. **

ES contract managers must ensure contracts or non-financial agreements include this provision.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 04 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-400-STEP Participation Document No./Name P-430-STEP Reporting Hours and Documentation Effective Date January 1, 2021

4 of 6 P-432-STEP - PR WORK ACTIVITIES

The reporting of verified participation hours requirement should be clearly indicated on the client’s Family Success Agreement *** and discussed with the client throughout the certification. A tracking mechanism such as a login/logout time function may be used for activities; such as, GED programs, technical and/or post-secondary institutions or an on-line distance learning curriculum.

For Job Search activities, the form STEP 11 should be used by the participant to document employer contacts, job search by telephone, in person, or via internet for learning of suitable job openings, applying and interviewing for jobs, and the results of such contacts. All contacts must be accompanied by the signature of an employer, work-site sponsor, or other responsible party. Daily supervision and documentation are required in order to count Job Search activities. Daily, in-person contact can be by telephone or electronic contact where those methods are suitable.

For all other work activities, the form STEP 34A or STEP 34B should be used to document participation hours. Accompanying supervisor’s or provider’s signature is required. Other acceptable methods of documenting participation hours in activities include:

● check stubs, ● written employer/provider records, or ● properly documented verbal verification of actual participation hours * in Person Notes.

P-433-STEP - PR DOCUMENTATION FOR EMPLOYMENT ACTIVITIES

Work-eligible recipients who are participating in Unsubsidized Employment, Subsidized Public Sector Employment, Subsidized Private Sector Employment, or On-the-Job Training (OJT) must provide documentation of participation hours to the STEP Coach at least every six months. This documentation may be in the form of:

● check stubs, ● written employer/provider records; such as time cards, sign-in and sign-out sheets, and rosters ● documented wage forms which include the actual hours of participation, the employer’s name/signature and telephone number, or ● documented verbal verification from the employer if, and only if, check stubs or written verification cannot be obtained.

Note: The STEP Coach must document the phone call including who verified the hours of participation and the number of hours in Person Notes. **

Based on valid documentation, the participation hours may be projected for up to six months or until the end of the FITAP certification period, whichever is shorter, if representative of continuing circumstances. The projection must be based on prior, documented actual hours of work. At the end of this six-month period, or at any time the worker becomes aware of a change in the client’s work situation, new valid documentation must be obtained and another six-month projection may be made.

This documentation requirement must be clearly indicated on the participant’s Family Success Agreement and must ** be discussed with the participant throughout the certification period. When possible, the form STEP 34A or STEP 34B, with appropriate signatures should be used to report participation hours in these activities.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-400-STEP Participation Document No./Name P-440-STEP Federal Participation Rates and Requirements Effective Date January 1, 2021

1 of 6 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

According to state law, all work-eligible recipients of FITAP are required to participate in the STEP Program. However, there are types of FITAP cases when a recipient would not count when calculating the federal participation rate.

EXEMPTIONS

The following types of FITAP cases are exempt when calculating federal participation rates:

● FITAP families including a parent personally providing care for a child under age one living in the home, if that parent's legal spouse and/or the other parent of the child is not also in the home. ● FITAP families including a caretaker relative other than a parent personally providing care for a child under age one living in the home, if the caretaker's legal spouse is not in the home. ● FITAP families including a parent who is providing care for a disabled family member living in the home as long as medical documentation is provided to support the need for the parent to remain in the home to care for the disabled family member. ● FITAP families that do not have an adult parent, an adult caretaker relative, or a minor parent head of household included in the FITAP certification because that individual receives SSI or is an alien who is ineligible due to immigration status.

II. PROCEDURES

The participation rate exemption for caring for a child under age one is limited to a total of 12 months per individual. The earliest month that this exemption can be applied is the month following the birth of the child, and the latest month that this exemption can be applied is the month of the child's first birthday.

The participation rate exemption for caring for a disabled family member living in the home must be supported by medical documentation stating the incapacity must be of a debilitating nature and expected to last for at least 30 days.

The FSA * must be completed. ** It should include a plan for the recipient to return to or begin participation in appropriate work activities based on medical documentation of the duration of the incapacity.

Although these FITAP families are exempt from the federal participation rate calculations, work- eligible families are not exempt from participation in assigned activities, including the Parenting Skills Program.

These participation rate exemptions must be verified, documented, and re-evaluated when the condition that required the exemption is expected to end.

2 of 6 ALL FAMILIES RATE AND REQUIREMENTS

A monthly average of 30 participation hours per week is required for a FITAP family to be counted toward the federal All Families participation rate. (See the following sections P-442-1 and P-442-2 for additional criteria).

Individual participation exceeding an average of 30 hours per week will not increase the All Families rate. If deemed feasible and necessary by the worker to expedite the client’s progress, or if required by the provider or employer, participation hours exceeding the 30 hours per week may be required. However, additional hours cannot be required for the sole purpose of providing a buffer for possible absences in the month. If hours exceeding the 30 hours are required but the participant only meets the 30-hour requirement, he cannot be sanctioned for failure to comply unless the hours exceeding the 30 hours are required by the provider or employer and are specified in the Family Success Agreement. ***

For the federal All Families participation rate, participation in the following activities is countable for the first 20 weekly hours of participation:

● Employment, including Unsubsidized Employment, Subsidized Public Sector Employment, and Subsidized Private Sector Employment ● Vocational Education (not to exceed 12-month limit) ● Job Search and Job Readiness not to exceed 120 or 180 hours and not to exceed 120 hours for a work-eligible individual with a 20 hour average weekly requirement or 180 hours for a work-eligible individual with a 30 hour average weekly work requirement. ● On-the-Job Training (OJT) ● Work Experience Program (WEP) ● Community Service Programs ● Provision of Child Care Services to an Individual who is Participating in a Community Services Program

For the federal All Families participation rate, participation in the following activities is countable for hours above the first 20 weekly hours of participation:

● Satisfactory Attendance at a Secondary School or in a Course of Study Leading to a Certification of General Equivalence Diploma (GED) * or High School Equivalency Test (HiSET), if the parent/caretaker does not have a high school diploma, GED, or HiSET ** ● Education Directly Related to Employment, if the parent/caretaker does not have a high school diploma, *** GED, * or HiSET ** ● Job Skills Training Directly Related to Employment

The All Families participation rate is calculated by dividing the number of countable FITAP families (where one adult participates the required number of hours per week in countable activities) by the total number of non-exempt FITAP families. Families that are granted good cause are included in the participation rate calculations.

FITAP families with work-eligible parents (not caretaker relatives) who are not included in the FITAP certification are also included in the All Families participation rate, unless that parent is not included because he or she receives SSI or is an alien who is ineligible due to immigration status. Refer to C-121-FITAP.

Beginning October 2001, the state’s required All Families participation rate is 50%.

STEP DEEMED TEEN COUNTABLES

Deemed Teen Countables are defined as FITAP recipients (married or single) who:

● Are head of household, and ● Are under age 20 (recipients are considered under age 20 in the month of their 20th birthday), and

o Maintain satisfactory attendance and satisfactory progress, as defined and verified by the educational institution attended, in Secondary Education/GED/* HiSET, ** or o Participate in Education Directly Related to Employment for a monthly average of 20 hours per week and maintain satisfactory progress.

Single-parent families are deemed to be countable for the federal All Families participation rate if at least one recipient in that family meets the Deemed Teen Countable definition.

All Families participation requirements described in P-440, (Deemed Single-Parent Families and Single Minor Parents) apply to teen parents who are head of household and do not meet the criteria for Deemed Teen Countables.

STEP DEEMED SINGLE-PARENT FAMILIES

A single parent/caretaker relative with a child under age six is deemed to be countable for the All Families participation rate if that parent/caretaker is engaged in an allowable work activity for a monthly average of 20 hours per week. For this purpose, allowable work activities include those that count for the first 20 hours of weekly participation.

Individual participation exceeding an average of 20 hours per week for these participants will not increase the All Families rate. If deemed feasible and necessary by the worker to expedite the client’s progress, or if required by the provider or employer, participation hours exceeding the 20 hours per week may be required. However, additional hours cannot be required for the sole purpose of providing a buffer for possible absences in the month. If hours exceeding the 20 hours are required but the participant only meets the 20-hour requirement, he cannot be sanctioned for failure to comply unless the hours exceeding the 20 hours are required by the provider or employer and are specified in the Family Success Agreement. ***

4 of 6 STEP GOOD CAUSE FOR SINGLE-PARENT FAMILIES

A single parent/caretaker relative who is personally providing care for a child under age six may claim good cause for failure or refusal to participate in an assigned work activity or for refusal to accept employment if the participant is unable to obtain needed child care for one of the following reasons:

● Unavailability of appropriate child care within a reasonable distance from their home or work site, ● Unavailability or unsuitability of child care by a relative or under other arrangements, or ● Unavailability of appropriate and affordable formal child care arrangements.

The condition for claiming good cause for failure or refusal to participate must be verified, documented, and re-evaluated when the condition is expected to end and at every redetermination. The participant must be notified of any change in participation requirements.

This special provision for single parents/caretakers applies only if the parent/caretaker's legal spouse and/or the other parent of the child are not in the home.

STEP SINGLE MINOR PARENTS

If a single parent/caretaker is under age 18, has a child at least 12 weeks of age, and does not have a high school diploma or its equivalent, * they must participate in a Secondary/GED/HiSET activity or in an alternative educational or training program approved by the STEP Coach. ** This federal provision applies to all FITAP minor parents, regardless of whether they are head of household or not.

This special provision for single parents/caretakers applies only if the parent/caretaker's legal spouse and/or the other parent of the child is not in the home.

STEP PARTICIPATION RATE CALCULATIONS

To determine the monthly number of hours that an individual or a family must participate in order to be countable for federal participation rate purposes:

LIMITATIONS FOR VOCATIONAL EDUCATION AND DEEMED TEEN COUNTABLES

The total number of countable participants in Vocational Education, combined with the total number of Deemed Teen Countables, cannot exceed 30% of the number of countable families.

For this 30% calculation, a countable participant in Vocational Education is defined as a countable participant who would not meet the minimum monthly participation requirements without the Vocational Education hours.

Example: In a 31-day month, a client participates 120 hours in WEP and 20 hours in Vocational Education. He is considered a countable participant in Vocational Education for this 30% calculation since he would not meet the minimum requirements without the Vocational Education hours. If this same client had participated 135 hours in WEP and 50 hours in Vocational Education, he would not be considered a countable participant in Vocational Education for this 30% calculation since he would meet the minimum requirements without the Vocational Education hours.

***

OTHER FEDERAL REQUIREMENTS

Parents or caretakers who have received FITAP cash assistance for 24 months since January 1997 (whether consecutive or not) are required to participate in an approved STEP activity (whether countable or not) in order to retain FITAP eligibility. This requirement is separate and apart from the 24-month time limit for receipt of FITAP cash assistance. The only exceptions to this requirement are recipients who meet the good cause criteria described in section P-440 (Good Cause for Single- Parent Families) or the exemption criteria described in Section P-440 (Exemptions).

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-500-STEP Sanctions/Good Cause Document No./Name P-510-STEP Sanctions Effective Date February 15, 2024

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

P-510-STEP - PO SANCTIONS

* An intensified, coaching case management approach allows staff to learn more about our participants and to offer opportunities to help our participants address and resolve their challenges. The STEP sanction philosophy must be fair, but it must hold our participants accountable and responsible for their success in overcoming these challenges. **

Sanctions are to be used as a last resort when FITAP work-eligible families have not met the required expectations of the STEP Program. A sanction is not considered a punishment, but is a consequence of not meeting program expectations.

***

II. PROCEDURES

P-510-STEP - PR SANCTIONS

*** * Coaches must fully explain the expectations of the STEP program and the relevance for remaining in the program. These expectations and consequences must be explained to the participant in detail during completion of the Family Success Agreement. In review and revise sessions, STEP coaches are expected to revisit the importance of participation. The STEP Coach must assist the participant in solving problems that arise. Solutions to these problems, good cause consideration, and potential sanctions must be discussed in supervisory conference.

Person Notes must contain adequate documentation that participants were informed of their expectations and consequences during the completion of the Family Success Agreement.

If good cause is explored and cannot be established, the appropriate STEP sanction must be requested and applied in a fair and consistent manner. In LITE, search for and access the participant’s referral and then navigate to the Request a Sanction tab, and click on the Create New Sanction button to send an automated request to the ES Case Maintenance worker, who will impose the sanction on the participant’s eligibility case. If the participant complies with STEP during the 13- day period of advance adverse action, the STEP Coach must contact the ES worker manually to cancel the sanction request.

Once sanctioned, the STEP Coach must work with the participant if they reapply for cash assistance to cure their sanction by first understanding the challenges and barriers that may have led to the sanction. The STEP Coach must then work with the participant to jointly determine solutions to those challenges in order to help participants be more successful in STEP **

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The appropriate STEP sanction shall be applied for FITAP families that include work-eligible recipients (or work-eligible parents who are not included in the FITAP certification) when the work- eligible recipient or the excluded parent fails to comply with the requirements of the program.

NOTE: STEP sanctions are not applied to caretaker relatives or parents not included because he or she receives SSI or is an alien who is ineligible due to immigration status.

II. PROCEDURES

STEP sanctions are applied when work-eligible recipients or work-eligible parents:

 Fail without good cause to complete a Family Assessment.

 Fail without good cause to keep scheduled appointment to complete a Family Success Agreement.

 Fail without good cause to return a signed Family Success Agreement.

 Fail to attend school or other educational classes designed to obtain a high school diploma or GED, as specified in the Family Success Agreement, when the work-eligible recipient or excluded parent is a minor parent who has not received a high school diploma or GED.

 Fail to attend parenting skills education without good cause and other training conducive to the unique needs of new parents, as specified in the Family Success Agreement, when the work- eligible recipient or excluded parent is pregnant or has a child under age 1.

 *** * Fail to make progress towards achieving self-sufficiency goals ** without good cause, as specified in the Family Success Agreement. In these cases, the sanction cannot be cured by participating in the activity prior to expiration of the advance notice of adverse action because the notice period will end prior to the required two weeks of satisfactory participation.

 Decline or refuse the opportunity for employment, quits a job without good cause, or voluntarily reduces earnings.

 Fail without good cause to meet other requirements specified in the Family Success Agreement, including but not limited to:

○ Cooperation with Child Support Enforcement, ○ Meeting immunization requirements for children, ○ Compliance with drug screening and treatment requirements, or

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-500-STEP Sanctions/Good Cause Document No./Name P-530-STEP Good Cause Effective Date January 1, 2021

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Sanctions shall be used as a last resort to inform participants that they have not met the expectations set forth in the Family Success Agreement.

II. PROCEDURES

When a work-eligible family’s failure or refusal to comply with STEP requirements described in the Family Success Agreement becomes known to the department, an Advance Notice of Adverse Action is sent by the * ES Worker to the client to impose the appropriate STEP sanction. If the client contacts the STEP Coach to claim a good cause reason for non-compliance, the STEP Coach must make a good cause determination, document the results of this determination in Person Notes, and email the ES Worker advising that the sanction must be removed if a good cause determination is approved. When possible, this good cause determination should be made jointly with the STEP Coach’s supervisor during the advance notice period for the proposed sanction.

During the 13-day advance notice period, if the STEP Coach determines that the client had a good cause reason which caused the non-compliance, the proposed STEP sanction does not occur and must be removed from LITE by the ES worker, preferably prior to expiration of the 13-day advance notice period. The STEP Coach should then attempt to assist the family with solutions to the problems which caused the failure to comply.

After the 13-day advance notice period, if the STEP Coach determines that the client had a good cause reason which caused the non-compliance, the STEP sanction is considered to have not occurred and must be removed from LITE by the ES worker. In this instance, corrective payments must be made to the client, if applicable. The STEP Coach should then attempt to assist the family with solutions to the problems which caused the failure to comply.

Note: To be eligible for good cause consideration, the reason should be reported within 10 days of knowledge of the change, but must be reported no later than 30 days from the expiration of the advance notice of decision.

The appropriate STEP sanction is imposed if the client:

● does not claim a good cause reason for non-compliance, ● claims a good cause reason for non-compliance but is determined not to have one, or ● does not cooperate with the STEP Coach in trying to determine if a good cause reason existed.

Note: When it becomes known that a STEP sanction is required, the STEP Coach must request a sanction in LITE, which routes a task to the ES worker who imposes the sanction. ** ***

P-531-STEP - PR GOOD CAUSE REASONS

When a work-eligible recipient fails to meet the requirements specified in the Family Success Agreement pertaining to employment and education activities, good cause can only be granted for the following reasons:

● Unavailability of appropriate child care within a reasonable distance from the participant’s home or activity site, after efforts have been made and assistance has been offered to secure such child care.

● Unavailability of appropriate transportation when the participant’s home and activity site are not within a reasonable walking distance, or if transportation is available but is cost prohibitive.

● Situations related to domestic violence. Any client who is granted good cause for this reason must be referred to a domestic violence * program.

● Situations related to the treatment of a mental or physical illness, including substance abuse treatment, when there is verification that participation in required activities would impair the treatment plan specified by a mental health or medical professional. Any client who is granted good cause for this reason shall incorporate the treatment plan into the Family Success Agreement. A STEP sanction would be applied if the client does not comply with the treatment plan, unless the client has good cause for not complying with the plan.

● Temporary, short-term illness as documented by a medical professional.

● Temporary care of a family member who is ill, as documented by a medical professional and when there is no other person available to provide the temporary care.

● Temporary emergency crisis, including but not limited to:

o Homelessness, o Fire o Accident o Hurricane o Flood o Dislocation due to natural causes o Other similar circumstances that can be documented.

The duration of the good cause period shall be as long as the STEP Coach, ** with supervisory approval, determines the condition(s) exist.

3 of 3 If approved, good cause may be granted for no more than six months. Consideration of a subsequent determination of good cause must be made by the 10th day of the last month of the initial good cause period.

For example, a work-eligible recipient’s child becomes ill during a month, causing the recipient to fail to meet participation requirements. The recipient is granted good cause for the failure to comply. The same thing occurs the next month, and the recipient is again granted good cause for failure to comply. The STEP * Coach ** then learns that the child’s illness is more serious, is expected to last a few months, and will require the recipient to provide care for the child for those few months. The recipient still meets the criteria for good cause because she is unable to obtain appropriate child care for the ill child. Once the child’s illness and the good cause period ends, the recipient may begin participating again, and if the child becomes temporarily ill again to prevent the recipient from meeting participation requirements for a given month, a good cause reason may be granted.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-500-STEP Sanctions/Good Cause Document No./Name P-540-STEP Sanction Periods Effective Date January 1, 2021

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Sanctions are to be used as a last resort when FITAP work-eligible families have not met the required expectations of the STEP Program.

II. PROCEDURES

When a work-eligible recipient fails to comply, without good cause, with STEP Program requirements as described in P-520-STEP, the following STEP sanctions are applied:

● First occurrence (STEP Sanction Code, Occurrence 1) - FITAP case closure for minimum of one month. Once the STEP 1 sanction is imposed, the FITAP case cannot be recertified until one month of FITAP benefits is missed and the sanctioned recipient complies, has a good cause reason, or is granted Good Cause * from STEP participation.

● Second occurrence (STEP Sanction Code, Occurrence 2) - FITAP case closure for minimum of two months. Once the STEP 2 sanction is imposed, the FITAP case cannot be recertified until two months of FITAP benefits are missed and the sanctioned recipient complies, has a good cause reason, or is granted Good Cause from STEP participation.

● Third and subsequent occurrences (STEP Sanction Code, Occurrence 3) - FITAP case closure for minimum of three months. Once the STEP 3 sanction is imposed, the FITAP case cannot be recertified until three months of FITAP benefits are missed and the sanctioned recipient complies, has a good cause reason, or is granted Good Cause from STEP participation.

All STEP sanctions and the client’s failure to comply details must be discussed with the STEP Supervisor and documented in Person Notes and in LITE using the Request a Sanction tab in the Referrals module.

The appropriate Failure to Comply Details ** *** * must be entered in LITE to reflect the specific reason for the non-compliance that caused the STEP sanction. Reasons include failure to comply with:

 Developing/signing an FSA,  FSA Activities – Participation/Progress/Verification, or  Refuse to accept employment – Quit – Terminate Reduced. **

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms or instructions associated with this policy.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Independence (EI) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-500-STEP Sanctions/Good Cause Document No./Name P-550-STEP Applying the Sanction Effective Date September 1, 2026

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

When a work eligible or non-work eligible family is determined to be in non-compliance with STEP requirements and does not have good cause, the appropriate STEP sanction will be applied.

II. PROCEDURES

When the STEP Coach *** enters a non-compliance entry in TuaPath, a task will be generated and routed to the FITAP Worker for processing in LITE.

The FITAP *** Worker must enter the appropriate STEP Non-Compliance Violation Type, including the correct Non-Compliance Reason and Decision Date in LITE.

When a STEP sanction is deemed appropriate for an adult parent/caretaker, it is applied to all adult members. In these instances, if a MUP is included in the FITAP certification, the STEP sanction is not applied to the MUP. However, when a STEP sanction is deemed appropriate for a MUP, it is applied to all adult members and the MUP. The STEP Coach must be careful to request a sanction for the correct members.

An Advance Notice of Adverse Action is required prior to the start of the STEP sanction and allows the client 13 days to comply prior to case closure. If the client complies during this period, the STEP Coach must manually contact the FITAP *** Worker with the date of compliance. The FITAP Worker will delete the sanction in LITE and run EDBC. Otherwise, the STEP referral will close automatically at the appropriate time (Refer to P-610-STEP).

If the STEP sanction is received the month prior or the month of Redetermination the sanction will be entered and processed in LITE at the time of receipt. The action will require a manual Advance Notice of Adverse Action.

The STEP sanction occurrence codes (1, 2, or 3) are tracked in LITE by member.

A STEP sanction is considered to have occurred once the Advance Notice of Adverse Action ends. The first month of the sanction period is the first month in which the client does not receive FITAP benefits following case closure. After the Advance Notice of Adverse Action expires and the sanction is actually imposed in LITE, the sanction can only be deleted from LITE if it is determined that the client had good cause at the time of non-compliance or if the client wins a subsequent appeal. In these situations, corrective FITAP payments must be made to the client.

If a client who is unwilling to participate voluntarily chooses FITAP case closure prior to a determination of STEP non-compliance, the case closure will not be considered a STEP sanction, unless the request for closure occurs after the Advance Notice of Adverse Action. In these instances, the FITAP *** Worker must document the case record to indicate that the client has been made aware that FITAP case closure could also affect eligibility for SNAP and Medicaid benefits.

2 of 2 APPLYING THE SANCTION FOR MULTIPLE NON-COMPLIANCES

When a client’s FITAP case is within the Advance Notice of Adverse Action period due to a STEP sanction and a subsequent non-compliance occurs, the STEP Coach must request a sanction for the subsequent non-compliance. If the FITAP case is still active in LITE, the FITAP *** Worker will enter the STEP sanction and send an Advance Notice of Adverse Action for the second non-compliance. If the FITAP case has closed, it is not appropriate to request a subsequent non-compliance.

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

A work-eligible recipient who has been sanctioned for failure to comply with STEP requirements may cure their STEP sanction by demonstrating and verifying that their failure to comply has ceased.

II. PROCEDURES

To end the failure to comply, this individual must:

● Be found to have a good cause reason,

● Indicate a willingness to comply when there is no available placement or adequate supportive services, or

● Satisfactorily comply with assigned program activities or requirements (assessment, CSE or drug testing compliance, etc.) as specified on previously-completed Family Success Agreement (FSA). ***

Note: The *FSA must be updated at least every six months. If a sanctioned individual applies for benefits and it has been more than six months since a FSA been completed, a new FSA ** must be completed within one week of certification.

A * FSA must be completed before support services can be authorized and before hours of participation can be entered in LITE **.

● Satisfactorily participate for two weeks in the previously-assigned program activity or an approved alternate activity, or

● Meet one of the following exemptions:

o FITAP families including a parent who is providing care for a disabled family member living in the home as long as medical documentation is provided to support the need for the parent to remain in the home to care for the disabled family member. o FITAP families that do not have an adult parent, an adult caretaker relative, or a minor parent head of household included in the FITAP certification because that individual receives SSI or is an alien who is ineligible due to immigration status.

All available supportive services should be provided while the sanctioned individual is attempting to cure his sanction by ending the failure to comply.

If the sanctioned individual is attempting to cure his sanction during the application period by satisfactorily participating for a two-week period and that two-week period cannot be completed prior

● determine a plan to allow the client to move forward, and

● determine a plan for addressing other potential barriers before they occur.

During the attempt to cure the sanction, it may be necessary to * amend the FSA if non-compliance resulted from an activity that was not appropriate for the individual. All attempts to cure the sanction must be documented in Person Notes **.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-700-STEP Supportive Services Document No./Name P-710-STEP Supportive Services Effective Date January 1, 2021

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Participants are provided supportive services to enable them to participate in the STEP Program.

Supportive services may also be provided to:

● FITAP recipients participating in approved activities necessary to meet exemptions to the FITAP time limits,

● FITAP recipients participating in the FITAP Drug Testing Program,

● FITAP recipients participating in approved activities when they are exempt from the participation rate calculations, or

● FITAP recipients participating in non-countable activities (refer to P-420-STEP, section P-428).

Supportive services payments are made to participants through direct deposit to the client’s bank account (checking or savings) or payments to a Stored Value Card account.

Before the * STEP Coach can enter authorization of direct payments to participants, written verification of expenses must be provided.

Direct advance payment or reimbursement may be made to the participant for the purchase of these services if it is determined that they are essential for STEP participation or to accept or maintain employment.

The STEP Coach may reduce, close, or deny in whole or in part an individual’s request for a support service payment if a need is not demonstrated or the purpose for the payment is not related to the individual’s Family Success Agreement.

The participant must provide verification from the provider of the need and anticipated cost before payment can be made.

Approval of advance payments can be made only with the concurrence of the STEP Supervisor.

II. PROCEDURES

The STEP Coach ** shall inform the participant of available supportive services as part of the initial family assessment and shall integrate the provision of any necessary supportive services into the Family Success Agreement (STEP 6), *** developed and signed by the participant.

To be eligible for reimbursement, supportive services other than child care must be approved by the * STEP Coach ** no later than the 10th day after the supportive services begin. The participant must provide verification from the service provider before payment can be made.

Exception: When a FITAP application is certified, supportive services may be provided for the entire month of FITAP application, regardless of when the supportive services began or when the FITAP application is certified.

There are no provisions for routine issuance of parish payments in STEP. All * STEP payments are issued through the LITE Payment System.

Supportive services provided or claimed for reimbursement must be reasonably related to the hours of participation.

Reimbursement of support services must be issued within 10 days of receipt of verification.

The STEP Coach must terminate ongoing supportive services payment authorizations prior to STEP referral closure in LITE **. ***

***

The participant must be notified by form STEP 12 within 10 days of all supportive services payments initially authorized or subsequently changed.

The participant must be notified by form STEP 12 within 10 days of the initial authorization of the transportation stipend and at case closure for the termination of the stipend. If an overpayment exists as a result of an administrative error, recovery should be initiated.

The * STEP Coach must coordinate supportive services with related services provided by other agencies.

Once advance payment is authorized, the client must provide the receipt of the expense within 10 days as stated on the STEP 12. A copy of the receipt should be saved in OnBase and the original returned to the participant. If a receipt is not provided within 10 days as requested, the STEP Coach is to complete form STEP 20 to obtain repayment. If the participant requests additional time to provide the receipt, document Person Notes allowing extra time to provide the receipt, but within thirty days of authorization.

After an advance payment has been made based on the verified anticipated cost, the STEP Coach must verify the actual cost. If the anticipated cost was greater than the actual cost, the STEP Coach is to initiate recovery for the difference. The participant must provide a personal check, business check, or money order to the parish office. A form STEP 20 must then be completed describing the circumstances of the overpayment. The check or money order, made payable to DCFS, must be attached to the form STEP 20 and forwarded to the ES Fraud and Recovery Unit. If the participant does not refund the overpayment, a referral must be made to the ES ** Fraud and Recovery Unit.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 04 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P 700-STEP Supportive Services Document No./Name P-720-STEP Transportation Effective Date March 1, 2021

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Transportation assistance must be provided when necessary for an individual to participate in STEP activities unless free transportation is available. These activities include those described in document P-710-STEP.

A transportation stipend of * $ 200 will be issued to STEP participants who are expected to participate or have already participated for at least one hour of countable or non-countable hours of participation in a work activity.

STEP participants are responsible for making their transportation arrangements utilizing the $200 stipend.

II. PROCEDURES

A transportation stipend in the amount of $200 ** will be issued to STEP participants who are in compliance with their Family Success Agreement and have either countable or non-countable hours of participation in a work activity.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms and instructions associated with this policy.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-700-STEP Supportive Services Document No./Name P-730-STEP Other Supportive Services Effective Date March 1, 2021

1 of 3 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

Other Supportive Services payments must be provided when necessary for an individual to participate in STEP activities, unless these services are available to the individual at no cost. These activities include those described in P-710-STEP.

II. PROCEDURES

Payments may be made as follows:

● Union Dues - actual amount verified by the employer or training facility, not to exceed $100.

● Other - up to * $600 ** combined maximum per participant per state fiscal year:

o Eyeglasses, - need verified by medical professional and not provided by Medicaid or other resource.

o Hearing Aids and other small medical appliances - need verified by medical professional and not provided by Medicaid or other resource.

o Uniforms/clothing - need verified by training facility or employer.

o Safety equipment - need verified by training facility or employer.

o Tools - need verified by training facility or employer. Tools may include any "tools of the trade" including, but not limited to carpenter's tools, drafting tools, nurse's watches, stethoscopes, training material and welding tools.

o Medical exams/tests, drug tests, and disease inoculations required by the employment or training site and not provided by Medicaid or other resource.

o Course prerequisite costs, employer mandated expenses, and other legitimate expenses that will facilitate employment or training, if approved by the STEP Supervisor and documented in Person Notes.

o Child care registration fees, that are mandated by the child care provider and not paid by the Child Care Assistance Program (CCAP), if approved by the STEP Supervisor and documented in Person Notes.

Note: The Louisiana Department of Education (LDE) issues payment for child care registration fees 60 days after CCAP certification. LDE will only issue one payment per year for registration fees. The year begins with the CCAP case’s Certification From date on the Childcare Assistance Program System (CAPS). The STEP Coach must verify with LDE via

o Transportation-related expenses documented in Person Notes, such as:

■ Car repairs. (Cost verified by a reputable mechanic). ■ Driver's license fees. ■ Vehicle registration and inspection fees. ■ Driver education. ■ Car insurance. (deposit/down payment).

Note: The owner and driver of the vehicle and the participant (if they will be driving) shall provide a copy of current proof of insurance, and a valid driver’s license. A copy of these documents must be obtained and uploaded to the participant’s case record documents in OnBase.

Other Supportive Services cannot be provided for:

● computer equipment (i.e. desktop, laptop, notebooks, tablets, printers, monitors, etc.), or

● medical services not described above, or

● traffic violation fines, court costs, drivers’ license penalties, or other legally-imposed penalties or fines, or

● the purchase of a vehicle.

The amount of money remaining in the participant's * $600 supportive services allowance will be shown on the screen and will be adjusted as funds are used. At the beginning of each State fiscal year (July 1), LITE will reset the supportive services allowance to $600. ** During the fiscal year, it may be necessary to request restoration of the supportive services allowance. Appropriate restoration situations include:

● Incorrect payment authorizations that have been canceled prior to check write.

● Incorrect payment authorizations that have been paid and proper recovery action has been initiated.

Send requests for supportive services restoration to the STEP Supervisor. Include justification for the restoration and the amount to be restored.

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms associated with this policy.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-700-STEP Supportive Services Document No./Name P-750-STEP Supportive Services During Application Process Effective Date January 1, 2021

1 of 1 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY Child care, transportation, and other supportive services may be provided for FITAP applicants who participate during the FITAP application process. *** Authorizations for payment of * STEP supportive services will be entered in LITE and the payments will be made through the LITE ** payment system.

II. PROCEDURES

There are three situations in which payments for these services may be authorized:

● The FITAP application is eventually certified. In these cases, the authorization for payment of services is entered * in LITE once the active STEP referral is generated upon ** FITAP certification.

● The FITAP application is rejected when there is an existing closed * STEP referral. ** In these cases, * LITE will allow the ** authorization for payment of services *** in * LITE based upon the FITAP application date, even though the referral status is closed. ** ***

● The FITAP application is rejected when there is no existing * STEP referral. In these cases, the ES worker will create a manual STEP referral prior to denying the application and LITE will allow the authorization for payment of services based upon the FITAP application date. LITE will update the manual referral’s active status to closed during the normal monthly disenrollment process. **

III. FORMS AND INSTRUCTIONS

There are no forms and instructions associated with this policy.

IV. REFERENCES

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name P – Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-700-STEP Supportive Services Document No./Name P-760-STEP Payment Option-Direct Deposit and Stored Value Cards Effective Date January 1, 2021

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

STEP supportive service payments are disbursed electronically. The electronic disbursements include Direct Deposits to the client’s bank account (checking or savings) or payments to a Stored Value Card account.

P-761-STEP - PO DIRECT DEPOSIT

Direct deposit is the electronic transfer of funds to the participant’s checking or savings account.

P-762-STEP - PO STORED VALUE CARD (SVC)

A Stored Value Card is the commercial term for a card-accessed account system where payments are electronically deposited in an account accessible for cash withdrawal or for credit purchases, similar to a debit card.

P-763-STEP - PO * STAFF ** RESPONSIBILITIES

Staff shall follow departmental procedures when informing FITAP applicants and STEP participants of payment methods and when managing payment errors contained in various * LITE Pentaho reports. **

II. PROCEDURES

STEP participants will select the payment method preferred. * The STEP Coach will enter the client’s checking or savings account information in LITE, or will enroll the client in a SVC account if they do not already have an existing SVC account. ** ***

P-761-STEP - PR DIRECT DEPOSIT

STEP participants who choose Direct Deposit must:

● Have an active checking or savings account in their name.

● Submit a completed Direct Deposit Authorization Form (OFS DD 1) with the required documentation for the selected method of deposit;

o For checking accounts, a voided check o For savings accounts, a statement from the financial institution showing the participant’s account number and routing number.

Note: If a voided check is unavailable, a statement from the financial institution is required.

2 of 4 If the participant’s name on the Direct Deposit Authorization Form (OFS DD 1) differs in any way from their name on their STEP case, the OFS DD 1 must be returned for proper completion.

To change or cancel the Direct Deposit account, the STEP participant must notify DCFS in writing by completing the OFS DD 1. When the STEP participant changes or cancels Direct Deposit, he should be given the option of providing new account information or being issued a Stored Value Card (SVC).

Information regarding payments made by Direct Deposit into the participant’s checking or savings account can be obtained from the participant’s financial institution.

P-761-STEP - PR STORED VALUE CARD (SVC)

An SVC will be issued to the * STEP participant who chooses SVC as their preferred payment method. ** ***

The SVC can be used to make purchases, get cash, and pay bills anywhere MasterCard debit is accepted. If cash is required, funds can be withdrawn from the card at an U.S. Bank, MoneyPass, and Allpoint ATM machine for free. If an Out of Network ATM is accessed, the client will be charged a small fee. Participants must activate their pre-paid SVC debit card by following the contracted financial institution (U.S. Bank) activation instructions.

One SVC will be used for all funds payable by DCFS to the cardholder. STEP participants receiving payments through a SVC who also receive child support payments from Child Support Enforcement will be issued only one card for all payments. * An automated Stored Value Card STEP Notice will be generated and mailed once in a lifetime for a STEP participant to notify them that they were previously issued a SVC and their STEP payments will be sent to the existing SVC account. LITE generates this notice when a user clicks “Check for existing SVC” button and the interface populates the existing SVC account information in LITE.

If a client’s address changes, the ES eligibility worker must update the client’s mailing address on their FITAP case. The updated address will be sent to the SVC account in the nightly batch. Advise clients that their address change will generally need two business days to be updated on their SVC account. After the address is updated on the SVC account, the client must then call U.S. Bank to request a replacement card if one is needed.

The client must activate the SVC card before their pending STEP Supportive Service payments will issue. Once activated, the nightly batch interfaces will generally need two business days before the funds will be available in the SVC account. ** ***

P-763-STEP - PR * STAFF ** RESPONSIBILITIES

The * FITAP intake worker is responsible for informing the FITAP applicant and the STEP Coach ** is responsible for informing the STEP participant of the payment methods.

3 of 4 * The Direct Deposit/SVC Information Sheet (OFS DD 1 IS) is automatically mailed to the applicant/recipient as a tool in selecting a payment option at certification. If Direct Deposit is chosen, the STEP Coach ** should provide an OFS DD 1 to the recipient to obtain their checking or savings account information.

Once the payment method has been established, the * STEP Coach must update the banking or SVC information on the LITE Stored Value Card/Direct Deposit screen ** immediately so the STEP participants’ supportive service payments will be issued timely.

***

The * STEP Coach is responsible for reviewing LITE Pentaho ** reports daily and making on-line corrections as necessary.

***

The * LITE Pentaho reports that must be reviewed daily are:

1. STEP Clients with Common Database Mismatches, 2. STEP EFT Pre Note Error Return Report, *** and the ** *** 3. * STEP SVC Enrollment Error Return Report. ***

The following * LITE Pentaho report must be reviewed monthly and appropriate action taken:

STEP Payments Pending Over 30 Days/EFT Error

This report is generated on the last day of the month for all STEP clients who have:

 an issuance status of “Pending” for over 30 days from the Process Date for a STEP Supportive Service Payment. The Process Date is the date that the payment created in the STEP Referrals module is moved by LITE to the Benefit Maintenance Module; or

 an Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) error that has been “Pending” for more than 30 days. EFT errors are issuances that were issued as “Paid”, but were rejected by the financial institution due to an error in the banking information and returned to DCFS. Once returned, the “Paid” issuance status was reset to “Pending” because the payment was rejected.

Pending payments must be researched to determine the cause of the error. The error must be corrected if possible.

If the documentation indicates additional participant contact or system updates are required to correct the problem, take appropriate action and monitor the case until the banking information is activated and the (funds) payables are deposited. The nightly batch process will automatically re-check the banking information to determine if the Pending payment can be released into an account. **

Division/Section 4-Economic Stability (ES) Chapter No./Name 04 – Family Assistance Manual (FAM) Part No./Name P-Strategies to Empower People (STEP) Program Section No./Name P-700-STEP Supportive Services Document No./Name P-770 STEP Recovery Effective Date March 1, 2012

1 of 2 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

The Department, in compliance with federal and state regulations, is mandated to collect overpayments and ineligible payments according to departmental policies and procedures.

II. PROCEDURES

All overpayments for supportive services and work activity placements must be promptly reported to the Fraud and Recovery Unit on a form STEP 20 except when the claim is a non-fraud claim of less than $100. This includes overpayments to both participants and providers.

All expenditures made on a participant's behalf during a period of ineligibility must also be reported to the Fraud and Recovery Unit.

Recovery action will be pursued by the Fraud and Recovery Unit in accordance with policy found in Chapter 16, the Fraud and Recovery Manual. The information on the form provides required case documentation on the acknowledgment, circumstances and explanation of the overpayment.

Ineligible payments or overpayments resulting from error or misrepresentation on the part of a provider will be recouped from the provider. Ineligible payments or overpayments resulting from error or misrepresentation on the part of the participant will be recouped from the participant.

Other supportive services overpayments can only be recouped from other supportive services benefits. Any recovery of other supportive services overpayments may be made from cash benefit payments only upon a voluntary request of the recipient family.

Voluntary return of benefits by the participant or provider to avoid an overpayment should be handled as follows:

● If the check has not been cashed, it should be voided and forwarded to DCFS Division of Fiscal Services Payment Management for processing. A cover memo should accompany the voided check to explain the circumstances surrounding the return.

● If the check has been cashed, and the repayment from the participant or provider is in the form of a personal check, business check or money order, then the appropriate form must be completed describing the circumstances. The check or money order, made payable to the Department of Children and Family Services, should be attached to the form STEP 20 and forwarded to the Fraud and Recovery Unit. This procedure must be followed no matter how promptly repayment was made and no matter the reason or circumstances.

● If the money rendered to the client is not used as intended then a recovery of the funds from the client will be initiated.

Division/Section Family Support Chapter No./Name 4 – Economic Stability (ES) Part No./Name S – Simplified Reporting Section No./Name S-100-FITAP-SNAP Introduction Document No./Name S-110-FITAP Introduction Effective Date January 1, 2023

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

SIMPLIFIED REPORTING (SR) ALLOWS THE AGENCY TO REDUCE AND SIMPLIFY THE RULES UNDER WHICH MOST SNAP HOUSEHOLDS INFORM THE STATE ABOUT CHANGES IN THEIR INCOME AND CIRCUMSTANCES DURING A CERTIFICATION PERIOD.

UNDER SIMPLIFIED REPORTING, SNAP HOUSEHOLDS, WITH THE EXCEPTION OF LaCAP HOUSEHOLDS, ALONG WITH ANY ASSOCIATED FITAP OR KCSP CASES, MUST SUBMIT A SIMPLIFIED REPORT AND REQUIRED VERIFICATION MIDWAY THROUGH THEIR CERTIFICATION PERIOD.

CHANGES THAT MUST BE REPORTED BY THE HOUSEHOLD AT SIMPLIFIED REPORTING ARE:

● CHANGES OF MORE THAN $100 IN UNEARNED INCOME,

● CHANGES IN THE SOURCE OF INCOME,

● CHANGES OF MORE THAN $100 IN EARNED INCOME,

● CHANGES IN HOUSEHOLD COMPOSITION,

● CHANGES IN RESIDENCE AND RESULTING CHANGES IN SHELTER COSTS,

● RESOURCES THAT EXCEED $2250 (FOR HOUSEHOLDS NOT CATEGORICALLY ELIGIBLE), AND

● CHANGES IN LEGALLY OBLIGATED CHILD SUPPORT PAYMENTS.

NO OTHER HOUSEHOLD CHANGES ARE REQUIRED TO BE REPORTED AT SIMPLIFIED REPORTING.

FITAP/KCSP households associated with a SNAP case in SR must follow the reporting requirements explained in the Family Success Agreement and report these changes within 10 days of knowledge of the change.

FITAP/KCSP households associated with a SNAP case in SR must report within ten days if the only child in the home moves out of the home.

ELIGIBILITY AND BENEFIT LEVEL FOR SIMPLIFIED REPORTING HOUSEHOLDS ARE DETERMINED PROSPECTIVELY BASED ON INFORMATION REPORTED ON THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT. THE DATE OF THE REPORT IS THE DATE THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT IS RECEIVED.

2 of 4 IF THE HOUSEHOLD REPORTED AN INTERIM CHANGE OR A NATIONAL DIRECTORY OF NEW HIRES (NDNH) HIT WAS RECEIVED OUTSIDE OF THE SIMPLIFIED REPORTING PROCESS AND ACTION WAS NOT TAKEN TO PROCESS THE CHANGE AND THE HOUSEHOLD DID NOT REPORT THE CHANGE ON THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT, THE CHANGE MUST BE REVIEWED AND DISCUSSED WITH THE HOUSEHOLD WHEN COMPLETING THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT. CASE NOTES MUST BE REVIEWED TO DETERMINE IF AN INTERIM CHANGE OR JOB REPORTED AS AN NDNH HIT NEEDS TO BE PROCESSED.

IF A SIMPLIFIED REPORTING HOUSEHOLD, ANOTHER AGENCY, ANOTHER PERSON, FRAUD HOTLINE, OR ANOTHER ENTITY WITHIN DCFS REPORTS A CHANGE OUTSIDE THE SIMPLIFIED REPORTING PROCESS, TIMELY ACTION MUST BE TAKEN IN ACCORDANCE WITH CHANGE PROCESSING PROCEDURES AS DEFINED IN C-820-FITAP/SNAP, C-830- FITAP/SNAP, AND C-840-FITAP/SNAP.

THE SIMPLIFIED REPORTING PROCESS IS COMPLETE WHEN A COMPLETE SIMPLIFIED REPORT, AS DEFINED IN S-510 FITAP/SNAP, INCLUDING ALL REQUIRED VERIFICATION, IS RECEIVED. DURING THE SIMPLIFIED REPORTING PROCESS:

● BENEFITS ARE DETERMINED BASED ON THE INFORMATION REPORTED ON THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT AND REQUIRED VERIFICATION.

● CHANGES THAT OCCUR AFTER THE COMPLETE SIMPLIFIED REPORT HAS BEEN RECEIVED ARE CONSIDERED TO BE OUTSIDE THE SIMPLIFIED REPORTING PROCESS, EVEN IF ACTION HAS NOT BEEN TAKEN ON THE CASE IN THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT MONTH. THESE CHANGES SHOULD BE MADE IN ACCORDANCE WITH CHANGE PROCESSING PROCEDURES AS DEFINED IN C-820-FITAP/SNAP, C-830-FITAP/SNAP AND C-840-SNAP/FITAP.

o EXAMPLE: A COMPLETE SIMPLIFIED REPORT IS RECEIVED ON SEPTEMBER 2nd. THE REPORTED CHANGES HAVE NOT BEEN PROCESSED. ON SEPTEMBER 25th, THE CLIENT CALLS TO REPORT THAT SHE LOST HER JOB. IT IS DETERMINED THAT THIS WOULD RESULT IN INCREASED BENEFITS. VERIFICATION MUST BE REQUESTED, ALLOWING THE HOUSEHOLD 10 DAYS TO PROVIDE THE REQUESTED VERIFICATION. IF THE VERIFICATION IS RECEIVED PRIOR TO CUTOFF IN SEPTEMBER, THE CASE WOULD BE AUTHORIZED BASED ON THE REPORTED CHANGE. IF THE VERIFICATION IS NOT RECEIVED PRIOR TO CUTOFF IN SEPTEMBER, UPDATE THE CASE USING THE INFORMATION PROVIDED ON THE COMPLETE SIMPLIFIED REPORT. IF THE VERIFICATION IS RECEIVED WITHIN 10 DAYS, THE CHANGE WOULD BE EFFECTIVE OCTOBER, WHICH IS THE MONTH FOLLOWING THE MONTH IN WHICH THE CHANGE WAS REPORTED. ISSUE SUPPLEMENTAL BENEFITS IF NEEDED. IF THE VERIFICATION IS RECEIVED MORE THAN 10 DAYS AFTER THE REQUEST FOR VERIFICATION, THE CHANGE WILL BE EFFECTIVE THE MONTH FOLLOWING THE MONTH IN WHICH THE VERIFICATION IS RECEIVED.

1 of 4 I. STATEMENT OF POLICY

SIMPLIFIED REPORTING (SR) ALLOWS THE AGENCY TO REDUCE AND SIMPLIFY THE RULES UNDER WHICH MOST SNAP HOUSEHOLDS INFORM THE STATE ABOUT CHANGES IN THEIR INCOME AND CIRCUMSTANCES DURING A CERTIFICATION PERIOD.

UNDER SIMPLIFIED REPORTING, SNAP HOUSEHOLDS, WITH THE EXCEPTION OF *** ELDERLY SIMPLIFIED APPLICATION PROCESS (ESAP), ALONG WITH ANY ASSOCIATED FITAP OR KCSP CASES, MUST SUBMIT A SIMPLIFIED REPORT AND REQUIRED VERIFICATION MIDWAY THROUGH THEIR CERTIFICATION PERIOD.

CHANGES THAT MUST BE REPORTED BY THE HOUSEHOLD AT SIMPLIFIED REPORTING ARE:

• CHANGES OF MORE THAN $100 IN UNEARNED INCOME,

• CHANGES IN THE SOURCE OF INCOME,

• CHANGES OF MORE THAN $100 IN EARNED INCOME,

• CHANGES IN HOUSEHOLD COMPOSITION,

• CHANGES IN RESIDENCE AND RESULTING CHANGES IN SHELTER COSTS,

• RESOURCES THAT EXCEED $3,000 (FOR HOUSEHOLDS NOT CATEGORICALLY ELIGIBLE), AND

• CHANGES IN LEGALLY OBLIGATED CHILD SUPPORT PAYMENTS.

NO OTHER HOUSEHOLD CHANGES ARE REQUIRED TO BE REPORTED AT THE SIMPLIFIED REPORT.

Simplified Reporting households are required to report if the household’s total income increases to more than 130% of the Federal Poverty Level for their household size. This includes reporting the income of a person who moves into the home if their income combined with the current SNAP household’s income increases to more than 130% of the Federal Poverty Level for their household size. Households are notified of the amount of the income limit for their household on the Automated Notice of Decision sent concerning each case action. These changes must be reported by the 10th day of the month following the month in which the household’s income increased to more than 130% of the Federal Poverty Level for their household size. A FITAP/KCSP household will be placed in Simplified Reporting at the time the associated SNAP case is placed in SR.

S-311-FITAP REPORTING INTERVALS
